# AI-Rulez

> Author, generate, validate and govern AI agent rules, skills, plugins and MCP configuration across 52 coding assistants. Review with verified model evidence, evaluate skills, lock and sign dependencies, and publish bundles. CLI, MCP server and Go API.

## Home

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/

<p align="center">
  <img src="assets/ai-rulez-banner.svg" alt="AI-Rulez" width="820" />
</p>

AI-Rulez keeps the instructions for your AI coding assistants in one place, `.ai-rulez/`, and generates the native
files of 52 assistants from it. You edit one source; `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/rules/`,
`.github/instructions/`, skill folders, MCP and settings files follow. AI-Rulez also validates that content, pins and
signs it, and packages it as plugins.

#### How it works

You write rules, context, skills, agents and commands as Markdown files and list the tools you use in
`.ai-rulez/config.toml`:

```toml
version = "5.0"
name = "acme"
presets = ["claude", "cursor", "codex", "copilot", "gemini"]
```

`ai-rulez generate` renders each tool's own layout from that one source:

```text
acme/
├── .ai-rulez/              # the source you edit
│   ├── config.toml
│   ├── rules/
│   ├── context/
│   └── skills/
├── AGENTS.md               # read by Codex, Cursor, Copilot and Gemini CLI
├── CLAUDE.md               # imports @AGENTS.md
├── .agents/skills/         # skills for tools that read .agents/skills
├── .claude/skills/         # skills for Claude Code
├── .gemini/settings.json   # points Gemini CLI at AGENTS.md
├── .mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .vscode/mcp.json, .codex/config.toml
└── ...
```

Change the source, run `generate` again, and every tool stays in sync. `ai-rulez generate --check` fails in CI when
the committed files drift from the source.

#### Get started

1. [Install](installation.md) the CLI, or run it with `npx ai-rulez@latest` or `uvx ai-rulez`.
2. Follow the [Quick start](quick-start.md): `init`, choose presets, add a rule, `generate`.
3. Commit `.ai-rulez/` together with the generated files.

Already have a `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` or `.cursor/rules/`? `ai-rulez init --from auto` imports them. Upgrading a
4.x project? See [Migrating to v5](migration-v5.md).

#### What you can do

| Area | What you do | Start with |
| ---- | ----------- | ---------- |
| **Author** | Write rules, context, skills, agents, commands and review checks; organize them with domains, profiles, roles and shared includes. | [Configuration](configuration.md), [Rules](rules.md), [Skill frontmatter](skills.md), [Domains and profiles](domains.md) |
| **Generate** | Render native files for 52 assistants, per project or in your home directory, with hooks, permissions and MCP servers translated for each. | [Supported harnesses](harnesses.md), [AGENTS.md](agents-md.md), [Hooks and settings](settings.md) |
| **Bundle and publish** | Package plugins and marketplaces, Agent Plugins and ARD manifests, and release them to GitHub, npm or OCI. | [Authoring plugins](plugins.md), [Publish](publish.md) |
| **Validate** | Lint configured projects, or plain `AGENTS.md`, `SKILL.md` and `.claude/` files with no configuration, using stable `AR` rule codes; catch harness traps; run repository verifiers in CI and git hooks. | [Strict validation](strict-validation.md), [Harness traps](harness-traps.md), [Verifiers](verifiers.md), [GitHub Actions](github-actions.md) |
| **Govern** | Pin sources and content in a lock file, record reviewer approvals, sign with Sigstore, enforce an organization policy and produce an SBOM. | [Trust model](trust-model.md), [Lock file](lockfile.md), [Signing](signing.md) |
| **Operate** | Serve configuration and skills over MCP, search skills, run evals, improve skills, review changes with a model and export telemetry. | [MCP server](mcp-server.md), [Evals](evals.md), [Review](review.md), [Judge](judge.md) |

The formats ai-rulez writes (AGENTS.md, Agent Skills, Agent Plugins, OKF, llms.txt, CycloneDX, SPDX, in-toto and
others) are checked against each standard's own schema or rules; [Standards conformance](standards.md) lists the
versions and known gaps.

#### Reference

- [CLI commands](cli.md) and the generated [CLI command reference](cli-reference.md).
- [Schema](schema.md): JSON schemas of the configuration and of every `--format json` report.
- [Architecture](architecture.md): how a source becomes generated files, and the package layout.
- [Standards conformance](standards.md): the open formats ai-rulez writes and how each is checked.

- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md).

#### Getting help

- `ai-rulez --help` and `ai-rulez <command> --help` describe every command and flag.
- `ai-rulez validate --explain AR001` explains a rule code and how to suppress it.
- `ai-rulez doctor` diagnoses a project (drift, removed presets, missing tools) without changing anything.
- Report problems on [GitHub](https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/issues).

This documentation covers ai-rulez v5 (`version = "5.0"` in `config.toml`).

## Installation

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/installation/

`ai-rulez` is a single binary, distributed through Homebrew, npm, PyPI and Go. Install it with the package manager you
already use, or run it without installing.

```bash
brew install goldziher/tap/ai-rulez
ai-rulez version
```

```text
ai-rulez version 5.10.0
```

#### Package managers

=== "Homebrew (macOS, Linux)"
    ```bash
    brew install goldziher/tap/ai-rulez
    ```

=== "npm"
    ```bash
    npm install -g ai-rulez
    # or
    pnpm add -g ai-rulez
    ```

    Requires Node.js 22 or newer. The package downloads the binary for your platform on first run and checks it
    against the release checksums.

=== "pip / pipx"
    ```bash
    pipx install ai-rulez
    # or
    pip install ai-rulez
    ```

    Requires Python 3.11 or newer.

=== "uv"
    ```bash
    uv tool install ai-rulez
    ```

Release binaries are built for Linux and macOS (amd64 and arm64) and Windows (amd64). Linux binaries need glibc 2.36 or
newer; Alpine (musl) is not supported.

#### Run without installing

```bash
npx ai-rulez@latest generate
pnpm dlx ai-rulez@latest generate
uvx ai-rulez generate
```

Pin a version (`npx ai-rulez@5.10.0`, `uvx --from ai-rulez==5.10.0 ai-rulez`) when a script or hook must not change
behavior between releases.

#### Go

```bash
go install github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/v5/cmd/ai-rulez@latest
```

The module path must include `/v5`; without it, `@latest` resolves to an old 1.x release.

`go install` builds with cgo and links the native library shipped in the Go module dynamically, so it needs a C
toolchain to build and the Go module cache to stay in place at run time. For a binary you distribute, use a release
package, or build a statically linked binary from a clone with [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez
cd ai-rulez
mise run build
./bin/ai-rulez version
```

To embed ai-rulez as a library instead, see [Embedding (Go API)](embedding.md).

#### Shell completion

=== "Bash"
    Add to `~/.bashrc`:

    ```bash
    source <(ai-rulez completion bash)
    ```

=== "Zsh"
    Add to `~/.zshrc`:

    ```bash
    source <(ai-rulez completion zsh)
    ```

=== "Fish"
    Add to `~/.config/fish/config.fish`:

    ```bash
    ai-rulez completion fish | source
    ```

=== "PowerShell"
    Add to your PowerShell profile:

    ```powershell
    ai-rulez completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
    ```

#### Git hooks

Run `generate` and `validate` before each commit so the generated files never drift from `.ai-rulez/`.

When you create a project, `ai-rulez init --setup-hooks` detects an existing pre-commit, Lefthook or Husky
configuration and adds ai-rulez to it; with none present it does nothing. `--setup-hooks` is an `init` flag, so in an
existing project add the hooks by hand:

=== "pre-commit / prek"
    Add to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

    ```yaml
    repos:
      - repo: https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez
        rev: v5.10.0
        hooks:
          - id: ai-rulez-recursive
          - id: ai-rulez-validate
    ```

    The hooks run only when a file under a `.ai-rulez/` directory changes. They use the `ai-rulez` on `PATH`, or
    download and cache a checksum-verified release binary when there is none.

    | Hook id | Runs |
    | ------- | ---- |
    | `ai-rulez-generate` | `generate` for the root `.ai-rulez/` |
    | `ai-rulez-recursive` | `generate --recursive` for every nested `.ai-rulez/` |
    | `ai-rulez-validate` | `validate --recursive` |
    | `ai-rulez-plugin-generate` | `generate --recursive --plugin --if-configured` |
    | `ai-rulez-plugin-verify` | `verify --recursive --plugin --if-configured` |

    Add the two plugin hooks if the repository publishes plugin bundles; `--if-configured` makes them do nothing in a
    repository without a `[plugin]` or `[marketplace]` block.

=== "Lefthook"
    Add to `lefthook.yml`:

    ```yaml
    pre-commit:
      commands:
        ai-rulez:
          glob: ".ai-rulez/**"
          run: ai-rulez generate --recursive --no-local
        ai-rulez-validate:
          glob: ".ai-rulez/**"
          run: ai-rulez validate --recursive --no-local
    ```

=== "Poly"
    See [Poly hooks](poly-hooks.md).

The shipped pre-commit hooks do not pass `--no-local`, so they read a developer's gitignored `config.local.toml` and
`.ai-rulez/local/` content like any local run. To check only the shared configuration, pass `--no-local` as the
Lefthook example does; with pre-commit, override the hook's arguments (`args: [validate, --recursive, --no-local]`). See
[Machine-local configuration in hooks](poly-hooks.md#machine-local-configuration-in-hooks).

#### CI

The `Goldziher/ai-rulez` GitHub Action installs a checksum-verified, cached binary with no Go, Node or Python setup:

```yaml
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v7
  - uses: Goldziher/ai-rulez@v5
    with:
      version: 5.10.0
  - run: ai-rulez generate --check
  - run: ai-rulez validate
```

`validate` fails on errors; add `--strict` to fail on warnings too.

See [GitHub Actions](github-actions.md) for version pinning, the governance gate and scheduled updates.

#### Next steps

Follow the [Quick start](quick-start.md) to create a configuration and generate your first files.

## Quick start

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/quick-start/

Set up ai-rulez in a repository, add a rule, and generate the files for five assistants. It takes about five minutes.

<p align="center">
  <img src="assets/quickstart.gif" alt="ai-rulez init and generate: one .ai-rulez source becomes the native files of several AI tools" width="820" />
</p>

You need the `ai-rulez` CLI ([Installation](installation.md)). To try it without installing, replace `ai-rulez` with
`npx ai-rulez@latest` or `uvx ai-rulez` in every command below.

!!! note "Already have instruction files?"
    If the repository already has a hand-written `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.cursor/rules/` or similar, start with
    `ai-rulez init --from auto` instead of `ai-rulez init acme` in step 1; see
    [Starting from existing files](#starting-from-existing-files). `generate` refuses to overwrite files it did not
    write.

#### 1. Create the configuration

Run `init` at the root of your repository:

```bash
ai-rulez init acme
```

```text
Created .ai-rulez/ for acme
...
Example content created:
  - rules/code-quality.md
  - context/architecture.md
  - skills/code-reviewer/SKILL.md
  - skills/ai-rulez/SKILL.md
```

`.ai-rulez/` now holds the configuration and some example content you can edit or delete:

```text
.ai-rulez/
├── config.toml
├── index.md
├── rules/
│   ├── code-quality.md
│   └── index.md
├── context/
│   ├── architecture.md
│   └── index.md
├── skills/
│   ├── ai-rulez/
│   │   ├── SKILL.md
│   │   └── index.md
│   ├── code-reviewer/
│   │   ├── SKILL.md
│   │   └── index.md
│   └── index.md
├── agents/
└── domains/
```

| Directory | Holds | Loaded by the assistant |
| --------- | ----- | ----------------------- |
| `rules/` | Instructions the assistant must follow | Always, or only for matching files |
| `context/` | Background: architecture, conventions, glossary | Always |
| `skills/` | `SKILL.md` playbooks with optional scripts and references | On demand, when the task matches the description |
| `agents/` | Subagent definitions | When delegated to |
| `domains/` | The same folders, per team or subsystem | When a profile selects the domain |

The `index.md` files list the content of each folder. `ai-rulez` maintains them; you do not edit them.

#### 2. Choose your tools

Open `.ai-rulez/config.toml` and set `presets` to the assistants your team uses:

```toml
version = "5.0"
name = "acme"
presets = ["claude", "cursor", "codex", "copilot", "gemini"]
```

The comment above `presets` in the generated file lists all 52 built-in presets; [Supported harnesses](harnesses.md)
describes what each one writes.

#### 3. Add a rule

```bash
ai-rulez add rule testing --priority high --content '# Testing

- Every bug fix ships with a regression test.
- Run `make test` before you commit.'
```

```text
Rule added successfully
.ai-rulez/rules/testing.md
```

The file it writes:

```markdown
---
type: Decision
title: Testing
x-ai-rulez:
  kind: rule
  id: testing
  metadata:
    priority: high
---

# Testing

- Every bug fix ships with a regression test.
- Run `make test` before you commit.
```

You can also create files by hand. `.ai-rulez/` is an [OKF](okf.md) bundle, so each file should have a `type`
(`Decision` for rules, `Concept` for context, `Playbook` for skills); `title` is optional. ai-rulez settings such as
`priority` and `paths` go under `x-ai-rulez.metadata`. See [Rules](rules.md) for path-scoped rules and activation modes.

#### 4. Generate

```bash
ai-rulez generate
```

```text
Warning: generate will write 1 new or changed command(s) that your tools will run (from .../acme/.ai-rulez/config.toml):
  hook       SessionStart: sh -c '...'  -> claude
Review them before you start a tool in this project. Silence with --yes or AI_RULEZ_ACK_COMMANDS=1.
INFO  Generating with configuration profile=default
INFO  Generation complete files=12
```

`generate` lists every command it adds to a tool's configuration so you can review it. The `SessionStart` hook here is
the default [remote-session hook](session-start.md), which runs `ai-rulez generate` when a cloud session starts.

The files it wrote:

| File | Used by |
| ---- | ------- |
| `AGENTS.md` | All rules and context, for Codex, Cursor, Copilot and (through `.gemini/settings.json`) Gemini CLI |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Claude Code; contains `@AGENTS.md`, so it loads the same instructions |
| `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | Skills for the tools that read `.agents/skills` |
| `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | Skills for Claude Code |
| `.gemini/settings.json` | Tells Gemini CLI to read `AGENTS.md` |
| `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json`, `.codex/config.toml` | The ai-rulez MCP server, in each tool's format |
| `.claude/settings.json` | The `SessionStart` hook |

The start of `AGENTS.md`:

```markdown
<!--
🤖 AI-RULEZ :: GENERATED FILE — DO NOT EDIT
Project: acme
Source: .ai-rulez/config.toml
...
-->

# acme

## Rules

### code-quality

**Priority:** high
...

### testing

**Priority:** high

- Every bug fix ships with a regression test.
- Run `make test` before you commit.

## Context

### architecture
...
```

To get one instruction file per tool
(`GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, ...) instead of a shared `AGENTS.md`, set `agents_md = false`; see
[AGENTS.md and .agents/skills](agents-md.md).

#### 5. Validate and commit

```bash
ai-rulez validate          # content, link and security checks
ai-rulez generate --check  # exits 2 if a generated file differs from the source
```

```text
validation: no findings in 1 root(s)
INFO  Generated files are up to date roots=1
```

Commit the source and the generated files together:

```bash
git add .ai-rulez AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md .agents .claude .codex .cursor .gemini .vscode .mcp.json
git commit -m "Add ai-rulez configuration"
```

Generated files are committed by default, so every teammate and CI job sees the same instructions. To keep them out of
git instead, set `gitignore = true` in `config.toml`; `generate` then maintains a managed block in `.gitignore`.

#### Day-to-day use

| Task | Command |
| ---- | ------- |
| Regenerate after editing `.ai-rulez/` | `ai-rulez generate` |
| Regenerate on every change | `ai-rulez generate --watch` |
| Add a skill, agent or command | `ai-rulez add skill db-migrations`, `ai-rulez add agent reviewer`, `ai-rulez add command release` |
| Add a personal, gitignored rule | `ai-rulez add rule my-notes --local` ([Local configuration](local-overrides.md)) |
| Remove everything `generate` wrote | `ai-rulez clean` |
| Diagnose the setup | `ai-rulez doctor` |

#### Starting from existing files

If the repository already has a hand-written `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.cursor/rules/` or similar, import it
instead of starting from the example content. In a repository without `.ai-rulez/`:

```bash
ai-rulez init --from auto
```

If you already ran `ai-rulez init`, `init --from` refuses to replace the existing `.ai-rulez/`; import into it
instead:

```bash
ai-rulez convert --write
```

Both run [convert](cli.md#ai-rulez-convert), which maps each file into `.ai-rulez/` and prints what it mapped,
approximated or dropped. The next `generate` replaces the originals with generated files. Without an import,
`generate` stops at the existing file:

```text
Error: refusing to overwrite 1 existing file(s) ai-rulez cannot prove it wrote: CLAUDE.md (an existing file ai-rulez did not write). Import the file with `ai-rulez convert --write`, move or delete it, or pass --force to overwrite it
```

#### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
| ------- | --- |
| ``error AR9B1 okf-type-invalid: frontmatter has no non-empty `type` `` | A hand-written file has frontmatter without `type`. Add `type` (step 3), or create the file with `ai-rulez add`. |
| `warning AR9B1 okf-type-invalid: no frontmatter block` | The file is plain Markdown. It still loads; add frontmatter with `type`, or run `ai-rulez migrate okf` to add it. |
| `warning AR9B0 okf-index-mismatch: concept ... is not listed` | Run `ai-rulez generate`; it refreshes the `index.md` listings. |
| A rule does not appear in a tool's file | Check the rule's `targets` and `paths` ([Rules](rules.md)) and that the tool is in `presets`. |
| `generate --check` fails in CI | Someone edited `.ai-rulez/` without regenerating. Run `ai-rulez generate` and commit the result. |

#### Next steps

- [Configuration](configuration.md): every key in `config.toml`.
- [Domains & profiles](domains.md): content per team, selected with `--profile`.
- [Skill frontmatter](skills.md) and [Rules](rules.md): activation, scoping and per-tool output.
- [Includes](includes.md) and [Installed skills](installed-skills.md): share content across repositories.
- [GitHub Actions](github-actions.md): check generated files and run validation in CI.

## Examples

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/examples/

Complete configurations for common setups. Each example shows the files you write in `.ai-rulez/`, the command you
run and what it generates.

Start every example from a project created with `ai-rulez init` (see the [Quick start](quick-start.md)). `init` makes
`.ai-rulez/` an [OKF](okf.md) bundle with `index.md` listings; a tree you build by hand without them is the deprecated
pre-OKF layout and logs a deprecation notice. In an OKF tree, content files use OKF frontmatter: a `type` (`Decision`
for rules, `Concept` for context, `Playbook` for skills), an optional `title`, and ai-rulez settings under
`x-ai-rulez.metadata`. `ai-rulez add` writes this frontmatter for you; `ai-rulez generate` keeps the `index.md`
listings up to date.

#### Rules scoped to part of the repository

A web project where TypeScript rules should load only when the assistant works on TypeScript files.

`.ai-rulez/config.toml`:

```toml
version = "5.0"
name = "web"
presets = ["cursor", "copilot", "codex"]

[rules]
scoped_fallback = "skill"
```

`.ai-rulez/rules/typescript.md`:

```markdown
---
type: Decision
title: TypeScript
x-ai-rulez:
  kind: rule
  id: typescript
  metadata:
    priority: high
    paths: ["src/**/*.ts", "src/**/*.tsx"]
---

# TypeScript

- Enable `strict` in `tsconfig.json`.
- Prefer `unknown` over `any`.
```

```bash
ai-rulez generate
```

Each tool with a rules folder gets the rule there, in its own scoping syntax. Codex has no rules folder, so
`scoped_fallback = "skill"` serves the rule as a skill that applies to the same paths:

```text
.cursor/rules/typescript.mdc                      # globs: src/**/*.ts,src/**/*.tsx
.github/instructions/typescript.instructions.md   # applyTo: src/**/*.ts,src/**/*.tsx
.agents/skills/rule-typescript/SKILL.md           # paths: [src/**/*.ts, src/**/*.tsx]
```

The rule is not in `AGENTS.md`, so it costs nothing while the assistant works on other files. Without
`scoped_fallback = "skill"`, `generate` inlines scoped rules into `AGENTS.md` for tools without a rules folder and
warns that the tools with one then load them in every session; see
[Glob-scoped rules and AGENTS.md](rules.md#glob-scoped-rules-and-agentsmd).

#### A skill with a script

Skills are loaded on demand: the assistant sees the `description` and reads the body only when the task matches.
Files next to `SKILL.md` (`scripts/`, `references/`, `assets/`) are copied with it.

```text
.ai-rulez/skills/release/
├── SKILL.md
└── scripts/
    └── check.sh
```

`.ai-rulez/skills/release/SKILL.md`:

```markdown
---
type: Playbook
title: Release
description: Cut a release of the web app. Use when asked to tag, version or publish a release.
x-ai-rulez:
  kind: skill
  id: release
---

# Release

1. Run `scripts/check.sh` and stop if it fails.
2. Bump the version in `package.json`.
3. Tag the commit `vX.Y.Z` and push the tag.
```

With the presets of the previous example, `ai-rulez generate` writes the skill, script included, to the shared skill
folder:

```text
.agents/skills/release/SKILL.md
.agents/skills/release/scripts/check.sh
```

Tools with their own skill folder get a copy there too, for example `.claude/skills/release/` for `claude`.

See [Skill frontmatter](skills.md) for `allowed-tools`, served skills and other keys.

#### One instruction file per tool, and an MCP server

By default all tools share one `AGENTS.md`. With `agents_md = false`, each tool gets its own root file. This example
also limits one rule to a single tool and adds an MCP server for every tool.

`.ai-rulez/config.toml`:

```toml
version = "5.0"
name = "billing"
agents_md = false
presets = ["claude", "gemini", "copilot"]

[[mcp_servers]]
name = "postgres"
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres@0.6.2", "${DATABASE_URL}"]
```

`.ai-rulez/rules/money.md`:

```markdown
---
type: Decision
title: Money
x-ai-rulez:
  kind: rule
  id: money
  metadata:
    priority: critical
---

# Money

- Store amounts as integer minor units, never floats.
```

`.ai-rulez/rules/claude-subagents.md`, written only for Claude Code:

```markdown
---
type: Decision
title: Subagents
x-ai-rulez:
  kind: rule
  id: claude-subagents
  metadata:
    targets: ["claude"]
---

# Subagents

- Run database migrations in a subagent, never in the main session.
```

```bash
ai-rulez generate
```

```text
CLAUDE.md
.claude/rules/money.md
.claude/rules/claude-subagents.md
GEMINI.md
.gemini/settings.json                       # postgres and ai-rulez MCP servers
.github/copilot-instructions.md
.github/instructions/money.instructions.md
.mcp.json                                   # postgres and ai-rulez MCP servers
.vscode/mcp.json
```

`${DATABASE_URL}` is written as a reference, never as the resolved value, in tools that support environment
references. `generate` also adds the ai-rulez MCP server itself; set `[mcp] self_server = false` to leave it out. See
[Configuration](configuration.md) for MCP server keys and [Rules](rules.md#targets) for `targets`.

#### Teams with domains and profiles

A platform repository where the backend and frontend teams each have their own rules. Root content applies to
everyone; a profile selects which domains are added.

```text
.ai-rulez/
├── config.toml
├── rules/security.md
└── domains/
    ├── backend/rules/database.md
    └── frontend/rules/components.md
```

Create the domains and their rules with the CLI:

```bash
ai-rulez domain add backend
ai-rulez domain add frontend
ai-rulez add rule security --priority critical --content '# Security

- Validate all user input.'
ai-rulez add rule database --domain backend --priority critical --content '# Database

- Use prepared statements.'
ai-rulez add rule components --domain frontend --content '# Components

- One component per file.'
```

Then define the profiles in `.ai-rulez/config.toml`:

```toml
version = "5.0"
name = "platform"
presets = ["claude", "cursor", "codex"]
default = "full"

[profiles]
full = ["backend", "frontend"]
backend = ["backend"]
frontend = ["frontend"]
```

```bash
ai-rulez generate                     # default profile "full": security, database, components
ai-rulez generate --profile backend   # security, database
ai-rulez generate --profile frontend  # security, components
```

Set `default` when you define `[profiles]`. Without it, a run without `--profile` includes no domain content and
`generate` warns. See [Domains & profiles](domains.md) and, for per-person filtering, [Roles](roles.md).

#### Shared rules from another repository

Keep organization-wide rules in one repository and include them everywhere. A version constraint picks the newest
matching tag.

```toml
version = "5.0"
name = "web"
presets = ["cursor", "codex"]

[[includes]]
name = "org-standards"
source = "https://github.com/acme/ai-standards.git"
version = "^1.2"
include = ["rules", "skills"]
merge_strategy = "local-override"
```

`include` limits what is taken from the source; `merge_strategy = "local-override"` (the default) lets a local item
with the same name win. Pin what was resolved in `.ai-rulez/ai-rulez.lock` and commit it with the configuration:

```bash
ai-rulez generate
ai-rulez lock
git add .ai-rulez
```

`ai-rulez lock --outdated` reports newer matching tags and `ai-rulez update` moves the pin. See [Includes](includes.md)
and [Lock file](lockfile.md).

#### Monorepo with nested projects

Each service keeps its own `.ai-rulez/` next to its code, and the repository root has one for shared conventions.

```text
acme/
├── .ai-rulez/
│   ├── config.toml
│   └── rules/commits.md
└── services/
    └── api/
        └── .ai-rulez/
            ├── config.toml
            └── rules/endpoints.md
```

```bash
ai-rulez generate --recursive
ai-rulez validate --recursive
```

Each root generates its own files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, ...) in its own directory. Tools that read nested
instruction files load the service's file in addition to the root's when they work in `services/api/`. A local
include in a nested project must stay inside that project's directory; share content across services with a git
include or the repository-root configuration. See [Monorepo](monorepo.md).

## Migrating to v5

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/migration-v5/

Upgrade a 4.x project to ai-rulez 5. `ai-rulez migrate v5` rewrites the configuration for you; the breaking changes
below are the ones you handle yourself. The complete list is in the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md).

#### Upgrade in four steps

1. Commit or stash your work, then preview the change list: `ai-rulez migrate v5 --dry-run`. Nothing is written.
2. Run `ai-rulez migrate v5`. It rewrites the project in place. Add `--recursive` for a repository with several
   `.ai-rulez/` directories.
3. Run `ai-rulez doctor`. It reports removed presets with their replacement, drifted outputs and generated paths git
   does not ignore.
4. Run `ai-rulez generate`, review the diff, and commit the sources and outputs together.

Then run `ai-rulez lock` once if the project has an `ai-rulez.lock` (see [Lock file](#lock-file)), and update CI
scripts for the [changed commands and flags](#commands-and-flags).

`migrate v5` reads only 4.x projects. Migrate a 2.x or 3.x project to 4.0 with ai-rulez 4.x first
(`npx ai-rulez@4 migrate v4`), then run `ai-rulez migrate v5`. Until a project is migrated, every v5 command stops with
the next step:

```text
Error: config version "4.2" is no longer supported: run `ai-rulez migrate v5`
Error: config version "3.0" is no longer supported; install ai-rulez 4.x to migrate it to 4.0, then run `ai-rulez migrate v5`
```

#### What `migrate v5` changes

A 4.x project:

```yaml
# .ai-rulez/config.yaml
# acme rules
version: "4.0"
name: acme
presets:
  - claude
  - windsurf
lint:
  budget:
    AR401: 3
```

```bash
ai-rulez migrate v5
```

```text
. (.ai-rulez): migrated
  [convert-format] .ai-rulez/config.yaml: converted to config.toml with keys, order and comments kept; config.yaml is removed
  [version] .ai-rulez/config.toml: version 4.0 -> 5.0
  [lint-ratchet] .ai-rulez/config.toml: [lint.budget] / [lint.tolerate] renamed to [lint.ratchet] (per-rule finding counts); size limits stay in [lint.budgets]
  [preset-rename] .ai-rulez/config.toml: preset windsurf renamed to devin (outputs move from .windsurf/ to .devin/; delete the old directory)
  [pin-default] .ai-rulez/config.toml: agents_md = false (v5 default: true, AGENTS.md is the canonical instruction file)
  [pin-default] .ai-rulez/config.toml: gitignore = true (v5 default: false, no managed .gitignore block)
  [pin-default] .ai-rulez/config.toml: [header] hashes = "full" (v5 default: "content", only the per-file Content-Hash)
  [pin-default] .ai-rulez/config.toml: [mcp] self_server = false (v5 default: true, generate adds the ai-rulez MCP server to .mcp.json)
migrated 1, unchanged 0, errors 0
```

The resulting `.ai-rulez/config.toml`:

```toml
# acme rules
version = "5.0"
name = "acme"
presets = ["claude", "devin"]
# Pinned by `ai-rulez migrate v5`: the 4.x default. Remove this line to take the v5 default.
agents_md = false
# Pinned by `ai-rulez migrate v5`: the 4.x default. Remove this line to take the v5 default.
gitignore = true

[lint]

[lint.ratchet]
AR401 = 3

# Pinned by `ai-rulez migrate v5`: the 4.x default. Remove this line to take the v5 default.
[header]
hashes = "full"

# Pinned by `ai-rulez migrate v5`: the 4.x default. Remove this line to take the v5 default.
[mcp]
self_server = false
```

Each change has a rule name, shown in brackets in the report:

| Rule | Rewrite |
| ---- | ------- |
| `version` | `version = "4.x"` becomes `version = "5.0"`; the rest of the line, including a comment, is kept. |
| `convert-format` | `config.yaml`, `config.yml` or `config.json` becomes `config.toml` with keys, order and comments kept, and the old file is removed. `$schema` becomes `schema`. |
| `local-overlay` | `config.local.yaml`, `.yml` or `.json` becomes `config.local.toml` (mode 0600). |
| `mcp-merge` | A separate `mcp.toml`, `mcp.yaml` or `mcp.json` is merged into `[[mcp_servers]]` in `config.toml` and removed. If `config.toml` already defines `mcp_servers`, the file is left in place with a warning; move the servers by hand. |
| `lint-ratchet` | `[lint.budget]` and `[lint.tolerate]` become `[lint.ratchet]` (per-rule finding counts). `[lint.budgets.<kind>]` (size limits) is unchanged. |
| `preset-rename` | The `windsurf` preset becomes `devin` and the removed `continue-dev` preset is dropped. With `--write`, `windsurf_model` in agent frontmatter becomes `devin_model`. |
| `skills-table` | A `[[skills]]` array is removed; skills in `.ai-rulez/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` are discovered without it. |
| `pin-default` | The four defaults that changed in v5 are pinned to their 4.x value so the generated output does not move: `agents_md = false`, `gitignore = true`, `[header] hashes = "full"` and `[mcp] self_server = false`. A key you already set is never touched. |
| `gitignore-block` | With `--adopt-defaults`, the managed `.gitignore` block is removed unless the configuration sets `gitignore = true`. |
| `command-rename` | `ai-rulez usage ...` and `ai-rulez report usage\|evals` inside hook, verifier and script commands become `ai-rulez telemetry ...`. |
| `frontmatter-alias` | `permission_mode` and `user_invocable` become `permissionMode` and `user-invocable`. Reported only; rewritten with `--write`. |

##### Options

| Flag | Effect |
| ---- | ------ |
| `--dry-run`, `-n` | Print the change list; write nothing. |
| `--check` | Like `--dry-run`, and exit 2 while a project still needs migration. Use it in CI. |
| `--adopt-defaults` | Take the v5 defaults instead of pinning the 4.x ones. Regenerate and review the diff. |
| `--write` | Also rewrite frontmatter aliases in the Markdown sources. |
| `--recursive` | Migrate every project found below the selected directory. |
| `--format json` | A machine-readable report: `schema_version` and one entry per project with `status`, `changes`, `warnings` and `error`. |
| `-C <dir or file>` | Migrate the project at that configuration directory or file, for example `-C plugin/.ai-rulez`. |

The rewrite is text-level, so comments survive, and the result is loaded again before it is written; a file that would
not load is reported and left alone. Running `migrate v5` again on a migrated project changes nothing. Exit codes: `0`
migrated or nothing to do, `1` a project could not be migrated, `2` `--check` found work.

#### Breaking changes

##### Configuration files

- **Only `version = "5.0"` is accepted.**
- **Only TOML is read.** `config.yaml`, `config.yml`, `config.json`, their `config.local.*` forms and separate `mcp.*`
  files stop every command with
  ``Error: found <path>: YAML and JSON configs are no longer read; run `ai-rulez migrate v5` to convert it to config.toml``.
  Markdown frontmatter is still YAML.
- **`init --format yaml|json` is removed**; `init` writes `config.toml`.
- **`[lint.budget]` and `[lint.tolerate]` are refused**; the table is `[lint.ratchet]`. The JSON report key is
  `ratchet_exceeded`.
- **`[[skills]]` is not a configuration key.** `skills` is the `[skills]` dynamic-loading table. Keep skills in
  `.ai-rulez/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, install them with `ai-rulez skill install`, or use `[[skill_sources]]`.
- **`[[plugins]]` has no effect** and `generate` warns about it. List the plugins to enable as
  `[[enabled_plugins]]` with `id = "name@marketplace"`; `generate` writes them to `.claude/settings.json` and
  `.codex/config.toml`. Delete any `.claude/plugins.json` or `.codex/plugins.json` an earlier version left.
- **The `compression` option is removed.** `generate` warns about it as an unknown key; `validate` and
  `generate --strict-config` fail.
- **`~/.ai-rulez.{toml,yaml,json}` and `./.ai-rulez.*` are not read.**

##### Defaults

| Setting | v5 default | 4.x behavior | Keep the 4.x behavior with |
| ------- | ---------- | ------------ | -------------------------- |
| `agents_md` | `true`: `AGENTS.md` is the single instruction file, `CLAUDE.md` imports `@AGENTS.md`, skills go to `.agents/skills` where the tool reads them | One root file per tool | `agents_md = false` |
| `gitignore` | `false`: generated files are committed | Managed `.gitignore` block | `gitignore = true` |
| `[header] hashes` | `"content"`: only the per-file `Content-Hash` line | Also a project-wide `Source-Hash` line, which rewrote every file on any edit | `hashes = "full"` (`"none"` drops both) |
| `[mcp] self_server` | `true`: `generate` adds the ai-rulez MCP server to the MCP files it writes | Not added | `self_server = false`, or `generate --no-self-mcp` |
| `[lock] enforce` | `true` whenever `ai-rulez.lock` exists | Off | `enforce = false` |
| `[lint.security] scan_imports` | On: includes and installed skills are scanned before anything is written | Off | `scan_imports = "off"` (or `"warn"`) |

`migrate v5` pins the first four unless you pass `--adopt-defaults`. Machine-local files (`config.local.*`,
`.ai-rulez/local/`) are ignored by git whatever `gitignore` says.

##### Commands and flags

- **`validate` runs the content checks by default**: dead links, globs that match nothing, missing hooks, oversize
  content and the security rules. A CI job that passed with `ai-rulez validate` can now exit 2. Fix the findings, lower
  a rule with `[lint.severity]`, record the current findings with `--update-baseline`, or keep the old configuration-only
  check with `validate --config-only`.
- **`--strict` means "warnings fail"** (`--fail-on warning`), and exists only on `validate`, `doctor` and
  `verifiers run`. Replace `validate --strict` with `validate` in scripts unless warnings should fail.
- **`verify` checks only signatures, approvals and plugin provenance** (`--attestation`, `--approvals`, `--self`,
  `--plugin`). Use `generate --check` to compare generated files with their sources; a bare `verify` exits 1 and says
  so.
- **`scan` runs only the security analyzer.** Hook and configuration findings are reported by `validate`.
- **`usage` and `report` are replaced by `telemetry`**, with no aliases. Regenerate hook blocks you wrote by hand
  with `ai-rulez telemetry hook`.

  | 4.x | 5.0 |
  | --- | --- |
  | `ai-rulez usage hook` | `ai-rulez telemetry hook` |
  | `ai-rulez usage record` | `ai-rulez telemetry record` (skill and item loads in one command) |
  | `ai-rulez usage feedback` | `ai-rulez telemetry feedback` |
  | `ai-rulez report usage <log>` | `ai-rulez telemetry report [log]` |
  | `ai-rulez report evals` | `ai-rulez telemetry report evals` |

- **Seven short flags, each with one meaning everywhere:** `-C` `--config`, `-D` `--debug`, `-T` `--token`, `-q`
  `--quiet`, `-y` `--yes`, `-n` `--dry-run` and `-o` `--output`. Every other short flag is removed; using one is an
  unknown-flag error.
- **Renamed and removed flags:**

  | 4.x | 5.0 |
  | --- | --- |
  | `--json`, `-j` | `--format json` |
  | `-n <dir>`, `--config-dir <dir>` on individual commands | `--config-dir <dir>`, a global flag with no short form |
  | `-d` (`--dry-run`) | `-n`, `--dry-run` |
  | `ai-rulez validate path/.ai-rulez` (positional configuration path, on every command) | `ai-rulez -C path/.ai-rulez validate` |
  | `generate --no-fetch`, `-f` | `generate --offline` |
  | `generate --strict` (unknown keys fail) | `generate --strict-config` (or `AI_RULEZ_STRICT=1`) |
  | `generate --update-gitignore` | `generate --gitignore` |
  | `clean --force`, `remove --force` and the other confirmation skips | `--yes`, `-y` |
  | `lock --strict` | `lock --refuse-findings` |
  | `sign --policy <file>` (sign a policy) | `sign --org-policy <file>` |
  | `sbom --format cyclonedx\|spdx-json` | `sbom --type cyclonedx\|spdx-json` |
  | `telemetry hook --format json\|toml` | `telemetry hook --syntax json\|toml` |
  | `export okf --out <dir>`, `eval run --out`, `eval import --out`, `publish emit --out` | `--output-dir <dir>` |
  | `review --out`, `search --out`, `verifiers run --out` and similar | `--output`, `-o` |
  | `--verbose`, `-V` | `--debug`, `-D` |
  | `--no-configure-cli-mcp`, `--skip-cli-mcp` | Removed (they had no effect) |
  | `mcp --transport`, `--address`, `--port` | Removed (the server is stdio only) |

  `convert --force`, `eval run --force` and `import okf --force` (overwrite or re-run) are unchanged. The `--policy`
  flags exist only on the commands that evaluate policy; `AI_RULEZ_POLICY` works everywhere. See
  [Flag conventions](cli.md#flag-conventions).
- **Removed command aliases:** `g` (`generate`), `clear` (`clean`), `v` and `check` (`validate`) and `check`
  (`list checks`). `gen` and `val` remain.
- **`migrate` has subcommands**, `migrate v5` and `migrate okf`; `migrate` alone prints help and `migrate v4` is an
  unknown command. Group commands such as `list` print their help and exit 0 when given no subcommand.
- **Stricter content names**, also through the MCP tools: a name must not end in `.md`, contain whitespace or start with
  `.` or `-`; `--targets` must name presets, paths or globs. `domain remove` refuses while a profile lists the domain.
- **An unknown `builtins` entry fails `validate`** with the valid choices.
- **The content commands honor the global `--config-dir` and `-C`** (`add`, `remove`, `show`, `edit`, `list`, `domain`,
  `profile`, `include`, `skill`), so a script that passed one now acts on that directory.
- **`eval run` prints text by default**; pass `--format markdown` for the previous output.

##### Output, errors and JSON

- **Results go to stdout, diagnostics to stderr.** Lists (`list`, `domain list`, `profile list`, `include list`,
  `skill list`), `clean --dry-run` and `lock --check` print on stdout; `-q` never hides them. `-q` hides progress and
  information but no longer hides warnings. Confirmation prompts are on stderr.
- **The content commands print the path they changed** on stdout (`add`, `remove`, `edit`, `domain add|remove`); the
  "added successfully" line is on stderr. They also take `--format json`.
- **One error format:** `Error: <message>`, an optional `Validation errors:` list and `Hint: <hint>` on stderr. Under
  `--format json`, a failure also prints an error document on stdout.
- **Every `--format json` document carries `schema_version`.** List commands and multi-profile `tokens` return
  `{"schema_version": 1, "items": [...]}` instead of a bare array; `publish verify --format json` always returns
  `{"schema_version": 1, "results": [...]}`. The schemas are in `schema/`; see [JSON contracts](cli.md#json-contracts).
- **`schema/catalog.schema.json` describes catalog version 2.** Version 1 is `schema/catalog.v1.schema.json`, and
  `catalog --format json` prints version 1 unless you pass `--schema-version 2`.
- **Unprefixed environment variables are ignored.** Use `AI_RULEZ_DEBUG=1` and `AI_RULEZ_QUIET=1` instead of `DEBUG`
  and `QUIET`.

##### Exit codes

Every command follows one contract: `0` success, `1` the command could not run, `2` findings, drift or a failed gate,
`3` only for `lock` (written, with served skills left unpinned). See [Exit codes](cli.md#exit-codes) for each command.
Changes that affect scripts:

- `validate` exits 2 on content findings (see above).
- `lock --check` without a lock file exits 1; run `ai-rulez lock` first.
- Declining the `generate --user --clean` prompt exits 1.
- An include that cannot be resolved (no network, deleted repository, no cached copy) makes `validate`, `doctor` and
  `generate` exit 1 and name it. `generate --offline` skips it with a warning.

##### Generation

- **`generate` refuses to overwrite a file it did not write**, such as a hand-written `CLAUDE.md`. Import it with
  `ai-rulez convert --write` (the next `generate` replaces it), move it, or pass `generate --force`. It never writes
  through a symlinked output.
- **Divergent shared outputs fail.** When two presets render different content to the same path, `generate` fails and
  names both. Make them agree, for example with `agents_md = true` or `[rules] mode = "inline"`.
- **Claude Code MCP servers are written only to `.mcp.json`**, which keeps `${VAR}` references; `.claude/settings.json`
  no longer receives `mcpServers`. An entry an earlier version wrote there is removed on the next `generate`.
- **`generate` warns about unknown configuration keys** and names the nearest known key; `--strict-config` fails
  instead.
- **`generate` lists new or changed commands** it writes into tool configuration (hooks, command-based MCP servers,
  `[permissions] allow` rules). It only warns; pass `--yes` or set `AI_RULEZ_ACK_COMMANDS=1` in CI.
- **`generate --dry-run` prints `unchanged:` and `edited:`** for files that need no write, besides `write-file:`.
- **`clean` keeps hand-edited generated files** with a warning; `clean --include-edited` removes them.
- **Check outputs are committed**: files generated from [checks](checks.md) are never added to the managed
  `.gitignore` block.
- **`tokens` totals include the skill, command and agent listing**, so `--budget` can fail where it passed.
- **Skill `evals/` directories are not bundled into plugins** unless `[plugin] include_evals = true`.
- **Custom preset and provider output paths are validated**: `..`, absolute paths and paths naming `.git`,
  `.ai-rulez`, `.hg` or `.svn` are rejected.
- **`init --from` runs `convert --write`**: it takes importer names (`auto`, `native`, `rulesync`, ...) or project paths
  (`.claude`, `CLAUDE.md`), imports MCP files, hooks and permissions too, and turns a root file such as `CLAUDE.md` into
  one context item (`ai-rulez convert --split-headings` splits it by heading).

##### Presets

| Change | Action |
| ------ | ------ |
| `windsurf` is renamed `devin`: outputs move from `.windsurf/` to `.devin/` and `windsurf_model` becomes `devin_model`. There is no alias. | `migrate v5` renames the preset; run it with `--write` for the frontmatter key, and delete `.windsurf/`. |
| `continue-dev` is removed, with no replacement. | `migrate v5` drops it; `doctor` reports it. |
| `codex` and `antigravity` write commands as skills (`.agents/skills/<id>/SKILL.md`). | None; the old files are removed on `generate`. |
| `codex` writes skills to `.agents/skills`. | Set `codex_skills_dir = ".codex/skills"` for the old location. |
| `cursor` user-level skills go to `~/.agents/skills`. | Run `generate --user`; `clean --user` removes the old copies. |
| `antigravity` no longer adds the ai-rulez MCP server itself. | None; `[mcp] self_server` (on by default) adds it. |
| `amp` no longer writes `.agents/agents`, which Amp does not read. | None. |
| `opencode` writes MCP servers as `mcp.<name>` with `enabled`. | None; the old `mcp.servers` entries are removed. |
| `zoocode` inlines rules into `AGENTS.md` instead of `.roo/rules`. | None. |

##### Lock file

- **`ai-rulez.lock` pins content.** Besides remote sources, it pins the ai-rulez version, every authored rule, context
  file, skill, agent, command, hook and settings source, the generated outputs and served skills, all as `sha256:`
  digests. Run `ai-rulez lock` once after upgrading, review the diff and commit it; a lock from 4.x or an earlier v5
  build reads as stale until you do.
- **`[lock] enforce` is on whenever the lock exists.** A remote include or installed skill the lock does not cover
  makes `generate` fail, `AR010` and `AR012` become errors, and `validate` reports source and output drift (`AR981`,
  `AR982`). `generate --check` also verifies authored content against an enforced lock.
- **`lock` and `update` scan what they pin.** A remote tree pinned to something new is scanned first; an error finding
  refuses the pin unless you pass `--accept-findings`. A served skill the scan refuses is left unpinned and `lock`
  exits 3; `--refuse-findings` makes it fail instead.
- **`generate --check` reports `blocked: <path>`** for a shared file that a machine-local input would change;
  `--allow-local-drift` accepts it.

See [Lock file](lockfile.md).

##### Supply-chain defaults

- **`http://` and `git://` remotes are rejected.** Use `https://`, `ssh://` / `git@host:path`, or a local path.
- **The git token is sent only to allowlisted hosts**: `github.com` by default, or the hosts in
  `AI_RULEZ_GIT_TOKEN_HOSTS` (which replaces the default, so list `github.com` too). The forge client (release dates,
  review-linked approvals) has its own allowlist, `AI_RULEZ_FORGE_HOSTS`; add your GitHub Enterprise host there. See
  [Forge client](forge.md).
- **A committed configuration cannot point outside the project.** A local include or `[[skill_sources]]` path that
  resolves outside the project is an error. Put such paths in `config.local.toml` or the user configuration.
- **Symlinked content must resolve inside the repository.** Other links are refused with a warning, and `validate`
  reports them. Symlinks inside includes, installed skills, skill sources and OKF bundles are never followed.
- **Repository content read at load time is capped at 8 MiB per file.**
- **Staged external scanners run confined** under `isolation = "auto"` where a sandbox backend exists. A scanner that
  writes outside its scratch directory fails with `AR9E3`; point it at `TMPDIR`/`HOME` or set `isolation = "none"`. See
  [Isolation](strict-validation.md#isolation).
- **An organization policy is read from the managed path** (`/etc/ai-rulez/policy.toml`,
  `/Library/Application Support/ai-rulez/policy.toml`, `%ProgramData%\ai-rulez\policy.toml`) besides `--policy` and
  `AI_RULEZ_POLICY`. Nothing changes on a machine without one. See [Organization policy](policy.md).

##### Egress settings come from the user, not the repository

`allow_network`, `base_url`, `api_key_env` and the price overrides of `[llm]`, and the egress keys of `[telemetry]`
(`allow_network`, `otlp_endpoint`, `headers_env`, `service_name`, `resource`, ...), are honored only from the user
configuration (`~/.config/ai-rulez/config.toml`) or the `AI_RULEZ_LLM_*` / `AI_RULEZ_TELEMETRY_*` environment
variables. A repository that sets them is ignored and reported (`AR9L1`, `AR9K1`). Move these settings to your user
configuration. See [Trust model](trust-model.md).

##### Validation rules

- **New rule codes** can fail a CI job that passed on 4.x. Every code is listed in
  [Strict validation](strict-validation.md). Lower or disable a rule with `[lint.severity]`, or accept the current
  findings with `validate --update-baseline`. Rule codes are never renumbered.
- **Top-level `[[hooks]]` are stricter**: a `script` path outside `A-Za-z0-9._/-` is rejected, and a missing or
  non-executable script is `AR504`/`AR505`.
- **Eval results are signed per user.** A record without a valid signature, such as one committed from another
  machine, is re-run by `eval run`. In CI, use `eval run --force`. See [Evals](evals.md).
- **The usage log is version 3**: the session field is a salted hash. Version 1 and 2 logs are still read.

#### OKF is the format of `.ai-rulez/`

`.ai-rulez/` is an [OKF](okf.md) bundle: each content file carries a `type` (and usually `title` and `x-ai-rulez`)
in its frontmatter and each directory has an `index.md`. `init`, `add` and the MCP tools write this layout. A migrated 4.x tree keeps loading
in the earlier layout, with a deprecation notice. Convert it with:

```bash
ai-rulez migrate okf --dry-run   # list what would change
ai-rulez migrate okf             # convert in place
ai-rulez generate --check        # the generated files are unchanged
```

```text
[converted] rules/style.md
[index] index.md
[index] rules/index.md
would convert 1, indexes 2, unchanged 0, skipped 0
```

`migrate okf` moves each file's frontmatter under `x-ai-rulez.metadata`, adds `type` (`Decision` for rules, `Concept` for
context, `Playbook` for skills, `Reference` otherwise) and `title` unless they exist, and writes the `index.md` files.
Bodies and skill resources (`references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/`) are not touched. A file with an unclosed frontmatter
block is skipped and reported. `--check` exits 2 while a tree still needs migration. The originals of rewritten files
are copied to `.ai-rulez.bak-okf-<timestamp>/` at the project root; delete it once you have reviewed the result, and
do not commit it.

After the conversion:

- `type`, `title` and `x-ai-rulez` are reserved frontmatter keys.
- A file you add by hand should have a `type` (`title` is optional). Frontmatter without `type` is an `AR9B1` error; a
  file with no frontmatter still loads, with an `AR9B1` warning. `generate` refreshes the `index.md`
  listings.
- `validate` also runs the OKF checks (`AR9B*`).

#### Go API

Packages under `internal/` are not a public API. Code that embeds ai-rulez should use
`github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/v5/pkg/airulez` (experimental; see [Embedding](embedding.md)). The module path is
`github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/v5` and the binary is `cmd/ai-rulez`:

```bash
go install github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/v5/cmd/ai-rulez@latest
```

Changes for code that used `internal/config` directly:

- The process-wide preset registry is gone (`config.GetPresetGenerator`, `config.PresetRegistry`,
  `config.RegisterPreset`, `config.RegisterRulesDir`); each generation carries its own registry.
- `config.LoadConfig` fails on a configuration with includes or installed skills unless it is given
  `config.WithResolvers` (or `config.WithoutRemote`).
- `config.SetPolicyEnforcer` is replaced by the load option `config.WithPolicy`.
- The V2/V3 helpers (`config.DetectConfigVersion`, `config.VersionDir`, `config.ConfigVersionV3`, `Config.IsV3`,
  `config.DecodeLegacyMCPFile`, `config.MigrateLocalOverlayToTOML`, `LocalOverlay.Format`) are removed.
- In `pkg/airulez`, the machine-local overlay is read only with `Options.WithLocal`; `Options.WithoutLocal` is removed.

#### See also

- [Supported harnesses](harnesses.md): what each preset writes.
- [Hooks and settings](settings.md) and [User-level configuration](user-scope.md).
- [Lock file](lockfile.md) and [Trust model](trust-model.md).
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): the complete list of changes in 5.0.0.

## Configuration

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/configuration/

`.ai-rulez/config.toml` declares which tools ai-rulez generates for, which content each profile selects, and how the generated files look. Keys are grouped by what they control; features with a page of their own get a short summary, their keys and a link.

#### Minimal configuration

`version` and `name` are the only required keys. `presets` names the tools to generate for:

```toml
version = "5.0"
name = "acme"
presets = ["claude", "cursor", "codex", "copilot"]
```

```bash
ai-rulez generate
```

With one rule in `.ai-rulez/rules/`, this writes a shared `AGENTS.md` (the rules and context), a `CLAUDE.md` that imports `@AGENTS.md`, the `ai-rulez` MCP server entry in `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json` and `.codex/config.toml`, and a `SessionStart` hook in `.claude/settings.json`. Commit the generated files with the sources; set [`gitignore = true`](#gitignore) to keep them out of git instead.

`ai-rulez init` scaffolds the directory and a commented `config.toml`. To keep only a configuration file and no content tree, see [Config without a .ai-rulez folder](config-without-folder.md).

#### Content layout

The configuration sits in the config directory next to the content it renders:

```text
.ai-rulez/
├── index.md             # OKF index (okf_version), one per directory
├── config.toml          # this reference
├── config.local.toml    # optional machine-local overlay (gitignored)
├── rules/*.md           # always-on or path-scoped instructions
├── context/*.md         # reference material
├── skills/<name>/SKILL.md
├── agents/*.md
├── commands/<name>.md   # or commands/<name>/COMMAND.md
├── checks/*.md          # code-review guidelines
├── domains/<name>/      # same folders, selected by profiles
└── local/               # machine-local content (gitignored)
```

| Directory | Holds | See |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rules/` | Instructions, always-on or scoped with `globs`/`paths` | [Rules](rules.md) |
| `context/` | Reference documentation rendered beside the rules | [Rules](rules.md) |
| `skills/<name>/` | `SKILL.md` plus optional `references/`, `scripts/` and `assets/` | [Skill frontmatter](skills.md) |
| `agents/` | Subagent definitions | [Agents](#agents) |
| `commands/` | Slash commands, flat (`deploy.md`) or directory form (`deploy/COMMAND.md` with resources) | [Commands](#commands) |
| `checks/` | Code-review guidelines | [Checks](checks.md) |
| `domains/<name>/` | The same folders for one area, included when a profile selects the domain | [Domains and profiles](domains.md) |
| `local/` | Personal content that is never committed | [Local configuration](local-overrides.md) |

`ai-rulez init` creates the tree as an [OKF](okf.md) bundle, with an `index.md` in each directory and item frontmatter under `x-ai-rulez.metadata`; `add`, `remove` and the MCP tools keep the indexes current. A tree without a root `index.md` still loads, with a deprecation notice on every command: run `ai-rulez migrate okf` (see [The native tree](okf.md#the-native-tree)).

The skill or command directory name is its id. Files under `references/`, `scripts/` and `assets/` are copied next to the generated `SKILL.md` and listed in its `## Resources` section; another subdirectory produces a warning. Build artifacts are left out; see [`bundle_exclude`](#bundle_exclude).

Instead of `.ai-rulez/`, content can come from `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/` ([`source = "agents"`](#source)), and the config directory can be `.config/ai-rulez/` (`ai-rulez init --config-dir .config/ai-rulez`).

##### Symlinks in content

A symlinked file or directory under `.ai-rulez/` (including `domains/` and `local/`) is followed only when its resolved target is inside the project (the git top-level, otherwise the directory holding `.ai-rulez/`). Any other symlink, including a dangling one, is refused: `generate` fails naming it and `validate` reports it as an error. Content read from includes, installed skills, skill sources and OKF bundles never follows symlinks; see [Includes](includes.md).

##### Agents

An agent is a Markdown file in `agents/` (or `domains/<name>/agents/`) whose frontmatter configures it and whose body is its prompt. Like every file in the tree it uses the [OKF form](okf.md#the-native-tree): `type`, then the agent's keys under `x-ai-rulez.metadata`; `description` stays at the top level. Each preset that supports subagents writes it in its own format (`.claude/agents/<id>.md`, `.codex/agents/<id>.toml`, `.cursor/agents/<id>.md`, ...).

```markdown
<!-- .ai-rulez/agents/security-reviewer.md -->
---
type: Reference
title: Security Reviewer
description: Reviews diffs for security regressions
x-ai-rulez:
  kind: agent
  id: security-reviewer
  metadata:
    tools: [Read, Grep, Glob]
    model: sonnet
    claude_model: opus
    effort: high
    skills: [secure-coding]
---

Review the diff for injection, leaked secrets and unsafe deserialization.
```

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `x-ai-rulez.id` | Agent id. Defaults to the file name. |
| `description` | When to use the agent; written to every preset and listed in the `## Agents` roster. |
| `tools` | Tool names (Claude Code names; presets translate or drop them). |
| `model` | Model used for every preset that writes one, unless something more specific is set. |
| `<preset>_model` | Model for one preset (`claude_model`, `copilot_model`, `opencode_model`, ...); wins over [`[defaults] model_by_preset`](#defaults) and `model`. |
| `effort` | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` or `inherit`; see [`[defaults]`](#defaults) for how each preset maps it. |
| `skills` | Skills the agent preloads. `validate` reports a name that is no skill as `AR302`. |
| `extends` | Append this agent to a lower-precedence agent of that name; see [Extending agents](#extending-agents). |
| `priority`, `targets` | Ordering and output selection, as for rules ([Targets](rules.md#targets)). |

The `claude` preset also passes Claude Code's subagent keys through with their YAML types: `disallowedTools`, `permissionMode`, `memory`, `maxTurns`, `mcpServers`, `hooks`, `background`, `isolation`, `color`, `initialPrompt`, `omitClaudeMd`; other presets ignore them. For OpenCode, `hidden` is written as a boolean and `temperature` and `top_p` as numbers. `validate` reports a key no tool reads as `AR303`; it currently also reports `extends` and the `<preset>_model` keys, which do work: list them in [`[lint] allowed_keys`](strict-validation.md) to silence it.

##### Commands

A command is a slash command, in one of two forms:

```text
.ai-rulez/commands/
├── pr-summary.md            # flat form
└── deploy/                  # directory form
    ├── COMMAND.md
    └── references/
        └── runbook.md
```

```markdown
<!-- .ai-rulez/commands/deploy/COMMAND.md -->
---
type: Reference
title: Deploy
description: Deploy the current branch to staging
x-ai-rulez:
  kind: command
  id: deploy
  metadata:
    argument-hint: "[service]"
---

Deploy $ARGUMENTS to staging, following references/runbook.md.
```

The directory form takes `references/`, `scripts/` and `assets/` like a skill. Keeping both `deploy.md` and `deploy/COMMAND.md` is an [output ID collision](#output-id-collisions). The frontmatter (under `x-ai-rulez.metadata`) takes the Claude Code skill and command keys (`description`, `argument-hint`, `arguments`, `allowed-tools`, `model`, `disable-model-invocation`, ...) plus `priority` and `targets`. Harnesses that run commands as skills get one (`.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` with its `references/`, `.agents/skills/deploy/` for Codex); others get their command file (`.cursor/commands/deploy.md`). [Supported harnesses](harnesses.md) lists where each preset writes commands.

#### Configuration discovery

Without `--config`, the CLI walks up from the working directory, stopping at the repository root and never going above the home directory. In each directory it tries, in order:

1. `.agents/ai-rulez.toml`: a project whose content is [`AGENTS.md` and `.agents/`](agents-source.md)
2. `.ai-rulez/config.toml`: the default layout
3. `.config/ai-rulez/config.toml`: the [`.config/` convention](https://github.com/pi0/config-dir)
4. `ai-rulez.toml`: a [configuration without a `.ai-rulez/` folder](config-without-folder.md)

The first match wins; when a config directory and `ai-rulez.toml` sit side by side, the file is ignored with a warning. `--config <file or dir>` selects a configuration exactly, and `--config-dir <name>` selects a config directory name below the working directory.

Only `config.toml` (TOML) is read, and its `version` must be `"5.0"`. A project with only a `config.yaml`, `config.yml`, `config.json`, a flat `ai-rulez.yaml`, or a `config.toml` with an older `version` fails with an error naming the file; run `ai-rulez migrate v5`. See [Migrating to v5](migration-v5.md).

#### Checks `generate` runs before it writes

`generate` checks `config.toml`, its layers and `config.local.toml` against the [JSON schema](schema.md), as `validate` does. An unknown key has no effect, so `generate` warns and names the nearest known key:

```text
WARN  Configuration problem: .ai-rulez/config.toml: unknown key "lock.enforc" (did you mean "enforce"?)
WARN  These keys have no effect; `ai-rulez validate` fails on them, `generate --strict-config` (or AI_RULEZ_STRICT=1) does too
```

`validate` always fails on an unknown key. `generate --strict-config`, or `AI_RULEZ_STRICT=1`, makes `generate` exit 1 too. `validate --strict` is a different switch: it makes warnings fail as well as errors (`--fail-on warning`); see [Strict validation](strict-validation.md). In CI, run:

```bash
ai-rulez generate --check   # committed outputs match the sources
ai-rulez validate           # unknown keys, content and security checks
```

See [GitHub Actions](github-actions.md) for a ready-made workflow.

`generate` also lists the commands it is about to write that your tools will run: `[[hooks]]` commands (with the digest of a hook `script`), `http` and `prompt` hooks, command-based `[[mcp_servers]]`, `[permissions] allow` rules, `[claude.settings.managed] env` entries, and plugin enablement and marketplace registration:

```text
Warning: generate will write 1 new or changed command(s) that your tools will run (from .ai-rulez/config.toml):
  hook       SessionStart: sh -c 'case "${CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE:-}" in ...  -> claude
Review them before you start a tool in this project. Silence with --yes or AI_RULEZ_ACK_COMMANDS=1.
```

Only commands that are new or changed since the last run on this machine are listed (every command on a fresh clone). The previous run is remembered in the user cache directory, never in the repository. The list is printed even with `--quiet`; control characters and anything that looks like a credential are escaped or shown as `<redacted>`. `--yes` or `AI_RULEZ_ACK_COMMANDS=1` silences it, and the MCP `generate_outputs` tool returns it as `new_commands`.

#### Project

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | string | required | Configuration version. Must be `"5.0"`. |
| `name` | string | required | Project name, shown in generated headers and used as the title of root instruction files. |
| `description` | string | none | Project description, written under the title. |
| `schema` | string | none | JSON schema reference for editors (the TOML spelling of `$schema`). |
| `$comment` | string | none | Free-form note, ignored. |

```toml
version = "5.0"
name = "acme-platform"
description = "Billing platform: Go services and a React front end"
```

#### Presets

`presets` names the tools to generate for: built-in preset names, custom presets as inline tables, or both.

```toml
presets = [
  "claude",
  "cursor",
  "gemini",
  "codex",
  { name = "team-guide", type = "markdown", path = "docs/AI_GUIDE.md" },
]
```

`presets` is optional. A configuration without presets (and without a `[plugin]` block) generates nothing; see [Lint-only configuration](config-without-folder.md#lint-only-configuration).

##### Built-in presets

There are 52 built-in presets. [Supported harnesses](harnesses.md) lists the files and features each one writes:

`aiassistant`, `amp`, `antigravity`, `augment`, `baz`, `bob`, `claude`, `cline`, `codebuddy`, `codebuff`, `codewhale`, `codex`, `commandcode`, `copilot`, `copilot-cli`, `cortex`, `crush`, `cursor`, `deepagents`, `devin`, `dsh`, `factory`, `gemini`, `gitlab-duo`, `goose`, `grok`, `hermes`, `junie`, `kilo`, `kimi`, `kiro`, `letta`, `mimocode`, `muse`, `omp`, `openclaw`, `opencode`, `pi`, `poolside`, `qoder`, `qwen`, `reasonix`, `replit`, `rovodev`, `takt`, `trae`, `vibe`, `warp`, `xum`, `zcode`, `zed`, `zoocode`.

Three more presets write no tool configuration:

| Preset | Writes |
| --- | --- |
| `okf` | An [Open Knowledge Format](okf.md) bundle of the content; see [`[okf]`](#okf). |
| `llms-txt` | An [`llms.txt`](llms-txt.md) index; see [`[llms_txt]`](#llms_txt). |
| `mcp` | The generic `.mcp.json`. It runs automatically whenever MCP servers are configured, so you do not name it. |

`windsurf` and `continue-dev` are not presets: `validate` and `generate` fail on them (`unknown built-in preset: "windsurf" (renamed to devin)`), and `ai-rulez doctor` reports them. Use `devin` for Windsurf. See [Migrating to v5](migration-v5.md).

##### Custom template presets

A preset table with `name`, `type` (`markdown`, `directory` or `json`), `path` and an optional Go `template` writes your rules and context to a file or folder of your choice:

```toml
[[presets]]
name = "team-guide"
type = "markdown"
path = "docs/AI_GUIDE.md"
```

The keys, preset types, template data and allowed output paths are documented in [Custom presets](profiles.md). For a tool that needs skills, agents, MCP or settings files, use a provider spec (next section).

##### Provider-backed presets (full parity)

A preset can point at a declarative provider spec instead of a template. A provider spec has the same reach as a built-in preset (root instruction file, skills, agents, commands, rule files, frontmatter, effort and model, MCP and hooks sidecars) and is validated against [`schema/provider.schema.json`](https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/blob/main/schema/provider.schema.json).

```toml
[[presets]]
name = "my-tool"
provider = ".ai-rulez/providers/my-tool.toml"
```

The path is relative to the project root and must stay inside it; the spec's `name` must equal the preset's `name`. A spec:

```toml
name = "my-tool"
directories = [".my-tool"]

[root]
file = "MY_TOOL.md"
sections = ["title", "rules_inline", "context_inline"]

[outputs.skills]
mode = "per_item_file"
dir = ".my-tool/skills"
filename = "{id}/SKILL.md"

[[sidecars]]
kind = "mcp_json"
path = ".my-tool/mcp.json"
emit_when = "has_mcp_servers"
```

`emit_when` takes `always`, `has_mcp_servers`, `has_plugins`, `has_resolved_effort`, `has_mcp_json_entries`, `has_mcp_servers_or_plugin_settings`, `has_resolved_effort_or_mcp_servers` or `has_hooks`. A provider without a `split` rules output (below) inlines every rule into its root file, and custom providers get no [machine-local](local-overrides.md) output.

###### Output path rules

Every output path a configuration names (a custom preset `path`, a provider spec's `root.file`, `outputs.*.dir`, `sidecars[].path` and `directories`, `okf.dir`, `marketplace.output_dir`, `codex_skills_dir`) follows the rules in [Output paths](profiles.md#output-paths).

###### Tool and model names in a provider spec

These keys under `[outputs.<kind>.frontmatter]` translate the canonical (Claude Code) tool and model names into the tool's own:

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `tool_names` | Table of canonical tool name to the tool's name (matched ignoring case). A tool the table does not name is dropped; an agent left with no tools writes no `tools` key. |
| `tool_case` | `"lower"` lower-cases every tool name after `tool_names`. |
| `model_aliases` | Table of resolved model (matched ignoring case) to the tool's model id; `""` drops the model. |
| `drop_bare_aliases` | Drops `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku` and `inherit` after `model_aliases`, so the agent inherits the session model. |

`[outputs.<kind>.body]` takes `replace` (placeholder to replacement in the item body, such as `{ "$ARGUMENTS" = "$prompt" }`) and `replace_flag` (a frontmatter key set to `true` when a replacement happened).

An `mcp` sidecar takes `transports` (`["stdio"]` leaves remote servers out), `env_ref_syntax` (`"dollar"`, `"env_prefix"`, `"braced"` or `"opencode_env"`: a value from a `${VAR}` placeholder is written as `$VAR`, `${env:VAR}`, `${VAR}` or `{env:VAR}` instead of the resolved secret) and `elements.project_only`. A `hooks` sidecar renders the top-level `[[hooks]]` in the format of the harness its `dialect` names (`claude`, `qwen`, `factory`, `kiro`, `vibe`, ...; see [Hooks and settings](settings.md)):

```toml
[[sidecars]]
kind = "hooks"
dialect = "qwen"
path = ".qwen/settings.json"
global_path = ".qwen/settings.json"
```

Sidecars that name the same `path` are merged into one document.

###### Split rule files in a provider spec

A `split` rules output makes a provider follow [`[rules] mode`](#rules) like the built-in presets:

```toml
[root]
file = "MY_TOOL.md"
sections = ["title", "rules_inline", "context_inline"]

[outputs.rules]
mode = "per_item_file"
dir = ".my-tool/rules"
filename = "{id}.md"
split = true
dialect = "claude"          # claude, cursor, trigger, copilot, cline, continue or junie
inline_filter = "path_scoped"
```

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `split` | `true`: split mode writes every rule (and path-scoped context item) to a file; inline mode writes only the items `inline_filter` selects. Requires `rules_inline` in `root.sections`; cannot be combined with `filter`. |
| `dialect` | Required with `split`. The frontmatter vocabulary of the rule files; cannot be combined with `body` or `frontmatter`. |
| `inline_filter` | `path_scoped`: the items that still get a file in inline mode. Omit to keep everything inline. |
| `dir` | Required with `split`; a relative path inside the project. |
| `filename` | Flat `{id}<ext>` template without `/`. |

The folder behaves like a built-in rules folder: hand-written files in it are never overwritten, and with `gitignore = true` generated files are ignored one by one.

#### Profiles and scopes

##### `default` and `profiles`

A profile is a named list of domains. `generate --profile <name>` (or `default`) renders the root content plus the domains the profile selects.

```toml
default = "full"

[profiles]
full = ["backend", "frontend", "qa"]
backend = ["backend", "qa", "builtin:docker"]
all-but-legacy = ["*", "!legacy"]
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | string | `"default"` | Profile used without `--profile`. A comma-separated value (`"base,backend"`) composes several profiles. |
| `profiles` | table of string arrays | none | Profile name to domain entries. |

A profile entry is one of:

| Entry | Selects |
| --- | --- |
| `backend` | A local or included domain. |
| `builtin:docker` | A [builtin](#builtins) pack, for this profile only. |
| `builtin:docker/container-standards` | One item of a builtin pack, for this profile only. |
| `*` | Every domain the configuration knows. |
| `!legacy` | Removes a domain from the selection. Exclusions apply after the positive entries, whatever their order. |

Root content, globally enabled builtins and domains that come from includes are always selected. A profile made only of exclusions is an error (write `["*", "!legacy"]`); an unknown domain name is a warning. Profile names cannot contain a comma, and a profile lists domains only, never other profiles.

Without a `default` key the built-in `default` profile applies: a profile you define as `default`; otherwise every domain when no profiles are defined; otherwise only root content, global builtins and included domains. See [Domains and profiles](domains.md) and [Profiles vs roles](roles.md#profiles-vs-roles).

##### `[[scopes]]`

A scope generates extra instruction files in a subdirectory, holding only that subdirectory's content. Tools load a subdirectory `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` on top of the root one, so the root content is not repeated.

```toml
[profiles]
web = ["frontend"]

[[scopes]]
path = "packages/web"
profile = "web"
presets = ["codex", "claude"]
```

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | required | Subdirectory, relative to the project root, without glob characters (`* ? [ ] { } , !`). |
| `profile` | string | the active profile | Profile whose domains the scope renders. |
| `presets` | array | `["claude", "codex"]` | Presets written in the scope. |
| `name` | string | none | Display name. |

A domain the root output already renders (a builtin, an include, or one the root profile selects) is not repeated in a scope, and a scope left with no content writes nothing. Rule files of a scope go to the root rules folders with the scope path as a glob prefix; see [Monorepo](monorepo.md).

##### `[[roles]]` and `[role_manifest]`

A role maps a job to a slice of the content: domains, include and exclude selectors per kind, inheritance, and a per-skill `skill_mode`. Select one with `generate --role <name>`; a comma-separated list composes roles. See [Roles](roles.md).

```toml
[role_manifest]
enabled = true                  # write <config dir>/roles.json

[[roles]]
name = "backend"
domains = ["backend"]
[roles.skills]
exclude = ["deploy-*"]
[roles.skill_mode]
migrate = "name-only"
```

`[[roles]]` keys: `name`, `description`, `extends`, `domains`, `skills`, `rules`, `agents`, `commands`, `checks`, `pin`, `skill_mode`, `delivery`, `match`. `[role_manifest]` keys: `enabled`, `skill_mode_fallback` (`drop` or `serve`).

#### Output files

##### `source`

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `ai-rulez`, `agents` | `ai-rulez` | Where content is read from. `agents` reads the root `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/` (Agent Skills in `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, plus `.agents/rules`, `agents`, `commands`, `context`, `checks` and `domains/<name>`) and never writes to them. |
| `agents_md_split` | boolean | `false` | With `source = "agents"`, read `AGENTS.md` as one context item per `##` heading (`agents-<heading slug>`) instead of one item named `agents`. |

A configuration in `.agents/ai-rulez.toml` implies `source = "agents"`. The agents source forces per-tool files and rejects `agents_md = true`. See [`.agents` as a source](agents-source.md).

```toml
source = "agents"
agents_md_split = true
```

##### `agents_md`

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `agents_md` | boolean | `true` | Render shared files once: always-on rules and context into one `AGENTS.md` (and `<scope>/AGENTS.md` for each scope), skills into `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. |

With `agents_md` on, the presets that read these files (for example `codex`, `opencode`, `claude`, `gemini`, `cursor`, `copilot`; [Supported harnesses](harnesses.md#instructions-rules-and-skills) has the full list) stop writing their own root file and skills directory:

- `claude` writes a `CLAUDE.md` that imports `@AGENTS.md` (or nothing; see [`[claude] claude_md`](#claude)).
- `gemini` gets `AGENTS.md` added to `context.fileName` in `.gemini/settings.json`; `GEMINI.md`, `.hermes.md` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` are not written.
- Rules folders (`.cursor/rules`, `.claude/rules`, ...) keep only the items that are not always-on.
- Skills with `targets`, agents, commands, MCP files and machine-local files stay per preset.

`agents_md = false` writes each preset's own files and removes the shared ones no preset still writes. Tool support and trade-offs are in [AGENTS.md and .agents/skills](agents-md.md).

##### `skip_outputs`

Output kinds ai-rulez never writes, overwrites or deletes, so you can hand-write them and let ai-rulez write the rest (installed skills, plugins, MCP servers, hooks, permissions). Default: empty.

```toml
skip_outputs = ["instructions"]
```

| Value | Skips |
| --- | --- |
| `instructions` | Every root instruction file (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md` and the other presets' root files, their `.local.md` and `AGENTS.override.md` variants, scope roots). Overrides `agents_md` and `claude_md`. |
| `agents_md` | The shared `AGENTS.md` (and `AGENTS.override.md`) and the shared `.agents/skills` tree. |
| `claude_md` | `CLAUDE.md`, at the root and in scopes. |
| `rules` | Rule files in every preset. |
| `skills` | Skill directories in every preset, installed skills included. A command written as a skill counts as a command. |
| `agents` | Agent files. |
| `commands` | Command and prompt files, including the skills that carry a command. |

Skipped files are left out of the manifest, the managed `.gitignore` block, `generate --check`, the lock's output digests and `clean`. A file an earlier run generated and that is now skipped stays where it is and is reported once as no longer managed. `config.local.toml` accepts the key too. See [Managing only remote skills and plugins](managing-remote-skills.md).

##### `[claude]`

Claude Code options.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `claude_md` | `shim`, `none` | `shim` | With `agents_md` on: `shim` writes a `CLAUDE.md` that imports `@AGENTS.md`; `none` writes no `CLAUDE.md` (root or scopes) and removes one a previous run generated. |
| `skills.hide_from_menu` | boolean | `false` | Write `user-invocable: false` on every skill that does not set it, so the skill is hidden from the `/` menu. A skill's own `user-invocable` wins. See [Skill frontmatter](skills.md#invocation-keys). |
| `settings` | table | none | Opt-in ownership of plugin keys in `.claude/settings.json`: `manage`, `register_marketplace`, `marketplace_source`, `auto_update`, `enable_plugins`, `disable_plugins`. See [Plugins](plugins.md). |
| `settings.managed` | table | none | `env` and `skill_overrides` entries of `.claude/settings.json`, owned entry by entry. See [Hooks and settings](settings.md). |

```toml
[claude]
claude_md = "none"

[claude.skills]
hide_from_menu = true
```

Claude Code reads `AGENTS.md` directly from version 2.1.277, so `claude_md = "none"` makes `AGENTS.md` the only instruction file.
