The token is sent only to `github.com` unless you list other hosts in the environment (a project file cannot widen
this):

```bash
export AI_RULEZ_GIT_TOKEN_HOSTS="github.com,gitlab.example.com"
```

The list replaces the default. An include on any other host is fetched without the token, with a warning. The token
is passed to git as a header for that host, so it does not appear in process arguments or in the cached clone's
`.git/config`. Grant it read-only repository access (`repo` on GitHub classic tokens, `read_repository` on GitLab).

Never put credentials in the URL: `include add` refuses `https://user:token@host/...`, and `validate` reports an
already committed credentialed source as `AR035`.

In CI:

```yaml
# GitHub Actions
- name: Generate
  env:
    AI_RULEZ_GIT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GIT_TOKEN }}
  run: npx ai-rulez@latest generate --check
```

```yaml
# GitLab CI
generate:
  script:
    - export AI_RULEZ_GIT_TOKEN="$CI_JOB_TOKEN"
    - ai-rulez generate --check
```

#### Pinning and caching

A git include without `ref` follows the default branch, so two machines can render different output. `ai-rulez lock`
records each git include's resolved commit and a content digest in `.ai-rulez/ai-rulez.lock`; later runs fetch that
commit and verify the digest. A branch or tag that is not locked is reported as `AR010`.

| Command                        | Behavior                                                                  |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ai-rulez lock`                | pin every include (and your own content) in `ai-rulez.lock`              |
| `ai-rulez update`              | move `version` pins to the newest matching tag                            |
| `ai-rulez generate --locked`   | fail on a source the lock does not cover (use in CI)                      |
| `ai-rulez generate --frozen`   | use only the cache, never the network, and verify it against the lock     |
| `ai-rulez generate --offline`  | use cached content; an include that cannot be resolved is skipped with a warning |

Remote includes are cached under `~/.cache/ai-rulez/includes/<name>-<hash>/` (mode `0700`), one tree per URL, path,
ref and pinned commit, so two checkouts that pin different commits never share a tree. See [Lock file](lockfile.md).

#### Errors and safety

- An include that cannot be fetched or merged is an error for `generate`, `generate --check`, `validate`, `doctor`
  and every other command that loads the configuration. An unreachable remote falls back to its cached copy when one
  exists. Only `--offline` turns a missing include into a warning.
- Included content never follows symlinks: a symlinked file or folder is skipped with a warning naming it.

#### Patterns

**Organization standards in one repository**, included everywhere:

```toml
[[includes]]
name = "org"
source = "https://github.com/acme/org-standards"
version = "^2.0"
```

**Several layers.** Includes do not nest, so list each layer, most general first:

```toml
[[includes]]
name = "org"
source = "https://github.com/acme/org-standards"

[[includes]]
name = "go"
source = "https://github.com/acme/go-guidelines"

[[includes]]
name = "payments-team"
source = "https://github.com/acme/payments-rules"
install_to = "payments"     # imported as the payments domain
```

**A monorepo** keeps shared content in a folder of the repository and includes it from each project's config, or
uses [`[[scopes]]`](monorepo.md) to render nested outputs from one configuration.

**Developing an include** next to its consumers: point `local_override` at your checkout in `config.local.toml`, so
the committed config keeps its pinned source:

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.local.toml
[[includes]]
name = "org"
local_override = "../org-standards"
```

`generate` then refuses to write tracked shared files (such as `AGENTS.md`) that the local override would change.
Pass `--allow-local-drift` to write them while you test, or `--no-local` to render the committed view. See
[Local configuration](local-overrides.md).

#### Troubleshooting

| Symptom                                            | Cause and fix                                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `local path ... is outside the project`            | Move the include to `config.local.toml` or the user config, or copy the content into the project. |
| `conflict detected in rules between base and include` | An include with `merge_strategy = "error"` has an item with an existing name. Rename one.     |
| Included item is missing                           | Your own item, or an earlier include, has the same name; or `include` leaves the kind out.      |
| `Directory must contain .ai-rulez/ subdirectory`   | `include add` with a bare local directory; add the entry to `config.toml` by hand.               |
| Output differs between machines                    | The include follows a branch. Run `ai-rulez lock` and commit `ai-rulez.lock`.                    |
| Include ignored, no error                          | A `local_override` that names a missing directory skips the include; run with `--debug`.        |

## Installed skills

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/installed-skills/

An `[[installed_skills]]` entry pulls one or more [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) from a git repository or a
local directory and writes them into every harness's skills folder, as if they were your own. Use it to ship a
library's usage guide with the library, or to share team skills across repositories without a full
[include](includes.md).

#### Example

```bash
ai-rulez skill install ai-rulez --source Goldziher/ai-rulez --trust warn
ai-rulez generate
ai-rulez lock
```

`skill install` adds the entry to `.ai-rulez/config.toml`:

```toml
[[installed_skills]]
name = 'ai-rulez'
source = 'Goldziher/ai-rulez'
trust = 'warn'
```

`trust = 'warn'` is needed for this skill because its text runs `npx ai-rulez@latest`, which the security scan
reports as an unpinned package run (`AR021`). Without it, `generate` still writes the skill, but `ai-rulez lock`
leaves it out of the served-skill pins and exits 3 (see [Security](#security)).

`generate` fetches `skills/ai-rulez/` from the repository and writes it, with its bundled files, to each preset's
skills folder. With `presets = ["claude", "copilot"]`:

```text
.agents/skills/ai-rulez/SKILL.md
.agents/skills/ai-rulez/references/cli-reference.md
...
.claude/skills/ai-rulez/SKILL.md
.claude/skills/ai-rulez/references/cli-reference.md
...
```

`ai-rulez lock` pins the commit (see [Pinning](#pinning)).

!!! tip "No `.ai-rulez/` folder needed"
    A project that keeps hand-written `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` can declare `[[installed_skills]]` in a root
    `ai-rulez.toml` (`ai-rulez init --minimal`). See [Config without a .ai-rulez folder](config-without-folder.md)
    and [Managing only remote skills](managing-remote-skills.md).

#### Installed skills vs skill sources

ai-rulez reaches skills in another repository in two ways:

| | Installed skill (`[[installed_skills]]`) | Skill source (`[[skill_sources]]`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What happens | The skill is fetched and written into the harness skill folders | The repository is served over MCP; nothing is written |
| How the agent sees it | Like a local skill, listed up front | Found on demand with `find_skill` |
| Scoped by | Profiles, roles, `domain`, `profiles` | `domain`, the [skills server](mcp-server.md#dynamic-skill-loading) and a role's `delivery` |
| Use it for | A few skills the agent should always have | A large catalog the agent should search instead of paying its tokens up front |

Both are pinned in `ai-rulez.lock`, scanned before use, and accept `include`, `exclude`, `name_prefix` and `trust`.
`ai-rulez skill install`, `list`, `update` and `remove` manage installed skills; skill sources are declared by hand
in `config.toml` (they use `url` instead of `source`). See [Skill sources](mcp-server.md#skill-sources).

#### Several skills from one repository

When `path` names a directory of skill directories, one entry installs several skills. `include` and `exclude` match
directory names; `name_prefix` keeps the names apart from your own:

```bash
ai-rulez skill install vendor --source ./vendor/acme-skills --include 'db-*' --name-prefix acme-
```

```toml
[[installed_skills]]
name = 'vendor'
source = './vendor/acme-skills'
include = ['db-*']
name_prefix = 'acme-'
```

With `vendor/acme-skills/skills/{db-migrate,db-seed,api-style}/SKILL.md` and `presets = ["cursor", "codex"]`,
`generate` writes:

```text
.agents/skills/acme-db-migrate/SKILL.md
.agents/skills/acme-db-migrate/cli.md
.agents/skills/acme-db-migrate/references/notes.md
.agents/skills/acme-db-seed/SKILL.md
.agents/skills/acme-db-seed/references/notes.md
```

`name` is then only the entry's label: `skill list` and `skill remove` use it.

#### Configuration

```toml
[[installed_skills]]
name = "ai-rulez"
source = "https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez"
version = "^5"                # newest tag in this range, moved by `ai-rulez update`

[[installed_skills]]
name = "my-lib"
source = "acme/my-lib"
path = "libs/my-lib/skill"    # default: skills/<name>
ref = "v2.0.1"
domain = "backend"            # selected by profiles and roles like backend content
trust = "warn"
```

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | required | Entry name. For a single-skill entry, also the skill name and the default directory `skills/<name>` |
| `source` | string | required | Where the skills come from; see [Source forms](#source-forms) |
| `path` | string | `skills/<name>`, or `skills` with `include`/`exclude` | Directory in the source holding the skill, or a directory of skills |
| `ref` | string | default branch | Branch, tag or commit |
| `version` | string | | Semver range of the source's tags (`^1.2`, `~2.1.0`), instead of `ref` |
| `tag_prefix` | string | | With `version`: only tags with this prefix (`v`, `skills/`) |
| `include_prerelease` | bool | `false` | With `version`: let pre-release tags match |
| `min_release_age` | string | | With `version`: skip tags younger than this (`7d`, `12h`) |
| `include` | list of globs | all | Keep skill directories whose name matches |
| `exclude` | list of globs | none | Drop matching directories; wins over `include` |
| `name_prefix` | string | | Prepended to every skill name and output directory (`acme-db-migrate/`) |
| `domain` | string | root | Put the skills in a [domain](domains.md) |
| `profiles` | list | all | Include the skills only in these profiles |
| `resources` | list of patterns | whole directory | What is bundled besides `references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/`; see [below](#what-is-bundled-with-a-skill) |
| `local_override` | string | | A local checkout used instead of the source; see [Local development](#local-development) |
| `trust` | `error` \| `warn` | unset | Scan level of the imported skills; see [Security](#security) |

An entry is a single skill when the directory at `path` holds a `SKILL.md`, and a directory of skills otherwise.

#### Source forms

| Form | Example | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Git URL | `https://github.com/acme/skills`, `git@github.com:acme/skills.git` | `https` and `ssh`; `http://` is refused |
| GitHub shorthand | `acme/skills`, `github:acme/skills` | Recorded in the lock as `https://github.com/acme/skills`. A bare `acme/skills` that names an existing directory in the project is a local path; `github:` is always GitHub |
| `file://` URL | `file:///srv/skills` | A git repository is cloned; any other directory is read in place |
| Local directory | `./vendor/skills`, `/abs/path` | Read in place |
| Home directory | `~/skills` | Local, expanded to your home directory (`~user/` is not supported) |

A local path in the committed config must resolve inside the project, symlinks included. A path outside it works
only from `config.local.toml` (`skill install --local`) or from the [user config](user-scope.md):

```bash
ai-rulez skill install lint --source ~/skills --local
```

Set `AI_RULEZ_ALLOW_FILE_URLS=1` to let a `file://` source point outside the project.

Never put a token in the URL: `skill install` refuses `https://user:token@host/...`, and `validate` reports a
committed one as `AR035`. Authenticate with your git credential helper or `AI_RULEZ_GIT_TOKEN`.

#### How skills are found

Below the entry's `path`, every directory holding a `SKILL.md` is a skill, up to six levels deep. Hidden directories,
`node_modules` and symlinks are skipped. If two skills share a directory name, the shallower one wins and the other
is skipped with a warning. One entry resolves to at most 200 skills. A skill whose `SKILL.md` cannot be read is
skipped with a warning, and a missing `description` only warns (the skill name is used instead); set it anyway, since
the description is how an agent decides when to load the skill.

When `path` is not set and nothing is at `skills/<name>`, the source is searched where harnesses keep skills: a
`SKILL.md` at the root (one skill named after the entry), then `skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.agents/skills/`,
`.codex/skills/`, `.cursor/skills/`, `.gemini/skills/`, `.github/skills/` and `.opencode/skills/`, in that order.
So a repository that keeps its skills in `.claude/skills/review/` installs with:

```bash
ai-rulez skill install review --source acme/tools
```

A local skill with the same name always wins; the installed one is skipped with
`Installed skill name conflicts with local skill, skipping`. Use `name_prefix` to keep both.

#### What is bundled with a skill

An installed skill arrives whole: every file in its directory is bundled, including documents beside `SKILL.md`
(`cli.md`) and folders of any name (`rules/`, `templates/`). `generate` lists them in a `Resources` section of the
generated `SKILL.md` (documents under References, scripts under Scripts, the rest under Assets) and writes each at
its relative path, so links in `SKILL.md` keep working:

```markdown
## Resources

This skill bundles supporting files. Read them on demand when the task calls for them — don't bulk-load.

### References

- [`cli.md`](cli.md) — cli doc
- [`references/notes.md`](references/notes.md) — ref
```

Left out by default: `evals/`, `agents/` (tool display metadata such as `openai.yml`) and hidden files. Git-ignored
files and the [`bundle_exclude`](configuration.md#bundle_exclude) defaults (`node_modules`, `.venv`, ...) are
skipped as for any skill. Your own skills under `.ai-rulez/skills/` keep the canonical layout; only installed
skills are bundled whole.

`resources` replaces the default. A pattern is a name, a path or a glob; a bare name matches at any depth, and `!`
removes what an earlier pattern added. `references/`, `scripts/` and `assets/` are always bundled.

```toml
resources = ["*", "!docs", "!templates", "!evals", "!agents", "!.*"]  # everything except docs/ and templates/
resources = ["rules"]                                                  # only rules/ besides the canonical folders
resources = ["*"]                                                      # also evals/, agents/ and hidden files
```

Limits that `resources` cannot lift:

- Credential-like files (private keys, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `.env.*`, `credentials.json`, Terraform state, ...),
  symlinks and special files are never bundled; each skipped credential file is named in a warning.
- A file over 8 MiB is skipped with a warning.
- One skill may bundle at most 2000 files and 16 MiB; one entry at most 20000 files and 64 MiB. Past that, the entry
  fails with an error. Narrow it with `include`/`exclude` or `resources`.

#### Pinning

`ref` defaults to the moving default branch. `ai-rulez lock` records the resolved commit and a content digest in
`ai-rulez.lock`:

```toml
[[skill]]
name = 'ai-rulez'
source = 'https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez'
path = 'skills/ai-rulez'
commit = '99407aa72968580a77a949258e399686acfa31d9'
digest = 'sha256:af3882d30acc484af8ff29699eb914891317ea06ec76440ec158982298e763cc'
```

Later runs fetch exactly that commit and fail if the content does not match the digest. A skill read from a local
directory is pinned as a `local-skill` item with the directory's tree digest, so editing it makes `lock --check` and
`generate --locked` fail until you run `ai-rulez lock` again.

| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `ai-rulez lock` | Pin every unpinned entry |
| `ai-rulez skill update [name...]` | Re-pin entries to the current commit of their `ref` |
| `ai-rulez update` | Move `version` entries to the newest allowed tag |
| `ai-rulez generate --locked` | Fail when an entry is missing from the lock or does not match |
| `ai-rulez generate --frozen` | Same, and never use the network |

See [Lock file](lockfile.md).

#### Security

Imported skill text is instruction text, so it is scanned for secrets, hidden characters, risky commands and
unpinned package runs ([Security checks](strict-validation.md#security-checks)) at three points:

| When | What blocks |
| --- | --- |
| `ai-rulez lock`, before pinning a new tree | Error findings refuse the pin (exit 2) unless you pass `--accept-findings` |
| `generate` | An error finding stops the run before anything is written. `trust = "error"` makes every finding an error, `trust = "warn"` every finding a warning; unset, [`[lint.security] scan_imports`](strict-validation.md#security-checks) decides (by default each finding keeps its own severity) |
| The [skills server](mcp-server.md#security-scan) and its `[[served]]` lock pins | `error`, or unset: any finding refuses the skill. `warn`: only findings that are errors in their own right. Unset, `[lint.security] scan_imports = "warn"` lowers the default to `warn` |

When the served view refuses a skill, `lock` still writes the lock, leaves that skill unpinned and exits 3
(`1 served skill(s) were left unpinned because the security scan refuses them`). Fix the finding, set
`trust = "warn"`, or pass `--refuse-findings` to fail without writing instead.

#### Local development

`local_override` points an entry at a local checkout while you work on the skill:

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.local.toml
[[installed_skills]]
name = "my-lib"
source = "acme/my-lib"
local_override = "../my-lib"
```

The override is the checkout root; `path` (default `skills/<name>`) is resolved inside it. If that directory has no
`SKILL.md`, the skill is skipped, not fetched from the source. Set it in `config.local.toml`: a `local_override` in
the committed config fails whenever the lock is enforced (an `ai-rulez.lock` exists, or under `--locked` or
`--frozen`).

#### Commands

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `ai-rulez skill install <name> --source <src> [flags]` | Add an entry. Every key above has a flag (`--path`, `--ref`, `--version`, `--include`, `--name-prefix`, `--resources`, `--trust`, `--domain`, `--profile`, `--local-override`, ...) |
| `ai-rulez skill install ... --local` | Write the entry to the gitignored `config.local.toml` instead |
| `ai-rulez skill list [--format json]` | List entries |
| `ai-rulez skill remove <name> [--yes]` | Remove an entry. With `--local`, a shared entry is hidden on this machine (`remove = true` in the overlay) |
| `ai-rulez skill update [name...]` | Re-pin in `ai-rulez.lock` |

```text
$ ai-rulez skill list
Installed skills:
  • vendor [local]
    Source: ./vendor/acme-skills
    Path: skills
```

The MCP server offers the same operations as `install_skill` (the same fields as `skill install`, plus `local`),
`uninstall_skill` and `list_installed_skills`. Full flag tables: [CLI reference](cli-reference.md#ai-rulez-skill-install).

#### Publishing a skill

To make a skill installable from your repository:

1. Put it at `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, with `name` and `description` frontmatter (see [Skills](skills.md)).
2. Add `references/`, `scripts/` or `assets/` as needed; any other files beside `SKILL.md` are bundled too.
3. Tag releases so consumers can use `version = "^1"`.

Consumers then run `ai-rulez skill install <name> --source <owner>/<repo>`.

#### Compared with includes

| | [Includes](includes.md) | Installed skills |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Imports | Rules, context, skills, agents, commands | Skills only |
| Source layout | A `.ai-rulez/` directory or a bare layout | A directory with `SKILL.md`, or a directory of them |
| Name conflicts | Configurable merge strategy | The local skill wins |
| Domains | Into a chosen domain | Root, or the `domain` key |
| Use for | Sharing a whole governance setup | Adding skills for a library or tool |

To import a whole harness plugin (skills, agents, commands, hooks and MCP servers), see
[Installed plugins](installed-plugins.md).

## Installed plugins

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/installed-plugins/

Import a harness plugin (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI or [Agent Plugins](agent-plugins.md)) and render its
skills, agents, commands, rules, hooks and MCP servers into every preset you generate. An
`[[installed_marketplaces]]` entry names a plugin marketplace; an `[[installed_plugins]]` entry imports one plugin
from a marketplace or straight from a repository. Imported content is pinned in `ai-rulez.lock` and scanned like
[installed skills](installed-skills.md).

To build a plugin from your own content instead, see [Authoring plugins](plugins.md).

#### Example

A marketplace in `vendor/acme-market` with one plugin:

```text
vendor/acme-market/
  .claude-plugin/marketplace.json      # {"name": "acme", "plugins": [{"name": "formatter", "source": "./plugins/formatter"}]}
  plugins/formatter/
    .claude-plugin/plugin.json
    skills/format-code/SKILL.md
    agents/style-reviewer.md
    commands/git/commit.md
    hooks/hooks.json
    .mcp.json
```

```bash
ai-rulez marketplace add acme --source ./vendor/acme-market
ai-rulez plugin install formatter --from acme
ai-rulez generate
```

The two commands add:

```toml
[[installed_marketplaces]]
name = 'acme'
source = './vendor/acme-market'

[[installed_plugins]]
name = 'formatter'
marketplace = 'acme'
```

With `presets = ["claude", "cursor", "gemini"]`, `generate` writes the plugin's content into each tool's own
folders:

```text
INFO  Installed plugin hooks are not imported; set enable_hooks = true to import them plugin=formatter hooks=1
...
.agents/skills/format-code/SKILL.md
.claude/agents/style-reviewer.md
.claude/skills/format-code/SKILL.md
.claude/skills/git-commit/SKILL.md
.cursor/agents/style-reviewer.md
.cursor/commands/git-commit.md
.cursor/mcp.json
.gemini/agents/style-reviewer.md
.gemini/settings.json
.mcp.json
```

A remote marketplace works the same way:

```bash
ai-rulez marketplace add acme --source acme/plugins --version "^1.2"
ai-rulez plugin install review-tools --source https://github.com/acme/review-tools --ref v2.0.1
ai-rulez lock
```

#### Supported formats

The layout is detected from the manifest; set `format` (`--layout`) to force `claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, `gemini`
or `agent-plugins`.

| Harness | Marketplace index | Plugin manifest | Imported |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (optional) | `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/`, `hooks/hooks.json`, `.mcp.json`, and the paths or inline objects the manifest's `skills`, `agents`, `commands`, `hooks` and `mcpServers` name |
| Codex | `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` | `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` | `skills/`, `.mcp.json`, `hooks.json`, and the manifest's `skills`, `mcpServers` and `hooks` |
| Cursor | `.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json` | `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` | `rules/` (as rules), `agents/`, `skills/`, `commands/`, `hooks/hooks.json`, `.mcp.json` or `mcp.json` |
| Gemini CLI extension | none | `gemini-extension.json` | `mcpServers`, the `contextFileName` file (as a rule), `commands/*.toml` (as commands), `skills/`, `agents/` |
| Agent Plugins | none | root `plugin.json` with an `agent-plugins.org` `$schema` | `skills/`, `mcp.json`, and the `com.anthropic.claude-code` (agents, commands, hooks) and `io.github.goldziher.ai-rulez` (rules) extensions |

- A directory with Claude Code's default folders and no manifest is a Claude Code plugin.
- A marketplace entry with `strict = false` that declares its own components needs no manifest.
- Skills are bundled whole, as for an [installed skill](installed-skills.md#what-is-bundled-with-a-skill).
- Agent, command and rule files keep their frontmatter. A nested command `git/commit.md` becomes `git-commit`.
- A Gemini TOML command becomes a prompt; its `{{args}}` and `!{...}` placeholders are kept as written.

#### Source forms

| Form | Example |
| --- | --- |
| GitHub shorthand | `acme/plugins`, `github:acme/plugins` |
| Git URL | `https://github.com/acme/plugins`, `git@github.com:acme/plugins.git`, `file:///srv/plugins` |
| Local directory | `./vendor/marketplace` (starts with `./`, `../` or `/`) |
| Index URL (marketplace only) | `https://example.com/marketplace.json` |

The rules of installed skills apply: `https` only, no credentials in a URL, no `..` in `path`, and a local path in
the committed config must stay inside the project (`config.local.toml` and the user config may leave it). A
`file://` repository outside the project needs `AI_RULEZ_ALLOW_FILE_URLS=1`.

A marketplace entry can name its plugin as:

- a relative path in the marketplace repository (`"./plugins/x"`; `metadata.pluginRoot` is prepended to a bare
  name);
- `{"source": "github", "repo": "owner/repo", "ref": "...", "sha": "..."}`;
- `{"source": "url" | "git", "url": "...", "ref": "...", "sha": "..."}`;
- `{"source": "git-subdir", "url": "...", "path": "sub/dir"}`, or Codex's `{"source": "local", "path": "./x"}`.

A relative path that is absolute, contains `..` or passes through a symlink is refused. Entries with other source
types (npm, pip) are listed as not installable.

#### Configuration

##### `[[installed_marketplaces]]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | required | Name that `[[installed_plugins]] marketplace` refers to |
| `source` | string | required | See [Source forms](#source-forms) |
| `path` | string | repository root | Directory holding the index |
| `ref` | string | default branch | Branch, tag or commit |
| `version`, `tag_prefix`, `include_prerelease`, `min_release_age` | | | Tag range instead of `ref`, as on [installed skills](installed-skills.md#configuration) |
| `trust` | `error` \| `warn` | unset | Scan level of the plugins read through it; `error` makes every finding an error |

##### `[[installed_plugins]]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | required | Plugin name |
| `marketplace` | string | | An installed marketplace to take it from |
| `plugin` | string | `name` | The marketplace entry, when it is called differently (`--entry`) |
| `source`, `path`, `ref` | string | | A plugin repository or directory, instead of `marketplace` |
| `version`, `tag_prefix`, `include_prerelease`, `min_release_age` | | | Tag range, for a plugin from `source` only |
| `format` | string | detected | Force the layout (`--layout`) |
| `include` | list | all | Import only these kinds: `skills`, `agents`, `commands`, `hooks`, `mcp`, `rules` |
| `exclude` | list | none | Skip these kinds; wins over `include` |
| `name_prefix` | string | | Prepended to every imported name and to skill output directories |
| `domain` | string | root | Put the content in a [domain](domains.md) |
| `profiles` | list | all | Include the content only in these profiles |
| `trust` | `error` \| `warn` | the marketplace's | Scan level |
| `enable_hooks` | bool | `false` | Import the plugin's hooks |
| `enable_mcp` | bool | `true` | Import the plugin's MCP servers |

A plugin from a marketplace follows the marketplace's `ref` or `version`; setting them on the plugin is an error.
`domain` and `profiles` scope everything except hooks, which are global.

When an imported name already exists (your own content first, then earlier plugins), the existing item wins and the
later one is skipped with a warning. Set `name_prefix` to keep both.

#### Hooks and MCP servers

- **Hooks are off by default.** A hook runs a command on every machine that uses the project, so set
  `enable_hooks = true` (`--enable-hooks`) to import them. Imported hooks are written only for the harness the
  plugin was made for.
- **MCP servers** are imported unless `enable_mcp = false`. Literal credentials in `env`, `args`, `url` or `headers`
  are replaced by `${VAR}` references and reported. The servers go through the same MCP checks and `[mcp]` policy as
  your own.
- **Plugin root variables.** A hook or MCP server that refers to `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, `${CODEX_PLUGIN_ROOT}`,
  `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` or Gemini's `${extensionPath}` is rewritten to the plugin's project-relative path when the plugin is
  a local directory inside the project:

    ```json
    "command": "./vendor/acme-market/plugins/formatter/fmt.sh"
    ```

    For a fetched plugin there is no such directory, so the hook or server is not imported (run with `--debug` to see
    each skipped component). `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` is never supported.
- **Permissions** are never imported: a plugin cannot add an allow rule.

#### Security

- Fetches share the include machinery: the git cache, credential handling (a token is sent only to allowlisted
  hosts) and the `sources.allowed_hosts` / `sources.deny_hosts` policy, which also applies to repositories a
  marketplace names.
- `ai-rulez lock` scans every file of a new marketplace or plugin tree, hook scripts and MCP definitions included,
  before pinning it. Error findings refuse the pin (exit 2) unless you pass `--accept-findings`. `trust = "error"`
  makes every finding an error.
- `generate` scans the imported content, hook commands, MCP definitions and the scripts they run again
  ([`[lint.security] scan_imports`](strict-validation.md#security-checks)).
- Symlinks are never followed, files and manifests are size-bounded, and a malformed manifest fails the load with an
  error naming the file.
- The [organization policy](policy.md) bounds plugin hooks and MCP servers (`AR748`); `sources.deny_digests` and
  [approvals](approvals.md) cover `marketplace` and `installed-plugin` entries.

#### Lock, update and refresh

`ai-rulez lock` pins remote marketplaces and plugins as `[[marketplace]]` and `[[plugin]]` entries. A plugin from a
marketplace is keyed `marketplace:<name>` and records where the index pointed as `origin`:

```toml
[[marketplace]]
name = 'acme'
source = 'https://github.com/acme/plugins'
commit = 'c13e0a4aef9a900cdca038afcf128cd21c3b1993'
digest = 'sha256:43808c6c446c9c2049b656805e85b6844a7dc013c16f85ce647318a32526dbdf'

[[plugin]]
name = 'formatter'
source = 'marketplace:acme'
commit = 'c13e0a4aef9a900cdca038afcf128cd21c3b1993'
digest = 'sha256:143280174a3af8f900dc0b4ba618ed2eb9e9c8b42d2270e1cebaacfb2a9c7627'
origin = 'https://github.com/acme/plugins#plugins/formatter'
```

| Source | What the lock records |
| --- | --- |
| Remote repository | `[[marketplace]]` / `[[plugin]]` with commit and tree digest |
| `https://.../marketplace.json` | A digest, no commit |
| Local directory inside the project | A `local-marketplace` or `local-plugin` item with the directory's tree digest (a local marketplace's plugins are covered by it) |

Editing any file of a local plugin, such as `hooks/hooks.json` or a hook script, makes `lock --check` and
`generate --locked` fail until you run `ai-rulez lock` again.

| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `ai-rulez lock --check` | Compare the lock offline |
| `ai-rulez lock [name] --kind marketplace\|plugin` | Refresh pins; refreshing a marketplace refreshes its plugins |
| `ai-rulez marketplace update [name...]`, `ai-rulez plugin update [name...]` | Re-pin plain refs to the current commit |
| `ai-rulez update --kind marketplace\|plugin [name]` | Move `version` entries to the newest allowed tag |
| `ai-rulez generate --locked` / `--frozen` | Fail on a missing, stale or mismatching pin (a moved branch, a retagged release, changed bytes) |
| `ai-rulez generate --offline` | Read the cache only |

`ai-rulez sbom` and `ai-rulez approve` list these entries. See [Lock file](lockfile.md).

#### Commands

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `ai-rulez marketplace add <name> --source <src>` | Add a marketplace (`--path`, `--ref`, `--version`, `--trust`, ...) |
| `ai-rulez marketplace list`, `remove <name>` | List or remove marketplaces |
| `ai-rulez plugin install <name> --from <marketplace>` | Install a plugin from a marketplace |
| `ai-rulez plugin install <name> --source <src>` | Install a plugin from a repository or directory |
| `ai-rulez plugin list`, `remove <name>` | List or remove plugins |

```bash
ai-rulez plugin install tools --source acme/tools --exclude hooks
ai-rulez plugin install tools --source acme/tools --enable-hooks --name-prefix acme-
```

Full flag tables: [CLI reference](cli-reference.md#ai-rulez-plugin-install). To change an entry on one machine only,
edit `config.local.toml` (see [Local configuration](local-overrides.md)).

To enable a plugin in a harness's own settings without importing it, use
[`[[enabled_plugins]]`](configuration.md#enabled_plugins) (see [Migrating to v5](migration-v5.md)).

## .agents as a source

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/agents-source/

With `source = "agents"`, ai-rulez reads your content from the open standards (the root `AGENTS.md` and the
`.agents/` directory) instead of `.ai-rulez/`, and generates every other tool's files from them. Use it when your team
already keeps its instructions and skills there and wants Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini, Copilot and the rest to get
the same content without moving a file. ai-rulez never writes `AGENTS.md` or anything under `.agents/` in this mode.

#### Example

```bash
ai-rulez init --source agents
```

This writes `.agents/ai-rulez.toml` and, if the project has none, a starter `AGENTS.md`. Choose the presets and add
content:

```toml
# .agents/ai-rulez.toml
version = "5.0"
name = "acme"
presets = ["claude", "codex", "cursor", "gemini"]
```

```text
AGENTS.md                          # project instructions
svc/api/AGENTS.md                  # instructions for svc/api
.agents/skills/release/SKILL.md    # an Agent Skill
.agents/rules/go-style.md          # a rule with paths: ["**/*.go"]
```

```text
$ ai-rulez generate
INFO  source = agents: AGENTS.md and .agents/ are the source and are not written skipped=12
INFO  Generation complete files=11
```

The result:

```text
CLAUDE.md                              # AGENTS.md text, inline
GEMINI.md                              # AGENTS.md text and rules
.claude/rules/go-style.md
.claude/rules/context-agents-svc-api.md   # svc/api/AGENTS.md, scoped to svc/api/**
.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md        # Claude Code does not read .agents/skills
.cursor/rules/go-style.mdc
.gemini/settings.json
...
```

Codex and Cursor read `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/skills` themselves, so they get no copy of the `AGENTS.md` text or the
skills; Cursor still gets `.cursor/rules/go-style.mdc`.

#### Layout

ai-rulez reads what the standards define as they define it, and uses folders named after their content for the rest.

| Content | Location | Defined by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Project instructions | root `AGENTS.md` | [AGENTS.md](https://agents.md) |
| Scoped instructions | `<dir>/AGENTS.md` | AGENTS.md (nested files) |
| Skills, with `references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/` | `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) |
| Rules | `.agents/rules/<name>.md` | Antigravity convention |
| Agents (subagents) | `.agents/agents/<name>.md` | Antigravity and Amp convention |
| Review checks | `.agents/checks/<name>.md` | Amp convention |
| Commands | `.agents/commands/<name>.md` | ai-rulez |
| Context files | `.agents/context/<name>.md` | ai-rulez |
| Domains | `.agents/domains/<name>/{rules,context,skills,agents,commands,checks}` | ai-rulez |

Each file has the format described in [Configuration](configuration.md#content-layout). Hooks, MCP servers,
permissions, presets, profiles and roles stay in the TOML configuration.

#### Where the configuration lives

| Configuration file | `source` | ai-rulez state (manifest, `ai-rulez.lock`, `config.local.toml`, layers, `local/`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.agents/ai-rulez.toml` (preferred) | implied `"agents"` | `.agents/.ai-rulez/` |
| `.ai-rulez/config.toml` | set `source = "agents"` | `.ai-rulez/` (its content folders are not read) |

When both files exist, `.agents/ai-rulez.toml` is used and `doctor` warns about the shadowed one. `config.<name>.toml`
layers and `config.local.toml` are read from the state directory, never from beside `.agents/ai-rulez.toml`.

#### What is read

- **Root `AGENTS.md`**: one context item named `agents`. Its first `# Title` is dropped when rendered. `list context`
  shows it with `AGENTS.md` as its path; `edit` and `remove` refuse it unless you split the file (below).
- **Nested `AGENTS.md`**: context scoped to its directory (see [below](#nested-agentsmd)).
- **`.agents/`**: scanned like the `.ai-rulez` tree, with the same formats, `bundle_exclude` and symlink policy (a
  symlink must resolve inside the project). A symlinked `AGENTS.md` is never read.
- **Generated files are ignored**: a file whose header is the ai-rulez generated banner is output of an earlier run,
  not source. `generate` names such files in a warning; delete them or replace them with your own.

#### Splitting AGENTS.md

Set `agents_md_split = true` to read the root `AGENTS.md` as one context item per `##` heading, so each section can
be listed, shown, edited and removed on its own:

```toml
agents_md_split = true
```

```text
$ ai-rulez list context
Context:
  (root):
    • agents
    • agents-conventions
    • agents-code-style
```

- The text before the first `##` is `agents`. Each section is `agents-<heading slug>` (`## Code Style` is
  `agents-code-style`); a repeated heading gets `-2`, `-3`. A heading inside a code fence does not split.
- `show context <item>` (MCP `read_context`) prints the section, heading line included. `edit context <item>` (MCP
  `update_context`) replaces it; `remove context <item>` (MCP `delete_context`) cuts it out. Every other byte of
  `AGENTS.md`, its line endings, BOM and file mode are kept.
- An edit that adds or drops a `##` heading, renames the section or is empty is refused.
- Items are rendered in name order, not in file order.
- Every item pins the whole file in `ai-rulez.lock`, so editing one section marks all of them changed for
  `lock --check`. Run `ai-rulez lock` to accept.

The setting requires the agents source; `validate` rejects it otherwise.

#### Nested AGENTS.md

`svc/api/AGENTS.md` becomes the context item `agents-svc-api`, scoped to `svc/api/**`, and each tool renders it the
way it renders a path-scoped rule (for example `.claude/rules/context-agents-svc-api.md` with `paths: [svc/api/**]`).
Tools that read nested `AGENTS.md` files themselves get no copy.

The search:

- skips symlinks, hidden directories and dependency and build trees (`node_modules`, `vendor`, `target`, `dist`,
  `build`, ...);
- honours `.gitignore` inside a git repository;
- stops at a directory with its own `.agents/ai-rulez.toml`, `.ai-rulez/config.toml` or
  `.config/ai-rulez/config.toml`, which is a separate project (`generate --recursive` handles it);
- goes at most eight directories deep and warns when it stops early;
- leaves out generated files, empty files and files that only point at another (`@AGENTS.md`).

When two directories produce the same slug (`a-b/` and `a b/`), each gets a short hash of its path
(`agents-a-b-1f2e3d4c`). Adding or removing one of them renames the other too.

Nested files are not split, and `list`, `show`, `edit` and `remove` do not see them: edit them by hand.

#### What generate writes

`generate` writes every tool's files except those that would land on `AGENTS.md`, a nested `AGENTS.md` or anything
under `.agents/`. Those outputs are dropped with one info line, so your files stay byte for byte and
`generate --check` stays clean.

- Every tool gets full files, as with `agents_md = false`: `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md` and the rules folders carry
  your always-on rules and context; skills, agents and commands go to each tool's own folders. `agents_md = true` is
  rejected.
- The `agents` item (your `AGENTS.md` text) is left out of the files of tools that load `AGENTS.md` themselves
  (Codex, Cursor, Copilot and the others in the [tool table](agents-md.md#tool-support)), so they never see it twice.
  Gemini CLI gets it in `GEMINI.md`.
- Such a tool receives your rules, agents and commands only where it has a place for them. Codex has no rules folder,
  so it reads only `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/skills`. Put what every tool must follow in `AGENTS.md`.
- An output below a symlink that leads into `.agents` (`.claude/skills -> ../.agents/skills`) is dropped with a
  warning, so nothing is written through the link.
- `generate --plugin` skips plugin outputs under `.agents/` (such as the Codex index
  `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`) with a warning.

#### Commands

| Command | Behavior with the agents source |
| --- | --- |
| `init --source agents` | Writes `.agents/ai-rulez.toml` and a starter `AGENTS.md`. `--config-dir .ai-rulez` writes `.ai-rulez/config.toml` with `source = "agents"` instead; `--force` keeps the old file as `<file>.bak-<timestamp>` |
| `init --source agents --from CLAUDE.md,.cursor`, `convert --into .agents` | Import other tools' files into the layout above. Files already in place are left as they are |
| `add`, `remove`, `list`, `show`, `edit` | Work on `.agents/rules`, `.agents/skills`, `.agents/domains/<name>` and the rest; machine-local content goes to `.agents/.ai-rulez/local` |
| `clean` | Never removes `AGENTS.md` or anything under `.agents`, even with `--include-edited` |
| `lock` | Pins `AGENTS.md`, nested `AGENTS.md` files and the `.agents` tree |
| `generate --watch` | Watches `AGENTS.md`, `.agents` and the nested `AGENTS.md` files found at start or after each run; a new nested file is picked up after the next run |
| `doctor` | Warns about a shadowed `.ai-rulez/config.toml`, `.ai-rulez` content that is not read, and generated files left in the source |
| `generate --recursive`, `validate --recursive` | Find nested `.agents/ai-rulez.toml` projects |
| `migrate okf` | Refused: it converts the `.ai-rulez` tree |

The [`[guard]`](settings.md#guard) hook keeps agents out of generated files only; `AGENTS.md` and `.agents` stay
editable.

To return to the `.ai-rulez` tree, set `source = "ai-rulez"` in `.ai-rulez/config.toml` and move the files back, or
run `ai-rulez convert --from native` over the generated tool files.

## Config without a .ai-rulez folder

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/config-without-folder/

Keep the whole ai-rulez configuration in one file, `ai-rulez.toml` at the project root, with no `.ai-rulez/` directory. Use it when the repository already has hand-written `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` and skills, and you want ai-rulez only for what a configuration file can declare.

#### Create it

```bash
ai-rulez init --minimal
```

This writes only `ai-rulez.toml`: a `#:schema` first line (editors such as taplo and Even Better TOML read it to find the [JSON schema](schema.md)), `version`, `name`, `presets` and commented examples of `[[installed_skills]]` and `[lint]`. An existing file is replaced only with `--force`, and `--minimal` cannot be combined with `--source agents`, `--from`, `--domains` or `--config-dir`.

Then declare what ai-rulez should manage, for example:

```toml
version = "5.0"
name = "acme"
presets = ["claude", "codex"]

[[installed_skills]]
name = "kreuzberg"
source = "https://github.com/kreuzberg-dev/kreuzberg"
include = ["xberg*"]
```

```bash
ai-rulez generate
```

#### What it does

A root `ai-rulez.toml` can declare:

- remote content: `[[installed_skills]]`, `[[installed_plugins]]`, `[[skill_sources]]` and `[[includes]]`
- `[[mcp_servers]]`, `[[hooks]]` and `[permissions]`, translated into each tool's native format
- `[lint]` settings for `ai-rulez validate`
- `ai-rulez.lock` settings (`[lock]`), pinning the remote sources and the generated outputs

`generate` installs the skills into each tool's skill folder and writes the MCP servers, hooks and permissions (for `claude`, including the default [`SessionStart` hook](session-start.md)). It writes no instruction file: `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, rule files and the `llms-txt` and `okf` indexes are never rendered, and a hand-written file at those paths is never overwritten or deleted. `clean` removes only what `generate` wrote.

Files in the project root:

| File | Purpose | Committed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ai-rulez.toml` | The configuration | yes |
| `ai-rulez.lock` | Pins written by `ai-rulez lock` | yes |
| `.ai-rulez-manifest.json` | The paths `generate` wrote | yes |
| `.ai-rulez-manifest.local.json` | Machine-local claims and digests | no, git-ignored |
| `ai-rulez.local.toml` | Optional [machine-local overlay](local-overrides.md#config-overlay) | no, git-ignored |

The local manifest is excluded through `.git/info/exclude`; once an overlay exists, the managed `.gitignore` block lists it and the local manifest. With `gitignore = true` the block also lists the overlay's lock and temp files (`.ai-rulez-local.*`), the generated outputs and `.ai-rulez-manifest.json`.

Everything else in the [configuration reference](configuration.md) applies, except what needs a content tree: settings that shape root instruction files and rule files (`agents_md`, `claude_md`, `compact`, `[[scopes]]`) have nothing to render, and layers are not supported; see [Limits](#limits).

#### Discovery order

`ai-rulez.toml` comes last in the [discovery order](configuration.md#configuration-discovery), so a config directory always wins: when one exists beside an `ai-rulez.toml`, `generate` and `doctor` warn that the file is ignored:

```text
WARN  ai-rulez.toml is ignored: the .ai-rulez/ directory takes precedence hint=keep one configuration; move settings you still need into .ai-rulez/config.toml
```

`--config ai-rulez.toml` (or `--config .`) selects the file explicitly, and `generate --recursive` finds an `ai-rulez.toml` that has no config directory beside it. A flat `ai-rulez.yaml` is refused with a pointer to `ai-rulez migrate v5`.

The [`.agents` source](agents-source.md) also uses a file named `ai-rulez.toml`, but in `.agents/`, with `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/` as content and the manifest, lock and local state in `.agents/.ai-rulez/`. In this layout the file is in the project root, there is no content, and the state files sit in the root under the names above.

#### CLI behavior

- `skill install|remove`, `include add|remove`, `lock`, `update --write-config` and the `local` commands edit `ai-rulez.toml` and `ai-rulez.local.toml`. A command that rewrites the file drops its comments.
- `add` and `remove` of `rule`, `context`, `skill`, `agent`, `command` and `check`, and `domain add`, fail: there is no content tree.

  ```text
  Error: Failed to add rule: cannot write content: no .ai-rulez/ directory (single-file configuration)
  ```

- `validate` and `scan` lint the configuration, the lock, installed and included content, and the hand-written instruction files they find. `doctor` reports drift, missing generated files and the environment checks, and does not lint instruction files. An empty content tree is not an error.

#### Lint-only configuration

A project that uses ai-rulez only as a linter needs no preset. Leave `presets` out, or set `presets = []`:

```toml
version = "5.0"
name = "lint"

[lint]
profile = "strict"
```

With no preset (and no `[plugin]` block), `validate`, `scan`, `[[lint.external]]`, `lock`, `sbom` and the other read commands work as usual, and `generate` writes nothing and exits 0:

```text
INFO  No presets are configured: nothing to generate (lint-only configuration)
```

Hand-written files such as `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/skills/` are never touched, and the default `agents_md = true` does not make `generate` write `AGENTS.md`. `generate --check` and `doctor` report no drift. Files an earlier run wrote stay until you run `ai-rulez clean`. A lint-only configuration works the same in the `.ai-rulez/` directory layout.

#### The ai-rulez MCP server

`[mcp] self_server` defaults to `true`, so `generate` writes `.mcp.json` with an `ai-rulez` server entry (`mcp --serve-skills` when skills are served), and `ai-rulez.lock` gains `[[served]]` pins and an `.mcp.json` output pin. To keep `.mcp.json` limited to your `[[mcp_servers]]`, turn it off:

```toml
[mcp]
self_server = false
```

`generate --no-self-mcp` does the same for one run.

#### Limits

- No content is read: `rules/`, `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/`, `checks/`, `domains/` and `verifiers/` folders in the project root are not ai-rulez content. Verifiers come from `[[verifiers]]` and imports.
- Rules and context from an `[[includes]]` entry have no instruction file to land in; only outputs that are not root instruction files (skills, rule files of tools with a rules folder) are written.
- `default_layers` and `config.<name>.toml` layers are not supported.
- Opt-in state (skills index, role manifest, scanner baseline, eval results) is written to the project root, and usage logs to `.ai-rulez-local.d/`. The telemetry commands and `improve` look for `.ai-rulez/`.
- The MCP `init_project` tool creates the directory layout only.

#### Troubleshooting

**`refusing to overwrite 1 existing file(s) ai-rulez cannot prove it wrote`.** `generate` would write a path where a file exists that has no ai-rulez `Content-Hash` header and is not in the manifest, so it may be hand-written. Nothing is written. Import the file (`ai-rulez convert --write`), move or delete it, or pass `generate --force` to overwrite it. To keep a hand-written file at a path ai-rulez would render, list that output kind in [`skip_outputs`](configuration.md#skip_outputs).

**An installed skill has the name of a hand-written skill.** In `.claude/skills/<name>/` or `.agents/skills/<name>/` this is the refusal above. Rename or remove one of them; `ai-rulez skill remove <name>` drops the installed entry.

**`generate --refresh-remote` refuses with "the security scan of the new tree has error findings".** Nothing was written and `ai-rulez.lock` is unchanged. Review the findings in the new version. To accept them, run `ai-rulez generate --refresh-remote --accept-findings`, or `ai-rulez update --accept-findings` and then `ai-rulez generate`. `ai-rulez lock --accept-findings` only re-pins what is already pinned; it does not move to the new version. `generate` scans imported content at the entry's `trust` level, so error findings stop it unless the entry sets `trust = "warn"` or `[lint.security] scan_imports = "warn"` is set.

## Local configuration

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/local-overrides/

Machine-local configuration that is never committed: scratch notes, per-machine paths, personal presets and MCP servers, secrets and experiments that belong to your checkout but not to the shared configuration.

```bash
ai-rulez add rule local-paths --local   # .ai-rulez/local/rules/local-paths.md
ai-rulez generate
```

Your tools load the local rule (for `claude`, from `CLAUDE.local.md` or `.claude/rules/local-paths.local.md`). Every local input and output is git-ignored; the only tracked change is the managed `.gitignore` block that the first run adds for the local inputs.

Local configuration belongs to one checkout. Instructions and skills that should follow you into every repository go to your home directories instead; see [User-level configuration](user-scope.md). The committed `config.<name>.toml` layers that `default_layers` activates for everyone are a different feature; see [Layered configuration](configuration.md#layered-configuration).

There are two layers, both git-ignored even with `gitignore = false`:

| Layer | Location | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Content tree | `.ai-rulez/local/` | Rules, context, skills, agents, commands and domains |
| Config overlay | `.ai-rulez/config.local.toml` | Settings merged onto `config.toml`: presets, profiles, MCP servers, includes, installed skills, ... |

Committed outputs never contain local content, so a teammate who checks out your branch sees only the shared configuration.

#### Content tree

```text
.ai-rulez/
├── config.toml
├── rules/                  # shared, committed
├── context/                # shared, committed
└── local/                  # machine-local, git-ignored
    ├── rules/
    ├── context/
    ├── skills/
    ├── agents/
    ├── commands/
    ├── checks/
    └── domains/<name>/     # selected by the active profile like shared domains
```

- It mirrors the shared layout, with the same file formats and frontmatter.
- Local domains are selected by the active profile like shared ones, and a profile defined in the overlay may name them.
- Local content is root-only: `[[scopes]]` never get local outputs.
- Files and directories the CLI or MCP tools create here are owner-only (`0600`, `0700`).
- A local skill, agent or command may not have the name of a shared one (skills and commands share one namespace); `generate` fails naming both files. A local rule or context item may reuse a shared name; see [Collisions](#collisions).

##### Generated output

A local rule follows the same routing as a shared rule of the preset (the [rules mode](rules.md#rules-mode) and [`agents_md`](configuration.md#agents_md) decide): a rule the preset writes to its rules folder becomes `<rulesdir>/<id>.local<ext>`. Local context, and rules the preset keeps inline, go to the file the tool loads for machine-local instructions:

- Local skills, agents and commands are written per item to the same paths as shared ones (`.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`). A preset that has no per-item output for them gets none, with one warning per preset.
- Content a preset has no place for (local context with `cursor`) is not written, with one warning per preset:

  ```text
  WARN  Machine-local content has no output for this preset and was not written preset=cursor items=context env
  ```

- Custom providers (`.ai-rulez/providers/`) get no local output.

| Preset | Local rules routed to files | Everything else | How the tool loads it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `claude` | `.claude/rules/<id>.local.md` | `CLAUDE.local.md` | Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.local.md` after `CLAUDE.md`, and its rules folder |
| `cursor` | `.cursor/rules/<id>.local.mdc` | not written | Rules folder |
| `devin` | `.devin/rules/<id>.local.md` | not written | Rules folder |
| `cline` | `.clinerules/<id>.local.md` | not written | Rules folder |
| `junie` | `.junie/rules/<id>.local.md` | `.junie/rules/ai-rulez.local.md` | `.junie/rules/*.md`, read beside a root `AGENTS.md`; a `.junie/AGENTS.md` or `.junie/guidelines.md` layout does not read the folder |
| `copilot` | `.github/instructions/<id>.local.instructions.md` | `.github/instructions/ai-rulez.local.instructions.md` (`applyTo: "**"`) | Path-specific instruction files |
| `antigravity` | `.agents/rules/<id>.local.md` | `.agents/rules/ai-rulez.local.md` (`trigger: always_on`) | Every `.agents/rules/*.md` with a `trigger` |
| `gemini` | none | `GEMINI.local.md` | Listed in `context.fileName` of `.gemini/settings.json` |
| `opencode` | none | `AGENTS.local.md` | Listed in `instructions` of `opencode.json` |
| `xum` | none | `AGENTS.local.md` | xum appends it to `AGENTS.md` |
| `pi` | none | `AGENTS.local.md` | The `.local` variant of pi's `AGENTS.md` |
| `codex` | none | `AGENTS.override.md` (root only) | Codex reads it instead of `AGENTS.md` in the same directory |
| `hermes` | none | `AGENTS.override.md` with `agents_md`; otherwise not written | Read instead of `AGENTS.md` in the AGENTS chain; `.hermes.md` has no local counterpart |
| `amp` | none | not written | Amp reads only `~/.config/amp/AGENTS.md` |

With `agents_md` on (the default), always-on rules are inlined rather than written to rule files, so `claude` puts always-on local rules into `CLAUDE.local.md`. With `rules.mode = "inline"`, only path-scoped local rules get a file. When `antigravity` and `gemini` are both configured and no `mode_by_preset` is set, Antigravity keeps all local rules in `ai-rulez.local.md`.

`AGENTS.override.md`:

- It repeats the `AGENTS.md` body of the same run and appends the local sections, because Codex reads it instead of `AGENTS.md`. Do not edit it: it is rebuilt on every `generate` and removed when the local content goes away.
- When local content exists but no `AGENTS.md` is generated, it is not written, and `generate` warns.
- One without a generated banner that is not in the local manifest is yours: it is never overwritten or deleted, and `generate` warns that Codex reads it instead of your local content.

A local rule named `ai-rulez` would collide with the `ai-rulez.local.*` file of `junie`, `antigravity` and `copilot`, so it is written as `ai-rulez-<hash>.local<ext>`.

##### Bookkeeping

- **Git ignore.** The overlay, the `local/` tree and the local manifest are always ignored, whatever `gitignore` says; with `gitignore = true` the managed block lists them on every machine. See [`gitignore`](configuration.md#gitignore).
- **Per-clone excludes.** The outputs your local inputs add (`CLAUDE.local.md`, `<rulesdir>/*.local.*`, `AGENTS.override.md`, a local skill, a `.claude/settings.json` only the overlay's hooks create, the files of an overlay-defined preset) go to a block of `.git/info/exclude`, so the shared `.gitignore` does not change with each contributor's files. Outside a git repository they go to the managed `.gitignore` block. `clean`, or a run with no local inputs left, removes the block.
- **Symlinked `.gitignore`.** Git does not read a `.gitignore` that is a symbolic link, and ai-rulez never writes through one: every ignore entry goes to `.git/info/exclude` instead.
- **Fail closed.** `generate` stops, listing the paths, when a machine-local or secret-bearing output, the overlay or the `local/` tree would not be ignored after the entries are written (for example because of a `!.ai-rulez/local/` line). Narrow the rule, or use `--no-local`.
- **Local manifest.** Local outputs are tracked in `.ai-rulez/.generated-manifest.local.json`, not in the committed manifest, so a teammate's `generate` never deletes your local files, and `clean`, or deleting the source under `.ai-rulez/local/` and regenerating, removes them. It also records what ai-rulez merged into settings documents shared with you.
- **Permissions.** The overlay, and every generated file holding a resolved MCP secret, is written `0600`.
- **Reserved names.** `*.local.*` in a rules folder is reserved; a hand-written file with such a name is skipped with a warning.

##### Settings documents shared with you

`.claude/settings.json`, `.gemini/settings.json`, `opencode.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.agents/settings.json` and `.xum/mcp.jsonc` can hold your settings beside what ai-rulez writes. For each document ai-rulez records the MCP servers, array elements and scalar keys it merged in, each with a digest of the value it wrote (never the value). Array elements are counted per value: if ai-rulez added one `Bash(git status)` rule, `clean` removes one, and an identical rule you wrote stays. A document ai-rulez wrote whole is recorded in the committed manifest; a document shared with you, or one carrying overlay content, in the local manifest.

`clean`, and `generate` once a preset, server or overlay entry is gone, take back exactly those entries while they still hold the value ai-rulez wrote; an entry you edited stays, with a warning. `generate --dry-run` lists these as `unmerge:` lines. The general ownership rules are in [Shared settings documents](settings.md#shared-settings-documents); what follows is specific to the local record.

- **No record** (a fresh clone, or a document merged before records existed). On `clean` only, ai-rulez removes what is identical to what it would write: a configured MCP server with the rendered value, the ai-rulez self entry, a `context.fileName` in one of its forms, `AGENTS.local.md` in `instructions`, and an OpenCode `$schema` that is the only key. A hand-written value that happens to be identical is removed too. A server dropped from the configuration before any run recorded it stays; delete it by hand.
- **Gemini `context.fileName`** is written whether or not local content exists, so Gemini loads `GEMINI.local.md` once it appears:

  | Your value | Result |
  | --- | --- |
  | One of ai-rulez's forms (`["AGENTS.md"]`, `["AGENTS.md", "GEMINI.local.md"]`, `["GEMINI.md", "GEMINI.local.md"]`) | Rewritten to the current form. |
  | Anything else | Kept (a string becomes a list); `GEMINI.local.md`, and `AGENTS.md` under `agents_md`, appended when missing. `clean` takes back only those names. |

  With `agents_md` off, a list without `GEMINI.md` gets a warning, because Gemini then ignores the generated file.
- **OpenCode.** `AGENTS.local.md` is appended to your `instructions` (`./AGENTS.local.md` counts as the same entry) and taken back by `clean`. `$schema` is written only into an `opencode.json` ai-rulez creates.
- **Comments (JSONC).** A document with comments or trailing commas is not rewritten. When only the `context.fileName` or `instructions` entry would be written, `generate` warns and the local file is not loaded until you add it by hand. When MCP servers must be written into such a document, `generate` stops with a hint. `clean` leaves it alone with a warning. `.xum/mcp.jsonc` is JSONC by definition: once you add a comment, the servers ai-rulez merged stay after `clean`, with a warning; remove them by hand.

##### Collisions

- A local rule with the name of a shared rule is allowed; its file is `<id>.local<ext>`, so nothing is overwritten.
- Two local rules that map to the same file name are written as `<id>-<hash>.local<ext>`.
- A local skill, agent or command with the name of a shared one fails `generate`, naming both files.

#### Config overlay

`config.local.toml` sits next to `config.toml` and is merged onto it in memory at load time, after every [layer](configuration.md#layered-configuration). It is never written into the shared configuration, and plugin bundles (`generate --plugin`) ignore it. In a [root `ai-rulez.toml` layout](config-without-folder.md) the overlay is `ai-rulez.local.toml`.

Create one with `ai-rulez local init`, or let `local set`, `--local` or the MCP `local: true` flag create it. The overlay is validated against `schema/ai-rules-local.schema.json` (see [Schema](schema.md)), and the merged result must be a valid configuration. Only TOML is read: a `config.local.yaml`, `.yml` or `.json` fails the load; see [Migrating to v5](migration-v5.md).

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.local.toml
presets = ["codex"]              # add codex on this machine
default = "dev"

[profiles]
dev = ["backend", "my-local-domain"]

[[mcp_servers]]
name = "github"                  # merges onto the shared "github" server
transport = "stdio"

[mcp_servers.env]
GITHUB_TOKEN = "${GITHUB_TOKEN}"   # see Environment references below

[[includes]]
name = "team-rules"
remove = true                    # drop a shared include on this machine
```

`${GITHUB_TOKEN}` resolves at `generate` time from `--env`, the environment or `.env`. A tool that expands references itself, such as a reader of `.mcp.json`, gets the reference `${GITHUB_TOKEN}` instead of the value; see [Environment references](configuration.md#environment-references).

!!! warning "Add presets, do not drop shared ones"
    The overlay is meant to add. Dropping a shared preset (`presets = ["!cursor"]`) currently deletes that preset's committed outputs (`.cursor/mcp.json`, ...) and rewrites the committed `.ai-rulez/.generated-manifest.json`; the [drift guard](#drift-guard) does not stop it. An added preset also records its MCP entries in the committed manifest. Do not commit those changes; restore them with `git checkout`, or run `generate --no-local` before committing.

##### Merge semantics

| Key kind | Keys | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scalars | `name`, `description`, `default`, `gitignore`, `compact`, `source`, `agents_md`, `codex_skills_dir`, ... | The local value wins. |
| Lists | Any list not named below (`skill_sources`, `bundle_exclude`, `skip_outputs`, `hooks`, the domain lists of `profiles`, ...) | The local list replaces the shared one. |
| Tables | `profiles`, `header`, `defaults`, `mcp`, `rules`, `claude`, `lint`, `lock`, `permissions`, `guard`, `session_start`, `role_manifest`, `delivery`, `placement`, `plugin`, `catalog`, `llm`, `verifiers_settings` | Merged per key, recursively; lists inside are replaced. A local value that is not a table (including `null`) is an error. |
| Other tables | `codex`, `domains`, `skills`, `okf`, `telemetry`, `usage`, `exposure`, `search`, ... | Merged per key, recursively; a local value that is not a table replaces the shared one. |
| `marketplace` | | Merged per key; `[[marketplace.plugins]]` merges entry by entry on `name`. |
| `presets` | | Ordered union: local entries are appended and duplicates collapse (a table beats a bare name; two tables merge, the local one winning). `"!name"` drops a shared preset. |
| Named lists | `mcp_servers`, `includes`, `installed_skills`, `installed_marketplaces`, `installed_plugins`, `plugins`, `marketplaces`, `scopes`, `roles`, `verifiers`, `plugins_authoring`, `marketplaces_authoring` | Entries merge by `name` (`scopes` by `path` when unnamed). A local entry with `remove = true` deletes the shared one; a new name is appended. |
| `builtins` | | The local value replaces the shared one. |
| `version` | | Must be a string equal to the shared version, if set. |
| `governance`, `signing`, `default_layers` | | Ignored with a warning: they are shared policy. |

Other rules:

- Unknown keys are an error. Error messages name keys and entry positions, never values.
- `validate` reports a literal credential in an MCP `env` or header value as `AR015`, in the overlay as in `config.toml`. Reference an environment variable (`"${GITHUB_TOKEN}"`) and keep the value in your shell or `.env`.
- Dropping a preset, or removing an entry, that the shared configuration does not have is a warning.
- `remove` is not valid on preset tables; use `"!name"`.
- Every named-list entry needs a `name` (a `scopes` entry a `name` or `path`). A duplicate local entry, or one that matches several shared entries, is an error.
- A local include or `local_override` may point outside the project; in the committed `config.toml` it may not. An overlay that is tracked by git gets the same check as `config.toml`, with a warning.
- The `[llm]` network and credential keys and the `[telemetry]` export keys are honored only from the user configuration, never from `config.toml` or the overlay. See the [trust model](trust-model.md).

#### Managing local configuration

##### `ai-rulez local`

| Command | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `local init` | Create a commented `config.local.toml` skeleton |
| `local show` | Print every key the overlay sets and the shared value it replaces (`--format json`, `--reveal`) |
| `local set <path> [value]` | Set a key (`--string`, `--stdin`) |
| `local unset <path>` | Remove a key |
| `local path` | Print the overlay path |

```bash
ai-rulez local set default dev
ai-rulez local set presets '["codex", "!cursor"]'
ai-rulez local set mcp_servers.github.command npx
printf %s "$TOKEN" | ai-rulez local set mcp_servers.github.env.GITHUB_TOKEN --stdin
ai-rulez local set 'mcp_servers["foo.bar"].command' npx
ai-rulez local show --format json
```

- **Values** are parsed as TOML literals, falling back to a plain string. Env and header values and text fields (`url`, `command`, `source`, `path`, `ref`, `description`, `name`, `transport`, `default`, `*_version`) are always strings. `--string` forces a string.
- **Secrets** go through `--stdin` (stored as a string), so they stay out of shell history.
- **Dotted names**: write a segment that contains a dot in brackets and double quotes, `mcp_servers["foo.bar"].command`.
- **Redaction**: `local show` prints values only for keys known to hold no credentials (`name`, `description`, `default`, `presets`, `gitignore`, `compact`, `builtins`, `profiles.*`, `defaults.effort*`, `defaults.omit_agent_fields`, `rules.mode*`, `header.style|hashes|timestamp`, `mcp.self_server`, `mcp.self_server_version`, and `transport`, `enabled`, `remove` of list entries), and only when the value has the expected type. Every other key shows `<redacted>`; `--reveal` prints everything.
- **Safety**: every write takes a file lock, writes the ignore entries first and validates the merged configuration; on failure the previous file is restored.
- The subcommands honour the global `--config` and `--config-dir`.

`profile list`, `include list` and `skill list` show the shared configuration and print how many entries the overlay adds; `local show` lists them.

##### `--local` on other commands

`--local` on CLI commands, and `local: true` on the MCP tools, send a change to the local layer:

| Target | Commands |
| --- | --- |
| `.ai-rulez/local/` | `add`, `remove`, `list`, `show` and `edit` of `rule`, `context`, `skill`, `agent`, `command` (create `local/checks/` files by hand) |
| Overlay | `profile add\|remove\|set-default`, `include add\|remove`, `skill install\|remove` |

```bash
ai-rulez add rule local-paths --local                   # .ai-rulez/local/rules/local-paths.md
ai-rulez add skill my-debug-skill --local
ai-rulez add rule team-notes --local --domain backend   # .ai-rulez/local/domains/backend/rules/
ai-rulez profile add dev backend my-local-domain --local
ai-rulez include add scratch ../scratch-rules --local
```

- `--local --domain <name>` writes to `.ai-rulez/local/domains/<name>/`; the local domain exists once it has content. `domain add|remove` and the MCP domain tools have no local form.
- Removing a shared include or installed skill with `--local` writes `remove = true` to the overlay. A shared profile cannot be removed locally.

#### Drift guard

The overlay can change files the team shares (an overlay MCP server adds an entry to `.mcp.json`, for example). To keep local values out of tracked files, `generate` also renders the shared view and classifies every output:

| Class | Meaning | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| local-only | Only the merged view produces the file | Written; kept out of git |
| drift | Both views produce the file, with different content | Written only if the file is git-ignored and untracked |
| suppressed | Only the shared view produces the file (the overlay dropped a preset or entry) | Removed, even when it is tracked (see the [warning](#config-overlay) on dropping presets) |

The run is blocked, writes nothing and exits non-zero when a drift file is tracked or not ignored, when a local-only file is tracked, or when git cannot say which files are tracked. The error names paths only, never content. `generate --dry-run` prints the plan and exits non-zero when it would be blocked:

```text
local-only: .claude/rules/scratch.local.md
drift: .mcp.json
allowed: .gemini/settings.json (drift, but git-ignored)
suppressed: .cursor/mcp.json
blocked: .mcp.json (shared output is tracked and would change)
```

Ways forward:

- Git-ignore the files, or untrack them.
- `generate --no-local` generates the shared view only, the one a teammate sees.
- `generate --allow-local-drift` writes anyway, which can put non-secret overlay values into tracked files. A generated MCP file that would carry a resolved secret is still refused unless it is git-ignored. The flag is CLI-only; the MCP server cannot bypass the guard.

If the shared view itself fails to render, the run fails: without it, local outputs cannot be told apart from shared ones. This happens, for example, when the overlay points a remote include at a local checkout while `ai-rulez.lock` is stale for it. `--allow-local-drift` skips lock enforcement for the includes the overlay replaces, with a warning, so you can try an include change from a local checkout before the lock is updated. Any other failure of the shared view needs a fix to the shared configuration, `ai-rulez lock`, or `--no-local`.

`Source-Hash` values in shared outputs come from the shared view, so a teammate regenerating sees no hash change; local-only outputs carry a hash of their local inputs, with the overlay entering it only in redacted form.

#### `--no-local`

`--no-local` ignores both layers. `generate`, `validate`, `scan`, `doctor`, `tokens`, `cost`, `catalog`, `config layers`, `roles`, `verifiers`, `review`, `llm` and the other commands that load the project accept it; `verify` always checks the shared view. A `--no-local` run neither deletes your local files nor removes their ignore entries. Use it in hooks and CI so results do not depend on one machine's overlay; see [Git hooks](poly-hooks.md).

#### Security notes

- The overlay and the local tree are written owner-only, and their ignore entries are written before the files; writers fail closed if the entries cannot be written.
- `local show` withholds values by default, and the MCP `read_config` tool returns the overlay's key paths only.
- The overlay enters generated headers only in redacted form: env and header values and arguments are replaced, and URLs lose their credentials, query and fragment.
- Do not use `--allow-local-drift` in shared scripts.

#### See also

- [Configuration reference](configuration.md#local-overlay)
- [CLI Commands](cli.md#local-configuration): `ai-rulez local` and `--local`
- [MCP Server](mcp-server.md): the `local` tool parameter
- [Rules](rules.md): rules mode and rule files

## Catalog

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/catalog/

`ai-rulez catalog` lists everything a project defines (rules, context, skills, agents, commands and checks) with
owner, version, token cost, lock digest, the roles that keep each item and its lint status. It prints a table, JSON
for tools, or a static website you can publish for reviewers. `ai-rulez catalog diff` compares two catalogs, for
example in a pull request.

#### Example

```text
$ ai-rulez catalog
KIND     DOMAIN  ID             OWNER  VERSION  TOKENS  ROLES
context  -       architecture   -      -        122     0
rule     -       code-quality   -      -        88      0
skill    -       ai-rulez       -      -        540     0
skill    -       code-reviewer  -      -        148     0

4 item(s), 0 role(s); lock: none
```

```text
$ ai-rulez catalog --html site/
wrote 14 files to site/ (4 items, 0 roles, 0 MCP servers)   catalog digest sha256:e5ed17e3...
lint: 0 errors, 0 warnings   lock: none
```

`OWNER` and `VERSION` come from the items' frontmatter; `ROLES` counts the [roles](roles.md) that keep the item.

#### JSON

```bash
ai-rulez catalog --format json                      # schema version 1 (default)
ai-rulez catalog --format json --schema-version 2
```

Version 1 ([`schema/catalog.v1.schema.json`](https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/blob/main/schema/catalog.v1.schema.json))
is the default and what the MCP `catalog` tool returns. Version 2
([`schema/catalog.schema.json`](https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/blob/main/schema/catalog.schema.json)) contains
every version 1 field plus:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `generated_by`, `project` | Tool name and version; project name, description and lock tree digest |
| `items[].ref` | Stable key `kind/domain/id` (domain `-` for root), such as `skill/-/code-reviewer`; a repeated key gets `#2`, `#3` |
| `items[].description` | From the frontmatter, verbatim (escape it when you render it) |
| `items[].source` | `{"type": "local"}` or `{"type": "include"}` |
| `items[].load_cost` | `listing_tokens` (what a harness always lists, such as a skill's name and description), `body_tokens` (loaded on use), `resource_tokens` and `resources` (bundled files) |
| `items[].lint` | `status` (`ok`, `warn`, `error`), counts and findings, from the same engine as `validate`; absent when lint could not run |
| `items[].excerpt` | First 2 KiB of the body as plain text; off with `--include-excerpt=false` |
| `items[].approval` | `null`, or `{required, status, reviewers, assurance, expires}`; see [Approvals](approvals.md) |
| `items[].eval`, `items[].usage` | With `--with-eval` / `--with-usage`; see [Eval and usage](#eval-and-usage) |
| `mcp_servers` | Each server's `ref`, `name`, `transport`, `command_basename`, `enabled`, `profiles`, `pinned`, and the names of its `env` and `headers` entries, marked `literal` or with the variable they reference; `warnings` flags an unpinned launch or a literal credential |
| `edges` | `{from, to, kind: "uses"}`: item `from` names skill `to` in its `skills:` frontmatter |
| `lint` | Project totals, counts per code, and findings no item owns |
| `notes` | Why a section is missing or narrowed |

A catalog never contains MCP arguments, URLs, env values or header values, which can hold secrets and internal
hostnames. Paths are relative to the configuration directory. A consumer should refuse a `schema_version` it does not
know.

```json
{
  "ref": "skill/-/code-reviewer",
  "kind": "skill",
  "id": "code-reviewer",
  "path": "skills/code-reviewer/SKILL.md",
  "description": "Specialized agent for code review and quality assurance",
  "delivery": "static",
  "source": {"type": "local"},
  "bytes": 685,
  "tokens": 148,
  "digest": "sha256:67cd967c...",
  "load_cost": {"listing_tokens": 13, "body_tokens": 148, "resource_tokens": 0, "resources": 0},
  "lint": {"status": "ok", "counts": {"error": 0, "warning": 0, "info": 0}, "findings": []},
  "approval": null,
  "roles": []
}
```

#### Eval and usage

```bash
ai-rulez catalog --format json --schema-version 2 --with-eval --with-usage
ai-rulez catalog --html site/ --with-eval=results/eval-results.json --with-usage=logs/usage.jsonl
```

Both are off by default. Without a value they read `eval-results.json` in the configuration directory (written by
[evals](evals.md)) and `local/usage.jsonl` (written by the [usage hooks](usage-telemetry.md)). A missing file is
noted in `notes` and the fields are omitted; a file that cannot be parsed is an error. To name a file literally
called `default`, write `./default`.

Only aggregates are copied:

- `eval`: `cases`, `pass_rate`, `passing`, `ablation_delta`, `trigger_precision`, `trigger_recall`, `stale` (the
  skill changed since the run), `verified` (signed by this machine's key) and `date`.
- `usage`: `invocations` and `last_seen` (a day). Sessions, harnesses, outcomes and feedback never enter the catalog.

Two skills that share an id cannot be told apart in the usage log, so their usage is left out (and said in `notes`).
The site gains Eval and Uses columns and per-item Eval and Usage tables.

#### Comparing catalogs

```bash
ai-rulez catalog diff main                         # a revision against the working tree
ai-rulez catalog diff v5.10.0 HEAD --format json
ai-rulez catalog diff before.json after.json --exit-code
```

```text
$ ai-rulez catalog diff HEAD
catalog diff: HEAD (404870d64340) -> working tree
totals: 4 -> 5 items   listing tokens 37 -> 37   body tokens 898 -> 901
items: 1 added, 0 removed, 0 changed
  + rule/-/naming   (3 tokens)
lint: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 infos -> 0 errors, 2 warnings, 1 infos
```
