The diff covers items (matched by `ref`; a change lists the fields that differ, such as digest, description, owner,
tokens, lint or approval status, roles), MCP servers, roles, dependency edges and lint totals. JSON output follows
[`schema/catalog-diff.schema.json`](https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/blob/main/schema/catalog-diff.schema.json).

Each argument is a catalog JSON file (version 2, or a site's `catalog.json`) or a git revision. With one argument the
other side is the working tree. A revision is read from git without touching your checkout, and both sides are built
from the shared configuration only:

- the machine-local overlay is left out;
- remote includes and installed skills are not resolved (no network), so compare two `catalog.json` files to cover
  them;
- untracked and ignored files are not part of a revision.

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Done (also when the catalogs differ, unless `--exit-code`) |
| `1` | The command could not run |
| `2` | With `--exit-code`: the catalogs differ |

#### Static website

```bash
ai-rulez catalog --html site/
ai-rulez catalog --html site/ --role backend --clean
```

The site has an overview (filter by name, domain, owner, kind and lint status), a page per item and per role, the
MCP servers, a dependency graph, the lock status, the lint findings, an About page, `catalog.json` (the version 2
document) and `robots.txt`.

- **Self-contained.** Links are relative, so it works from `file://` or any URL path. Nothing is fetched (no fonts,
  CDN or analytics), and every page works without JavaScript; the script only adds filtering, paging and copy
  buttons.
- **Reproducible.** The same input gives the same bytes. The footer shows the tool version and the SHA-256 of
  `catalog.json` instead of a date, so you can regenerate and compare to detect a tampered hosted copy.
- **Safe to render.** Every string is HTML-escaped; links are built from slugs, never from source text. Invisible
  and direction-changing characters are replaced with U+FFFD and the item is marked "contains hidden characters".
  Bodies are shown as plain text unless you enable [Markdown excerpts](#markdown-excerpts).
- **Strict Content-Security-Policy.** Each page carries `default-src 'none'; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self';
  script-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'`. Send the same as a response header from your host, plus
  `frame-ancestors 'none'`.
- **Protected output directory.** The directory must be new, empty, or hold the `.ai-rulez-catalog` marker an
  earlier run wrote. A directory with `.git` or `.ai-rulez` is always refused. `--clean` removes only files the
  marker lists that still hold the recorded bytes.
- **No secrets.** The run is refused when an item the site would publish has a secret finding (`AR001`) in its
  excerpt or description. Remove the secret, or pass `--allow-findings AR001`.

The dependency graph (`graph.html`) draws the items that name skills in their `skills:` frontmatter, left to right,
as a static SVG with the same edges listed in a table. A name resolves to the skill in the same domain, else the root
skill, else the only skill with that name; anything ambiguous or unresolved is left out and listed in `notes`. Above
150 items only the table is shown.

A published catalog exposes names, descriptions, owners, token costs and lint findings: publish it only where the
configuration itself may be read.

##### Freshness check

```bash
ai-rulez catalog --html site/ --check
```

Renders the site in memory and compares it with the directory, writing nothing:

```text
site/ differs from the catalog site that would be generated:
  unexpected  items/extra.html
run `ai-rulez catalog --html site/` to regenerate it
Error: catalog site is out of date
```

Exit `0` when the directory matches, `2` when a file is changed, missing or unexpected (or the directory does not
exist), `1` when the check could not run. Use it in CI to keep a committed site current. `--check` and `--clean`
cannot be combined.

##### Markdown excerpts

`--render-markdown` (or `render_markdown = true`) shows excerpts as formatted Markdown: paragraphs, headings (shifted
to `h3`-`h6`), lists, quotes, code, emphasis and rules. It stays safe:

- raw HTML is shown as text;
- links and images are not followed: the label or alt text is kept and the destination is shown as text;
- nesting and size are capped.

The excerpt is still the first 2 KiB of the body, so a long document may be cut mid-structure.

#### Configuration

```toml
[catalog]
title = "Acme catalog"       # site title (--base-title)
include_excerpt = true       # body excerpts (--include-excerpt)
exclude_owners = false       # leave owner names out (--no-owners)
indexable = false            # let search engines index the site (--indexable)
max_items_per_page = 200     # overview rows per page (--max-items-per-page)
render_markdown = false      # Markdown excerpts (--render-markdown)
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `AI-Rulez catalog` | Site title |
| `include_excerpt` | `true`, `false` when `indexable` | Include body excerpts (site and version 2 JSON) |
| `exclude_owners` | `false` | Leave owner names out of the site and version 2 JSON |
| `indexable` | `false` | Drop `robots.txt` and `noindex` |
| `max_items_per_page` | `200` (`0` means 200) | Rows per overview page; all rows stay in `index.html`, so find-in-page and the no-JavaScript view show everything |
| `render_markdown` | `false` | Render excerpts as Markdown |

Every key is optional; a flag overrides it. The table can also be set in `config.local.toml`.

#### Flags

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--format text\|json`, `--schema-version 1\|2` | Output format |
| `--html <dir>` | Write the site |
| `--role <name>` | With `--html`: only the items this role keeps |
| `--check`, `--clean` | With `--html`: compare without writing; remove files the site no longer has |
| `--base-title`, `--include-excerpt`, `--no-owners`, `--indexable`, `--max-items-per-page`, `--render-markdown` | See [Configuration](#configuration) |
| `--allow-findings <codes>` | With `--html`: publish despite these findings |
| `--with-eval[=FILE]`, `--with-usage[=FILE]` | Add eval and usage aggregates |
| `--no-local` | Ignore the machine-local overlay |

See the [CLI reference](cli-reference.md#ai-rulez-catalog).

## Monorepos

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/monorepo/

A large repository needs each agent to see the instructions for the code it is working on, and not much more.
ai-rulez gives you three tools, which you can combine:

| Tool | Use it when | What you get |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Domains and profiles](domains.md) | Teams or services share one repository and one configuration | One set of root files, with the content of the selected domains |
| [`[[scopes]]`](#scopes) | Packages need their own instructions, loaded when an agent works there | Root files plus `<package>/AGENTS.md`, `<package>/CLAUDE.md`, ... and path-scoped rule files |
| [Nested configurations](#nested-configurations) | Packages are owned separately and keep their own `.ai-rulez/` | One independent project per directory, generated with `--recursive` |

<p align="center">
  <img src="assets/monorepo.gif" alt="ai-rulez generate --recursive over two nested roots, recursive validation, and a token budget check" width="820" />
</p>

#### Example

A repository with shared rules, an `api` and a `web` domain, and one scope per package:

```text
.ai-rulez/
  config.toml
  rules/security.md                    # every package
  domains/api/rules/errors.md          # packages/api only
  domains/api/rules/go-style.md        # paths: ["**/*.go"]
  domains/web/rules/components.md      # packages/web only
packages/api/
packages/web/
```

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml
version = "5.0"
name = "acme"
presets = ["claude", "cursor", "codex"]

default = "api"

[profiles]
api = ["api"]
web = ["web"]

[[scopes]]
path = "packages/api"
profile = "api"                  # presets default to codex and claude

[[scopes]]
path = "packages/web"
profile = "web"
presets = ["claude", "cursor"]
```

`ai-rulez generate` writes:

```text
AGENTS.md                                  # root: security
CLAUDE.md                                  # @AGENTS.md
packages/api/AGENTS.md                     # errors, go-style
packages/api/CLAUDE.md                     # @AGENTS.md
packages/web/AGENTS.md                     # components
packages/web/CLAUDE.md
.claude/rules/packages-api/go-style.md     # paths: [packages/api/**/*.go]
...
```

Each scope file holds only the scope's own content: tools load a nested `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` on top of the root
file, so repeating the root rules would load them twice.

#### Domains and profiles

Put cross-cutting content (architecture, security, git workflow) at the root of `.ai-rulez/`, and team- or
service-specific content in `domains/<name>/`. A profile selects domains:

```toml
default = "full"

[profiles]
full = ["backend", "frontend", "qa"]
backend = ["backend", "qa"]
frontend = ["frontend", "qa"]
```

```bash
ai-rulez generate --profile backend      # root content plus backend and qa
```

See [Domains and profiles](domains.md) for the layout and [Roles](roles.md) to select content per kind of task
rather than per team.

#### Scopes

A `[[scopes]]` entry writes a second set of root files in a subdirectory, from its own profile:

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | | Label used in messages |
| `path` | required | Directory relative to the project root; no glob characters |
| `profile` | the active profile | Profile whose domains the scope renders |
| `presets` | `["codex", "claude"]` | Presets that write files in the scope |

A domain the root output already contains is not repeated in a scope, and a scope left with nothing writes no files.
See [`scopes`](configuration.md#scopes) for the full reference.

##### Scoped rule files

Root files (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md`, ...) are written in the scope directory, but rule files of a scope
go to the **root** rules folder, with the scope path as a qualifier and glob prefix. Not every tool reads a nested
rules folder (Copilot reads only the repository root), so this is the one placement that every preset with a rules
folder reads.

| Preset | Scoped rule file for `packages/api`, rule `style` |
| --- | --- |
| Claude | `.claude/rules/packages-api/style.md` |
| Cursor | `.cursor/rules/packages-api/style.mdc` |
| Copilot | `.github/instructions/packages-api/style.instructions.md` |
| Devin, Cline, Junie | `<rules dir>/packages-api--style.md` |
| Antigravity | `.agents/rules/packages-api--style.md` |

- Globs are relative to the scope: `paths: ["**/*.go"]` becomes `packages/api/**/*.go`, and a rule without globs
  (or with only negated globs) gets `packages/api/**`.
- A glob that leaves the scope with `..` skips that rule for the scope, with a warning.
- `auto` and `manual` rules keep their mode, so they are not limited to the scope; `generate` warns once per scope.
- With `[rules] mode = "inline"`, only path-scoped items move to the root folder; the rest stays in the scope's root
  file.
- Two rules that map to the same file get a `-<6 hex>` suffix with a warning (see [File names](rules.md#file-names)).
  Two scopes that produce the same qualifier (`packages/api` and `packages-api`) fail; rename one.

Limitations:

- Copilot (`.github/copilot-instructions.md`) and Junie read their root instruction file at the repository root
  only, so content left inline in a scope's copy never reaches them, and `generate` warns. Use path-scoped rules or
  `[rules] mode = "split"` for those presets.
- Custom presets whose rules output is not split keep a scope's rules in the scope directory, with a warning.

#### Nested configurations

When a package keeps its own `.ai-rulez/` (or `.agents/ai-rulez.toml`), it is an independent project. Process every
configuration below the current directory with `--recursive`:

```text
$ ai-rulez generate --recursive
...
✅ Total: Generated 18 file(s) from 2 config(s)

$ ai-rulez generate --check --recursive
[1/2] .ai-rulez/config.toml (47ms)
[2/2] services/billing/.ai-rulez/config.toml (42ms)
INFO  Generated files are up to date roots=2

$ ai-rulez validate --recursive
[2/2] services/billing/.ai-rulez/config.toml (79ms)
validation: no findings in 2 root(s)
```

```toml
# services/billing/.ai-rulez/config.toml
version = "5.0"
name = "billing"
presets = ["claude", "gemini"]
```

- Roots are processed concurrently, one worker per CPU. `generate --check --recursive` and `validate --recursive`
  report in path order, so output and exit code are the same on every run; `--quiet` and `--format json` silence
  the `[n/N]` progress lines.
- A root that authors a plugin or marketplace and configures no preset is built as a bundle, as
  `generate --plugin` would, and skipped by `generate --check --recursive`; check it with `verify --plugin`. See
  [Authoring plugins](plugins.md).
- Use `--debug` to see where time goes on a large repository.

##### The shared `.gitignore` block

With `gitignore = true`, a recursive run writes one managed block in the `.gitignore` at the top of each git
repository, holding the patterns of every root inside it (`svc/CLAUDE.md`, `svc/.claude/skills/`, ...).
`generate --recursive --check` verifies each block once.

- A nested directory with its own `.git` gets its own block; a repository whose root sets `gitignore = false` is
  never written for other roots.
- The root's own entries are unanchored (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`), so they also match nested roots' files.
- To commit generated files, list them in each root's [`gitignore_exclude`](configuration.md#gitignore_exclude),
  for example `gitignore_exclude = ["**/AGENTS.md", "**/CLAUDE.md", ".claude/"]`. Each root applies its list to its
  own outputs only.

#### Nested instructions over MCP

Packages often already hold `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, `.agents/` or `skills/`, and a harness loads them
only once it works in that directory. An agent planning at the root, or changing several packages, can ask the MCP
server what applies to a path:

```bash
ai-rulez mcp --serve-skills --discover-skills
```

`find_skill`, `find_context` and `load_context` then take a `path` or `scope`; the nearest scope wins a skill name.
The index reads the files that exist, so it needs no `generate` run. It is cached between runs
(`[mcp] index_cache`), refreshed while the server runs, and an agent can add a skill to a scope with `create_skill`
when `allow_write` is on. See:

- [Monorepos, scopes and nested context](mcp-server.md#monorepos-scopes-and-nested-context)
- [The index cache](mcp-server.md#the-index-cache)
- [Live refresh of the index](mcp-server.md#live-refresh-of-the-index)
- [Writing a skill into a scope](mcp-server.md#writing-a-skill-into-a-scope)

#### See also

- [AGENTS.md and .agents/skills](agents-md.md#scopes-local-files-and-hashes): what a scope's `AGENTS.md` contains per
  preset
- [Glob-scoped rules and AGENTS.md](rules.md#glob-scoped-rules-and-agentsmd)

## Supported harnesses

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/harnesses/

ai-rulez has 52 built-in presets, one per AI coding harness. A preset writes the harness's native layout: its file
names, frontmatter, directories and settings documents. List the presets you use in `config.toml`; for a harness that
is not listed, write a [provider-backed custom preset](configuration.md#provider-backed-presets-full-parity).

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml
presets = ["claude", "cursor", "codex", "gemini"]
```

```bash
ai-rulez generate
```

With one path-scoped rule, one always-on rule, a skill, an agent, a command and an MCP server, those four presets
write:

```text
AGENTS.md                         # every rule for codex and gemini (the path-scoped one inlined); imported by CLAUDE.md
CLAUDE.md                         # @AGENTS.md
.mcp.json                         # MCP servers (Claude Code reads the root file)
.claude/settings.json             # the default [session_start] hook
.claude/rules/api.md              # path-scoped rule
.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md
.claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md      # the command, as a user-invocable skill
.claude/agents/reviewer.md
.cursor/rules/api.mdc
.cursor/commands/ship.md
.cursor/agents/reviewer.md
.cursor/mcp.json
.agents/skills/deploy/SKILL.md    # shared by codex, cursor and gemini
.agents/skills/ship/SKILL.md      # the command, as a codex skill
.agents/skills/ship/agents/openai.yaml
.codex/agents/reviewer.toml
.codex/config.toml                # MCP servers
.gemini/agents/reviewer.md
.gemini/settings.json             # MCP servers
```

Codex and Gemini CLI have no rules folder, so the path-scoped rule is also inlined into `AGENTS.md`, which Claude
Code and Cursor read too; `generate` warns about it and suggests `[rules] scoped_fallback = "skill"`.

`ai-rulez init` lists every built-in preset in a comment of the new `config.toml`. Three more preset names are
not harnesses: `mcp` (only the root `.mcp.json`), [`okf`](okf.md) and [`llms-txt`](llms-txt.md).

#### Feature matrix

`yes` means the preset writes that output at project level, `-` that it does not (the reason is under
[Skipped features](#skipped-features)).

- **Rules**: a native rules folder. `-` means rules are inlined into the root instructions file (`letta` has none,
  so it gets no rules).
- **Commands**: slash commands. Where the harness has no command folder, a command is written as a skill (`claude`,
  `codex`, `antigravity`, `devin`, `warp`) or as a prompt or workflow file (`copilot`, `pi`, `cline`, `kiro`).
- **Hooks** and **Perms**: `yes` renders into a project file; `user` renders only with
  [`generate --user`](user-scope.md), because the harness reads them from the user configuration only. See
  [Hooks and settings](settings.md) and [Permissions](permissions.md).
- **Checks**: [code-review guidelines](checks.md).
- `copilot-cli` permissions cover only `WebFetch` URL rules, and `gitlab-duo` hooks only the `SessionStart` event.
- **User**: supported by `generate --user`; see [User-level configuration](user-scope.md#where-things-go).

#### What each preset writes

The paths below are the project-level outputs with the default `agents_md = true`: always-on rules and context go
into one shared `AGENTS.md` and skills into one shared `.agents/skills/`, which every preset that reads them uses
instead of its own copy (see [AGENTS.md and .agents/skills](agents-md.md)). `<id>` is the item's name. Every project
also gets the root `.mcp.json`, whatever its presets: it carries the ai-rulez MCP server
([`[mcp] self_server`](configuration.md#mcp), on by default) and any servers you declare.

(`.augment/code_review_guidelines.yaml`), `cursor` (`.cursor/BUGBOT.md`), `factory`
(`.factory/skills/review-guidelines/SKILL.md`), `gitlab-duo` (`.gitlab/duo/mr-review-instructions.yaml`), `kilo`
(`REVIEW.md`), `qwen` (`.qwen/review-rules.md`) and `rovodev` (`.rovodev/.review-agent.md`).

User-level paths are listed in [User-level configuration](user-scope.md#where-things-go).

#### Cross-cutting behavior

- **Shared outputs.** Presets that write the same path (`AGENTS.md`, `.agents/skills/`, the root `.mcp.json`) must
  render identical bytes. `generate` fails and names the presets when they diverge. See
  [AGENTS.md and .agents/skills](agents-md.md).
- **Merged documents.** Settings files that also hold your own keys (`.claude/settings.json`, `opencode.json`,
  `.codex/config.toml`, `.qwen/settings.json`, ...) are merged, not replaced: ai-rulez owns only the keys, array
  elements and map members it writes, and comments in JSONC, TOML and YAML survive. See
  [Settings document merge behavior](configuration.md#settings-document-merge-behavior).
- **External plugins.** `[[enabled_plugins]]` enables a plugin from another marketplace for `claude`
  (`enabledPlugins`, `extraKnownMarketplaces`), `codex` (`[plugins."<id>"]`) and `opencode` (the `plugin` array).
  The other presets have no equivalent and skip it. See
  [Enable a plugin from another marketplace](plugins.md#enable-a-plugin-from-another-marketplace).
- **MCP environment references.** Where the harness expands `${VAR}`-style references itself, the reference is
  written instead of the secret. See [Environment references](configuration.md#environment-references).
- **Built-in names.** A skill, command or agent named like a harness built-in replaces it, is renamed, or is
  unreachable, depending on the harness. `validate` checks every output against the harnesses that load it,
  including those that only read a shared directory such as `.agents/skills/`: AR9U0 for a built-in name, AR9U1
  for a name the harness refuses to load. See
  [Built-in names of harnesses](strict-validation.md#built-in-names-of-harnesses).
- **Tool and model names.** Frontmatter tool names are translated to each harness's own names, and bare Claude model
  aliases (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`) are dropped where the harness has no such model.

#### Skipped features

A `-` in the matrix is a deliberate skip: ai-rulez does not approximate a format the harness does not document.

##### Instructions, rules, skills and agents

| Preset | Skipped | Reason |
| ------ | ------- | ------ |
| `aiassistant` | root file | AI Assistant has no root instructions file; every rule and context item becomes a `.aiassistant/rules/` file |
| `amp` | agents | Amp has no agent file of its own and does not read the `.agents/agents` format |
| `baz` | rules folder, commands, MCP | Baz reads only instruction files from the default branch; it ignores `.claude/commands` and does not read `.claude/rules`. See [Baz](baz.md) |
| `bob` | agents | Bob's modes live in an aggregated `custom_modes.yaml`, not in one file per agent |
| `codebuff` | rules, agents, commands | Codebuff documents only `AGENTS.md`, skills and MCP |
| `codewhale` | agents | Subagents are TOML profiles whose strict schema the preset cannot produce |
| `crush` | rules folder, agents, commands | Crush has no rules folder, agent or command format |
| `cline` | MCP | Cline has no project MCP file |
| `cortex` | rules folder, MCP | Cortex reads only `AGENTS.md`; MCP servers live in `~/.snowflake/cortex/mcp.json` |
| `dsh` | MCP | Servers live in the home-level `cordis.patch.yml` |
| `gemini` | rules folder, commands | Rules stay in the root file; project commands are not generated (see the [plugin runtime](plugins.md) for `commands/<name>.toml`) |
| `gitlab-duo` | skills, rules folder | GitLab documents skills only inside plugins; Duo CLI reads one rules file, `.gitlab/duo/chat-rules.md` |
| `goose` | rules folder, commands | goose has no rules folder, and recipes are not slash commands |
| `hermes` | skills | Skills come only from the shared `.agents/skills` that `agents_md = true` writes |
| `letta` | rules, MCP | Letta documents no instructions, rules or MCP file a project can use |
| `muse` | MCP | MCP servers live only in the user `settings.json` |
| `openclaw` | everything but the root file | Only `AGENTS.md` is written |
| `poolside` | agents | Subagents are entries of the settings file, which the preset does not generate |
| `replit` | rules, agents, commands, MCP | Replit reads `replit.md` and `.agents/skills` only |
| `rovodev` | commands, MCP | Saved prompts need a `prompts.yml` manifest; `.rovodev/mcp.json` is inert until `config.yml` points at it |
| `takt` | MCP | Takt keeps MCP definitions inside workflow YAML |
| `trae` | root file | Trae has no root instructions file |
| `vibe` | agents | A Vibe agent is a TOML profile plus a separate prompt file |
| `xum` | commands | Xum documents no slash-command file |
| `zoocode` | agents | Custom modes are one aggregated `.roomodes` file |
| `zed` | agents, commands, rules folder | Zed has no rules folder, subagent or command format; rules go to the root file |
| `amp`, `codex`, `commandcode`, `deepagents`, `dsh`, `factory`, `hermes`, `kimi`, `mimocode`, `muse`, `opencode`, `pi`, `poolside`, `reasonix`, `rovodev`, `vibe`, `warp`, `xum`, `zcode`, `zoocode` | rules folder | The harness has no rules folder (or one it does not auto-load); rules are inlined into the root file |
| `aiassistant`, `dsh`, `gitlab-duo`, `hermes`, `muse`, `trae`, `warp` | agents | The harness documents no agent file |
| `aiassistant`, `amp`, `copilot-cli`, `cortex`, `deepagents`, `dsh`, `hermes`, `kimi`, `muse`, `poolside`, `trae`, `vibe` | commands | The harness documents no command file |
| `hermes` | MCP | The harness documents no project MCP file |

##### Hooks

Sixteen presets generate no `[[hooks]]`: `aiassistant`, `baz`, `codebuff`, `codewhale`, `dsh`, `muse`, `omp`,
`openclaw`, `replit`, `rovodev`, `takt`, `trae`, `warp`, `xum`, `zed` and `zoocode`. `generate` names them in one
warning. `junie`, `zcode`, `hermes` and `kimi` read hooks from the user configuration only, so they get hooks from
`generate --user`. Events, matchers and timeouts per harness are in
[Hooks and settings](settings.md#more-settings-file-harnesses).

##### Permissions

The harnesses without a documented, committable permission file that can hold the rules get nothing from
`[permissions]`, and `generate` names them in a warning. The reasons are in [Permissions](permissions.md#not-translated).
`zed`, `hermes` and `kimi` read permissions from the user configuration only.

##### User scope

`aiassistant`, `baz`, `codebuff`, `replit` and `xum` have no documented user-level location for anything
`generate --user` writes, so they are reported and skipped. User-level MCP servers are never generated.

## Custom presets

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/profiles/

`presets` in `.ai-rulez/config.toml` lists the tools ai-rulez generates for. Most projects use only built-in presets
(`claude`, `cursor`, `copilot`, `codex`, `gemini`, ...; all 52 are listed in [Supported harnesses](harnesses.md)). A
custom preset writes your rules to a file or folder of your choice, for a tool or a document ai-rulez does not ship.

Looking for profiles (named sets of domains)? See [Domains and profiles](domains.md).

#### Example

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml
presets = [
  "claude",
  "cursor",
  { name = "review-bot", type = "markdown", path = "docs/REVIEW_BOT.md", template = """
# {{ .Name }} conventions
{{ range .Rules }}
## {{ .Name }}{{ if .Priority }} ({{ .Priority }}){{ end }}

{{ .Content }}
{{ end }}""" },
  { name = "rules-dir", type = "directory", path = ".mytool/rules" },
  { name = "rules-json", type = "json", path = "build/rules.json" },
]
```

With two rules, `commit-messages` (`priority: high`) and `typescript` (`priority: medium`), `ai-rulez generate`
writes the built-in outputs plus:

```markdown
<!-- docs/REVIEW_BOT.md -->
# acme conventions

## commit-messages (high)

Use Conventional Commits.


## typescript (medium)

No `any`.
```

```text
.mytool/rules/
├── commit-messages.md
└── typescript.md
```

`build/rules.json`:

```json
{
  "Context": [],
  "Description": "",
  "Domains": {},
  "Name": "acme",
  "Rules": [
    { "Content": "Use Conventional Commits.\n", "Name": "commit-messages", "Priority": "high" },
    { "Content": "No `any`.\n", "Name": "typescript", "Priority": "medium" }
  ],
  "Skills": [],
  "Version": "5.0"
}
```

#### Preset keys

A custom preset is an inline table in the `presets` array, mixed freely with built-in names. A config with only
custom presets can also use `[[presets]]` tables.

| Key        | Type   | Meaning                                                                                  |
| ---------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`     | string | required; identifies the preset in messages; a template can match it against a rule's `Targets` |
| `type`     | string | `markdown`, `directory` or `json`                                                        |
| `path`     | string | output file (`markdown`, `json`) or folder (`directory`), relative to the project root   |
| `template` | string | optional Go template for `markdown` and `json`; see [Templates](#templates)              |
| `provider` | string | path to a provider spec instead of `type` and `path`; see below                          |

`path` must stay inside the project; see [Output paths](#output-paths).

!!! note "For a full tool, use a provider spec"
    The `markdown`, `directory` and `json` types render rules and context only. If the tool needs skills, agents,
    commands, per-file frontmatter, model or effort settings, or an MCP file, the same feature set as a built-in
    preset, point `provider = "..."` at a declarative provider spec instead. See
    [Provider-backed presets](configuration.md#provider-backed-presets-full-parity).

#### Preset types

| Type        | Writes                                                                                              |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `markdown`  | one file at `path`. Without a `template`: a title, the project description, and the rule, context and skill sections. |
| `directory` | one `<id>.md` file per rule in the folder `path`, with a `# <id>` heading and the priority line. Only rules are written. |
| `json`      | one file at `path`. Without a `template`: the [template data](#template-data) as indented JSON.      |

```toml
[[presets]]
name = "dev-guide"
type = "markdown"
path = "docs/AI_DEVELOPMENT_GUIDE.md"
```

#### Templates

`markdown` and `json` presets take a `template` in Go's [`text/template`](https://pkg.go.dev/text/template) syntax.
Only the built-in template functions are available (`len`, `printf`, `eq`, `index`, `and`, `or`, `not`, ...) and the
actions `range`, `if` and `with`. Any other function fails the run:

```text
Error: generate presets: generate preset review-bot: parse template: template: custom:1: function "now" not defined
```

##### Template data

| Field          | Contents                                                                  |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.Name`        | project name                                                              |
| `.Description` | project description                                                       |
| `.Version`     | config version                                                            |
| `.Rules`       | rules of the active profile, root and domains together, in priority order |
| `.Context`     | context files, likewise                                                   |
| `.Skills`      | skills, likewise                                                          |
| `.Domains`     | map of domain name to `{ Name, Rules, Context, Skills }`                  |

Each rule and context entry has `Name` and `Content`, plus `Priority` and `Targets` when the frontmatter sets them
(`Priority` is left out with `compact = true`). A skill entry also has `Body` (the instructions only), `Resources`
(each with `Kind`, `RelPath`, `Content`, `Description`) and its other frontmatter keys; its `Content` includes the
inlined reference files.

#### Output paths

The same rules apply to every output path a configuration names: a custom preset `path`, a provider spec's
`root.file`, `outputs.*.dir`, `sidecars[].path` and `directories`, `okf.dir`, `marketplace.output_dir` and
`codex_skills_dir`. `validate` and `generate` reject:

- an empty, absolute or drive- or UNC-prefixed path, and any `..` segment;
- a `.git` segment anywhere in the path (including the Windows spellings `.git.` and `git~1`);
- a path under `.ai-rulez/`, `.config/ai-rulez/`, `.hg/` or `.svn/`.

A preset may write a file that CI or a developer tool runs (`.github/workflows/`, `Makefile`, `.vscode/tasks.json`);
the `generate` summary lists it as `exec-file` before writing.

#### Ordering

Rules and context are ordered by priority (`critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `minimal`), then by name. Set
`priority` in a rule's frontmatter to move it.

#### Targeting content at a preset

Frontmatter [`targets`](rules.md#targets) limits a rule to some outputs of the built-in presets. The `markdown`,
`directory` and `json` presets do not apply it: they receive every rule of the active profile. A template can filter
on the `Targets` field itself:

```text
{{ range .Rules }}{{ $bot := false }}{{ range .Targets }}{{ if eq . "review-bot" }}{{ $bot = true }}{{ end }}{{ end }}
{{ if or (not .Targets) $bot }}## {{ .Name }}

{{ .Content }}{{ end }}{{ end }}
```

#### Built-in presets and rules folders

Under the default `[rules] mode = "split"`, built-in presets with a rules folder (`.claude/rules/`,
`.cursor/rules/`, `.github/instructions/`, ...) get one file per rule, and with `agents_md = true` (the default) the
always-on rules go to the shared `AGENTS.md`. See [Rules](rules.md#rules-mode) for each preset in each mode, and
[AGENTS.md and .agents/skills](agents-md.md).

`mcp` is a utility preset that writes the generic `.mcp.json`. It runs automatically when MCP servers are
configured; you do not need to list it.

#### Troubleshooting

| Symptom                                   | Cause and fix                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `function "..." not defined`              | The template uses a function that is not a Go built-in. Rewrite it with `range`/`if`. |
| `has an unsafe 'path'`                    | `path` leaves the project or points into a control directory; see [Output paths](#output-paths). |
| The output is missing a rule              | The rule's domain is not in the active profile, or the template filters it out.     |
| A warning that hooks are not generated    | Custom presets have no hook support; hooks are written for built-in presets only.    |

## AGENTS.md and .agents/skills

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/agents-md/

`AGENTS.md` and `.agents/skills/` are the cross-tool conventions for project instructions and
[Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io). With `agents_md = true` (the default), ai-rulez writes them once and every
preset that reads them stops writing its own copy: Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, Devin and the others read the
shared files, and `CLAUDE.md` becomes a one-line import of `AGENTS.md`.

```toml
agents_md = true    # the default
# agents_md = false # every preset writes its own files
```

To keep `AGENTS.md` as your own source file instead of ai-rulez output, see [.agents as a source](agents-source.md).
To write `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` by hand and keep ai-rulez away from them, use
[`skip_outputs`](configuration.md#skip_outputs) (`"agents_md"`, `"claude_md"` or `"instructions"`).

#### Example

```toml
version = "5.0"
name = "acme"
presets = ["claude", "codex", "cursor", "gemini", "copilot"]
```

With an always-on rule `security`, a rule `go-style` with `paths: ["**/*.go"]`, a skill `release` and an agent
`reviewer`, `generate` writes:

```text
AGENTS.md                                     # security, and go-style with an "Applies to" line
CLAUDE.md                                     # banner + @AGENTS.md
.agents/skills/release/SKILL.md               # shared skills tree
.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md               # Claude Code does not read .agents/skills
.claude/rules/go-style.md
.cursor/rules/go-style.mdc
.github/instructions/go-style.instructions.md
.gemini/settings.json                         # context.fileName: ["AGENTS.md", "GEMINI.local.md"]
.claude/agents/reviewer.md
.codex/agents/reviewer.toml
.cursor/agents/reviewer.md
.gemini/agents/reviewer.md
.github/agents/reviewer.agent.md
.mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .vscode/mcp.json, .codex/config.toml, .claude/settings.json
```

No `GEMINI.md`, no `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, no `.github/skills/` and no `.claude/rules/security.md`: those
tools get the content from `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/skills`. With `agents_md = false` the same project writes 24
files instead of 18.

```markdown
<!-- CLAUDE.md, after the generated banner -->
@AGENTS.md
```

#### What changes

- Always-on rules and context go into one `AGENTS.md`, plus `<scope>/AGENTS.md` for each [`[[scopes]]`](monorepo.md#scopes)
  entry.
- Skills without `targets` go into one `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` tree (see [Skills](#skills)).
- Presets that read the shared files stop writing their own root file (`GEMINI.md`, `.hermes.md`,
  `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, ...), their copy of `AGENTS.md` and their own skills folder.
- Commands that `codex`, `antigravity`, `devin` and `warp` run as skills go to the shared tree as user-invocable
  skills (`disable-model-invocation: true`, plus `agents/openai.yaml` for Codex), unless a skill has the same id. A
  command with `targets` stays in each targeted preset's own skills folder.
- Everything else stays per preset: path-scoped rule folders, agents, other commands, MCP files and settings.

#### Tool support

`V` verified against official docs or source, `P` partial or experimental, `N` not supported, `?` not verified. The
last two rows are tools that matter because they can shadow `AGENTS.md`. Tool behavior changes quickly; re-check a
cell before relying on it.

| Tool                       | Root `AGENTS.md`                                                  | Nested `AGENTS.md`                                          | Precedence and double-loading                                                                                                                                  | `.agents/rules` | `.agents/skills`                                                     | Agents, commands                                   |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code                | P, recent versions only, and only when no `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` or `CLAUDE.local.md` exists in cwd or an ancestor | V lazily, when a file in a subdirectory without any `CLAUDE.md` is read | `@AGENTS.md` import in `CLAUDE.md` never loads twice. `CLAUDE.local.md` suppresses `AGENTS.md` unless the user-level `instructionFiles` setting is `claude-md-and-agents-md`. Reads `.claude/AGENTS.md`, not `AGENTS.local.md` | N               | N (`.claude/skills`)                                                 | N (`.claude/agents`, `.claude/commands`)           |
| Codex CLI                  | V                                                                 | V project root down to cwd only; no lazy loading below cwd  | Per directory first of `AGENTS.override.md`, `AGENTS.md`, fallback names; concatenated root-down; `project_doc_max_bytes` 32 KiB                               | N               | V repo-local, cwd up to repo root; `~/.agents/skills`                | ? (`.codex/agents/*.toml`)                         |
| Cursor                     | V                                                                 | V any subdirectory, more specific wins                      | ? Docs call `AGENTS.md` an alternative to `.cursor/rules`; co-presence and deduplication not documented                                                         | N               | V `.agents/skills`, `.cursor/skills`, nested ones anywhere           | V `.cursor/agents`, `.claude/agents`, `.codex/agents`; no `.agents/agents` |
| Copilot cloud agent, CLI   | V                                                                 | V nearest file in the tree takes precedence                 | Cloud agent: all relevant instruction sets are provided, no deduplication. CLI: removes duplicate copies of identical instructions, defines no general precedence | N               | V `.github/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.agents/skills`               | ? (`.github/agents`)                               |
| Copilot in VS Code         | V chat and agent                                                  | P experimental `chat.useNestedAgentsMdFiles`                | Additive. `CLAUDE.md` needs `chat.useClaudeMdFile`                                                                                                              | N               | V same three locations                                               | ?                                                  |
| Devin                      | V always-on rule; `agents.md` also recognized                     | V subdirectory file is a glob rule `<dir>/**`               | Same rules engine as `.devin/rules`                                                                                                                            | N               | V `.agents/skills`, native `.devin/skills`                          | ? workflows                                        |
| Gemini CLI                 | N by default: reads only `GEMINI.md` unless `context.fileName` lists more | V for configured names, hierarchical and on file access | Only names in `context.fileName` load (`.gemini/settings.json`); `@file.md` imports work in `GEMINI.md`                                                          | N               | V `.agents/skills` beats `.gemini/skills` within a tier              | N (`.gemini/agents`, `.gemini/commands` only)      |
| Antigravity                | V                                                                 | V `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md` or `.agents/rules/` in any subdirectory | Cumulative; directory level wins on conflict. 24 KB per file, 20k tokens in aggregate                                                                          | V any directory level, immediate `.md` children only, `trigger` frontmatter | V `<workspace>/.agents/skills`; legacy `.agent/skills`               | ? workflows are being superseded by skills         |
| Junie                      | V                                                                 | ? not documented                                            | `.junie/AGENTS.md` first; else `AGENTS.md` + `.junie/rules/*.md`; else legacy `.junie/guidelines.md`; identical content deduplicated                           | N               | V `.junie/skills`, `.agents/skills`                                  | ?                                                  |
| Cline                      | V                                                                 | ? shipped code reads the root file only                     | Listed beside `.clinerules`, `.cursorrules`; per-file toggles                                                                                                  | N               | V in code (`.agents/skills`); docs list only `.cline/skills` and others | N                                                  |
| opencode                   | V                                                                 | V lazily, nearest file per read                             | Finds the first existing of `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTEXT.md` and stacks every ancestor copy of it                                                         | N               | V `.agents/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.opencode/skills`             | N (`.opencode`)                                    |
| Amp                        | V                                                                 | V when the agent reads a file in the subtree                | Per directory `AGENTS.md`, else `AGENT.md`, else `CLAUDE.md`                                                                                                    | N               | V `.agents/skills` in project and parents                            | ?                                                  |
| xum                        | V                                                                 | V                                                           | `AGENTS.md` > `AGENT.md` > `CLAUDE.md`; also `AGENTS.local.md`                                                                                                  | N               | ?                                                                    | ?                                                  |
