## Permissions

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/permissions/

`[permissions]` is one allow / ask / deny list for every harness that has a native permission file. You write Claude
Code permission rules once in `.ai-rulez/config.toml`, and `ai-rulez generate` translates them into each harness's
own file and format. A rule a harness cannot express exactly is skipped with a warning, never widened.

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml
presets = ["claude", "codex", "cursor"]

[permissions]
allow = ["Bash(git status)", "Bash(npm run test:*)"]
ask   = ["Bash(git push:*)"]
deny  = ["Read(./.env)", "Bash(rm -rf:*)"]
```

`generate` writes the rules verbatim for Claude Code:

```json
// .claude/settings.json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Bash(git status)",
      "Bash(npm run test:*)"
    ],
    "ask": [
      "Bash(git push:*)"
    ],
    "deny": [
      "Read(./.env)",
      "Bash(rm -rf:*)"
    ]
  }
}
```

Codex rules match command prefixes, so the exact-command allow and the path deny are left out:

```text
# .codex/rules/ai-rulez.rules
# Generated by ai-rulez from [permissions]. Do not edit; change .ai-rulez/config.toml and regenerate.
...
prefix_rule(
    pattern = ["npm","run","test"],
    decision = "allow",
)

prefix_rule(
    pattern = ["git","push"],
    decision = "prompt",
)

prefix_rule(
    pattern = ["rm","-rf"],
    decision = "forbidden",
)
```

Cursor's `Shell()` rules take one command name, so neither allow fits, and Cursor has no ask list:

```json
// .cursor/cli.json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [],
    "deny": [
      "Read(.env)",
      "Shell(rm:-rf*)"
    ]
  }
}
```

Every skipped rule is reported:

```text
WARN  [permissions] allow rule "Bash(git status)" not generated for codex: Codex rules match a token prefix, so an exact-command allow would be widened
WARN  SECURITY: [permissions] deny rule "Read(./.env)" is NOT enforced by codex: Codex has no rule surface for Read (paths, domains and MCP tools need a permission profile, which replaces sandbox_mode) severity=error hint=enforce it another way (sandbox, hook) or remove the harness from the project
WARN  [permissions] ask rules are not generated for cursor: it has no ask list and prompts for whatever is not allowed
WARN  [permissions] allow rule "Bash(git status)" not generated for cursor: Cursor's Shell() rules take a command name; a multi-word, exact or wildcard allow cannot be expressed without widening it
WARN  [permissions] allow rule "Bash(npm run test:*)" not generated for cursor: Cursor's Shell() rules take a command name; a multi-word, exact or wildcard allow cannot be expressed without widening it
```

Run `ai-rulez generate --dry-run` to see the warnings without writing files.

#### Rule syntax

A rule is `Tool` or `Tool(specifier)`, as in Claude Code:

| Rule | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Bash`, `Read`, `Edit`, `WebFetch` | every call of the tool |
| `Bash(npm run test:*)` | a command and any arguments; `:*` is the legacy form of `npm run test *` |
| `Bash(git status)` | exactly that command |
| `Bash(git * --force)` | a command glob |
| `Read(./.env)`, `Edit(src/**)`, `Write(dist/**)` | a path glob: `./x` or `x` is relative to the working directory, `/x` to the project root, `//x` is absolute, `~/x` is in the home directory |
| `WebFetch(domain:example.com)` | a host |
| `mcp__github__create_issue`, `mcp__github` | an MCP tool, or every tool of a server |
| `Task(Explore)` | a subagent |

Every translator uses the same parser, so a rule means the same thing everywhere. A rule that does not parse is
skipped with a warning.

`validate` reports an allow rule that permits every call of a tool (`Bash`, `Bash(*)`, `*`, `WebFetch`) as `AR506
permission-overbroad`. Deny and ask lists are not checked. ai-rulez does not evaluate rules; the harness does (Claude
Code applies deny over ask over allow).

#### What a translation guarantees

- **A rule is never widened.** When a harness cannot express an allow exactly (it matches command prefixes where you
  wrote an exact command, one `edit` permission covers every edit tool, `?` is a wildcard where Claude Code treats it as
  a literal), the allow is skipped with a warning.
- **A deny is never lost silently.** A deny a harness cannot enforce is reported as
  `SECURITY: [permissions] deny rule "..." is NOT enforced by <harness>: <why>`. A preset with no permission file at
  all is named in one warning. Enforce such rules another way (a sandbox, a hook) or leave the harness out.
- **Ask rules** are written where the harness has an ask list. Where it prompts for everything that is not allowed, ask
  rules are not written and one warning says so.
- **Your own rules survive.** Array entries and map members are owned one by one, and comments in JSONC, TOML and YAML
  stay. Removing a rule from `config.toml` removes exactly that entry on the next `generate`; `clean` takes back what
  `generate` wrote. A rule you wrote that equals a configured one stays yours on `clean`. A setting you already have
  with another value is kept, with a warning, so a rule of yours is never relaxed.
- **Project-wide only.** A `[[scopes]]` subdirectory renders no permissions.

#### Harnesses

"Rules" lists what each harness can express; everything else is skipped as described above.

| Harness | File | Format | Allow / ask / deny | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `claude` | `.claude/settings.json` | JSON | yes / yes / yes | all (verbatim) |
| `codex` | `.codex/rules/ai-rulez.rules` | Starlark | yes / `prompt` / `forbidden` | command prefixes only |
| `opencode` | `opencode.json` | JSONC | yes / yes / yes | commands, read, edit, webfetch, websearch, task |
| `kilo` | `kilo.jsonc` | JSONC | yes / yes / yes | as `opencode` |
| `mimocode` | `.mimocode/mimocode.jsonc` | JSONC | yes / yes / yes | as `opencode` |
| `gemini` | `.gemini/settings.json` | JSON | yes / no / yes | command prefixes; whole tools |
| `cursor` | `.cursor/cli.json` | JSON | yes / no / yes | commands, read, write, webfetch, mcp |
| `copilot` | `.vscode/settings.json` | JSONC | yes / yes / prompt only | commands, edits, urls |
| `copilot-cli` | `.github/copilot/settings.json` | JSONC | yes / no / yes | URLs only |
| `zoocode` | `.vscode/settings.json` | JSONC | yes / no / yes | command prefixes |
| `devin` | `.devin/config.json` | JSONC | yes / yes / yes | commands, read, write, fetch, mcp |
| `qwen` | `.qwen/settings.json` | JSON | yes / yes / yes | Claude syntax |
| `codebuddy` | `.codebuddy/settings.json` | JSON | yes / yes / yes | Claude syntax |
| `commandcode` | `.commandcode/settings.json` | JSON | yes / yes / yes | Claude syntax (`Shell`) |
| `qoder` | `.qoder/settings.json` | JSON | yes / yes / yes | Claude syntax, no WebFetch |
| `letta` | `.letta/settings.json` | JSON | yes / `alwaysAsk` / yes | Bash, Read, Edit |
| `grok` | `.grok/config.toml` | TOML | yes / yes / yes | commands, read, edit, mcp, whole web tools |
| `vibe` | `.vibe/config.toml` | TOML | yes / no / yes | command prefixes; deny of read and edit paths; whole-tool deny |
| `poolside` | `.poolside/settings.yaml` | YAML | yes / no / yes | commands, paths |
| `omp` | `.omp/config.yml` | YAML | yes / yes / yes | commands; whole tools |
| `augment` | `.augment/settings.json` | JSONC | yes / no / yes | commands; whole tools |
| `zed` | `~/.config/zed/settings.json` (`--user` only) | JSONC | yes / yes / yes | commands, edit (deny/ask), fetch, mcp tools |
| `hermes` | `~/.hermes/config.yaml` (`--user` only) | YAML | yes / no / yes | commands |
| `kimi` | `~/.kimi-code/config.toml` (`--user` only) | TOML | yes / yes / yes | Bash, bare Read |

##### User-level files

[`generate --user`](user-scope.md) writes the user-level counterpart of every harness above that has one:
`~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.codex/rules/ai-rulez.rules`, `~/.gemini/settings.json`,
`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `~/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc`, `~/.config/mimocode/mimocode.jsonc`,
`~/.copilot/settings.json` (`copilot-cli`), `~/.qwen/settings.json`, `~/.codebuddy/settings.json`,
`~/.commandcode/settings.json`, `~/.letta/settings.json`, `~/.grok/config.toml`, `~/.vibe/config.toml`,
`~/.config/poolside/settings.yaml`, `~/.omp/agent/config.yml`, `~/.augment/settings.json`, `~/.qoder/settings.json`,
and the `permissions` key of `~/.config/devin/config.json`. `cursor`, `copilot` and `zoocode` have a project file only.
`zed`, `hermes` and `kimi` read permissions from the user file only, so a project `generate` writes nothing for them
and warns once.

##### Per-harness details

- **codex** ([rules](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/rules), marked experimental by Codex):
  `prefix_rule(pattern=[argv tokens], decision=...)`; the most restrictive match wins. Paths, domains and MCP tools
  need a permission profile (`default_permissions`), which cannot be combined with `sandbox_mode`, so those rules are
  not generated. ai-rulez
  owns the whole rules file; put your own rules in another `*.rules` file.
- **opencode, kilo, mimocode** ([OpenCode permissions](https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/)): the last matching rule
  wins, so a rule that would come after an overlapping, stricter one is skipped rather than allowed to relax it. `Bash`
  prefixes become `cmd *`; a `WebFetch` domain becomes `https://host/*` (a deny also covers `http` and the bare host).
  MCP tool names are not a permission key, so MCP rules are skipped.
- **gemini** ([configuration](https://geminicli.com/docs/reference/configuration/)): `tools.allowed` and
  `tools.exclude` of `settings.json`, which match command prefixes and whole tools, never a path or a domain. Project
  policy files (`.gemini/policies/*.toml`) are documented as non-functional, so they are not used.
- **cursor** ([permissions](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/permissions)): `Shell(git)` covers every `git`
  command, so only single-word prefixes can be allowed; a multi-word deny uses `Shell(git:push*)`. There is no ask
  list. `permissions.allow` and `permissions.deny` are both required, so a deny-only config writes `"allow": []`.
- **copilot** ([approvals](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/approvals)): `true` auto-approves and `false`
  always asks. VS Code has no hard deny, so a deny is written as `false` and reported as not enforced. Read and MCP
  rules have no setting. `copilot` and `zoocode` share `.vscode/settings.json`.
- **zoocode**: the longest matching prefix wins and a tie goes to deny, so an allow longer than a deny prefix of it is
  skipped. Command auto-approval also needs the extension's auto-approve toggle, which is not a settings value.
- **copilot-cli** ([config directory](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-config-dir-reference)):
  tool permissions are session flags; only `allowedUrls` and `deniedUrls` can be committed.
- **devin** ([permissions](https://docs.devin.ai/cli/reference/permissions)).
- **qwen, codebuddy, commandcode, qoder, letta**: Claude Code syntax under `permissions.{allow,ask,deny}`. Command Code
  calls the shell tool `Shell`. Command Code and Qoder match a bare path at any depth, so paths are written
  project-rooted (`/src/**`). Qoder's Edit rule covers Write, so a Write allow is skipped. Letta's `ask` list does not
  override a broader allow, so ask rules go to `alwaysAsk`.
- **grok** ([permissions](https://docs.x.ai/build/features/permissions)): the project config holds `[permission]`.
  The WebFetch domain syntax is not documented, so only a bare `WebFetch` rule is written.
- **vibe**: setting `allowlist` or `denylist` replaces Vibe's shipped default for that list. Path denies are written as
  `*/<glob>` because Vibe matches the absolute path; a path allow cannot be scoped, so it is skipped.
- **poolside** ([tool permissions](https://docs.poolside.ai/tool-permissions)): the project file takes
  project-relative paths only.
- **omp**: `bash.patterns` is first-match-wins; ai-rulez appends deny, ask, then allow after your own patterns, so a
  pattern of yours that matches first still wins. There is no per-path or per-domain matcher.
- **augment** ([permissions](https://docs.augmentcode.com/cli/permissions)): only allow and deny; a command rule is a
  `shellInputRegex`; no path or domain matcher.
- **zed** ([tool permissions](https://zed.dev/docs/ai/tool-permissions)): `agent.tool_permissions` is read from the
  user settings only. Read tools are not permission-gated in Zed, so read rules are skipped (use `private_files`).
- **hermes, kimi** ([Hermes security](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/security),
  [Kimi config files](https://moonshotai.github.io/kimi-code/en/configuration/config-files.html)): user-level files
  only.

#### Not translated

These harnesses have no documented, committable permission file that can hold the rules, so they get nothing from
`[permissions]` and `generate` names them in a warning:

| Harness | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `amp` | Amp has no permission rules; only whole-tool `amp.tools.disable` |
| `pi` | Pi has no permission mechanism; `defaultTools` only enables or disables whole tools |
| `cline` | Command permissions exist only as the `CLINE_COMMAND_PERMISSIONS` environment variable, not a file |
| `kiro` | The permissions in `.kiro/agents/*.json` are documented with conflicting shapes, and the workspace permissions file lives outside the repository |
| `factory` | The project settings path is documented as `settings.local.json`, and `commandDenylist` means "ask", not "deny" |
| `crush` | `crush.json` has `allowed_tools` (whole tools) and no deny |
| `rovodev` | The location of the bash rules and their match order are not documented consistently |
| `takt` | Only a coarse permission mode (`readonly`, `edit`, `full`), no rules |
| `antigravity` | Only the user-level CLI file is documented, not a project path |
| `goose`, `junie`, `deepagents`, `warp` | User-level files with whole-tool, allow-only, exact-command or regex semantics that cannot hold the rules without widening them |

The other presets without a permission row (`aiassistant`, `baz`, `bob`, `codebuff`, ...) have no permission surface.

#### Matching semantics that change a rule

Where a harness matches differently from Claude Code, ai-rulez adjusts the rule so it means the same or less:

- **Whole-command regular expressions (`augment`, `zed`).** The harness tests one regex against the command string, so
  `^git log(\s|$)` would also match `git log; rm -rf /`. An allow is written as
  `^git log([ \t][^;&|\n\r`$()<>]*)?$`: the command, then arguments free of separators, substitution, grouping and
  redirections (a command that uses them is not auto-approved). A deny is written broader: Augment's also matches the
  command after a separator, a subshell or a backtick, and Zed's stays anchored because Zed tests every chained
  sub-command. A deny cannot see through a wrapper (`env git push`, `sh -c 'git push'`): enforce important denies
  with a sandbox as well.
- **Bare prefixes (`zoocode`, `gemini`, `copilot`).** Zoo Code and Gemini match with a plain prefix test, so `git`
  would approve `gitk`: allow prefixes are written with a trailing space (`git `). For VS Code an allow is written as
  the anchored regex `/^git status(\s|$)/`. Denies stay plain prefixes, since a broader deny only blocks more.
- **Paths (`opencode`, `kilo`, `mimocode`).** Patterns are matched against the path relative to the worktree, and `*`
  matches `/` too. An allow with a single `*` (`Read(./src/*.go)`) or `?` would widen, and a home or absolute path
  allow would never apply, so these are skipped. A deny is written for the root and for any depth (`.env` and
  `**/.env`); a home or absolute deny is written as given and reported as `SECURITY: ... may not be enforced`.
- **Domains.** `WebFetch(domain:Host.COM)` is lowercased. OpenCode-family denies also cover `https://host:*` and
  `http://host:*`, because `https://host/*` does not match a URL with a port.

#### Lossy cases at a glance

- A command glob (`Bash(git * --force)`) is skipped wherever the harness matches prefixes only (`codex`, `gemini`,
  `cursor`, `devin`, `vibe`, `zoocode`).
- A path or domain rule is skipped wherever the harness approves whole tools only (`gemini`, `omp`, `augment`, `vibe`
  allow, `codex`).
- A skipped allow means a prompt where you wanted none; a skipped deny is reported as `SECURITY: ...`.

#### See also

- [Hooks and settings](settings.md): hooks, the generated-file guard and file ownership.
- [Supported harnesses](harnesses.md): what every preset writes.

## Run generate in remote sessions

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/session-start/

A remote (cloud) agent session starts from a fresh clone of the repository. Generated files are there only when they
are committed, and they are current only when nobody changed a source since the last `generate`. Run
`ai-rulez generate` when the session starts, and the agent always works with the outputs of the committed sources.

```bash
# the environment's setup script
npm install -g ai-rulez
ai-rulez generate --yes
```

#### Choosing an approach

| Approach | Harnesses | Runs |
| -------- | --------- | ---- |
| [A setup script](#setup-script) | any harness whose cloud environment runs a setup script | once, when the environment is built |
| [`[session_start]`](#the-session_start-hook) | Claude Code (on by default) | at every remote session start |
| [A `SessionStart` hook of your own](#a-sessionstart-hook-for-other-harnesses) | harnesses with a `SessionStart` event | at every session start, local ones included |
| [Commit the outputs](#committed-outputs) | any harness | never; CI checks they are current |

The approaches combine: a project can commit its outputs, check them in CI and still regenerate in Claude Code's
remote sessions.

#### Setup script

Most cloud agent environments run a setup script before the agent starts. Install ai-rulez there and run `generate`:

```bash
pip install ai-rulez          # or: npm install -g ai-rulez, uv tool install ai-rulez, brew install goldziher/tap/ai-rulez
ai-rulez generate --yes --locked
```

`--yes` silences the notice about new hook and MCP commands. Use `--locked` when you commit `ai-rulez.lock`: it
fetches exactly the pinned remote includes and installed skills, and fails when the lock does not cover them. Without
a lock file, drop it.

`ai-rulez session-start --when always` is an alternative that never fails the script: it runs `generate` with a
timeout, uses `--locked` automatically when `ai-rulez.lock` exists, and prints one line on stderr when something goes
wrong (see [What the command does](#what-the-command-does)). It also prints the Claude Code briefing JSON on stdout,
which a setup script can ignore; set `[session_start] prompt = false` to leave it out.

The environment's network policy must allow the package registry you install from, and the hosts of any remote
`includes`.

#### The `[session_start]` hook

Currently supports Claude Code only: it relies on Claude Code's `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE` variable and on its
`SessionStart` output format.

For a project that generates for `claude`, `generate` adds a `SessionStart` hook to `.claude/settings.json` that runs
`ai-rulez session-start`. In a remote session the command regenerates the outputs and gives the agent a short
briefing; in a local session it does nothing. No configuration is needed; these are the keys and their defaults:

```toml
[session_start]
# generate = true        # false removes the hook (and the briefing with it)
# when = "remote"        # "remote": act only when CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE is set; "always": every session
# mode = "auto"          # auto | locked | frozen | plain
# timeout = 120          # seconds the whole run may take before it is killed
# version = "5.10.0"     # pin npx and uvx to a release; default is the latest published one
# command = ["ai-rulez"] # replaces the launcher; runs without a shell; excludes version
# prompt = true          # inject the briefing
# prompt_text = "..."    # replaces the briefing; {{server}} is the ai-rulez MCP server's name
```

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | ---- | ------- | ------- |
| `generate` | boolean | `true` | Add the hook |
| `when` | string | `"remote"` | `"remote"` acts only when `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE` is `1` or `true` (any case); `"always"` acts in every session |
| `mode` | string | `"auto"` | How `generate` uses the lock file; see [Modes](#modes) |
| `timeout` | integer | `120` | Seconds the whole run may take (1 to 900) |
| `version` | string | latest release | The version the `npx` and `uvx` fallbacks run |
| `command` | list | none | Run this launcher (plus `session-start`) directly, without a shell; excludes `version` |
| `prompt` | boolean | `true` | Return the briefing |
| `prompt_text` | string | built in | Replaces the briefing; `{{server}}` expands to the MCP server's name |

`generate = false` with any other key is a validation error. `generate --user` never adds the hook.

##### What is written

`generate` merges one entry into the `SessionStart` array of `.claude/settings.json` and leaves the rest of the file
alone. `generate = false`, or `ai-rulez clean`, removes only that entry.

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      {
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "sh -c 'case \"${CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE:-}\" in 1|[Tt][Rr][Uu][Ee]) ;; *) exit 0;; esac; ... exit 0'",
            "timeout": 150
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The hook `timeout` is the run timeout plus 30 seconds, so the command's own bound fires first. A project whose own
`[[hooks]]` already run `ai-rulez session-start` on `SessionStart` keeps its group and gets no second one. Other `SessionStart` hooks of yours stay next to the managed one.

The hook exists in a remote clone only when `.claude/settings.json` is committed. With `gitignore = true`, or a
`.gitignore` that covers `.claude/`, the clone has no hook and nothing runs. `ai-rulez doctor` warns about both cases.
In a fresh clone, `generate` leaves the committed hook in place even though the clone has no machine-local manifest.

##### How the hook finds ai-rulez

The hook is a short `sh` script that tries, in order, and stops at the first that runs:

1. `ai-rulez session-start` (an `ai-rulez` on `PATH`)
2. `npx -y ai-rulez@latest session-start`
3. `uvx --from ai-rulez@latest ai-rulez session-start`

`version` pins the fallbacks (`npx -y ai-rulez@<version>`, `uvx --from ai-rulez==<version>`). When none of them runs,
the script prints one line on stderr and exits 0, so the session starts. `ai-rulez doctor` prints this order.

With `when = "remote"` the environment check comes first, so on a developer's machine the hook returns immediately and
`npx` downloads nothing. The `npx` and `uvx` attempts run from an empty temporary directory, so a project `.npmrc`,
`node_modules/.bin` or uv configuration cannot substitute the package.

`command = ["ai-rulez"]` replaces the script with `ai-rulez session-start` run directly. Use it when the environment
installs the binary, and on Windows hosts, where the default launcher needs a POSIX shell. The command checks
`CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE` itself, so `when` still applies.

##### The briefing

With `prompt = true` the command returns

```json
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"..."}}
```

and Claude Code adds `additionalContext` to the start of the conversation. The text is built from the configuration
(at most 2 KiB, no timestamp) and says:

1. that the generated rules, skills, agents and commands come from the sources in the configuration directory, and
   that a change belongs there;
2. when the ai-rulez MCP server is enabled (`[mcp] self_server`), that it offers tools to create, update, validate and
   generate the configuration;
3. when skills are served (`delivery = "served"` or a skill source), how to find and load them, as
   `[mcp] skills_instructions` writes it into the instruction files;
4. when the generate step failed, one line saying so.

`prompt_text` replaces items 1 to 3; the failure line stays. `prompt = false` drops the briefing and keeps the
regeneration.

#### A `SessionStart` hook for other harnesses

For a harness with a `SessionStart` event (Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot and others; see
[Hooks and settings](settings.md#events)), declare the hook yourself:

```toml
[[hooks]]
event = "SessionStart"
targets = ["codex", "gemini", "cursor"]
[[hooks.hooks]]
command = "ai-rulez generate --yes --quiet"
timeout = 120
```

The hook runs at every session start, local sessions included, because these harnesses set no variable ai-rulez can
use to tell a remote session apart. The briefing is not available: its JSON format is Claude Code's. Some harnesses
ask you to trust project hooks before they run them (see [Trust and review](settings.md#trust-and-review)).

A `SessionStart` group of your own that runs `ai-rulez session-start` replaces the built-in hook for every harness,
whatever its `targets`. Add `claude` to its `targets` when Claude Code should keep it.

#### Committed outputs

Commit the generated files and fail CI when they drift from the sources:

```bash
ai-rulez generate --check   # exits 2 and lists the differing files
```

A fresh clone then has every output, current as of the last commit, with nothing to run. See
[GitHub Actions](github-actions.md).

#### What the command does

`ai-rulez session-start` is what the hook runs, and you can run it yourself:

```bash
echo '{"source":"startup"}' | CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true ai-rulez session-start
ai-rulez session-start --when always --generate-mode plain
```

| Step | Behavior |
| ---- | -------- |
| Project | `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, else the payload's `cwd`, else the working directory; the configuration is found by walking up to the git work tree. No configuration: silent no-op. Outside a work tree: one line on stderr. |
| Gate | Unless `when` is `"always"`, `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE` must be `1` or `true`; otherwise it exits 0 and prints nothing. |
| Generate | On the payload `source` `startup`, `resume` or none. `clear` and `compact` keep the session's working tree, so they only get the briefing. |
| Briefing | The JSON document on stdout, unless `prompt = false`. |
| Exit | Always 0. |

Flags override the configuration: `--when`, `--generate-mode` (the `mode` key) and `--timeout` (seconds).

`generate` runs as a child process (`generate --yes --quiet`), so the timeout kills its whole process tree and stdout
carries only the JSON document. The child gets a scrubbed environment: the base variables, proxy and certificate
settings, and `AI_RULEZ_*` settings, but no tokens or other credentials of the session. A lock in the temporary
directory keeps two hooks that start together from running two generates at once.

A failure is one line on stderr, the existing files stay as they were, and the briefing says so:

```text
ai-rulez session-start: generate failed: <reason>; generated files may be out of date
```

##### Modes

| `mode` | `generate` runs with |
| ------ | -------------------- |
| `auto` (default) | `--locked` when `ai-rulez.lock` exists, otherwise no lock flag |
| `locked` | `--locked` (fails when `ai-rulez.lock` is missing) |
| `frozen` | `--frozen`: only the local cache, verified against the lock |
| `plain` | no lock flag |

A locked run tries `--locked --offline` first and goes online once only if that fails. The command never writes
`ai-rulez.lock`; that stays with `ai-rulez lock`. See the [lock file](lockfile.md).

##### Network policy

Remote environments usually reach the network through a proxy that allows named hosts. The hook needs
`registry.npmjs.org` for `npx` (or `pypi.org` for `uvx`) when `ai-rulez` is not installed, plus the hosts of any
remote `includes`. A request the policy refuses (HTTP 403 or 407) is not retried, and the error names the host:

```text
ai-rulez session-start: generate failed: the network policy denied github.com; generated files may be out of date
```

Allow the host, or install `ai-rulez` in the setup script and set `command = ["ai-rulez"]`. `ai-rulez doctor`, run in a
remote session, probes the npm registry and reports a denied or unreachable one.

#### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| ------- | ----- | --- |
| Nothing runs in a remote Claude Code session | `.claude/settings.json` is not committed or is gitignored | Commit it; `ai-rulez doctor` reports this |
| `no ai-rulez, npx or uvx could run; skipped` | None of the launchers is installed | Install ai-rulez, Node or uv in the setup script |
| `the network policy denied <host>` | The proxy blocks the registry or an include host | Allow the host, or install ai-rulez and set `command` |
| Regeneration in every local session | `when = "always"`, or a hand-written `SessionStart` hook | Use `when = "remote"`, or a setup script |
| `generate --check` shows drift for the hook | The committed settings differ from what `generate` renders | Run `generate` and commit `.claude/settings.json` |

## User-level configuration

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/user-scope/

`ai-rulez generate --user` renders a personal configuration into the per-user directories each harness reads
(`~/.claude`, `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.codex`, `~/.gemini`, `~/.config/opencode`, `~/.copilot`, `~/.pi/agent`, and the
others in [Where things go](#where-things-go)). Your own instructions and skills then follow you into every
repository, including ones that do not use ai-rulez. Nothing is written to the home directory without `--user`.

```toml
# ~/.config/ai-rulez/config.toml
version = "5.0"
name = "me"
presets = ["claude", "codex", "cursor"]

[permissions]
deny = ["Bash(rm -rf:*)"]
```

With one rule and one skill in `~/.config/ai-rulez/`:

```console
$ ai-rulez generate --user --dry-run
user-level plan (profile default, home /home/me)
  write:   /home/me/.agents/skills/review/SKILL.md
  write:   /home/me/.claude/CLAUDE.md
  write:   /home/me/.claude/rules/small-prs.md
  write:   /home/me/.claude/skills/review/SKILL.md
  write:   /home/me/.codex/AGENTS.md
  write:   /home/me/.codex/rules/ai-rulez.rules
  merge:   /home/me/.claude/settings.json (ai-rulez keys only)
  2 project-shaped output(s) have no documented user-level location and are not written
WARN  cursor reads ~/.agents/skills, ~/.claude/skills, so these skills load twice: review
```

#### The user config

The user config has the same schema as a project config. It lives in `~/.config/ai-rulez/` (or
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ai-rulez`), or in any directory you pass with `--config <dir>`:

```text
~/.config/ai-rulez/
  config.toml
  rules/        skills/        agents/        domains/
```

`presets`, `profiles`, `default`, `builtins`, `includes`, `installed_skills`, `[[hooks]]`, `[permissions]` and
`[claude.settings.managed]` work as in a project. Project-only features do nothing at user level: MCP servers,
`[[scopes]]`, `[plugin]`/`[marketplace]`, `agents_md`, the `.local` overlay and gitignore management. A preset with no
documented user-level location is reported and skipped.

`generate --user` ignores the project in the working directory, except to warn when a skill of the same name exists
at both levels.

##### Profiles and roles per machine

Keep shared content at the top level and one domain per role, then choose the role per machine with `default` in the
user config, or per run with `--profile`:

```toml
default = "backend"

[profiles]
backend = ["backend"]
frontend = ["frontend"]
```

```bash
ai-rulez generate --user --profile frontend
```

Switching the role removes the files of the old one on the next run.

For finer control, declare `[[roles]]` (domains, per-kind `include` and `exclude` selectors, inheritance, and a
per-skill `skill_mode` that becomes `skillOverrides` in `~/.claude/settings.json`) and select one with `--role`, which
excludes `--profile`:

```bash
ai-rulez generate --user --role backend-engineer --yes
```

ai-rulez does not decide who holds a role; an external tool picks the name. See [Roles](roles.md) and
[Integrating an identity tool or UI](roles.md#integrating-an-identity-tool-or-ui).

#### Commands

```bash
ai-rulez generate --user --dry-run     # list every path that would be written, merged, skipped or removed
ai-rulez generate --user               # same list, then asks before writing (interactive terminal)
ai-rulez generate --user --yes         # no prompt (required in a non-interactive shell)
ai-rulez clean --user                  # remove exactly what generate --user wrote
```

The write list is printed before the first write, whatever the flags. `--user` cannot be combined with `--recursive`
or `--plugin`.

#### Safety

- **Only documented locations.** An output is written only where the preset's user-level layout (the table below)
  places it. Everything else a preset renders (project-only rules folders, MCP files) is dropped and counted;
  `--debug` names each one.
- **Your files are never replaced.** A file that exists and was not written by ai-rulez (not in the manifest, no
  generated banner, not byte-identical to the output) is skipped and listed as `skip:`. A skill directory that holds
  one is skipped whole. A `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` you wrote stays yours.
- **Shared settings documents are merged.** `~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.codex/hooks.json`, `~/.cursor/hooks.json`,
  `~/.gemini/settings.json` and the other settings documents get only the keys ai-rulez owns (hooks, permissions,
  `env`, `skillOverrides`; see [Hooks and settings](settings.md) and [Permissions](permissions.md)); every other key
  survives `generate` and `clean`. The generated-file [`[guard]`](settings.md#guard) and the
  [`[session_start]`](session-start.md) hook are never added at user level.
- **No symlink escapes.** Every destination, resolved through symlinks, must stay inside the home directory (or a
  relocated tool home). A `~/.claude` symlinked into `~/dotfiles` is followed; one that points out of the home
  directory stops the run before anything is written. A symlinked file is skipped, except for settings documents.
- **Clean removes only what was recorded.** The manifest is `~/.config/ai-rulez/.generated-manifest.json`, plus
  `.generated-manifest.local.json` for the keys merged into shared documents. `clean --user`, and `generate --user`
  after you drop content, remove a file only when it is listed there and, if it carries a generated header, still
  looks generated. Directories that `generate --user` created (`~/.cursor`, `~/.claude/skills/<id>`, ...) are removed
  once empty; a directory that existed before, or still holds a file of yours, is never removed. If you keep
  `~/.config/ai-rulez` in a dotfiles repository, ignore the two manifest files there.
- **`--dry-run` writes nothing**, not even the manifest.
- **Only an absolute home is used.** `generate --user` refuses a relative `$HOME`.

#### Where things go

Each preset maps its project outputs onto its user-level layout. Kinds: `instructions` is the root instructions file,
`rules` a rules folder, `skills`, `agents` and `commands` the matching folders, `settings` a shared config document.
At user level only [hooks, permissions and managed settings](settings.md) are merged into a `settings` document,
never MCP servers, and nothing is written to it when the config has none. Claude Code renders commands as skills, so
they share the `skills` row.

Presets not in the table have no documented user-level location for anything `--user` writes, and are reported and
skipped: `aiassistant`, `baz`, `codebuff`, `replit` and `xum`. User-level MCP servers are not generated.

##### Relocated tool homes

When a tool's home variable is set to an absolute path, every path in that tool's home moves there:
`CODEX_HOME=/data/codex` writes `/data/codex/AGENTS.md` and `/data/codex/hooks.json`, while Codex's skills stay in the
shared `~/.agents/skills`.

| Variable | Harness |
| -------- | ------- |
| `CODEX_HOME` | `codex` |
| `DEEPAGENTS_HOME` | `deepagents` |
| `DSH_HOME` | `dsh` |
| `HERMES_HOME` | `hermes` |
| `KIMI_CODE_HOME` | `kimi` |
| `QWEN_HOME` | `qwen` |
| `VIBE_HOME` | `vibe` |

A relative value is ignored with a warning, and a value that is the filesystem root, the home directory or one of its
ancestors is refused. The files are recorded in the manifest, so `clean --user` removes them from the relocated
directory; the symlink and hand-authored-file rules apply there too. A relocated home itself is never removed.

#### Project and user scope together

Harnesses read both scopes, so the same skill can load twice. `generate --user` warns in two cases.

**One harness reads several user directories.** OpenCode reads `~/.config/opencode/skills`, `~/.claude/skills` and
`~/.agents/skills`; Cursor reads `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.cursor/skills`, `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.codex/skills`;
Gemini CLI, Copilot and Codex read `~/.agents/skills` as well as their own. Generating skills for `claude` and
`opencode` therefore installs each skill twice for OpenCode. Keep to presets that share a directory (`codex`, `gemini`
and `cursor` all use `~/.agents/skills`; `pi` uses `~/.pi/agent/skills`), or accept the duplicates.

**A skill also exists in the project you run from.** The harness's documented precedence decides which copy runs:

| Harness | Same name at user and project level |
| ------- | ----------------------------------- |
| Claude Code | the user-level skill runs (personal over project) |
| Gemini CLI | the workspace skill runs (workspace over user) |
| Codex | both are listed; same-named skills are not merged or overridden |
| OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot, pi | no precedence is documented; keep names unique |

Instruction files are concatenated rather than overridden (Claude Code and Gemini CLI load the user-level file, then
the project's; Codex loads the global `AGENTS.md` first), so no warning is needed for them.

## Baz

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/baz/

The `baz` preset writes the files the [Baz](https://baz.ai) pull request reviewer reads from a repository. Baz has no
repository config file: its settings live in its web UI, and a repository influences it only through instruction
files. The preset turns path-scoped rules into `AGENTS.md` files in the directories they apply to, so Baz applies each
rule only to the code it is about.

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml
presets = ["baz"]
```

```markdown
<!-- .ai-rulez/rules/api.md -->
---
type: Decision
title: API
x-ai-rulez:
  kind: rule
  id: api
  metadata:
    paths:
      - "services/api/**/*.py"
---

Validate request bodies.
```

`ai-rulez generate` writes the root `AGENTS.md` with the always-on rules, and the path-scoped rule into the directory
its glob points to:

```markdown
<!-- services/api/AGENTS.md (generated header omitted) -->
# services/api

Instructions for `services/api/` and everything below it.

## Rules

### api

_Applies to: `services/api/**/*.py`_

Validate request bodies.
```

#### What Baz reads

From Baz's [Skills & Instructions](https://baz.ai/docs/agents/skills-and-instructions):

| Pattern | Where |
| ------- | ----- |
| `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules`, `.clauderc`, `.coderabbit.yaml`, `*BUGBOT.md` | any depth, scoped to the file's directory and below |
| `.cursor/rules/*.md(c)`, `.cursor/BUGBOT.md`, `.claude/*.md`, `.claude/agents/*.md(c)`, `.agent(s)/*.md(c)` | repository root only |
| Skill folders `.claude/skills/*`, `.cursor/skills/*`, `.agent(s)/skills/*`, each with a top-level `SKILL.md` or `AGENTS.md` | repository root only |

- `.claude/commands/` and `.cursor/commands/` are ignored, and `.claude/rules/` is not read.
- There is no precedence: every guideline whose directory covers a changed file applies.
- Files are read from the **default branch**. An edit on a feature branch does not affect the review of that branch.
- Baz keeps rules a reviewer can check by reading code and drops agent-behavior, process and "run this tool"
  instructions, so write review rules as code conventions.

#### What the preset generates

| Output | Content |
| ------ | ------- |
| `AGENTS.md` | Always-on rules and context; the same file `codex`, `opencode`, `amp` and the other `AGENTS.md` presets write |
| `<dir>/AGENTS.md` | Path-scoped rules and context whose globs point into `<dir>` |
| `.agents/skills/<id>/SKILL.md` and resources | Skills |
| `.claude/agents/<id>.md` | Agents, with `name` and `description` frontmatter |

It writes no commands, no MCP servers and no `.claude/rules/`. Baz reads skills and agents at the repository root
only, so a [`[[scopes]]`](monorepo.md) run writes only the scope's `AGENTS.md`. An item with `targets` is written when a
target names `baz` or `AGENTS.md`.

#### Options

All keys go in `[rules]`:

```toml
[rules]
baz_scoped = "nested"   # nested | root
baz_default = "all"     # all | none
baz_rest = "root"       # root | skip
baz_unscoped = "root"   # root | skip
baz_dedupe = false
baz_dedupe_max = 0
baz_budget = 0

[rules.baz]
include = ["db-dao"]    # with baz_default = "none"
```

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | ---- | ------- | ------- |
| `baz_scoped` | string | `"nested"` | `nested` writes path-scoped items to the `AGENTS.md` of their directory; `root` keeps them in the root `AGENTS.md` with an `_Applies to:_` line |
| `baz_default` | string | `"all"` | `all` nests every path-scoped item; `none` nests only items that opt in |
| `rules.baz.include` | list | `[]` | Rule and context names that opt in under `baz_default = "none"` (case-insensitive, with or without `.md`) |
| `baz_rest` | string | `"root"` | `skip` leaves path-scoped items that `baz` does not select out of the root `AGENTS.md` |
| `baz_unscoped` | string | `"root"` | `skip` leaves path-scoped items with no directory out of the root `AGENTS.md` |
| `baz_dedupe` | boolean | `false` | Write an item that points into several sibling directories once, to their parent's `AGENTS.md` |
| `baz_dedupe_max` | integer | `0` (off) | Collapse an item that would be copied into more than this many directories to the directory covering all of them |
| `baz_budget` | integer | `0` (off) | Warn when the Baz `AGENTS.md` files together exceed this many bytes |

Only the Baz `AGENTS.md` files change with these keys; the output of the other presets is the same in every mode.

#### Path-scoped rules

With `baz_scoped = "nested"`, a rule or context item with `paths` or `globs` goes to the `AGENTS.md` of the directory
its globs point into. The directory is the leading wildcard-free part of each positive glob: `{a,b}` is expanded,
several directories get a copy each, and a directory below another listed one is covered by it. The scope of a nested
file is the whole directory, which can be wider than the glob; the `_Applies to:_` line keeps the exact globs.

The item stays in the root `AGENTS.md` when:

- a positive glob has no directory (`**/*.py`, `*.md`), or only negated globs are set;
- the directory does not exist, is a `[[scopes]]` path, is inside the configuration directory or `.git`, belongs to
  another ai-rulez root nested in the project (`generate` warns and names the rule), or is outside the project;
- `baz_scoped = "root"`.

An item that moves to a nested file is left out of the root `AGENTS.md` for every preset that writes it, so the
shared file stays identical.

##### Path-scoped rules with no directory

A rule scoped by `**/BUILD`, `**/*.go` or `.mcp.json` names no directory, so it cannot be nested and the root
`AGENTS.md` inlines it with its `_Applies to:_` line. Any harness that reads the root file then loads that rule in every
session, on top of its own copy in a rules folder (`.claude/rules/`, `.cursor/rules/`). `baz_unscoped = "skip"` leaves
such rules out of the root file.

`skip` applies only while `baz` is the only preset writing the root `AGENTS.md` and `baz_scoped = "nested"`. When
`codex`, `opencode`, `amp` or another preset that reads `AGENTS.md` is configured, they need the rule, so the file keeps
it.

##### Rules Baz does not select

With `baz_default = "none"`, rules that do not opt in, and rules excluded with `!baz`, are not nested, so the root
`AGENTS.md` keeps inlining them. `baz_rest = "skip"` leaves them out of the root file. Like `baz_unscoped`, it applies
only while `baz` is the only preset writing the root `AGENTS.md` and `baz_scoped = "nested"`. When `baz_budget` is
exceeded, the warning also names the path-scoped rules the root file inlines.

#### Narrowing the nested surface

A rule with many globs is copied into every directory they point into, so a large monorepo can grow one nested
`AGENTS.md` per service.

- **`baz_default = "none"`** nests only items that opt in. The others stay in the root `AGENTS.md`, which Baz also
  reads, so nothing is lost; it is only not duplicated into the directory files.
- **`baz_dedupe = true`** writes an item whose globs point into several sibling directories once, to the parent's
  `AGENTS.md` (`services/AGENTS.md` instead of `services/api/AGENTS.md` and `services/web/AGENTS.md`).
- **`baz_dedupe_max = <K>`** collapses an item that would be copied into more than K directories to the directory
  covering all of them, even without `baz_dedupe`. When they share only the repository root (`platform/`, `deploy/`,
  `tools/`), the item goes to the root `AGENTS.md`; with `baz_unscoped = "skip"` the root is off limits and the copies
  stay.
- **`baz_budget = <bytes>`** makes `generate` warn when the root and nested Baz `AGENTS.md` files together exceed the
  budget, naming the largest files. It never fails the run.

##### Per-rule opt-in and opt-out

- **`targets: ["!baz"]`** in a rule's frontmatter excludes it from everything `baz` writes on its own: the nested
  `AGENTS.md` files, skills and agents. A negated target wins over a positive one, and a rule whose targets are all
  negated is still written for every other preset. `!baz` does not remove a rule from the root `AGENTS.md`, which other
  presets share; restrict the rule with targets that name those presets instead.
- **`[rules.baz] include`** opts rules in by name under `baz_default = "none"`. Under the default `"all"` it makes no
  difference.

```toml
[rules]
baz_default = "none"

[rules.baz]
include = ["dao"]
```

`baz: true` in a rule's metadata opts it in the same way, but `validate` reports it as an unknown key (`AR303
frontmatter-key-unknown`). Prefer `include`, or add `allowed_keys = ["baz"]` to `[lint]` to silence the finding:

```markdown
<!-- .ai-rulez/rules/dao.md -->
---
type: Decision
title: DAO conventions
x-ai-rulez:
  kind: rule
  id: dao
  metadata:
    paths:
      - "services/db/**/*.go"
    baz: true
---

Every query goes through the DAO layer.
```

#### Using it with other presets

- **`claude`**: Baz reads `.claude/skills/` and `.claude/agents/`, so with `claude` configured `baz` writes neither,
  and nothing is read twice. Claude Code's commands are written as user-invocable skills under `.claude/skills/`,
  which Baz reads as skills. With the default `CLAUDE.md` (which imports `@AGENTS.md`), Claude Code loads only the root
  `AGENTS.md`, not the nested ones; without a `CLAUDE.md` (`[claude] claude_md = "none"`), Claude Code can also load a nested
  `AGENTS.md` when it reads a file in that directory, so a scoped rule can reach it twice. Limit such a rule with
  `targets`.
- **`codex`, `opencode`, `amp`, `xum`** and the other `AGENTS.md` presets share the root `AGENTS.md`. With
  `agents_md = true` (the default) it and `.agents/skills/` are written once, and `baz` adds its nested files.
- **`cursor`** and other presets that write `.cursor/rules`: Baz reads those files too, so a rule can reach it from
  both `.cursor/rules` and `AGENTS.md`. Baz applies every in-scope guideline, so contradictory rules produce
  contradictory feedback.

#### Limits

- Nothing reaches Baz until it is on the default branch.
- The preset cannot change Baz's UI settings (draft reviews, ignored branches, custom reviewers); an organization
  admin configures those.
- Baz does not read nested `.claude/` and `.cursor/` directories. `baz` never writes them, but another preset in a
  `[[scopes]]` run can.
- Baz reads committed files only, so machine-local configuration has no effect on it.

## Authoring plugins

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/plugins/

`ai-rulez generate --plugin` packages the skills, commands, agents, MCP servers and hooks of your `.ai-rulez/` project
as installable **plugin bundles** for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Kimi, OpenCode, Factory, Hermes, Pi,
GitHub Copilot and [Agent Plugins](agent-plugins.md) clients, plus a **marketplace index**. Where plain `generate`
configures assistants inside your repository, a plugin bundle is something other people install into their own tools,
without running ai-rulez.

The `[plugin]` block carries the packaging metadata; the content comes from your existing skills, commands and agents.
To turn a bundle into a release archive and upload it, see [Publish](publish.md).

!!! note "Authoring vs. installing"
    This page covers the producer side: `[plugin]`, `[[plugins_authoring]]` and `[marketplace]`. To install or enable
    someone else's plugin, see [Installed plugins](installed-plugins.md) and
    [Enable a plugin from another marketplace](#enable-a-plugin-from-another-marketplace).

#### Quick start

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml
version = "5.0"
name = "acme-tools"

[plugin]
name = "acme-tools"
version = "1.2.0"
description = "Code review skills and an MCP server for Acme repositories."
license = "MIT"
repository = "https://github.com/acme/acme-tools"
keywords = ["review", "mcp"]
runtimes = ["claude", "cursor", "codex", "gemini"]

[plugin.author]
name = "Acme Tooling"
email = "tooling@acme.example"

[[plugin.mcp]]
name = "acme-docs"
command = "${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/mcp-launch.sh"
args = ["serve"]

# Codex requires an interface block
[plugin.interface]
display_name = "Acme Tools"
short_description = "Acme code review."
long_description = "Review skills and a docs MCP server for Acme repositories."
developer_name = "Acme Tooling"
category = "Developer Tools"
capabilities = ["Read"]
default_prompt = ["Review this pull request"]
```

The project also has a skill in `.ai-rulez/skills/review-pr/` (`SKILL.md`, `index.md` and `scripts/lint.sh`, in the
[OKF](okf.md) layout), a command `.ai-rulez/commands/triage.md`, and the
launcher `scripts/mcp-launch.sh` at the repository root. A skill directory is bundled whole.

```bash
ai-rulez generate --plugin --dry-run   # list what would be written
ai-rulez generate --plugin
```

```text
plugin bundle:
write-file: .claude-plugin/plugin.json
write-file: skills/review-pr/SKILL.md
write-file: skills/review-pr/index.md
write-file: skills/review-pr/scripts/lint.sh
write-file: commands/triage.md
write-file: .cursor-plugin/plugin.json
write-file: .cursor-plugin/skills/review-pr/SKILL.md
write-file: .cursor-plugin/skills/review-pr/index.md
write-file: .cursor-plugin/skills/review-pr/scripts/lint.sh
write-file: .cursor-plugin/commands/triage.md
write-file: .codex-plugin/plugin.json
write-file: .mcp.json
write-file: gemini-extension.json
write-file: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json
write-file: .ai-rulez-generated.json
```

A single-plugin repository is its own bundle: the files land at the repository root, and the marketplace index lists
the plugin with `"source": "./"`. `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "acme-tools",
  "description": "Code review skills and an MCP server for Acme repositories.",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "author": {
    "name": "Acme Tooling",
    "email": "tooling@acme.example"
  },
  "repository": "https://github.com/acme/acme-tools",
  "license": "MIT",
  "keywords": ["review", "mcp"],
  "mcpServers": {
    "acme-docs": {
      "command": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/mcp-launch.sh",
      "args": ["serve"]
    }
  }
}
```

The same server is `./scripts/mcp-launch.sh` in `.mcp.json` (Codex) and `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json`, and
`${extensionPath}/scripts/mcp-launch.sh` in `gemini-extension.json`.

Commit the bundle and keep it in sync:

```bash
ai-rulez verify --plugin      # exit 2 when a bundle file was edited, removed or added by hand
ai-rulez validate             # manifest, root-component and version checks
```

The root-component (`AR9T0`) and version-drift (`AR961`) findings are warnings; `validate --strict` makes them fail.

```text
Drifted plugin outputs:
  changed      .claude-plugin/plugin.json
  extra        skills/review-pr/notes.md

Error: generated plugin output is stale

Hint: Run ai-rulez generate --plugin and commit the regenerated output
```

Users then add the repository as a marketplace or extension in their tool (for Claude Code,
`claude plugin marketplace add acme/acme-tools`; Gemini CLI, `gemini extensions install <url>`; for Cursor and Codex,
see the vendor's plugin documentation linked from [Supported Harnesses](harnesses.md)). Another ai-rulez project can
install it with [Installed plugins](installed-plugins.md).

#### Runtimes

`runtimes` selects the bundles. Without it, the eight default runtimes are generated; `pi`, `copilot` and
`agent-plugins` are opt-in and must be listed.

| Runtime | Default | Manifest | Bundles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `claude` | yes | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` | skills, commands, agents, hooks, MCP, statusline; writes the marketplace index |
| `cursor` | yes | `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` | skills, commands, hooks (`.cursor-plugin/hooks/hooks.json`), MCP |
| `codex` | yes | `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` and `.mcp.json`, or a root `plugin.json` ([layouts](#codex)) | skills, MCP |
| `gemini` | yes | `gemini-extension.json` | MCP and hooks inline; commands opt-in |
| `kimi` | yes | `kimi.plugin.json` | skills, MCP, interface |
| `opencode` | yes | `.opencode/plugins/<name>.js` and `package.json` | skills, commands, agents, MCP ([adapter](#opencode)) |
| `factory` | yes | `.factory-plugin/plugin.json` | metadata only |
| `hermes` | yes | `.hermes/plugins/<name>/` and `.hermes/package/` | skills, commands, agents ([adapter](#hermes)) |
| `pi` | opt-in | `package.json`, `.pi/skills/`, `.pi/prompts/` | skills, commands as prompt templates |
| `copilot` | opt-in | root `plugin.json`, `mcp.json`, `.github/plugin/marketplace.json` | skills, agents, MCP |
| `agent-plugins` | opt-in | root `plugin.json`, `mcp.json` | skills, MCP ([Agent Plugins](agent-plugins.md)) |

A component a runtime has no documented format for is not generated, and `generate` warns when you configured one
(for example commands or hooks for `copilot`, or MCP servers for `pi`).

Skills and their supporting files are copied verbatim. Commands are converted where the runtime needs another format
(Gemini TOML, Pi prompt templates). Content written in [Open Knowledge Format](okf.md) gets native frontmatter in the
bundle: `type`, `title` and `x-ai-rulez` are removed and the entries of `x-ai-rulez.metadata` move to the top level.

#### Plugin metadata

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | required | Lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starting with a letter or digit, no `..`. Becomes a directory and file name in every runtime. `agent-plugins`, `copilot` and the Codex root layout also require at most 64 characters, an alphanumeric last character, and no `_` or `--` |
| `description` | string | required | One-line description |
| `version` | string | required | A semantic version. Clients that install from git keep their cached copy until it changes, see [Version drift](#version-drift) |
| `version_from` | string | none | `package.json`, `pyproject.toml` (`project.version`) or `Cargo.toml` (`package.version`) to read the version from; excludes `version` |
| `display_name` | string | none | Human-readable name |
| `homepage`, `repository`, `license` | string | none | Copied into the manifests |
| `category`, `keywords`, `tags` | string, string list | none | Marketplace metadata |
| `brand_color`, `icon`, `logo` | string | none | UI metadata |
| `runtimes` | string list | the eight defaults | Bundles to generate |
| `content_root` | string | the config directory | Project-relative directory holding plugin-only `skills/`, `commands/` and `agents/`, to keep the shipped payload apart from your repository's own content |
| `include_domains` | string list | none | Domains (names or globs) whose content is bundled too, see [Domain content](#domain-content-and-per-domain-plugins) |
| `include_evals` | bool | `false` | Bundle each skill's `evals/` and the project's `.ai-rulez/evals/`, see [Evals](evals.md) |
| `include` | string list | none | Globs of extra files for the Agent Plugins package, see [Bundling files](agent-plugins.md#bundling-files) |
| `shared_resources` | string list | none | Directories copied into every bundled skill, see [Shared resources](#shared-resources-across-skills) |
| `provenance_headers` | bool | `true` | Write the generated-file header into bundled Markdown, JS, TS and Python files |
| `skills_dir_owned` | bool | `false` | Treat the bundle's skills directory as fully generated, see [Drift](#drift-and-cleanup) |
| `spec` | string | `1.0.0` | Agent Plugins version (`1.0.0` or `1.1.0`) for `agent-plugins`, `copilot` and the Codex root layout |
| `package_manager` | string | none | `packageManager` of the OpenCode and Pi `package.json`, such as `pnpm@9.15.0` |
| `opencode_dependency` | string | `^2.0.26` | Version range of the `@opencode/plugin` dependency |
| `opencode_dependency_enabled` | bool | `true` | `false` drops the `@opencode/plugin` dependency |

| Table | Keys |
| --- | --- |
| `[plugin.author]` | `name`, `email`, `url`. `name` is required for the Claude marketplace index (its `owner`) and for Codex |
| `[[plugin.mcp]]` | `name`, `command`, `args`, `env`, `transport`, `url`, see [MCP servers](#mcp-servers) |
| `[[plugin.hooks]]` | `event`, `matcher`, `[[plugin.hooks.hooks]]`, see [Hooks](#hooks) |
| `[plugin.statusline]` | `script`, `command`; Claude Code only |
| `[plugin.interface]` | the Codex and Kimi UI block, see [Codex](#codex) |
| `[plugin.codex]`, `[plugin.cursor]`, `[plugin.gemini]`, `[plugin.kimi]`, `[plugin.hermes]`, `[plugin.pi]` | see [Runtime-specific settings](#runtime-specific-settings) |

A version bump can live in one place with `version_from`:

```toml
[plugin]
name = "acme-tools"
description = "Code review skills and an MCP server for Acme repositories."
version_from = "package.json"
```

The resolved version replaces `version` in every manifest and in `ai-rulez.lock`, so a bump in `package.json` shows as
drift until you regenerate. `validate` reports a missing file or version key.

#### MCP servers

`[[plugin.mcp]]` declares the plugin's MCP servers. When the plugin declares none, the project's enabled
`[[mcp_servers]]` are bundled instead.

Write launch paths once with `${PLUGIN_ROOT}`; each runtime gets its own form:

| Runtime | `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/run.sh` becomes |
| --- | --- |
| Claude | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/run.sh` |
| Gemini | `${extensionPath}/scripts/run.sh` |
| Cursor, Codex, Kimi, Agent Plugins, Copilot | `./scripts/run.sh` |
| OpenCode | `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/run.sh`, expanded by the adapter at load time |

- Remote servers use `transport = "http"` (or `"sse"`) and a `url`.
- Header values are never bundled; `generate` warns when a server has `headers`.
- A disabled server is carried as `disabled: true` into the OpenCode bundle; the other runtimes have no such flag, so
  it is bundled enabled and `generate` warns.
- Files the command points at must exist in the installed plugin. In a single-plugin repository the plugin root is the
  repository root, so keep the launcher there (`scripts/mcp-launch.sh` above).

For Gemini, declare the environment variables a server needs as extension settings; Gemini prompts for them and
stores `sensitive` values in its keychain:

```toml
[[plugin.gemini.settings]]
name = "Docs token"
description = "Token for the Acme docs server."
env_var = "ACME_DOCS_TOKEN"
sensitive = true
```

Setting names and environment variables must be unique; environment variable names use letters, digits and
underscores.

#### Hooks

Hooks are declared once and rendered into each runtime's hook format (Claude `hooks/hooks.json`, Cursor
`.cursor-plugin/hooks/hooks.json`, Gemini inline in `gemini-extension.json`).

```toml
[[plugin.hooks]]
event = "SessionStart"
matcher = "startup"

[[plugin.hooks.hooks]]
script = "scripts/bootstrap.sh"        # relative to the project root; copied to hooks/bootstrap.sh
timeout = 30
status_message = "Preparing acme-tools..."

[[plugin.hooks]]
event = "PreToolUse"
matcher = "Bash"

[[plugin.hooks.hooks]]
command = "acme-guard check"           # must exist on the user's machine
if = "Bash(git push *)"
```

The Claude rendering of the first hook:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      {
        "matcher": "startup",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "\"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/bootstrap.sh\"",
            "timeout": 30,
            "async": false,
            "statusMessage": "Preparing acme-tools..."
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | A Claude Code lifecycle event: `SessionStart`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, ... An unknown event is a warning, not an error |
| `matcher` | The event's matcher. Events without a subject (`UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `PostToolBatch`, ...) ignore it, and `validate` warns |
| `type` | Handler type; default `command` |
| `command` | An executable already on the user's machine, passed through verbatim |
| `script` | A project file bundled into the plugin's `hooks/` directory and run from there. Exactly one of `command` and `script` |
| `args` | Arguments; with `args` the executable is spawned directly, without a shell |
| `timeout` | Seconds; `0` uses the runtime default |
| `async` | Run without blocking (default `false`) |
| `if` | One permission rule such as `"Bash(git *)"` or `"Edit(*.ts)"`. Claude Code evaluates it only on `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `PermissionRequest` and `PermissionDenied`; on other events a handler with `if` never runs, and `validate` warns |
| `status_message` | Shown while the handler runs (`statusMessage`) |

A `SessionStart` hook has no declarative guard: a bootstrap script must check for itself whether its work is done.

#### Shared resources across skills

Skills in one plugin often link to the same reference docs or templates. `shared_resources` copies directories
(relative to the content root) into **every** bundled skill, for every runtime, so a skill still works when installed
on its own:

```toml
[plugin]
shared_resources = ["references", "templates"]
```

- `references/style.md` lands at `skills/<name>/references/style.md` in each skill.
- A `SKILL.md` link that climbs out to the shared directory (`../../references/style.md`) is rewritten to the copy
  (`references/style.md`).
- A shared file that clashes with a file the skill already has is an error.
- The copies are recorded like the skill's own files, so `verify --plugin` reports changes.

A symlink inside a skill directory follows the same policy as plain `generate`
([Symlinks in content](configuration.md#symlinks-in-content)): a link to a target inside the project is copied, any
other link is skipped with a warning.

#### Runtime-specific settings

##### Codex

Codex requires `[plugin.author] name` and a `[plugin.interface]` block with `display_name`, `short_description`,
`long_description`, `developer_name`, `category`, `capabilities` and `default_prompt`. Optional interface keys:
`website_url`, `privacy_policy_url`, `terms_of_service_url`, `brand_color`, `composer_icon`, `logo`, `logo_dark`,
`screenshots`. Kimi reads the same block.

```toml
[plugin.codex]
manifest = "root"     # legacy (default) | root | both
marketplace = true    # also write .agents/plugins/marketplace.json for a single-plugin repository
```

| `manifest` | Writes |
| --- | --- |
| `legacy` | `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` with the `interface` block, and `.mcp.json` |
| `root` | the Agent Plugins layout Codex prefers: a root `plugin.json` with the interface under `extensions["com.openai"]`, `skills/` and a root `mcp.json` |
| `both` | both manifests |

The root layout follows `[plugin] spec` and the Agent Plugins name rules, and shares the root `plugin.json` with the
`agent-plugins` and `copilot` runtimes. With [`source = "agents"`](agents-source.md#what-generate-writes),
`.agents/` belongs to the project and the Codex marketplace index is skipped with a warning.

##### Copilot

`runtimes = ["copilot"]` writes the Agent Plugins layout that Copilot CLI and the Copilot cloud agent read: a root
`plugin.json`, `skills/<name>/`, a root `mcp.json`, custom agents at `com.github.copilot/agents/<name>.agent.md`, and a
single-plugin marketplace at `.github/plugin/marketplace.json`. Copilot documents no file format for plugin commands
or hooks, so they are not written.

##### Cursor

`[plugin.cursor] marketplace = true` also writes `.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json` for a single-plugin repository
(`source` is `.`). For marketplaces with several plugins, set `[marketplace] cursor_index = true`. To publish a Cursor
team marketplace, see the [`cursor-team-marketplace` emitter](publish.md#emitters).

##### Gemini

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[plugin.gemini] context_file_name` | `contextFileName` of the extension (default `GEMINI.md`) |
| `[plugin.gemini] commands` | `true` bundles each command as `commands/<name>.toml`; `$ARGUMENTS` becomes `{{args}}`. Shell (`!{...}`) and file (`@{...}`) injections are not translated |
| `[[plugin.gemini.settings]]` | `name`, `description`, `env_var`, `sensitive`, see [MCP servers](#mcp-servers) |

##### Kimi

`[plugin.kimi]` takes `skill_instructions` and `session_start_skill`, written to `kimi.plugin.json`.

##### Pi packages

```toml
[plugin]
name = "acme-tools"
version = "1.2.0"
description = "Skills and prompts for Acme repositories."
repository = "https://github.com/acme/acme-tools"
runtimes = ["pi"]
```

```bash
ai-rulez generate --plugin
pi install git:github.com/acme/acme-tools
```

The package holds `.pi/skills/<name>/` and `.pi/prompts/<name>.md` (rendered from your commands) and a root
`package.json` with the `pi-package` keyword, the generated files in `files`, and a `pi` block listing the skills and
prompts. On GitHub its name is `@<owner>/pi-<plugin-name>` (`@acme/pi-acme-tools`). Pi packages carry skills and
prompts only; MCP servers, hooks and agents are skipped with a warning.

| `[plugin.pi]` key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `skills_dir` | `.pi/skills` | Where skills are written. Set `skills` to reuse the root `skills/` tree the Claude, Codex and Agent Plugins bundles write, instead of a second copy |
| `skills_entry` | `each` | `directory` lists the skills directory once in `pi.skills` and `files`, so adding a skill does not change `package.json` |
| `package_name` | `@<owner>/pi-<plugin-name>` | Explicit npm name |
| `package_json` | `generate` | `merge` updates only the keys ai-rulez owns (`name`, `version`, `description`, `author`, `repository`, `keywords`, `pi`, `files`) and keeps the rest (`devDependencies`, `scripts`, ...); an authored `name` is kept unless `package_name` is set. `verify --plugin` then checks only the owned keys |

With `runtimes = ["pi", "opencode"]` both share one `package.json`, named `@<owner>/opencode-<plugin-name>`, with
OpenCode's entry points and Pi's resources. If the two would render a different shared key, generation fails with
"runtime npm manifests disagree".

To publish on npm (which also lists the package in the [Pi package catalog](https://pi.dev/packages)), see
[Publish: npm](publish.md#npm); the published name is `<scope>/<plugin-name>`:

```bash
ai-rulez publish --to npm --npm-scope @acme --public --execute --yes
pi install npm:@acme/acme-tools
```

##### OpenCode

The OpenCode bundle is a v2 plugin, a default export `{ id, setup(ctx) }`:

| File | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `.opencode/plugins/<name>.js` | your adapter `.ai-rulez/opencode/index.js`, copied verbatim; without one, a generated module that only registers the bundled content |
| `.opencode/ai-rulez-content.js` | `registerBundledContent(ctx)`, which registers the bundled skills, commands, agents and MCP servers |
| `.opencode/ai-rulez-bundle.json` | the MCP servers and agent settings resolved at generation time |
| `.opencode/skills/`, `commands/`, `agents/` | the content |
| `package.json` | `main` and `exports` pointing at the plugin, and a dependency on `@opencode/plugin` |

OpenCode does not discover the content directories of an installed plugin, so a hand-written adapter must call the
helper from `setup`:

```js
import { registerBundledContent } from "../ai-rulez-content.js";

export default {
  id: "acme-tools",
  async setup(ctx) {
    await registerBundledContent(ctx);
  },
};
```

- **MCP servers** become OpenCode `local` (command array and `environment`) or `remote` (`url`) servers. At load time
  `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` expands to the plugin directory and `${NAME}` to `process.env.NAME` (empty when unset). A plugin runs
  inside OpenCode and can read its whole environment, so install only plugins you trust. Top-level directories an MCP
  server reaches through `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/...` are added to `package.json` `files`.
- **Agents** take their model as the `opencode` preset resolves it (`opencode_model`, then
  `defaults.model_by_preset.opencode`, then `model`). A bare alias such as `sonnet` is omitted with a warning, so the
  agent inherits the session model.
- **SDK dependency.** For an adapter that does not import `@opencode/plugin`, set
  `[plugin] opencode_dependency_enabled = false`.

To use the bundle:

1. **Copy it into a project.** Copy `.opencode/plugins/<name>.js`, `.opencode/ai-rulez-content.js`,
   `.opencode/ai-rulez-bundle.json` and the `.opencode/skills/`, `commands/` and `agents/` directories, plus any
   top-level directory an MCP server uses (such as `scripts/`), keeping their paths. Restart OpenCode.
2. **Point `opencode.json` at a directory.** Add `"plugins": ["./vendor/acme-tools"]`, where the directory is a copy of
   the bundle with an `index.js` at its root: `export { default } from "./.opencode/plugins/acme-tools.js";`. OpenCode
   loads a directory's `index.js` and ignores `package.json` `main`.

`generate` warns, without failing, when it finds a v1 OpenCode plugin (an exported function that returns hooks, or an
import of `@opencode-ai/plugin`) in `.ai-rulez/opencode/index.js`, in `.opencode/plugin(s)/`, or in a local path of
`opencode.json`. OpenCode v2 does not run v1 plugins; see the
[v1 migration guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/migrate-v1).

##### Hermes

Put Hermes registrations in `.ai-rulez/hermes/index.py` (or point `[plugin.hermes] source` at another
project-relative file). The generator copies it to `.hermes/plugins/<name>/hermes.py`, writes `__init__.py` and
`plugin.yaml`, and bundles the skills, commands and agents. The same content is packaged as a Python project under
`.hermes/package/`, published as `<name>-hermes-plugin`. Without a source file, a no-op `register(ctx)` is generated.
Hermes loads project plugins only with `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS=true`.

```toml
[plugin.hermes]
source = "plugin/hermes.py"
requires_python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = ["httpx>=0.28", "example-tool[cli]; python_version >= '3.11'"]
```

`dependencies` are PEP 508 requirements from a package index; direct references (`name @ url`) are rejected. They are
written to the wheel's `project.dependencies` and to `python_dependencies` in both Hermes manifests. Nothing is
installed at generation time.

#### Single plugin vs. monorepo

A repository with one `[plugin]` block is a **single-plugin** marketplace whose only entry has `source: "./"`. The
bundle root is the repository root, so every path a host loads from a plugin root ships to each user. `validate`
and `verify --plugin` warn (`AR9T0 root-component-shipped`) about such a path that exists at the root but is
not part of the bundle: `.mcp.json`, `hooks/`, `agents/`, `commands/`, `settings.json`, `bin/`, a root `plugin.json`,
and the other Claude Code and Codex plugin paths. A maintainer's own `.mcp.json` would otherwise be installed for
everyone. Set `[plugin] content_root`, or move the plugin into a member directory.

For a **monorepo** with several plugins, each its own ai-rulez project, the root declares a `[marketplace]` with
`members`:

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml at the repository root
[marketplace]
name = "acme"
description = "Curated Acme plugins."
members = ["plugins/review", "plugins/notify"]

[marketplace.owner]
name = "Acme Tooling"
email = "tooling@acme.example"
```

Each member (`plugins/review/.ai-rulez/config.toml`, ...) has its own `[plugin]` block. `generate --plugin` at the root
renders every member's bundle in its directory and writes one root index, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (and
`.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` for Codex), listing each member as `source: "./plugins/<dir>"`. Members write no
index of their own.

#### Several plugins from one root

One project can also define several plugins that each select part of the root's content, without separate member
projects:

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml
[[plugins_authoring]]
name = "acme-review"
version = "1.2.0"
description = "Code review skills."
runtimes = ["claude", "cursor"]
skills = ["review-*"]            # by name or glob
commands = ["triage"]

[plugins_authoring.author]
name = "Acme Tooling"

[[plugins_authoring]]
name = "acme-notify"
version = "0.3.0"
description = "Desktop notifications."
runtimes = ["claude"]
skills = ["notify-*"]
```

```text
.claude-plugin/marketplace.json
.ai-rulez-generated.json
plugins/acme-notify/.claude-plugin/plugin.json
plugins/acme-notify/skills/notify-desktop/SKILL.md
plugins/acme-review/.claude-plugin/plugin.json
plugins/acme-review/.cursor-plugin/plugin.json
plugins/acme-review/commands/triage.md
plugins/acme-review/skills/review-pr/SKILL.md
...
```

The index is named after the project and lists `./plugins/acme-notify` and `./plugins/acme-review`.

An entry bundles **only** what it selects; an empty selector selects nothing. A selector that matches nothing is a
warning (`AR9T1`).

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `name`, `description`, `version`, `author`, `license`, `homepage`, `repository`, `category`, `keywords` | metadata, as in `[plugin]` |
| `runtimes` | bundles to write |
| `skills`, `commands`, `agents` | root content, by name or glob |
| `domains` | domains whose skills, commands and agents are bundled |
| `mcp_servers` | names of root `[[mcp_servers]]`; none by default |
| `hooks` | hook groups, as `[[plugin.hooks]]` |
| `default_enabled`, `relevance` | marketplace entry fields, see [Marketplace entries](#marketplace-entries) |

The runtime tables (`[plugin.codex]`, `[plugin.interface]`, `[plugin.pi]`, ...), `include`, `shared_resources` and
`content_root` are not available per definition; a plugin that needs them stays a `[plugin]` in its own member
project. `[plugin]` cannot be combined with `[[plugins_authoring]]`.

Each definition can live in its own file, `.ai-rulez/plugins/<name>.toml`, with the entry's keys at the top level
(`name` may be omitted and must equal the file name when present). A
[layer](configuration.md#layered-configuration) can add, override (by `name`) or remove (`remove = true`) an entry.

| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `generate --plugin --plugin-name acme-review` | writes only that plugin; the indexes are left alone |
| `verify --plugin --plugin-name acme-review` | checks only that plugin |
| `verify --plugin --format json` | adds a `plugins` array with each plugin's status |

##### Several marketplaces from one root

Each `[[marketplaces_authoring]]` entry is one marketplace that lists plugin definitions by name, so a plugin can be
offered in several:

```toml
[[marketplaces_authoring]]
name = "acme-public"
description = "Published plugins"
plugins = ["acme-review", "acme-notify"]
output_dir = "marketplaces/public"

[[marketplaces_authoring]]
name = "acme-internal"
plugins = ["acme-review"]
output_dir = "marketplaces/internal"
cursor_index = true
```

Each marketplace gets `<output_dir>/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (plus the Codex index when a listed plugin targets
Codex, and the Cursor index with `cursor_index`), its own provenance sidecar, and `<output_dir>/plugins/<name>/` for
each plugin, so each directory can be published on its own. `output_dir` values must be unique and not nested inside
each other. `[marketplace]` and `[[marketplaces_authoring]]` cannot be combined. Use
`--marketplace-name NAME` with `generate --plugin` and `verify --plugin` to work on one marketplace. A marketplace can
also live in `.ai-rulez/marketplaces/<name>.toml`.

[`publish`](publish.md#several-plugins) releases only the Claude index closest to the project root.

#### Domain content and per-domain plugins

A project that keeps content in `.ai-rulez/domains/<name>/` can ship it as plugins.

To add domain content to the `[plugin]` bundle, list the domains:

```toml
[plugin]
include_domains = ["backend", "ui"]   # or ["*"]
```

On a name collision the root item wins, then the domain earlier in name order. Builtin domains are never bundled.

To ship **one plugin per domain**:

```toml
[marketplace]
name = "acme"
description = "Acme skill packs"
output_dir = "tools/acme-marketplace"   # default: the project root

[marketplace.from_domains]
name_prefix = "acme-"        # plugin "acme-backend" from domains/backend
exclude = ["scratch"]        # include defaults to every domain
version = "1.0.0"            # default: the [plugin] version, else 1.0.0
default_enabled = false
runtimes = ["claude"]        # default: the [plugin] runtimes, else the defaults
```

`generate --plugin` writes `<output_dir>/plugins/<name>/` for each domain and one
`<output_dir>/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` with `source: "./plugins/<name>"` entries (and the Codex index when a
plugin targets `codex`). A domain without bundleable content is skipped with a warning. When a domain disappears, the
next `generate --plugin` deletes the files it generated for that plugin.

In this mode the `[plugin]` block is optional and only supplies defaults (author, license, homepage, repository,
version, category, keywords, runtimes). `owner` falls back to the `[plugin]` author. `members` and domain plugins can
be combined only when `output_dir` is unset.

##### Marketplace entries

`[[marketplace.plugins]]` declares a plugin by hand, mixing root content and domains; it replaces a derived plugin of
the same name and takes the same keys as `[[plugins_authoring]]`:

```toml
[[marketplace.plugins]]
name = "acme-essentials"
skills = ["development-standards", "personal-*"]
domains = []
default_enabled = true

[marketplace.plugins.relevance]        # when Claude Code suggests the plugin
topic = "Terraform"

[marketplace.plugins.relevance.signals]
cli = ["terraform"]
files_read = ["**/*.tf"]
```

Entries carry `version`, `category`, `keywords`, `defaultEnabled` and `relevance` (signals `cwd`, `cli`, `hosts`,
`files_read`, `manifest_deps`; at least one).

##### Keep a skill out of `.claude/skills`

By default every skill and command is also written to `.claude/skills` by the `claude` preset. `[placement]` makes
some plugin-only:

```toml
[placement]
default = "core"                          # core or plugin
plugin = ["domains/*"]                    # names or globs; "domains/<domain>/<name>" also matches
```
