```toml
core = ["domains/backend/python-conventions", "git-*"]
honor_targets = true                      # skills whose frontmatter `targets` omit claude are kept out too
```

An item's frontmatter `placement: core|plugin` wins, then `core`, then `plugin`, then `default`. Placement only changes
the Claude preset's `.claude/skills` output: plugin bundles always contain the item, and other presets write every
skill.

`ai-rulez list --placement` prints each skill and command with its destination, its domain and the plugins that bundle
it, and flags a plugin-only item that no enabled or catalogued plugin bundles.

##### Register the marketplace in `.claude/settings.json`

```toml
[claude.settings]
manage = true                          # default false
register_marketplace = true            # default when managing: extraKnownMarketplaces.<marketplace name>
enable_plugins = ["acme-essentials"]   # enabledPlugins."acme-essentials@acme": true
disable_plugins = []                   # ...: false
# marketplace_source = { source = "github", repo = "acme/skills" }   # default: a directory source at output_dir
# auto_update = true
```

Only these entries are owned: every other key in the file is kept, an entry removed from the config is removed on the
next `generate`, and `clean` removes what was written. The default source is a `directory` relative to the repository
(`"./tools/acme-marketplace"`). Claude Code applies `extraKnownMarketplaces` only after the user trusts the folder.

`enable_plugins` and `disable_plugins` take a bare plugin name (qualified with the `[marketplace]` name) or a full
`name@marketplace` id. A block with only full ids needs no `[marketplace]`.

In a linked git worktree, Claude Code resolves a relative `directory` source against the main checkout, so plugin edits
in the worktree are not visible to it; `validate` warns about this. Set `marketplace_source` to an absolute
`directory` or a `github`/`git` source to test from a worktree.

##### Enable a plugin from another marketplace

`[[enabled_plugins]]` switches on a plugin this project does not author, for the Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode
presets at once:

```toml
[[enabled_plugins]]
id = "lint-kit@acme-market"                 # <name>@<marketplace>, required
marketplace = { name = "acme-market", source = "acme/plugins", type = "github" }   # optional
opencode = "@acme/lint-kit-opencode"        # optional npm package for OpenCode
```

| Preset | File | Written |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `claude` | `.claude/settings.json` | `enabledPlugins."<id>": true`, and with `marketplace`, `extraKnownMarketplaces.<name>` |
| `codex` | `.codex/config.toml` | `[plugins."<id>"]` with `enabled = true` |
| `opencode` | `opencode.json` | the `opencode` package appended to `plugin`, only when `opencode` is set |

| `marketplace` key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | must equal the marketplace part of `id` |
| `type` | `github` (`source` is `owner/repo`), `git` (an `https://` or `ssh://` URL, or `git@host:path`), `url` (an `https://` URL) or `directory` (a project-relative path) |
| `source` | the location, in the form `type` requires; `http://` and `git://` are rejected |
| `ref` | a branch or tag, for `github` and `git` |

Leave `marketplace` out when the harness already knows it. Only the written entries are owned, as for
`[claude.settings]`, and the declaration needs no `[claude.settings] manage`. With `generate --user` the entries go to
the user-level files; a `directory` marketplace is an error there. `generate` lists the marketplace registration and
the plugin as items to acknowledge, like hooks.

Conflicts are errors at load: an id in both `[[enabled_plugins]]` and `disable_plugins`, or a `marketplace` that would
replace the project's own registered `[marketplace]`.

##### Catalog skill

```toml
[marketplace.catalog_skill]
enabled = true                 # default false
name = "plugin-catalog"
```

Generates a skill listing each plugin, its default state, the skills it bundles and how to install or enable it. It is
written like a root skill to the preset outputs and is never bundled into a plugin. A root skill with the same name
wins.

#### Drift and cleanup

<p align="center">
  <img src="assets/plugin-drift.gif" alt="ai-rulez verify --plugin reporting changed and extra files in a plugin bundle, then generate --plugin restoring it" width="820" />
</p>

Every bundle has a `.ai-rulez-generated.json` sidecar that records a content hash and file mode for each generated
file. Bundled Markdown, JavaScript, TypeScript and Python files also carry a generated-file header after their
frontmatter (turn it off with `provenance_headers = false`; the sidecar still records the hashes).

`ai-rulez verify --plugin` compares the bundle with the sidecar and its sources without writing anything, and exits 2
on drift:

| Drift kind | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `changed` | a generated file was edited |
| `missing` | a generated file was deleted |
| `stale-source` | the sources changed since the bundle was generated |
| `obsolete` | a file an earlier run generated that the sources no longer produce, kept because you edited it |
| `extra` | an unrecorded file inside a generated skill directory (or, with `skills_dir_owned`, anywhere in the skills directory) |
| `mode` | a file's executable bit differs from the record, for example after a zip round trip. A sidecar written on Windows records no modes; regenerate on Linux or macOS if the bundle ships scripts |
| `symlink` | a generated output path is a symlink |

`generate --plugin` repairs drift:

- It deletes generated files whose source was removed, then the directories they leave empty. An obsolete file you
  edited is kept with a warning, and `verify --plugin` fails until you remove it.
- It deletes unrecorded files inside generated skill directories (a stray `notes.md`). Your sources (the config
  directory and `content_root`) are never touched.
- It refuses to write through a symlink.
- `generate --plugin --dry-run` lists each deletion as `delete-stale: <path>` and each kept file as
  `keep-obsolete: <path>`.

`skills_dir_owned = true` declares the skills directory (`skills/`, `.pi/skills`, ...) fully generated: a leftover skill
directory from a rename, or any stray file there, is reported as `extra` and removed. A Pi `skills_dir` that points
into your sources cannot be owned.

##### Version drift

A client that installed a plugin from a git-hosted marketplace keeps its cached copy until the plugin's version
changes. `ai-rulez validate` reports `AR961 plugin-version-drift` (warning) when a plugin's generated content differs
from its committed sidecar at `HEAD` while its version is unchanged. Bump `version` with every content change.

##### CI and hooks

```bash
ai-rulez generate --recursive --plugin --if-configured
ai-rulez verify --recursive --plugin --if-configured
```

`--if-configured` succeeds without doing anything in a project that has no `[plugin]` or marketplace authoring
configuration, so a shared hook catalog can run on every repository; it does not hide errors. A marketplace root is
processed once with its members. See [Poly hooks](poly-hooks.md) for a pre-commit setup and the
[`check` action](github-actions.md#governance-gate-check) (`plugin: true`) for CI.

A plugin-only root (no preset) is built in plugin mode by plain `generate --recursive`; see
[Nested configurations](monorepo.md#nested-configurations).

#### See also

- [Agent Plugins](agent-plugins.md)
- [Publish](publish.md)
- [Installed plugins](installed-plugins.md)

## Agent Plugins

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/agent-plugins/

The `agent-plugins` plugin runtime packages your skills and MCP servers as an [Agent Plugins](https://agent-plugins.org)
directory: a root `plugin.json`, a `skills/` tree and an `mcp.json`, which any client that implements the standard can
load. ai-rulez validates the package against the official JSON Schemas of the spec version you choose, and drops (and
reports) anything a conformant client would skip.

| Spec | Status | `$schema` of `plugin.json` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `1.0.0` | published; the default | `https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json` |
| `1.1.0` | working draft | `https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.1.0/plugin.schema.json` |

`mcp.json` carries the matching `mcp.schema.json`. The `copilot` runtime and the `codex` runtime with
`[plugin.codex] manifest = "root"` write the same package and follow the same `spec` (see
[Authoring plugins](plugins.md#runtime-specific-settings)).

#### Example

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml
version = "5.0"
name = "acme-tools"

[plugin]
name = "acme-tools"
version = "1.2.0"
description = "Code review skills and an MCP server for Acme repositories."
license = "MIT"
repository = "https://github.com/acme/acme-tools"
keywords = ["review", "mcp"]
runtimes = ["agent-plugins"]
include = ["scripts/**"]          # ship .ai-rulez/scripts/ in the package
# spec = "1.1.0"                  # optional; 1.0.0 when unset

[plugin.author]
name = "Acme Tooling"
email = "tooling@acme.example"

[[plugin.mcp]]
name = "acme-docs"
command = "${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/mcp-launch.sh"
args = ["serve"]
env = { ACME_TOKEN = "${ACME_TOKEN}" }
```

The source tree holds `.ai-rulez/skills/review-pr/` (a `SKILL.md` and `scripts/lint.sh`) and
`.ai-rulez/scripts/mcp-launch.sh`.

```bash
ai-rulez generate --plugin
```

```text
WARN  Agent Plugins: env ACME_TOKEN = "${ACME_TOKEN}" is dropped: Agent Plugins expands no environment placeholder, so the client must supply ACME_TOKEN itself ...
INFO  Plugin generation complete files=...
```

The package is written at the project root:

```text
plugin.json
mcp.json
skills/review-pr/SKILL.md
skills/review-pr/scripts/lint.sh
scripts/mcp-launch.sh
.ai-rulez-generated.json
```

`plugin.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json",
  "name": "acme-tools",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "description": "Code review skills and an MCP server for Acme repositories.",
  "author": {
    "name": "Acme Tooling",
    "email": "tooling@acme.example"
  },
  "repository": "https://github.com/acme/acme-tools",
  "license": "MIT",
  "keywords": ["review", "mcp"]
}
```

`mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/mcp.schema.json",
  "mcpServers": {
    "acme-docs": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "./scripts/mcp-launch.sh",
      "args": ["serve"]
    }
  }
}
```

The `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/` command became `./`, and the `ACME_TOKEN` forward was dropped: the client must provide that
variable itself. The drop is reported as `AR9O3`, so `validate --strict` exits 2 until you remove the `env` line.

Check the package:

```bash
ai-rulez verify --plugin      # fails when a generated file was edited or no longer matches its sources
ai-rulez validate --strict    # AR9O0-AR9O5 for anything a conformant client would skip
```

#### Field mapping

| ai-rulez | Package | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[plugin] name` | `plugin.json` `name` | 1-64 characters from `a-z0-9.-`, starting and ending alphanumeric, no `--` or `..` |
| `[plugin] version`, `description`, `homepage`, `repository`, `license`, `keywords` | the same keys | `version` may come from `version_from` |
| `[plugin.author]` `name`, `email`, `url` | `author` | omitted when empty |
| `[plugin] spec` | `$schema` of `plugin.json` and `mcp.json` | |
| `[plugin.interface]` (codex root layout only) | `extensions["com.openai"].interface` | keys sorted |
| skills (`.ai-rulez/skills/<name>/`) | `skills/<name>/`, with `SKILL.md`, `scripts/`, `references/` and other files | a skill without a `description`, or whose `name` differs from its directory, is not packaged |
| `[[plugin.mcp]]`, or `[[mcp_servers]]` when the plugin declares none | `mcp.json` `mcpServers.<name>` | see [MCP servers](#mcp-servers) |
| `enabled = false` on a server | not packaged | the format has no disabled flag; reported as `AR9O4` |
| `[plugin] include` | the matched files, at their relative path | see [Bundling files](#bundling-files) |
| agents, commands, hooks | not written | outside the standard; see [Extensions](#extensions) |
| rules, context | not written | read back on [import](#import) only |

#### MCP servers

| Server | `mcp.json` entry |
| --- | --- |
| stdio (`command`) | `type = "stdio"`, `command`, `args`, `env` |
| `transport = "http"` | `type = "streamable-http"`, `url`; the URL must be HTTPS, or HTTP to localhost |
| `transport = "sse"` | `type = "sse"`, `url` |

Clients expand only `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` and `${PLUGIN_DATA}`, and only in `args`, `env` values and `cwd`. ai-rulez
applies these rules:

- `command` is one token: a bare name (`npx`) or a `./` path inside the package. `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/server` is
  rewritten to `./bin/server`. A `./` path that is not in the package is a warning (`AR9O2`); ship the file with
  [`include`](#bundling-files).
- An `env` entry that only forwards a variable of the same name (`API_KEY = "${API_KEY}"`) is left out, with a
  warning (`AR9O3`). The client has to supply `API_KEY`.
- Any other `${VAR}` in `args`, `env`, `url` or `headers` is an error (`AR9O3`): the server is not packaged,
  `validate` fails and `publish` stops.
- `PLUGIN_ROOT` and `PLUGIN_DATA` may not be set in `env`; the client supplies them.

#### Bundling files

A package may carry arbitrary files beside `plugin.json`, `mcp.json` and `skills/`, and a stdio `command` may point
into them. `[plugin] include` lists globs of files to copy:

- Globs are matched against the content root: `[plugin] content_root` when set, otherwise the config directory
  (`.ai-rulez/`). The matches are written at the same relative path at the package root, so
  `.ai-rulez/scripts/mcp-launch.sh` becomes `scripts/mcp-launch.sh`. For the other runtimes, which have no `include`,
  keep such a file at the repository root yourself (see [Authoring plugins](plugins.md#mcp-servers)).
- `**` crosses directories, `*` and `?` do not, and a trailing `/` matches everything below a directory.
- Matched files are copied verbatim, keeping their relative path and executable bit, and are recorded in
  `.ai-rulez-generated.json`, so `verify --plugin` reports a changed or missing copy.
- `plugin.json`, `mcp.json`, `skills/` and the provenance sidecar are never matched, so a broad glob cannot overwrite
  them.
- A glob that is absolute or contains `..` is rejected when the configuration loads.

`include` applies to the packages this page describes (`agent-plugins`, `copilot`, and `codex` with the root layout).
For copying shared reference files into every skill, see
[Shared resources across skills](plugins.md#shared-resources-across-skills).

#### Extensions

Content only one client understands goes under a reverse-domain namespace, either as manifest data
(`plugin.json` `extensions.<namespace>`) or as files (`<namespace>/...`). Clients ignore namespaces they do not
implement.

| Namespace | Content | Written by `generate --plugin` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `com.openai` | the Codex `interface` block (manifest data) | with the `codex` root layout |
| `com.github.copilot` | `agents/<name>.agent.md` | with the `copilot` runtime |
| `com.anthropic.claude-code` | `agents/<name>.md`, `commands/<name>.md`, `hooks/hooks.json` | no; read on import |
| `io.github.goldziher.ai-rulez` | `rules/<name>.md`, `context/<name>.md` | no; read on import |

#### Validation

`validate` builds the package in memory and checks it as a client would load it. `publish` runs the same check
on the bundle it packages, in `--dry-run` as well, and stops with exit status 2 on the first error. Only single-plugin
projects are checked by `validate`; marketplace members are checked when they are published.

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `AR9O0` | `plugin.json` is missing or invalid, the spec version is unsupported, or an extension namespace is invalid |
| `AR9O1` | a skill breaks the Agent Skills rules (name, description, frontmatter) or is not at `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` |
| `AR9O2` | `mcp.json` or a server fails the schema or the rules for `command`, `url` and headers |
| `AR9O3` | an unsupported `${VAR}` placeholder |
| `AR9O4` | a field or server that cannot be packaged was left out (warning) |
| `AR9O5` | a path or link resolves outside the package root, or a file cannot be read |

`ai-rulez validate --explain AR9O3` prints the rule with examples.

Every generated file is recorded with its `Content-Hash` in `.ai-rulez-generated.json`, so `verify --plugin` covers `plugin.json`, `mcp.json`, the skills and included files. The output is deterministic: sorted,
no timestamps, two-space JSON with a trailing newline.

#### Publishing

The standard defines no archive, registry or signature. The package travels in the regular [publish](publish.md)
outputs (release archive, npm package or OCI artifact) and is signed with the rest of the release.

To get a directory that holds only the Agent Plugins files, without the other runtimes' manifests, use the
`agent-plugins` emitter:

```bash
ai-rulez publish emit agent-plugins --output-dir out
```

```text
out/acme-tools/plugin.json
out/acme-tools/mcp.json
out/acme-tools/scripts/mcp-launch.sh
out/acme-tools/skills/review-pr/SKILL.md
out/acme-tools/skills/review-pr/scripts/lint.sh
```

Like every `publish` command, `publish emit` runs the [publish preflight](publish.md#pipeline) first: the project must
be committed and locked (`ai-rulez lock`), and the bundle up to date. The emitter reads the generated package back,
validates it and writes it again, one directory per plugin. To convert
the package to another spec version, set the `spec` option:

```toml
[[publish.emitters]]
name = "agent-plugins"
options = { spec = "1.1.0" }
```

#### Import

`ai-rulez convert` reads an Agent Plugins directory into an `.ai-rulez/` tree:

```bash
ai-rulez convert --from agent-plugins --source ./some-plugin --into "$PWD/.ai-rulez" --write
```

`--into` is relative to `--source` unless absolute; without it the tree is written to `./some-plugin/.ai-rulez/`.

| Package | Becomes |
| --- | --- |
| `plugin.json` | the `[plugin]` block, with `runtimes = ["agent-plugins"]` (and `spec` when not 1.0.0) |
| `skills/<name>/` | skills, with their `scripts/`, `references/` and other files |
| `mcp.json` | `[[mcp_servers]]` |
| `com.anthropic.claude-code`, `com.github.copilot`, `io.github.goldziher.ai-rulez` | agents, commands and rules |

The report lists what has no equivalent: other files at the package root, unknown namespaces, `hooks/hooks.json` and a
server `cwd`. A manifest without `version` or `description` cannot form a `[plugin]` block, so none is written and the
report says so. The generated-file header ai-rulez writes into Markdown is removed on import.

#### See also

- [Authoring plugins](plugins.md): all plugin runtimes and the `[plugin]` block.
- [Publish](publish.md)

## Agentic Resource Discovery

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/ard/

The `ard` emitter publishes your skills, remote MCP servers and plugin for discovery through
[Agentic Resource Discovery](https://agenticresourcediscovery.org/) (ARD): one `ard.json` manifest that registries and
agents fetch from `https://<domain>/.well-known/ard.json`.

!!! warning "The specification is a proposal"
    ai-rulez implements ARD **spec v0.91** and validates the manifest against the entry schema of
    [ards-project/ard-spec](https://github.com/ards-project/ard-spec) at commit `b76f235`. Media types and field names
    can still change.

#### Example

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml
version = "5.0"
name = "acme-tools"

[plugin]
name = "acme-tools"
version = "1.2.0"
description = "Code review skills and an MCP server for Acme repositories."
repository = "https://github.com/acme/acme-tools"
keywords = ["review", "mcp"]
runtimes = ["agent-plugins", "claude"]

[plugin.author]
name = "Acme Tooling"

[[mcp_servers]]
name = "acme-search"
description = "Search Acme documentation."
transport = "http"
url = "https://docs.acme.example/mcp"
headers = { Authorization = "Bearer ${DOCS_TOKEN}" }

[ard]
publisher = "acme.example"
namespace = "tools"

[ard.queries]
acme-search = ["search the acme docs", "find the acme api reference"]
```

With one skill, `review-pr`, in `.ai-rulez/skills/`:

```bash
ai-rulez publish emit ard --output-dir ard
```

```text
WARN  ard: AR9S3 urn:air:acme.example:tools:acme-tools: no representativeQueries: ...
WARN  ard: AR9S3 urn:air:acme.example:tools:review-pr: no representativeQueries: ...
wrote ard/ard.json
```

`ard/ard.json` (trimmed):

```json
{
  "entries": [
    {
      "identifier": "urn:air:acme.example:tools:acme-search",
      "displayName": "acme-search",
      "type": "application/mcp-server-card+json",
      "data": {
        "$schema": "https://static.modelcontextprotocol.io/schemas/v1/server-card.schema.json",
        "description": "Search Acme documentation.",
        "name": "example.acme/acme-search",
        "remotes": [ ... ],
        "version": "1.2.0"
      },
      "description": "Search Acme documentation.",
      "representativeQueries": ["search the acme docs", "find the acme api reference"],
      "updatedAt": "2026-11-05T16:23:33Z"
    },
    {
      "identifier": "urn:air:acme.example:tools:acme-tools",
      "displayName": "acme-tools",
      "type": "application/vnd.ai-rulez.plugin+json",
      "url": "https://github.com/acme/acme-tools/releases/download/v1.2.0/acme-tools-1.2.0.tar.gz",
      "description": "Code review skills and an MCP server for Acme repositories.",
      "tags": ["agent-plugins", "mcp", "review"],
      "version": "1.2.0",
      "updatedAt": "2026-11-05T16:23:33Z"
    },
    {
      "identifier": "urn:air:acme.example:tools:review-pr",
      "displayName": "review-pr",
      "type": "application/ai-skill+md",
      "url": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/acme/acme-tools/v1.2.0/.ai-rulez/skills/review-pr/SKILL.md",
      "description": "Review a pull request against Acme conventions. Use when asked to review a diff or PR.",
      "updatedAt": "2026-11-05T16:23:33Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

The `AR9S3` warnings say the skill and the plugin have no representative queries; see
[Representative queries](#representative-queries) for where they come from.

#### Configuration

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `publisher` | string | required | The fully qualified domain name that serves `/.well-known/ard.json` |
| `namespace` | string | required | A short name for this project's resources; colons separate sub-segments (`team:tools`) |
| `base_url` | string | none | An `https` URL where the skill files are served. When set, skill entries point at `<base_url>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and the emitter writes those files next to `ard.json` |
| `plugin_type` | string | `application/vnd.ai-rulez.plugin+json` | The media type of the plugin entry |
| `[ard.queries]` | table of string lists | none | Representative queries by resource name; replaces the derived queries of that resource |

Every identifier is `urn:air:<publisher>:<namespace>:<name>`. Configuration loading rejects a publisher that is not a
fully qualified domain name, and a namespace or name with characters outside letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.

#### Generate

| Command | Output |
| --- | --- |
| `ai-rulez publish emit ard [--output-dir DIR]` | only the manifest (and skill files with `base_url`), in `DIR` (default `emit/ard/`) |
| `ai-rulez publish --emit ard` | `dist/emit/ard/ard.json`, as part of a [release](publish.md) |

Add `[[publish.emitters]] name = "ard"` to run it on every publish. Both commands run the
[publish preflight](publish.md#pipeline) first, so the project must be committed and locked, with the plugin bundle
generated.

#### Entries

| Resource | `type` | Location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Root skill | `application/ai-skill+md` | `url`: with `base_url`, `<base_url>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`; otherwise the raw `SKILL.md` on GitHub at the release tag `v<version>` |
| Remote MCP server (enabled `[[mcp_servers]]` or `[[plugin.mcp]]` with a URL) | `application/mcp-server-card+json` | `data`: the [MCP server card](mcp-server-card.md) |
| Plugin | `plugin_type` | `url`: the release archive on the repository's releases page, or `<base_url>/<archive>` when there is no repository |

- Only root skills are listed; domain skills are not.
- Stdio MCP servers are left out, because a server card describes remote endpoints. A remote server whose URL is not
  `https` is an error (`AR9S2`). Servers whose URL could carry a secret are skipped the same way as for [server cards](mcp-server-card.md#skipped-servers). Header and environment
  values never reach the manifest.
- Raw skill URLs are only known for github.com. For another host, set `base_url`.
- A plugin built with the [Agent Plugins](agent-plugins.md) runtime is tagged `agent-plugins`.

| Field | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `displayName` | the resource name |
| `description` | the skill's or server's description, or the plugin description |
| `version` | a skill's `metadata.version` frontmatter; the plugin version |
| `tags` | skill `keywords` frontmatter; plugin `keywords` |
| `capabilities` | the plugin `category` |
| `updatedAt` | the release time: `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, else the commit time. The same commit always gives the same bytes |

#### Representative queries

Registries build their search index from `representativeQueries`. Each entry needs 2 to 5; outside that range is a
warning (`AR9S3`). For a skill they are taken, in order, from:

1. the frontmatter list `representative_queries`;
2. the prompts of the skill's eval cases that expect it to trigger (`expect_trigger: true`), excluding near misses;
3. the frontmatter list `triggers`.

A plugin takes the first query of each of its skills, then the second, and so on. An MCP server has nothing to derive
queries from, so list them under `[ard.queries]`. An `[ard.queries]` entry replaces the derived queries of that
resource.

```markdown
---
name: review-pr
description: Review a pull request against Acme conventions. Use when asked to review a diff or PR.
representative_queries:
  - review this pull request
  - check my diff against the acme conventions
---
```

#### Validation

`validate` builds the manifest in memory and checks it against the pinned schema. `publish` runs the same
check and prints the emitter's warnings in `--dry-run` too.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [AR9S0](strict-validation.md#ar9s0-ard-manifest-invalid) | error | the manifest fails the schema |
| [AR9S1](strict-validation.md#ar9s1-ard-identifier-invalid) | error | an identifier breaks the `urn:air` grammar, or two resources share one |
| [AR9S2](strict-validation.md#ar9s2-ard-entry-invalid) | error | an entry has both or neither of `url` and `data`, or a non-https `url` |
| [AR9S3](strict-validation.md#ar9s3-ard-queries-out-of-range) | warning | fewer than 2 or more than 5 representative queries |
| [AR9S4](strict-validation.md#ar9s4-ard-not-declared) | error | the `ard` emitter is requested without an `[ard]` table |

#### Hosting

Serve the manifest at `https://<publisher>/.well-known/ard.json` with:

- HTTPS only;
- `Content-Type: application/json`;
- `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so browser-based agents can read it.

With `base_url`, copy the whole output directory (`ard.json` and `skills/`) to the host.

Other ways to point consumers at the manifest:

- **HTML link.** Add `<link rel="ard" href="https://acme.example/ard.json">` to a page's `<head>`.
- **DNS.** The specification describes DNS-based discovery but does not settle the record format yet. ai-rulez
  writes no DNS record; check the current specification before adding one.

#### Not generated

The optional `trustManifest` is not written: no trust framework can verify a Sigstore identity as a domain credential.

#### See also

- [MCP server cards](mcp-server-card.md)
- [Publish](publish.md)

## MCP server cards

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/mcp-server-card/

The `mcp-server-card` emitter writes an [MCP Server Card](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/seps/2127-mcp-server-cards)
(SEP-2127) for each remote MCP server of your project. A card is a small JSON document that a client or registry reads
before it connects: it names the server and lists the endpoints and the headers the client must supply.

!!! warning "Experimental schema"
    The card schema comes from the experimental
    [server-card extension](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/experimental-ext-server-card) and can change before a
    versioned schema is published. ai-rulez pins it at commit `526201b`.

#### Example

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml
version = "5.0"
name = "acme-tools"

[plugin]
name = "acme-tools"
version = "1.2.0"
description = "Code review skills and an MCP server for Acme repositories."
repository = "https://github.com/acme/acme-tools"
runtimes = ["claude"]

[plugin.author]
name = "Acme Tooling"

[[mcp_servers]]
name = "acme-search"
description = "Search Acme documentation."
transport = "http"
url = "https://docs.acme.example/mcp"
headers = { Authorization = "Bearer ${DOCS_TOKEN}" }
```

```bash
ai-rulez publish emit mcp-server-card --output-dir cards
```

```text
wrote cards/acme-search.json
```

`cards/acme-search.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://static.modelcontextprotocol.io/schemas/v1/server-card.schema.json",
  "name": "io.github.acme/acme-search",
  "description": "Search Acme documentation.",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "remotes": [
    {
      "type": "streamable-http",
      "url": "https://docs.acme.example/mcp",
      "headers": [
        {
          "name": "Authorization",
          "isRequired": true,
          "isSecret": true
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The header value (`Bearer ${DOCS_TOKEN}`) is not in the card; the card only says the client must send an
`Authorization` header and that it is a secret.

#### Generate

| Command | Output |
| --- | --- |
| `ai-rulez publish emit mcp-server-card [--output-dir DIR]` | only the cards, in `DIR` (default `emit/mcp-server-card/`); no release is built |
| `ai-rulez publish --emit mcp-server-card` | the cards in `dist/emit/mcp-server-card/`, as part of a [release](publish.md) |

Both run the [publish preflight](publish.md#pipeline) first, so the project must be committed and locked
(`ai-rulez lock`), and its plugin bundle up to date. To run the emitter on every publish, declare it in the configuration:

```toml
[[publish.emitters]]
name = "mcp-server-card"
options = { namespace = "com.acme", version = "2.0.0" }   # both optional
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `namespace` | see [Name](#what-a-card-holds) | the reverse-DNS prefix of each card's `name` |
| `version` | the `[plugin]` version, else `0.0.0` | the `version` of every card |

The emitter reads the enabled servers of `[[mcp_servers]]` and `[[plugin.mcp]]`. It fails when none of them has a URL.

#### What a card holds

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | `<namespace>/<server>`. Characters outside letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` in the server name become `-`. The namespace is the `namespace` option, else the reversed `[ard] publisher` (`acme.example` gives `example.acme`), else derived from the repository: `github.com/acme/...` gives `io.github.acme`, another host such as `git.acme.test/team/...` gives `test.acme.git.team` |
| `description` | the server's `description`, cut to 100 characters, or `MCP server <name>` without one |
| `version` | the `version` option, else the plugin version, else `0.0.0` |
| `remotes[].type` | `streamable-http` for `transport = "http"` (or a `url` with no transport); `sse` for `transport = "sse"` |
| `remotes[].url` | the server URL, as written |
| `remotes[].headers` | one required input per header, by name. `isSecret` is set when the name looks like a credential (such as `Authorization`), or the value is a `${VAR}` placeholder, including one resolved from `.env` |

`title`, `icons`, `repository`, `websiteUrl`, URL variables, `supportedProtocolVersions` and `_meta` are not generated.

#### Skipped servers

A card is public, so the emitter never writes a value and skips servers that could leak one. Each skipped server is
reported as a warning; the note never repeats a URL.

| Server | Result |
| --- | --- |
| stdio (a `command`, no `url`) | skipped: a card describes remote endpoints only |
| URL with a query string or a fragment | skipped |
| URL with an unresolved `${...}` placeholder | skipped |
| URL path segment that looks like a credential (a prefix such as `sk-`, `ghp_` or `AKIA`, a known token shape, or an opaque string of 32 or more letters and digits, including a UUID) | skipped |
| URL with credentials (`https://user:pass@host`) | refused with an error |

Environment values are never read into a card.

#### With ARD

The [Agentic Resource Discovery](ard.md) manifest lists each remote server as an `application/mcp-server-card+json`
entry whose `data` is the same card. ARD additionally requires an `https` URL.

#### See also

- [Publish](publish.md): the release pipeline and the other emitters.
- [Agentic Resource Discovery](ard.md).

## Publish

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/publish/

`ai-rulez publish` turns the generated [plugin bundle](plugins.md) into release artifacts: a reproducible `tar.gz`, a
manifest, checksums, release notes and a plan. Building is local and offline. Nothing leaves the machine unless you pass
`--execute --yes`, and then the upload goes through the platform's own tooling (`gh` for GitHub releases, `npm` for
npm, the Docker credential store for OCI registries). ai-rulez never stores or logs a credential.

[Emitters](#emitters) render extra formats from the same plugin; the [`ard`](ard.md),
[`mcp-server-card`](mcp-server-card.md) and [`agent-plugins`](agent-plugins.md) emitters each have their own page.

#### Quick start

From a project with a `[plugin]` block (see [Authoring plugins](plugins.md#quick-start)):

```bash
ai-rulez generate --plugin
ai-rulez lock
git add -A && git commit -m "acme-tools 1.2.0"
git tag v1.2.0 && git push --tags

ai-rulez publish --to github-release --dry-run      # preflight, then print the artifacts and the command
ai-rulez publish --to github-release --execute --yes
ai-rulez publish verify dist
```

The dry run prints what it would write and run:

```text
preflight   validate --strict ok | lock ok | verify --plugin ok | secrets 0
signature   none
artifacts   would write 6 files to /work/acme-tools/dist
            RELEASE_NOTES.md                         sha256:188cc8d8...  403 bytes
            SHA256SUMS                               sha256:c0df2f4d...  350 bytes
            acme-tools-1.2.0.manifest.json           sha256:d4a01a9e...  3299 bytes
            acme-tools-1.2.0.tar.gz                  sha256:110cc9fa...  1937 bytes
            ai-rulez.lock                            sha256:d248d9a0...  645 bytes
            publish-plan.json                        sha256:3564a26b...  2016 bytes
would run   gh release create v1.2.0 --repo acme/acme-tools --title 'acme-tools 1.2.0' --notes-file RELEASE_NOTES.md --verify-tag acme-tools-1.2.0.tar.gz acme-tools-1.2.0.manifest.json ai-rulez.lock SHA256SUMS
credentials gh authentication (GH_TOKEN or `gh auth login`); not read by ai-rulez
```

Without `--to`, `ai-rulez publish` only builds `dist/`. `publish verify` checks a dist directory or a downloaded
release:

```text
verified acme-tools 1.2.0: 4 files match SHA256SUMS, the manifest and the archive (signature: none)
```

#### Pipeline

1. **Resolve.** `[plugin] name` and `version` are required.
2. **Preflight**, stopping before anything is written:
    - `validate` (the content checks, failing at your `fail_on`, at most `error`);
    - `lock --check`;
    - `verify --plugin`;
    - a secret scan of every bundle file, using the security scan's patterns.

    A symlink in the bundle is an error, and the machine-local overlay is never loaded. When the bundle holds an
    [Agent Plugins](agent-plugins.md) package, it is checked against the specification (`AR9O0`-`AR9O5`), in
    `--dry-run` as well.
3. **Policy gates** from [`[publish]`](#configuration): `require_signature` (`AR9N7`) and `require_approved`
   (`AR9N8`).
4. **Build** the dist directory, signing the archive when asked.
5. **Upload**, only with `--to` and `--execute --yes`.

The working tree must be clean and every bundle file must be tracked by git (`AR9N3`). `--allow-dirty` waives both;
the manifest then records `dirty = true`. Changes under the dist directory are ignored.

#### Dist directory

| File | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `<name>-<version>.tar.gz` | the bundle: every file `generate --plugin` writes for the published runtimes |
| `<name>-<version>.manifest.json` | each file with its size and digest, the source (repository, commit, dirty flag), the lock tree, the runtimes, and the signature, SBOM and approval records ([schema](schema.md)) |
| `ai-rulez.lock` | a copy of the lock without its `[[approval]]` records, so reviewer emails and notes stay in the repository. `lock --check` against the copy behaves as against the original |
| `SHA256SUMS` | `sha256sum -c` format; every file except itself and the plan |
| `RELEASE_NOTES.md` | the bundle digest, runtimes, lock tree, commit, and the [changes since the previous release](#release-notes) |
| `publish-plan.json` | the artifacts with digests and the exact commands `--execute` runs; no timestamps or local paths |
| `<name>-<version>.tar.gz.sigstore.json` | with signing: the archive signature |
| `<name>-<version>.attestation.sigstore.json` | with signing: a signed statement binding the name, version, archive, lock and SBOM |
| `<name>-<version>.sbom.cdx.json` | with `--sbom`: the project's CycloneDX [SBOM](sbom.md) |
| `marketplace/` | with `--marketplace`: the [pinned marketplace index](#pinned-marketplace-and-channels) |
| `emit/<emitter>/` | output of [emitters](#emitters) and `--template` files |
| `npm/`, `oci/manifest.json` | the npm package directory, or the OCI manifest, for those targets |

The archive holds only files that `generate --plugin` writes. A file you keep in the repository yourself, such as an
MCP launcher script at the repository root, is not in it; ship such files with
[`[plugin] include`](agent-plugins.md#bundling-files) or install the plugin from git.

`--dist DIR` changes the directory (default `dist`). It must be new, empty, or the output of an earlier publish, whose
artifacts are replaced; any other non-empty directory is refused.

The archive is byte-identical for the same bundle and commit: entries sorted, regular files only, uid/gid 0, modes
`0644` or `0755`, no gzip name or time. The mtime is `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, else the committer time of `HEAD`. Build
releases with one ai-rulez version: the gzip bytes can differ between versions. The signature is the only artifact that
differs between runs.

#### Targets

| `--to` | Upload | Credentials |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `github-release` | `gh release create` | `gh` (`GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `gh auth login`) |
| `npm` | `npm pack`, then `npm publish` | your npm config (`npm login`, `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`) |
| `oci` | an OCI artifact pushed to a registry | the Docker credential store (`docker login`) |

##### GitHub release

```bash
ai-rulez publish --to github-release --execute --yes
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--tag` | `v<version>` | release tag; it must already exist on the remote (`gh ... --verify-tag`) |
| `--repo` | `[publish.github_release] repo`, else `[plugin] repository`, else the origin remote | `OWNER/REPO` or `HOST/OWNER/REPO` |
| `--force` | off | upload into an existing release, replacing its assets (`gh release upload --clobber`) |

Without `--force`, `--execute` refuses a release that already exists. A signed release also uploads the signature and
attestation; an SBOM release uploads the SBOM. `gh` runs with a filtered environment (the system basics, the `GH_*` and
`GITHUB_*` token and host variables, `XDG_*` directories, proxy and certificate settings). A missing `gh` is `AR9N4`.

##### npm

```bash
ai-rulez publish --to npm --npm-scope @acme --dry-run
```

```text
would run   npm pack --ignore-scripts --pack-destination npm ./npm/package
would run   npm publish ./npm/acme-acme-tools-1.2.0.tgz --access restricted --ignore-scripts
registry    https://registry.npmjs.org/ (npm runs from an empty temporary directory with explicit --userconfig and --globalconfig; no project .npmrc applies)
credentials npm authentication (npm login, or NODE_AUTH_TOKEN in an .npmrc); not read by ai-rulez
```

The package is written to `npm/package/`: the bundle files plus a release `package.json`.

- **Name.** `<scope>/<plugin name>`. A scope is required (`[publish.npm] scope` or `--npm-scope`), so nothing lands in
  the unscoped public namespace by accident. A generated runtime name such as `@acme/pi-acme-tools` becomes
  `@acme/acme-tools`.
- **Access.** `restricted` unless `[publish.npm] access = "public"` or `--public`.
- **Dist-tag.** `--channel NAME`. A prerelease version (`1.4.0-rc.1`) needs one (`AR9N6`).
- **`package.json`.** Carries `files`, the repository, and an `ai-rulez` key with the archive digest, lock tree and
  runtimes. Existing runtime metadata (Pi resources, OpenCode entry points and dependencies, keywords, license) is kept.
  A manifest with `private: true` or any `scripts` field is rejected. When the bundle has its own runtime
  `package.json` (OpenCode, Pi), that manifest is rewritten, so the bundle's `.ai-rulez-generated.json` is left out of
  the npm package; the release archive keeps it.
- **Existing versions.** `--execute` re-verifies the dist directory, runs `npm view` and refuses a version the registry
  already has.
- **Isolation.** npm runs from an empty temporary directory with your user and global npm config named explicitly, so a
  `.npmrc` committed in the repository never applies. `--execute` asks npm for the effective registry and refuses one
  that is not `https://`.
- **Custom registry.** A registry set by `[publish.npm] registry` in the committed configuration would receive your
  npm token, so it is refused unless you confirm it with `--confirm-registry URL`. The public registry and a registry
  from your own npm configuration need no confirmation.
- **Signing.** The signature covers the release archive, not the tarball npm packs. `require_signature` therefore fails
  an npm release (`AR9N7`), and a signed npm release prints a warning. Publish the signed archive with
  `--to github-release` or `--to oci`.
- **Provenance.** `npm publish --provenance` only works inside CI with an OIDC identity, so it is not part of the plan.
  Run `publish --to npm` without `--execute` in that CI job, then run the two planned commands yourself with
  `--provenance` added to `npm publish`.

##### OCI

```bash
ai-rulez publish --to oci --oci-ref ghcr.io/acme/acme-tools --dry-run
```

```text
push        ghcr.io/acme/acme-tools:1.2.0 (manifest sha256:34e071ec...)
credentials registry credentials from the Docker credential store (`docker login`), read only for the registry named by ref
```

`--oci-ref` (or `[publish.oci] ref`) is a repository `host/path` without a tag; the tag is the plugin version (`+`
becomes `_`). The artifact layout:

```text
artifactType  application/vnd.ai-rulez.bundle.v1
config        application/vnd.ai-rulez.manifest.v1+json      the bundle manifest
layers        application/vnd.ai-rulez.bundle.v1.tar+gzip     the archive
              application/vnd.ai-rulez.lock.v1+toml           the lock
              application/vnd.cyclonedx+json                  the SBOM, with --sbom
              application/vnd.dev.sigstore.bundle.v0.3+json   the signature and attestation, when signed
annotations   org.opencontainers.image.{created,version,source,revision}
```

The manifest is reproducible and its digest is recorded in the plan; `--execute` rebuilds it from the dist files and
refuses to push if it differs. Because a tag is mutable, `--execute` also refuses to move an existing tag to a different
digest unless `--force`; pushing the identical artifact again is a no-op. Plain HTTP is used only for loopback
registries. Consumers should pin by digest: `ghcr.io/acme/acme-tools@sha256:...`.

##### Several plugins

A `[marketplace]` with `members` or domain plugins publishes one bundle per plugin, taken from the generated Claude
marketplace index (so the `claude` runtime must be generated):

```text
dist/plugins/<name>/   a complete dist directory per plugin
dist/aggregate/        plugins.json, marketplace/ and emit/ for all plugins, with SHA256SUMS and a plan
```

- `--only NAME` limits the plugins.
- Targets are per plugin: GitHub tags `<name>-v<version>`, npm packages `<scope>/<name>`, OCI repositories
  `<ref>/<name>`. `--tag` does not apply.
- `--runtime` keeps only the listed runtimes of each plugin; a member that ships none of them is refused (`AR9N6`).
- `--execute` checks every plugin's target first and uploads nothing if any check fails. A failure part-way (a
  registry outage) names the plugins already published; fix the cause and rerun, with `--force` where a release is
  already out.
- `publish verify dist` verifies every plugin and the aggregate checksums, and fails (`AR9N5`) when a listed plugin
  directory is missing or changed or an unlisted one is present. `plugins.json` is not signed; trust comes from each
  plugin's own signed release.

`publish` reads the Claude index closest to the project root, so with several
[`[[marketplaces_authoring]]`](plugins.md#several-marketplaces-from-one-root) entries it publishes only that one.

#### Pinned marketplace and channels

`--marketplace` writes `marketplace/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`: the bundle's Claude marketplace index with every
relative `source` replaced by one pinned to the release commit:

```json
"source": {
  "source": "github",
  "repo": "acme/acme-tools",
  "ref": "v1.2.0",
  "sha": "ee285bdde14184518b0317f7ea3bf1f2de93094b"
}
```

| Plugin location | Source type |
| --- | --- |
| repository root on github.com | `github` (`repo`, `ref`, `sha`) |
| repository root on another host | `url` (`url`, `ref`, `sha`) |
| a subdirectory | `git-subdir` (`url`, `path`, `ref`, `sha`) |

Claude Code checks out `sha`, so the index stays valid if the tag moves. Every other field of the entry is kept.

`--channel NAME` writes `marketplace/<name>/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` instead, pinned to the ref that
`[publish.marketplace.channels]` names for that channel (the release tag when the channel is not listed). Commit each
channel's index to the branch users register as a marketplace. `--channel` is also the npm dist-tag.

#### Emitters

An emitter renders the files a distribution channel needs from the published plugin, without network access.
`--emit NAME` (repeatable) or `[[publish.emitters]]` runs it into `dist/emit/<name>/`. `ai-rulez publish emit NAME
[--output-dir DIR]` writes only that emitter's files (default `emit/<name>/`) and no release; it still runs the full
[preflight](#pipeline), so the project must be committed, locked and its bundle up to date.

| Emitter | Output | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cursor-team-marketplace` | `.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json` and `plugins/<name>/`, ready to commit to the repository a Cursor team marketplace imports; needs the `cursor` runtime | verified |
| `agent-plugins` | one validated [Agent Plugins](agent-plugins.md#publishing) directory per plugin, without other runtimes' files; needs the `agent-plugins` or `copilot` runtime, or `codex` with the root layout; option `spec` | verified |
| `ard` | the [Agentic Resource Discovery](ard.md) manifest `ard.json`; needs `[ard]` | verified |
| `mcp-server-card` | one [MCP server card](mcp-server-card.md) per remote MCP server; options `namespace`, `version` | verified |
| `port` | one [Port](https://docs.port.io/api-reference/create-an-entity/) entity JSON per plugin and skill, plus `index.json`; option `blueprint` (default `agent_skill`) | experimental |
| `aws-agent-registry` | one [`CreateRegistryRecord`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/agent-registry-control/latest/APIReference/API_CreateRegistryRecord.html) request body per skill and per plugin | experimental |
| `kiro-steering` | [Kiro steering](https://kiro.dev/docs/steering/) files at `.kiro/steering/*.md` from the root rules and skills, plus `distribution.json` for MDM packaging | experimental |
| `template` | any text, from a Go `text/template` over the release (`--template FILE`) | verified |

Experimental emitters write formats that have no published schema to test against. They refuse to run without
`--experimental` (`AR9N6`) and then report `AR9N9` as a warning.

A template sees the fields `Name`, `Version`, `Tag`, `Repo`, `Commit`, `AIRulezVersion`, `Runtimes`, `BundleFile`,
`BundleDigest`, `BundleSize`, `LockTree`, `LockDigest` and `Files`, and the function `json`:

```text
{{ .Name }} {{ .Version }} ({{ .BundleDigest }}) from {{ .Repo }}@{{ .Commit }}
```

#### Signing

```bash
ai-rulez publish --to github-release --sign-key cosign.key --execute --yes   # a key
ai-rulez publish --to github-release --sign-keyless --execute --yes          # Fulcio + Rekor, e.g. in CI
```

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--sign-key FILE` | sign with a PEM private key; use ECDSA P-256 (cosign keys work). The password comes from `AI_RULEZ_SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD`, `COSIGN_PASSWORD`, or the variable named by `--sign-key-password-env` |
| `--sign-tlog` | with `--sign-key`: also record the signature in the Rekor log |
| `--sign-keyless` | sign with a short-lived Fulcio certificate and record it in Rekor. The certificate names your identity in a public log, so use a key for a private repository |
| `--sign-token-env`, `--sign-interactive`, `--fulcio-url`, `--rekor-url` | keyless options |

`--dry-run` signs nothing and contacts nothing. Signing uses the same code as [`ai-rulez sign`](signing.md).

A release is signed twice:

- `<name>-<version>.tar.gz.sigstore.json` is a signature over the exact archive bytes, the form
  `cosign sign-blob --bundle` writes, so `cosign verify-blob --bundle <file>.sigstore.json --key cosign.pub <file>`
  verifies it.
- `<name>-<version>.attestation.sigstore.json` is a signed in-toto statement whose subjects are the archive, the lock
  copy and the SBOM, and which records the plugin name, version, lock tree, source and approval summary. It ties the
  unsigned manifest to the signed files.

`publish verify` reports a signed release as `unverified` until you name who you trust:

```bash
ai-rulez publish verify dist --key cosign.pub
ai-rulez publish verify ghcr.io/acme/acme-tools@sha256:... \
  --identity https://github.com/acme/acme-tools/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v1.2.0 \
  --issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
```

```text
verified acme-tools 1.2.0: 6 files match SHA256SUMS, the manifest and the archive (signature: verified)
signer: key sha256:afde1a64...
```

Naming a trusted signer (`--key`, `--identity`) implies `--require-signature`, so a release whose signature was
stripped fails. A keyless check uses `--trusted-root`, or the root `ai-rulez trust update` cached.

#### Policy gates

```toml
[publish]
require_signature = true   # AR9N7: publish fails unless it signs the archive
require_approved  = true   # AR9N8: publish fails unless the governance policy's items are approved
```

`require_approved` uses [approvals](approvals.md): every item the `[governance]` policy selects needs a valid approval
in `ai-rulez.lock`. It also fails when no policy selects anything. When a policy is active, the manifest records
`approval = { required, approved }` whether or not the gate is on.

#### SBOM

`--sbom` runs `ai-rulez sbom` and ships the CycloneDX document next to the archive. The manifest records it, the OCI
artifact carries it as a layer, and `publish verify` checks it. The SBOM has no timestamp and no approval status, so it
keeps the release reproducible and no reviewer identity leaves the repository. See [SBOM](sbom.md).

#### Release notes

`RELEASE_NOTES.md` lists what changed in the lock since the previous release: added, changed and removed items (kind,
id, domain, short digest) and remote pins, never content. The previous release is the closest tag reachable from `HEAD`
other than the release tag (for a multi-plugin release, the closest earlier `<name>-v*` tag). `--since TAG` picks
another tag and fails when that tag holds no lock. Without a previous tag, the section is omitted.

#### Runtime filtering

`--runtime R` (repeatable) or `[publish] runtimes` limits the bundle to some of the plugin runtimes. The full bundle is
verified first; the subset is rendered again by the same generator, so shared files are identical. A runtime that is
not in `[plugin] runtimes` is an error (`AR9N6`). `--runtime` wins over the table.

#### Configuration

```toml
[publish]
runtimes = ["claude", "cursor"]   # default: the [plugin] runtimes
require_signature = false
require_approved = false
allow_dirty = false

[publish.github_release]
repo = "acme/acme-tools"          # default: [plugin] repository, else origin

[publish.oci]
ref = "ghcr.io/acme/acme-tools"   # no tag; the tag is the version

[publish.npm]
scope = "@acme"
access = "restricted"             # or "public"
registry = "https://npm.acme.example"

[publish.marketplace.channels]
canary = "main"                   # channel -> the git ref its index pins

[[publish.emitters]]
name = "agent-plugins"
options = { spec = "1.1.0" }

[[publish.emitters]]
name = "template"
template = "tools/release-entity.tmpl"   # inside the project, never through a symlink
output = "release-entity.json"
```

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `runtimes` | string list | the `[plugin] runtimes` | runtimes to publish |
| `require_signature` | bool | `false` | fail unless the archive is signed (`AR9N7`) |
| `require_approved` | bool | `false` | fail unless the governance policy's items are approved (`AR9N8`) |
| `allow_dirty` | bool | `false` | allow uncommitted changes, as `--allow-dirty` |
| `github_release.repo` | string | `[plugin] repository`, else origin | the release repository |
| `oci.ref` | string | none | OCI repository, without a tag |
| `npm.scope` | string | none | npm scope, required for `--to npm` |
| `npm.access` | string | `restricted` | `restricted` or `public` |
| `npm.registry` | string | your npm config | registry URL; needs `--confirm-registry` |
| `marketplace.channels` | table | none | channel name to git ref |
| `[[emitters]]` | `name`, `options`, `template`, `output` | none | emitters run on every publish |

There are no credential keys: registries authenticate through their own tools and environment. An unknown key under
`[publish]` fails the schema check. Flags win over the table, but a flag never lowers a policy the table sets.

#### Verify

`ai-rulez publish verify <dir|oci-ref>` checks, offline:

- every `SHA256SUMS` entry, and that no unlisted file is present (the plan and `SHA256SUMS` excepted);
- the manifest against the archive (every file, size and digest);
- the lock copy against the manifest;
- the plan against the manifest, so an edited plan cannot run a different command;
- the archive's determinism rules;
- with a trusted signer, the signature and the attestation;
- that the `name` and `version` in the archive's own runtime manifests match the release manifest.

An OCI reference is pulled into a temporary directory first; `verify` prints the digest it resolved to and warns when
you named a tag. Each file, and the archive's total uncompressed size, is capped at 512 MiB. Exit status: 0 verified,
1 unreadable, 2 mismatch.

#### Exit codes and errors

`publish` exits 0 when done, 1 when the run could not complete, and 2 when a gate failed. `--format json` prints the
result as JSON (on `publish`, `publish emit` and `publish verify`). The `--policy*` and `--discover-org` flags apply
an organization policy to the preflight, as for `validate`; see [Organization policy](policy.md).

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `AR9N0` | a preflight gate failed: strict validation, the lock check or plugin verification |
| `AR9N1` | the bundle holds a symlink, a path outside the project, or a name that cannot name a release file |
| `AR9N2` | the secret scan found a credential in the bundle |
| `AR9N3` | no version, a dirty tree, an untracked bundle file, or no commit |
| `AR9N4` | the upload failed: `gh` or `npm` missing, the release or version exists, or the tool exited non-zero |
| `AR9N5` | `publish verify` found a mismatch |
| `AR9N6` | invalid `[publish]` table, flag or option: unknown emitter, runtime or channel, a bad tag, scope or OCI reference |
| `AR9N7` | `require_signature` is set and the bundle is unsigned, or its signature does not verify |
| `AR9N8` | `require_approved` is set and selected content lacks a valid approval |
| `AR9N9` | an experimental emitter ran (warning) |

`ai-rulez validate --explain AR9N3` prints a code's explanation.

## Strict validation

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/strict-validation/

`ai-rulez validate` checks that the configuration loads and matches the schema, then lints the content: globs that
select nothing, links and references that point nowhere, hooks that cannot run, oversized or duplicate items, and
security problems such as secrets and prompt injection. Each problem is a finding with a stable code, a severity and a
`file:line`, so you can gate CI on it, baseline it, or accept it with a reason.

<p align="center">
  <img src="assets/validate.gif" alt="ai-rulez validate flags a defect, --explain describes it, and generate --check fails on drift" width="820" />
</p>

#### Example

A rule links to a guide that does not exist, and a skill grants unrestricted `Bash` and names a script it does not
ship:

```text
$ ai-rulez validate
.ai-rulez/rules/api.md:12: error AR201 link-unresolved: link target "../../docs/errors.md" does not exist
...
.ai-rulez/skills/deploy/SKILL.md:5: warning AR007 tool-breadth: allowed-tools grants "Bash", which lets the skill run anything; narrow it (for example Bash(git status:*)) or list it in lint.security.allowed_tools
.ai-rulez/skills/deploy/SKILL.md:10: error AR402 skill-resource-missing: "scripts/deploy.sh" was not found relative to this skill's directory (.ai-rulez/skills/deploy) or relative to the repo root (.)

validation: 2 error(s), 2 warning(s), 0 info across 1 root(s)
  AR007 tool-breadth                 1
  AR201 link-unresolved              1
  AR402 skill-resource-missing       1
  ...
risk (advisory, never fails the run): high (score 66/100)
  high       33  .ai-rulez/rules/api.md
  high       33  .ai-rulez/skills/deploy/SKILL.md
```

The run exits 2 because of the errors. Ask what a rule means and how to silence it:

```text
$ ai-rulez validate --explain AR007
AR007 tool-breadth

Default severity: warning
Analyzer:         security (scope: item)
Finds:            allowed-tools grants an unrestricted tool such as Bash(*)

Why it matters
  An unrestricted allowed-tools entry lets the skill run any command without a prompt, so the blast radius is the whole account.

Bad
  `allowed-tools: Bash(*)`

Good
  `allowed-tools: Bash(git status:*), Read`

Suppress
  - inline: <!-- ai-rulez-lint-ignore: AR007 --> on the line before, or on, the offending line
  - config.toml: [lint] ignore = ["AR007"]
  ...
Docs: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/strict-validation/#ar007-tool-breadth
```

Common invocations:

```bash
ai-rulez validate                                  # schema, then content checks; exit 2 on errors
ai-rulez validate --strict                         # warnings fail too (--fail-on warning)
ai-rulez validate --changed=origin/main            # report only what a branch touched
ai-rulez validate --format sarif --output ai-rulez.sarif   # upload to code scanning
ai-rulez validate --recursive                      # every nested root of a monorepo
ai-rulez validate --config-only                    # the configuration file alone, no content checks
ai-rulez scan                                      # the security checks alone
```

#### What validate checks

1. **The configuration.** The configuration file is checked against the JSON schema (an unknown or misspelled key is
   an error), then for structure: includes resolve, ids are unique, `[lint]` settings are valid. A failure here exits
   1 and the content is not linted. `--config-only` stops after this step; it refuses `--strict` and the flags that
   need the content checks (`--format`, `--fail-on`, `--fix`, `--path`, the baseline flags, ...).
2. **The content.** Every analyzer runs over the content tree and reports findings (see [Rule index](#rule-index)).

Paths and globs are resolved like this:

- **Tracked files.** Globs, paths and hook files resolve against `git ls-files` plus untracked files that git does not
  ignore. Outside a git repository the directory is walked.
- **Repository root.** The git toplevel of the configuration, else the directory that holds it. For a configuration
  checked out away from its repository (a scratch copy, a CI artifact), pass `--repo-root <dir>` or set
  `AI_RULEZ_REPO_ROOT`; the root must be inside a git work tree.
- **Nested roots.** A nested root resolves globs and paths from the repository top or from its own directory,
  whichever matches, and may name skills, agents, commands and rules of an ancestor root. Without `--recursive`,
  `validate` checks one root and names the nested roots it skipped.
- **Only files you own.** Content from builtins and includes resolves names but is not reported on, except by the
  security checks (see [Imported content](#imported-content)).
- **Prose, not code.** Fenced code blocks and inline code are ignored for links; backticked tokens are read only as
  paths or slash commands.

#### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Configuration valid, no finding at or above the fail threshold |
| 1 | The configuration is invalid or cannot be loaded, a `[lint]` setting is invalid, or the flags conflict |
| 2 | Findings at or above the threshold |

The threshold is `--fail-on` (`error`, `warning`, `info` or `none`; `--strict` is `--fail-on warning`), else the
threshold of `--lint-profile`, else `[lint] fail_on`, else the threshold of `[lint] profile`, else `error`. `--strict`
with any other `--fail-on` is an error. With a structured `--format` (anything but `text`), stdout holds only the report.

#### Without a configuration file

`validate`, `scan` and `doctor` also work in a repository with no ai-rulez configuration. They print
`no ai-rulez config found; linting detected files` on stderr and lint the files found by convention, as hand-written
sources:

- `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `GEMINI.md`, at the root and in subdirectories;
- every `SKILL.md`, with its `references/`, `scripts/` and `assets/`;
- `.claude/{skills,agents,commands,rules}` at any depth, `.agents/**` and `.cursor/rules`;
- an `.ai-rulez/` content tree without a `config.toml`;
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `marketplace.json`, `hooks/hooks.json`, `.claude/settings.json` hooks and
  `.mcp.json`.

```text
$ ai-rulez validate
no ai-rulez config found; linting detected files
.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md:8: error AR402 skill-resource-missing: "references/checklist.md" was not found relative to this skill's directory (.claude/skills/release) or relative to the repo root (.)
AGENTS.md:3: error AR201 link-unresolved: link target "CONTRIBUTING.md" does not exist

validation: 2 error(s), 0 warning(s), 0 info across 1 root(s)
...
```

The implicit configuration has no presets, includes, hooks or MCP servers and the default `[lint]` settings. Nothing
is written. `--exclude <glob>` leaves files out of the detection, and `--path` or `--glob` replace it with the files
you name. A baseline is read from `--baseline <file>`, or by default only when an `.ai-rulez/` directory exists. A
home or filesystem-root directory outside git is refused instead of walked. `generate`, `clean`, `lock` and
`validate --config-only` still need a configuration. To keep `[lint]` settings without an `.ai-rulez/` folder, see
[Lint-only configuration](config-without-folder.md#lint-only-configuration).

A project **with** a configuration also lints the convention files its configuration does not cover, such as a
hand-written `.claude/skills/x/SKILL.md`. A file that carries the ai-rulez generated header, or that a `generate` run
recorded in its manifest, is an output and is skipped (see [Generated files](#generated-files)); each one skipped is
named on stderr and in the `notices` of the JSON report. A custom header (`[header]` text, or `hashes = "none"`) is
not recognized as generated, so such a file is linted as a source.

#### Files outside the content tree

To lint a marketplace, a plugin or a skill kept outside the content tree, name it:

```bash
ai-rulez validate --path catalog                  # a file or a directory, repeatable
ai-rulez validate --glob "plugins/**/*.json"      # a glob relative to the project root, repeatable
```

```toml
[lint]
paths = ["catalog", "vendor/skills"]   # always linted, relative to the project root
```

- Everything must resolve inside the project root. A `--path` that does not exist, leaves the root, or names an
  unreadable file or one over 2 MiB exits 1. A file matched by a glob that cannot be linted is only a notice.
- A file that is picked but not linted is named on stderr as `<file>: not linted (<reason>)` and in the `notices` of
  the JSON report: over 2 MiB, binary, not a regular file, a symlink out of the project, a generated file, or a skill
  that could not be loaded.
- Plugin manifests, marketplaces, hook files and MCP files are recognized by content wherever they are. Markdown is
  classified by name and place (`SKILL.md` is a skill, files below `agents/`, `commands/`, `rules/` and `checks/` are
  of that kind, other markdown is context).
- Any other text file you name (`.env`, YAML, TOML) is scanned for secrets (`AR001`) only.
- Directories and globs take tracked and non-ignored untracked files, so `--path .` never lints an ignored
  `node_modules`.
- `--path` and `--glob` cannot be combined with `--update-baseline`; put the paths in `[lint] paths` to baseline them.
  With `--recursive`, each root lints the matching files below it, and a file outside every root is linted at the
  repository root.

#### Generated files

The content checks judge what you wrote. `--outputs` (or `[lint] lint_outputs = true`) also lints what `generate`
writes into `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/skills/`, `.cursor/rules/` and the other harness files, using the bytes
a run would write now:

```bash
ai-rulez validate --outputs
```

- The security, references and descriptions analyzers run on generated markdown; budgets and metadata do not.
- A finding on a generated file is marked `[generated output]` in text, `"source": "output"` in JSON and
  `properties.source` in SARIF. A problem the authored source already has is reported once, at the source.
- `--fix` never edits a generated file: fix its source and run `generate`.

#### Configuration

Every key is optional. Put the table in `config.toml`; a `config.local.*` overlay may override individual keys.
An unknown code, severity, analyzer or content kind is an error (exit 1), never a silently disabled check.

| Key | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fail_on` | string | Lowest failing severity: `error` (default), `warning` or `none` |
| `profile` | string | `default`, `strict` or `permissive`; see [Profiles](#profiles) |
| `analyzers` | array | Run only these analyzers; see [Analyzers and scopes](#analyzers-and-scopes) |
| `ignore` | array | Codes or names dropped everywhere |
| `ignore_paths` | array | Globs of source files whose findings are dropped |
| `tracked_only` | boolean | Report no findings in untracked files; see [Untracked files](#untracked-files) |
| `paths` | array | Extra files and directories to lint; see [Files outside the content tree](#files-outside-the-content-tree) |
| `lint_outputs` | boolean | Also lint generated files; see [Generated files](#generated-files) |
| `example_paths` | array | Files whose every line is an [example region](#example-regions) |
| `allow_paths` | array | Repository paths that may be referenced without existing (`AR401`, `AR402`) |
| `known_names` | array | Skills, agents, rules and commands provided outside this tree (`AR301`) |
| `allow_overrides` | array | Intentional shadowing: `name` or `domain/name` (`AR703`), `name` or `preset:name` (`AR808`, `AR9U0`) |
| `allowed_keys` | array | Extra frontmatter keys (`AR303`) |
| `skill_roots` | array | Directories `AR808` treats as harness skill roots; see [Skill roots](#skill-roots) |
| `agents_md_only` | boolean | Report stray `CLAUDE.md` files when `AGENTS.md` is canonical (`AR9Q0`) |
| `agents_md_only_allow` | array | `CLAUDE.md` locations `AR9Q0` accepts |

Sub-tables:

```toml
[lint]
fail_on = "error"
ignore = ["AR803"]
ignore_paths = ["domains/legacy/**"]
allow_paths = [".claude/**", "bazel-*/**"]
known_names = ["superpowers-brainstorm"]

[lint.severity]                    # error | warning | info | off, by code or name
AR401 = "error"
anchor-unresolved = "off"

[[lint.ignore_rules]]              # some rules in some files; see Rule-scoped ignores
rules = ["AR901", "AR902"]
paths = ["playground/**"]

[[lint.accept]]                    # one finding, with a reason; see Accepting one finding
rule = "AR007"
path = ".claude/skills/foo/SKILL.md"
match = "Bash"
reason = "the skill runs git and gh; narrowing would break step 3"

[lint.ratchet]                     # tolerated findings per rule; see Baseline and tolerated findings
AR401 = 12

[lint.budgets.skill]               # size budget per kind: rule, context, skill, agent, command
max_lines = 400
max_tokens = 4000                  # 0 keeps the default, a negative value removes the limit

[lint.description]
min_length = 20                    # default 20
max_length = 1024                  # default 1024
require_use_when = true            # turns on AR803 at warning
near_duplicate_threshold = 0.85    # AR702, default 0.85

[lint.require_metadata]            # required frontmatter keys per kind (AR951)
skill = ["owner"]

[lint.metadata.last_verified]      # typed metadata (AR951, AR952, AR953)
type = "date"                      # string (default) | date | enum
max_age_days = 90
required = true
kinds = ["skill"]

[lint.metadata.tier]
type = "enum"
values = ["gold", "silver"]

[lint.security]
scan_imports = "error"             # unset | off | warn | error; see Imported content
allowed_hosts = ["github.com", "*.example.org"]   # turns on AR008
allowed_tools = ["Bash"]           # unrestricted allowed-tools entries that are accepted (AR007)
injection_phrases = ["as root user"]
directive_tags = ["assistant"]     # AR018 element names besides <system> and <override>
trusted_orgs = ["acme"]            # owners AR033 accepts "official" for
secret_patterns = [{ name = "internal token", regex = "corp_[a-z0-9]{10}" }]

[lint.capability]
max_network_commands = 3           # AR030, default 5

[lint.load_budgets]                # AR964 harness limits by id, in the limit's unit
claude-skill-listing = 1200        # also: claude-skill-listing-total, codex-agents-chain, codex-skill-listing, windsurf-rule-file, cursor-rule-lines

[lint.builtin_names]               # AR9U0, AR9U1; see Built-in names of harnesses
allow = ["gemini:help", "usage"]

[lint.builtin_names.extra]
claude = ["acme-deploy"]

[lint.risk]                        # see Risk score
error = 30

[lint.traps]
extra_harnesses = ["cursor"]       # see Harness Traps

[lint.evals]                       # see Evals
require = true                     # turns on AR962 at warning
min_pass_rate = 0.8                # AR998
```

Default size budgets (lines / tokens): rule 200 / 2500, context 300 / 3000, skill 500 / 5000, agent 300 / 3000,
command 300 / 3000. Tokens are counted with the `cl100k_base` tokenizer and are approximate. `[[lint.external]]` and
`[lint.scanner_policy]` are described under [External scanners](#external-scanners), `[lint.traps]` in
[Harness Traps](harness-traps.md), `[lint.evals]` in [Evals](evals.md).

#### Suppressing findings

| Scope | How |
| --- | --- |
| One line | `<!-- ai-rulez-lint-ignore: AR401, AR301 -->` on the line before or on the line; without codes it silences every finding there |
| One rule everywhere | `[lint] ignore = ["AR401"]`, or `[lint.severity] AR401 = "off"` |
| Every rule in some files | `[lint] ignore_paths = ["glob"]` |
| Some rules in some files | [`[[lint.ignore_rules]]`](#rule-scoped-ignores) |
| One finding, with a reason | [`[[lint.accept]]`](#accepting-one-finding) |
| Existing findings while you fix them | [A baseline](#baseline-and-tolerated-findings) |

```markdown
<!-- ai-rulez-lint-ignore: AR401, AR301 -->
See `legacy/old-tool/README.md` and the `retired-helper` skill.
```

An organization policy that protects a code refuses `ignore_paths`, `ignore_rules` and `accept` for it and reports
the attempt as `AR740` (see [Organization policy](policy.md)).

##### Rule-scoped ignores

`[[lint.ignore_rules]]` drops the listed rules in the listed files and keeps every other finding in them:

```toml
[[lint.ignore_rules]]
rules = ["AR901", "AR902"]     # codes, names, or a pattern over codes (AR9*, AR40?)
paths = ["playground/**"]      # globs relative to the repository root or to .ai-rulez/
reason = "scratch projects"    # optional
```

- An entry needs at least one rule and one path. An unknown code, a pattern that matches no code or a malformed glob
  is an error when the configuration loads.
- Paths name source files: a finding on a generated file is not covered by the path of its source.
- An ignored finding never reaches the baseline or a `[lint.ratchet]` count.

##### Accepting one finding

`[[lint.accept]]` accepts the findings of one rule in one file that a selector names, with a required reason. It is
reviewed in a normal pull request, and every other finding in the file stays reported.

```toml
[[lint.accept]]
rule = "AR007"                                  # one code or name, no wildcards
path = ".claude/skills/foo/SKILL.md"            # a glob, as in ignore_paths
match = "Bash"                                  # case-sensitive substring of the message
line = 4                                        # optional; match and/or line is required
reason = "the skill runs git and gh; narrowing would break step 3"
```

- A finding is accepted when its rule, file, message (`match`) and, when set, line all fit. Every finding of the rule
  in the file whose message contains `match` is accepted, so pick a specific one.
- An accepted finding does not count toward the exit code or a ratchet. The JSON report keeps it with
  `"accepted": true` and the reason as `accept_reason`; `--update-baseline` does not write it.
- An entry that accepts nothing is reported as `AR9I0` (`accept-unused`, warning) on `config.toml`, unless the run
  could not have produced the finding (the rule is off, its analyzer was not selected, or the run linted only named
  files that do not match).

##### Baseline and tolerated findings

A **baseline** records the findings you accept today, so only new findings fail the build. `[lint.ratchet]` caps how
many findings of one rule are tolerated.

```bash
ai-rulez validate --update-baseline --baseline-reason "legacy, tracked in ACME-42"
git add .ai-rulez/lint-baseline.json
ai-rulez validate                     # exit 2 only for findings not in the baseline
ai-rulez validate --strict-baseline   # stale entries fail too, so the baseline only shrinks
```

```text
$ ai-rulez validate
validation: no findings in 1 root(s)
baseline: 4 finding(s) accepted
```

`.ai-rulez/lint-baseline.json` (`--baseline <file>` names another, which must exist) holds one entry per finding:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "entries": [
    {
      "fingerprint": "ar1:105276fd3c01f14ec2d158da",
      "code": "AR402",
      "file": ".ai-rulez/skills/deploy/SKILL.md",
      "message": "\"scripts/deploy.sh\" was not found relative to this skill's directory (.ai-rulez/skills/deploy) or relative to the repo root (.)",
      "reason": "legacy, tracked in ACME-42",
      "expires": "2026-12-31"
    }
  ]
}
```

- **Matching.** An entry matches by `fingerprint` (see [Fingerprints](#fingerprints)), never by line number: the
  finding stays accepted while the file changes around it, and a different finding of the same rule is new.
- **`--update-baseline`** rewrites the file to accept every current finding, keeps the `reason` and `expires` of
  entries that still match, drops the rest, and exits 0. A security finding (`AR0xx`) needs a reason. Findings in
  untracked files are never written. It cannot be combined with `--since`, `--changed`, `--path`, `--glob`,
  `--analyzer`, `--lint-profile`, `--fix`, `--fix-unsafe` or `--strict-baseline`. It needs a configuration directory
  or `--baseline <file>`, and with `--baseline <file>` a single root (not a `--recursive` run over several).
- **Accepted findings** stay visible (`"accepted": true` in JSON, a SARIF `suppression`) but do not count.
- **Stale entries** (their finding is gone) are reported as information; `--strict-baseline` makes them fail. An entry
  of an analyzer that did not run is never stale.
- **`expires`** (`YYYY-MM-DD`, optional): after that day the finding counts as new and the entry is listed as expired.
  Set `AI_RULEZ_TODAY` to pin the date in tests.
- **Ratchet.** `[lint.ratchet]` maps a code or name to the number of unaccepted findings tolerated. One more and all
  of that rule's findings count again (`ratchet: AR401 has 13 finding(s), over its ratchet of 12`, JSON key
  `ratchet_exceeded`), whatever their severity. It is applied per root, after the baseline. It is a different table
  from `[lint.budgets.<kind>]`, the size budgets.

#### Automatic fixes

```bash
ai-rulez validate --fix --dry-run      # print a unified diff, change nothing
ai-rulez validate --fix                # apply the safe fixes
ai-rulez validate --fix-unsafe         # also apply fixes that can change meaning
```

| Rule | Fix | Tier |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AR303` frontmatter-key-unknown | Rename a key that differs from a known key only by case or separators (`allowed_tools` to `allowed-tools`) | safe |
| `AR304` frontmatter-value-invalid | Write a quoted `"true"`/`"false"` of a boolean key as a YAML boolean | safe |
| `AR806` fence-unclosed | Add the closing fence | safe |
| `AR807` final-newline-missing | Add the final newline | safe |
| `AR502`, `AR503`, `AR505` | `chmod +x` the file and stage the bit (`git update-index --chmod=+x`) | safe |
| `AR9C7`, and `AR9CA` rows of kind `key-misspelt` | Rename a misspelt frontmatter key (`user_invocable` to `user-invocable`) in a hand-written harness file | safe |
| `AR804` skill-name-invalid | Rewrite `name:` to the normalized name or the directory name | unsafe: the name is how the skill is invoked |

- Fixes edit authored sources under the configuration directory, plus hand-written harness files for the trap fixes.
  They never edit a generated file or a symlink, and never fix a security finding or a baselined one.
- An edit is skipped when the file changed since the lint run. Files are rewritten atomically with their permissions
  and line endings; a second `--fix` changes nothing.
- The run then reports what is left, and the exit code reflects that. Run `ai-rulez generate` so the fixes reach the
  generated files.

#### Analyzers and scopes

Every rule belongs to an **analyzer** (a family of checks) and has a **scope**: `file` (a line of a file), `item` (one
