| `anchor` | Heading in the item's file that findings point at; a missing heading is `AR9H2` |
| `severity` | `error`, `warning` (default) or `info` |
| `message`, `fix` | Shown with every failure |
| `when_changed` | Globs that select the scoped files (see below) |
| `exclude` | Globs removed from the scope |
| `[verifiers.require.<predicate>]` | Exactly one predicate table |
| `[[verifiers.examples]]` | Self-tests: `name`, `files`, `changed`, `expect` (`pass`, `fail`, `not_applicable`) |

The same keys work inline in `config.toml`: an entry without `type` is a spec, and its `name` is the `id`.

```toml
[[verifiers]]
name = "no-todo-in-go"
rule = "style"
when_changed = ["src/**/*.go"]

[verifiers.require.forbid]
regex = "TODO"
in = "diff-added"
```

##### Predicates

| Predicate | Fields | Holds when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `regex` | `regex`, `in`, `files` | the pattern matches in each scoped file (`in = "same-file"`, default), in each scoped file's added lines (`diff-added`), or in at least one file (`any-file`) |
| `forbid` | same as `regex` | the pattern does not match |
| `file_exists` | `path`, `exists` (default `true`) | the path exists, or with `exists = false` does not; `path` may use a template |
| `paired` | `for_each`, `requires_changed` or `requires_exists` | for every scoped file matching `for_each`, the derived path was changed too, or exists |
| `glob_count` | `files`, `exclude`, `min`, `max` | the number of repository files matching `files` is within bounds |
| `command` | `argv`, `pass_files`, `timeout_s`, `expect_exit` | the program exits with `expect_exit` (default 0); see [Command predicate](#command-predicate) |
| `llm` | `checklist`, `model`, `max_diff_bytes` | a model finds no checklist item violated; see [LLM checklist verifiers](#llm-checklist-verifiers) |
| `all` / `any` / `not` | arrays of predicate tables (`not`: one) | boolean composition, at most 4 levels deep |

Combinators repeat the table: `[[verifiers.require.all]]` followed by `[verifiers.require.all.regex]`, or
`[verifiers.require.not.file_exists]`.

- **Scope.** `when_changed` selects the changed files that still exist (all files when no `--since` or `--staged` is
  given). A predicate that examines scoped files (`same-file` and `diff-added`, `paired`, a templated `file_exists`)
  needs it. When it selects nothing, the status is `not_applicable` and the run does not fail.
- **Whole tree.** `requires_exists`, `any-file`, `glob_count` and `file_exists` see unchanged files too.
- **`diff-added`** looks only at added lines, so `forbid` with it ratchets a rule on legacy code: only new violations
  fail. With `--all` and in self-tests every line counts as added.
- **Templates** in `paired` and `file_exists`: `{path}`, `{dir}`, `{stem}` (file name without extension), `{ext}`
  (with the dot) and `{rel}`. In `for_each`, `{rel}` captures the rest of the path: `src/api/{rel}.py` matches
  `src/api/v1/users.py` with `rel = v1/users`. A derived path must stay inside the project.
- **Matching.** Line endings are normalized to LF. Binary files and files over 5 MiB are skipped and listed in the
  result's `notes`. A finding quotes at most 120 characters, with credential-looking text masked.

```toml
[[verifiers]]
id = "new-endpoints-have-tests"
rule = "api-conventions"
when_changed = ["src/api/**/*.py"]

[verifiers.require.paired]
for_each = "src/api/{rel}.py"
requires_changed = "tests/api/test_{stem}.py"
```

##### Command predicate

`command` calls an existing linter instead of re-implementing it.

```toml
[[verifiers]]
id = "lockfile-in-sync"
skill = "dependency-updates"
when_changed = ["package.json", "package-lock.json"]

[verifiers.require.command]
argv = ["npm", "ci", "--dry-run"]   # no shell; argv[0] is looked up on PATH or is a path inside the project
pass_files = "stdin0"               # "args" appends the scoped files, "stdin0" writes them NUL-separated to stdin
timeout_s = 120                     # capped by [verifiers_settings] max_timeout_s (default 300)
expect_exit = 0
```

- **Opt-in.** Nothing runs without `--allow-exec` (`verifiers run`, `verifiers test`) or
  `AI_RULEZ_VERIFIERS_ALLOW_EXEC=1`. `generate`, `validate`, hooks and the MCP server never run a verifier command. In
  CI, pass it only for trusted refs: a pull request from a fork can carry its own verifiers.
- **Not run is an error, never a pass.** Without `--allow-exec`, or when the program is missing, cannot start or times
  out, the verifier ends with status `error` and `AR9H3`. Under `not` a refusal is not inverted into a pass.
- **Execution.** No shell, the project root as working directory, at most 64 KiB captured per stream, the process
  group killed at the timeout. On a non-zero exit the finding shows the first line of stderr (else stdout).
- **Environment.** The program gets only `PATH`, `HOME`, `USER`, `TMPDIR`, `TZ`, the locale variables, `CI`,
  `NO_COLOR` and `TERM=dumb`, plus the names in `[verifiers_settings] command_env`, which refuses credential-looking
  and proxy names.
- **No network sandbox.** Restrict network access with an OS sandbox or your CI egress policy.
- A verifier from an include may use `command` only when the include is trusted; see
  [Imported verifiers](#imported-verifiers). Flat verifiers have no `command` type.

##### Changed-only runs

`--since REV` evaluates the files changed between the merge base of `REV` and `HEAD`, plus uncommitted and untracked
files (renames detected). `--staged` evaluates what is staged. `--since`, `--staged` and `--all` are mutually
exclusive. When the base cannot be used (an unknown revision, no common ancestor in a shallow clone, `--staged` in a
repository without commits) the run exits 1 instead of passing. Flat verifiers ignore `--since` and `--staged` and
always check the whole repository.

##### Output

| Format | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| `text` | The table plus a block per failure (default) |
| `json` | Summary, mode and results; [`schema/verifiers-report.schema.json`](https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/blob/main/schema/verifiers-report.schema.json) |
| `sarif` | SARIF 2.1.0. `ruleId` is `AR9H1/<verifier id>` (a flat verifier's name), the location is the subject file, `relatedLocations` is the declaring rule's anchor line, and fingerprints survive line shifts |
| `junit` | One suite per rule (`rule:<id>`, `skill:<id>`, `config` for flat verifiers), one case per verifier and subject; `not_applicable` is `skipped`, a failure below `--fail-on` is a passing case |

`--output FILE` writes the report to a file. `--fail-on error|warning|info|none` sets the lowest failing severity.
Control characters in file names and messages are escaped, so a file name cannot rewrite the terminal.

##### Codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `AR9H1` `verifier-failed` | A predicate did not hold; the severity is the verifier's own |
| `AR9H2` `verifier-invalid` | Bad regex, unknown or missing target, missing `anchor` heading, two predicates, bad template or example, unknown key, duplicate `id`, symlinked or oversized file |
| `AR9H3` `verifier-command-failed-to-run` | A `command` predicate was refused (no `--allow-exec`, an untrusted include), could not start, or timed out |
| `AR9H4` `verifier-llm-skipped` | An `llm` verifier was not evaluated (LLM use off, over budget, content withheld, unusable reply, `--estimate`); status `skipped`, never a pass |
| `AR9H5` `verifier-dead-scope` | `when_changed` matches no file; with `--strict-applicability` or `[verifiers_settings] warn_dead` |
| `AR9H6` `verifier-no-examples` | A spec has no `[[verifiers.examples]]`; with `[verifiers_settings] require_examples` |

`ai-rulez validate --explain AR9H1` describes each code. Two statuses never fail a run: `skipped` (an `llm` verifier
that was not evaluated) and `inactive` (see [Active profile and role](#active-profile-and-role)).

##### Self-tests

`verifiers test [name...]` runs each spec's `[[verifiers.examples]]` offline in a temporary directory that holds the
example's `files`; the `changed` files count as changed and entirely added. Exit 0 when every example matches, 2 when
one does not or a declaration is invalid, 1 when the configuration does not load or a name is unknown. The examples
of an `llm` verifier are used by [calibration](#calibrating-llm-verifiers), not by `test`.

#### LLM checklist verifiers

An `llm` predicate asks a model whether the added lines break a checklist. Its verdict is advisory: it is reported
at most as `warning` unless the verifier is [calibrated](#calibrating-llm-verifiers).

```toml
[[verifiers]]
id = "errors-are-actionable"
rule = "error-handling"
when_changed = ["src/**/*.go"]       # required

[verifiers.require.llm]
checklist = [
  "New error messages say what the caller can do about the failure.",
  "No error swallows the original cause without wrapping it.",
]
model = ""                           # default: the [llm] model
max_diff_bytes = 24000               # changed text per call (1024 to 200000); larger changes are split
```

- **Placement.** `llm` is the root predicate or a direct member of `all`. Inside `all`, the deterministic members run
  first; when one fails, the model is not asked.
- **Opt-in.** It needs `--allow-llm`, plus `allow_network = true` and a model in the user configuration (or
  `AI_RULEZ_LLM_*`); a repository configuration cannot turn the network on. See [LLM access](llm.md). Otherwise the
  verifier is `skipped` with `AR9H4`.
- **What is sent.** The added lines of the scoped files with three lines of context. A hunk that holds a
  credential-looking string or a hidden character is withheld and never sent. Nothing else leaves the machine.
- **Strict replies.** Each checklist item gets `pass`, `fail` or `not_applicable`; a `fail` must quote an added line
  of the named file verbatim, or it is dropped.
- **Cost.** Responses are cached by request, so a re-run on an unchanged diff costs nothing. `--max-cost` (default
  $0.50, `0` removes the cap) refuses a call that could exceed what is left, on top of the `[llm]` budget.
  `--estimate` prints the files, byte counts and cost bound per call and calls nothing.
- Provider errors, timeouts and budget refusals skip the verifier (`AR9H4`) and are reported.

#### Calibrating llm verifiers

A model's `fail` is a claim. To let one fail the run, label examples and measure how often it is right:

```toml
[[verifiers.examples]]
name = "swallows the cause"
changed = ["a.go"]
expect = "fail"
[verifiers.examples.files]
"a.go" = "package a\nfunc f() error { return errors.New(\"failed\") }\n"
```

`ai-rulez verifiers calibrate [name...] --allow-llm` runs every example of the `llm` verifiers through the model and
writes `.ai-rulez/verifiers/calibration/<id>.json`; commit it. The record holds the verifier, digests of the predicate
tree and the examples, the prompt version, the model and date, the confusion counts (`tp`, `fp`, `fn`, `tn`),
precision and recall with 95% Wilson intervals, and a `status`. It passes at a precision of at least 0.80 on at least
10 examples, with at least 3 expected to fail and 3 to pass, none unevaluated. `--estimate` prints what would be sent;
`--no-write` only prints. Exit 2 when a record does not pass (it is still written).

`verifiers run --gate-llm` then lets a failing `llm` verifier declared `severity = "error"` fail the run, as long as
its record is current (same predicate tree, `when_changed`, `exclude`, examples, prompt version and model) and passes.
Otherwise the verdict stays capped at `warning` and the report says why.

#### Suggesting verifiers

`ai-rulez verifiers suggest <id>` (`--kind rule|skill|agent|command`) asks the model for up to `--max-proposals`
(default 5) verifiers for a prose rule and prints the ones that survive deterministic checks. Nothing is written
unless you pass `--write`, which saves them to a new `.ai-rulez/verifiers/suggested-<id>.toml`.

- **What is sent:** the item text and a repository summary (up to 60 directory names and the 12 most common file
  extensions), no file content. The gates of `llm` verifiers apply (`--allow-llm`, `allow_network`, `--max-cost`,
  `--estimate`).
- **What comes back:** only `forbid`, `regex`, `file_exists`, `paired` and `glob_count` predicates, never `command` or
  `llm`, at most `warning`.
- **Checks:** each candidate must pass the validation of a hand-written spec, its own pass and fail examples must
  behave as claimed offline, and it is run against the repository to count today's failures. A `forbid` without
  `in = "diff-added"` that matches an everyday library call or fails on more than 10 files is rejected.
- **Replay:** each candidate is replayed over the last `--replay N` merged changes (default 10, at most 100, 0 turns it
  off); one that would have flagged many reviewed changes is noisy, and the output says so
  (`replay: would have flagged 2 of 8 merged diff(s)`).

A rule that cannot be checked mechanically gets `No verifier proposed` with the model's reason. Exit 0 even with no
proposal, 1 when it could not run.

#### Active profile and role

A spec whose rule, skill, agent or command is not part of the active selection is `inactive`: listed, never run,
never failed. The selection follows `generate`: `--role`, else `--profile`, else the configured `default` profile,
else the built-in `default` profile. A target that does not exist at all is `AR9H2`. An unknown profile or role exits 1.

#### Imported verifiers

An include may carry `<include>/verifiers/*.toml`, and an installed skill `<skill>/verifiers/*.toml`. They load like
your own (shown as `include:<name>/verifiers/<file>` or `skill:<name>/verifiers/<file>`) and are pinned with their
source in `ai-rulez.lock`. An include with an `include = [...]` filter brings no verifiers.

A verifier from an include may use `command` only when:

1. the include is listed in `[verifiers_settings] trust_exec_from`, **and**
2. the include is pinned in `ai-rulez.lock`.

Otherwise the declaration is `AR9H2` and nothing runs, whatever `--allow-exec` says. A verifier from an installed
skill can never use `command`. Imported `llm` verifiers are allowed and still need `--allow-llm`.

#### Local overlay

`config.local.toml` may declare `[[verifiers]]`; a local entry replaces the shared one with the same name. See
[Local configuration](local-overrides.md).

#### Settings

```toml
[verifiers_settings]          # not [verifiers]: that name is the array of verifiers
max_timeout_s = 300           # cap on a command predicate's timeout_s (1 to 900)
max_file_bytes = 5242880      # largest file a content predicate reads (default 5 MiB)
require_examples = false      # report a spec without examples (AR9H6)
warn_dead = false             # report a when_changed that matches no file (AR9H5)
trust_exec_from = []          # includes whose verifiers may use command (they must be pinned in the lock)
command_env = ["MY_FLAG"]     # extra environment variable names passed to commands
```

`trust_exec_from` must name a declared include. The table is pinned in the lock, so widening trust shows up in
review.

#### Lock

Every verifier declaration is pinned in `ai-rulez.lock` as kind `verifier` (see [Lock file](lockfile.md)). Lowering a
severity, widening an `exclude` or deleting a verifier changes the pin, so `lock --check` and `[lock] enforce` make a
weakened check visible in review.

## Session exposure and areas

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/exposure/

In a large repository, every session starts with the same context: the root instruction file, the unconditional
rules, the listing of root skills and agents, and the MCP server names. When that text names one team's service, every
session is pulled toward it, and a skill that belongs to one part of the tree competes with the skills of every other
part. An **area map** in the `[exposure]` table names the parts of the repository (the areas), the directories each one
claims and the words that identify it. ai-rulez then shows what a session loads at its start, which area every
artifact belongs to, and where an area's words leak into the shared start-of-session text.

Currently supports Claude Code only (`harness = "claude"`): the commands read the native Claude Code files
(`CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, `.mcp.json`, enabled plugins), whichever presets generated them.

#### Example

A monorepo with two services and shared tooling:

```text
acme/
├── .ai-rulez/
│   ├── config.toml
│   ├── context/architecture.md      # as created by ai-rulez init
│   ├── rules/code-quality.md        # as created by ai-rulez init
│   └── skills/
│       ├── account-lookup/SKILL.md
│       ├── ci-debug/SKILL.md
│       └── invoice-retry/SKILL.md
├── services/
│   ├── billing/
│   └── search/
└── tools/ci/
```

`ai-rulez generate` writes the three skills to `.claude/skills/` at the root, so all three are listed at the start of
every session. Describe the areas in `.ai-rulez/config.toml`:

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml (excerpt)
presets = ["claude", "cursor"]

[exposure]
harness = "claude"

[[exposure.areas]]
name = "billing"
owner = "team-billing"
paths = ["services/billing"]
terms = ["invoice", "ledger"]
ambiguous = ["account"]

[[exposure.areas]]
name = "search"
owner = "team-search"
paths = ["services/search"]
terms = ["reindex", "ranking"]
ambiguous = ["account"]

[[exposure.areas]]
name = "platform"
owner = "team-platform"
paths = ["tools"]
terms = ["terraform", "ci"]
shared = true                # repository-wide tooling: its terms may appear at session start
```

`ai-rulez exposure leakage` reports the area terms in the start-of-session text:

```text
$ ai-rulez exposure leakage
Leakage at session start: 6 artifacts checked
violations: 2  warnings: 1  accepted: 0
violations by area:
  billing: 2
...
findings:
  warning AR9W1 billing/search/account .claude/skills/account-lookup/SKILL.md:1: account-lookup: Look up an account by email or id. Use when asked who owns an account.
  violation AR9W0 billing/invoice .claude/skills/invoice-retry/SKILL.md:1: invoice-retry: Retry failed invoice payments and re-run the ledger export. Use when an invoice is stuck in pending.
  violation AR9W0 billing/ledger .claude/skills/invoice-retry/SKILL.md:1: invoice-retry: Retry failed invoice payments and re-run the ledger export. Use when an invoice is stuck in pending.
```

`ai-rulez validate` reports the same findings, so the check runs in CI with the rest of [validation](strict-validation.md):

```text
$ ai-rulez validate
.claude/skills/account-lookup/SKILL.md:1: warning AR9W1 exposure-area-term-ambiguous: skill "account-lookup" at session start names term "account" of area "billing/search"
.claude/skills/invoice-retry/SKILL.md:1: error AR9W0 exposure-area-term: skill "invoice-retry" at session start names term "invoice" of area "billing"
.claude/skills/invoice-retry/SKILL.md:1: error AR9W0 exposure-area-term: skill "invoice-retry" at session start names term "ledger" of area "billing"

validation: 2 error(s), 1 warning(s), 0 info across 1 root(s)
...
```

Fix them:

1. Move `invoice-retry` into a nested root for the billing service (see [Monorepo](monorepo.md)): move the skill
   directory to `services/billing/.ai-rulez/skills/invoice-retry/`, add `services/billing/.ai-rulez/config.toml`, and
   run `ai-rulez generate --recursive`. The skill is now written to `services/billing/.claude/skills/`, which Claude
   Code loads only when a session works in that directory.

```toml
# services/billing/.ai-rulez/config.toml
version = "5.0"
name = "billing"
presets = ["claude"]
```

2. `account-lookup` serves every team. Place it explicitly and accept the ambiguous word with a reason:

```toml
[exposure.skill_areas]
account-lookup = "billing"

[[lint.accept]]
rule = "AR9W1"
path = ".claude/skills/account-lookup/SKILL.md"
match = 'names term "account"'
reason = "support staff look up accounts of every service"
```

`ai-rulez exposure inventory` shows what loads when, and which area each artifact belongs to:

```text
$ ai-rulez exposure inventory
Session inventory of /work/acme (claude; plugins enabled, loaded: none)

PHASE      KIND        NAME                        TOKENS  AREA                   PATH
start      mcp_server  ai-rulez                    3       unclassified (none)    .mcp.json
start      claude_md   CLAUDE.md                   385     unclassified (none)    CLAUDE.md
start      settings    settings.json               0       unclassified (none)    .claude/settings.json
start      skill       account-lookup              23      billing (skill_areas)  .claude/skills/account-lookup/SKILL.md
start      skill       ci-debug                    27      platform (terms)       .claude/skills/ci-debug/SKILL.md
on_demand  mcp_server  ai-rulez                    3       billing (path)         services/billing/.mcp.json
on_demand  claude_md   services/billing/CLAUDE.md  96      billing (path)         services/billing/CLAUDE.md
on_demand  settings    settings.json               0       billing (path)         services/billing/.claude/settings.json
on_demand  skill       invoice-retry               30      billing (path)         services/billing/.claude/skills/invoice-retry/SKILL.md

9 artifacts: 5 start (438 tokens, unknown included), 4 on_demand, 0 manual, 0 unknown
```

`ai-rulez exposure` sums up what a session started at the root costs before it touches a file:

```text
$ ai-rulez exposure
start of session: 5 artifacts, ~438 tokens
skill listing: 2 skills, 189 chars of 8000 budget (200000 token window)
start tokens by kind:
  claude_md: 385
  skill: 50
  mcp_server: 3
  settings: 0
artifacts by phase and kind:
  start: skill 2, claude_md 1, mcp_server 1, settings 1
  on_demand: claude_md 1, mcp_server 1, settings 1, skill 1
  manual: none
tokens if loaded, by phase:
  start: 438
  on_demand: 129
heaviest at start:
  ~385 claude_md CLAUDE.md
  ~27 skill .claude/skills/ci-debug/SKILL.md
...
```

`exposure leakage` now exits 0 and lists the accepted finding with its reason. To keep the start of every session
small, add `start_budget` (see [Start-of-session budgets](#start-of-session-budgets)).

#### Configuration

Every key is optional. Without an `[exposure]` table the commands still work (without areas), and only `AR9W4` of the
validation rules runs.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `harness` | string | `"claude"` | Harness whose load model applies; only `"claude"` |
| `context_window` | integer | `200000` | Model context window in tokens, for the skill listing budget |
| `plugins` | string | `"enabled"` | Repository-marketplace plugins whose skills are listed at start: `none`, `enabled` (those `.claude/settings*.json` enable) or `all` |
| `start_budget` | integer | `0` (off) | Most estimated start-of-session tokens; turns on `AR9W3` |
| `collision_min_score` | number | `0` (off) | Lowest overlap score between listings of different areas; turns on `AR9W2` and is the default `--min-score` of `exposure collisions` |
| `areas_file` | string | | Area map in its own file, relative to the project root |
| `[[exposure.areas]]` | array of tables | | The areas (inline form) |
| `[exposure.skill_areas]` | table | | Explicit owners of skills: skill name (or `plugin:skill`) to area name |

Keys of an area:

| Key | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Required. Unique, lower-kebab (`a-z`, `0-9`, single hyphens). `unclassified` is reserved |
| `paths` | array of strings | Directories the area claims, relative to the repository root (see [Path claims](#path-claims)) |
| `terms` | array of strings | Words that name the area (see [Term matching](#term-matching)) |
| `ambiguous` | array of strings | Words the area shares with others (`account`, `query`); they never decide an area on their own |
| `shared` | boolean | Repository-wide tooling: its terms classify artifacts but are allowed at session start |
| `owner` | string | Free text, reported as is |
| `description` | string | Free text, reported as is |
| `declare` | string | Repository path a session of this area works on; validated and reported by `exposure areas` |

##### Areas file

The map lives either inline or in `areas_file`, never both. The file must stay inside the project root and uses
`[[area]]` and `[skill_areas]`. An unknown key in it is an error.

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml (excerpt)
[exposure]
areas_file = "tools/context/areas.toml"
```

```toml
# tools/context/areas.toml
[[area]]
name = "billing"
owner = "team-billing"
paths = ["services/billing"]
terms = ["invoice", "ledger"]

[[area]]
name = "platform"
paths = ["tools"]
shared = true
terms = ["terraform"]

[skill_areas]
account-lookup = "billing"
```

#### Matching

##### Path claims

- A path is a directory prefix with no leading or trailing slash: `services/billing` claims that directory and
  everything below it, not `services/billing2`.
- A trailing `*` makes a name prefix: `services/billing_*` claims `services/billing_api` and `services/billing_jobs/x`.
  `vendor/*` claims everything below `vendor`, not `vendor` itself.
- A leading `!` excludes: `"!services/billing_legacy"` keeps the area from claiming that directory.
- When several areas claim a directory, the longest matching path wins; on a tie, the area listed first wins.

##### Term matching

- Terms and ambiguous words are trimmed and lowercased; matching ignores case.
- A term that contains `_`, `/` or `.` (`ledger_sync`, `@acme/ui`, `api.v2`) matches anywhere in the text.
- Any other term matches as a whole word, where only ASCII letters and digits continue a word: `invoice` matches
  `Invoice`, `INVOICE_ID` and `team_invoice`, not `invoices` or `reinvoice`.
- Longer terms are tried first, so `ledger_sync` wins over `ledger`.
- Repository paths are not words: a path that starts with the first segment of a path claim followed by `/`
  (`services/billing/README.md`) is ignored up to the next space, quote, backtick, bracket, comma or semicolon.
- A word that is both a term and ambiguous in one area counts as a term.

##### Classification

An artifact (a skill, rule, agent, `CLAUDE.md`, MCP server) gets the first area that applies:

1. for a skill, its entry in `skill_areas` (a plugin skill is looked up as `plugin:skill`, then by its bare name);
2. the area with the most specific path claim on the artifact's directory (for a skill, the directory that holds its
   `.claude` directory; for a plugin skill, the plugin's directory);
3. the area with the most distinct terms in its text, ambiguous words not counted; a tie gives none. A skill's text is
   its listing line; a plugin skill's is its qualified name;
4. otherwise `unclassified`.

`exposure areas` and `exposure inventory` report the result with its source: `skill_areas`, `path`, `terms` or `none`.
A skill at the repository root is best placed with `skill_areas` until it moves under its area's directory, where the
path claim gives the same answer.

#### What a session loads

The inventory follows Claude Code's load model for a session started at the inspected root:

| Phase | Artifacts |
| --- | --- |
| `start` | The root `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, rules without `paths:`, the listing line of every root skill (`.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, and `.claude/commands/**/*.md`), root agents, the server names of the root `.mcp.json`, and the enabled plugins with their skills |
| `on_demand` | Anything in a subdirectory, and anything gated by `paths:`, once a matching file is touched |
| `manual` | Skills with `disable-model-invocation: true` or set to `user-invocable-only` in `skillOverrides`: only the user runs them |
| `unknown` | A root rule or skill whose gate cannot be read (see [A gate that cannot be read](#a-gate-that-cannot-be-read)); counted as `start` |

- `.claude/settings.local.json` applies over `.claude/settings.json`. `skillOverrides` `off` removes a skill,
  `name-only` blanks its description, and `claudeMdExcludes` globs exclude `CLAUDE.md` files and rules.
- A skill's listing line is `name: description when_to_use`, capped at 1536 characters.
- Tokens are estimated as UTF-8 bytes divided by 3.9. A file over 1 MiB is not read; its size still counts.
- `@path` imports in a `CLAUDE.md` or rule are followed up to five levels, and their text counts toward the importing
  file's tokens. An import that cannot be followed (an absolute or `~` path, a path outside the project, an unreadable
  file) is listed in `import_problems`.
- Not modeled: `CLAUDE.local.md`, user and managed settings, symlinked directories, and the agents, commands and MCP
  servers of plugins.

#### Commands

All commands are offline and deterministic. They inspect the project root, or `--root DIR` to see what a session
started in `DIR` sees, with paths printed relative to `DIR`. The configuration is `-C` when given, else the one
discovered from `DIR` upwards, so on a directory with a nested root (`--root services/billing` in the example), pass
`-C .ai-rulez` (or `--areas`) to keep the project's area map. `--areas FILE` replaces the configured map with a file in the [areas file](#areas-file) format, so you can try
a map before you configure it.

| Flag | Commands | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--format text\|json` | all | Output format |
| `--plugins none\|enabled\|all` | all | Plugins whose skills are listed; default `[exposure] plugins`, else `enabled` |
| `--areas FILE` | all | Area map file to use instead of the `[exposure]` table |
| `--root DIR` | all | Directory to inspect; default the project root |
| `--context-window N` | `exposure` | Context window for the listing budget; default `[exposure] context_window`, else 200000 |
| `--harness claude` | `exposure` | Harness whose load model applies; only `claude` |
| `--with-text` | `inventory` | Include each artifact's text (with `--format json` only) |
| `--min-score N` | `collisions` | Lowest score reported, 0 to 1; default `[exposure] collision_min_score`, else 0.1 |
| `--limit N` | `collisions` | Pairs printed, highest score first (default 20; 0 prints all) |

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | The report was printed |
| 1 | The command could not run: a bad flag, an invalid configuration or area map, or no area map for `areas`, `collisions` and `leakage` |
| 2 | `exposure`: start tokens exceed `start_budget`. `exposure leakage`: a violation or a stale acceptance |

##### `ai-rulez exposure`

The start-of-session report: estimated start tokens in total and by kind, the skill listing against Claude Code's
listing budget, the artifacts per phase, and the heaviest artifacts at start. The listing budget is 1% of the context
window at 4 characters per token: 8000 characters at 200000 tokens. Past it, Claude Code keeps the skill names but drops
descriptions, which carry the words a request is matched against. `descriptions_capped` in the JSON counts skills whose
listing passes the 1536-character cap. JSON:
[`schema/exposure-report.v1.schema.json`](https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/blob/main/schema/exposure-report.v1.schema.json).

##### `ai-rulez exposure inventory`

Every artifact with its kind, phase, visibility (`always`, `path_gated`, `manual_only`), listing text, tokens,
frontmatter status and, with an area map, its area and `area_source`. JSON:
[`schema/exposure-inventory.v1.schema.json`](https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/blob/main/schema/exposure-inventory.v1.schema.json).

```json
{"kind": "skill", "source": "file", "name": "account-lookup", "qualified_name": "account-lookup",
 "path": ".claude/skills/account-lookup/SKILL.md", "scope": ".", "visibility": "always", "phase": "start",
 "paths": [], "listing_text": "account-lookup: Look up an account by email or id. Use when asked who owns an account.",
 "listing_chars": 86, "truncated": false, "text_bytes": 86, "text_sha256": "e589…", "tokens": 23,
 "line_offset": 0, "frontmatter": {"ok": true}, "area": "billing", "area_source": "skill_areas"}
```

##### `ai-rulez exposure areas`

The area map as loaded (terms normalized) and the area of every artifact with its source. Use the JSON to compare
the map with another classifier. JSON:
[`schema/exposure-areas.v1.schema.json`](https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/blob/main/schema/exposure-areas.v1.schema.json).

```text
$ ai-rulez exposure areas
Area map of /work/acme: the [exposure] table (3 areas, 1 skill_areas)

AREA          OWNER          SHARED  ARTIFACTS  PATHS
billing       team-billing   no      5          services/billing
search        team-search    no      0          services/search
platform      team-platform  yes     1          tools
unclassified                         3
...
```

##### `ai-rulez exposure collisions`

The model picks a skill or agent by its listing, so two listings of different areas that share most of their words
compete for the same requests. The command compares every listing at session start with every listing of another area
and ranks the pairs by the Jaccard index of their words (shared words over all words of both). Words are lowercase
runs of a letter and two or more letters or digits, less common stopwords. `unclassified` counts as an area of its
own. JSON:
[`schema/exposure-collisions.v1.schema.json`](https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/blob/main/schema/exposure-collisions.v1.schema.json).

With a `search-lookup` skill ("Look up a document by email or id in the search index. Use when asked who owns a
document.") added at the root of the example:

```text
$ ai-rulez exposure collisions --min-score 0
Collisions of /work/acme (plugins enabled, min score 0.00): 1 of 1 pair among 3 listings

SCORE  FIRST                 AREA     SECOND               AREA          SHARED
0.60   skill account-lookup  billing  skill search-lookup  unclassified  asked, email, look, lookup, owns, who
```

To separate two listings, start each description with the nouns of its own area rather than the words every skill
of the repository uses.

##### `ai-rulez exposure leakage`

The `AR9W0` and `AR9W1` findings of `validate` (see [Area term leakage](#area-term-leakage)), each marked
`violation`, `warning` or `accepted`, plus the `[[lint.accept]]` entries for those rules that accepted nothing.
`[lint.severity]`, `ignore_paths`, `[[lint.ignore_rules]]` and inline ignore comments apply; a baseline does not.
A start-of-session file that could not be read is listed as `unchecked`; it is not a finding. JSON:
[`schema/exposure-leakage.v1.schema.json`](https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/blob/main/schema/exposure-leakage.v1.schema.json).

#### Area term leakage

The leakage rules read the text a session sees at its start: the root `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/CLAUDE.md`,
unconditional root rules, the listing line of each root skill and agent, the server names of the root `.mcp.json`,
the enabled plugin names and, with `plugins = "enabled"` or `"all"`, the listings of the plugin skills that load.

| Code | Default | Reports |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AR9W0` `exposure-area-term` | error | A term of an area that is not `shared`, on any line of that text |
| `AR9W1` `exposure-area-term-ambiguous` | warning | A skill or agent listing that names no term at all but some ambiguous words; the area is every area that uses the word, joined by `/` (`billing/search`) |
| `AR9W6` `exposure-skill-area-unknown` | warning | A `skill_areas` key that names no skill of the inventory, on its line in the areas file or the configuration |

Text that a `CLAUDE.md` pulls in with an `@path` import (such as the `@AGENTS.md` that `generate` writes) counts toward
start tokens, but is not checked for terms.

The message of `AR9W0` and `AR9W1` is stable, so an acceptance can match on it:

```text
<kind> "<name>" at session start names term "<term>" of area "<area>"
```

Accept a finding in `[[lint.accept]]` with a reason. `match` is a case-sensitive substring of the message; `path` is
the file of the finding (`.mcp.json` for a server, the settings file that enables a plugin). An entry that accepts
nothing is reported as `AR9I0` and fails `exposure leakage`. See
[Accepting one finding](strict-validation.md#accepting-one-finding).

```toml
[[lint.accept]]
rule = "AR9W0"
path = ".mcp.json"
match = 'mcp_server "billing-'
reason = "server names stay in the root .mcp.json; their tools are deferred"
```

#### Start-of-session budgets

Two checks read the start-of-session report, computed with `[exposure] plugins` and `context_window`:

- **`AR9W3` `exposure-start-budget`** reports start tokens over `[exposure] start_budget`. Setting the budget turns
  the rule on at error, and `ai-rulez exposure` exits 2 in the same case. A start-of-session `@path` import that cannot
  be followed also fails the budget, because the total cannot be known.
- **`AR964` `load-budget-exceeded`**, row `claude-skill-listing-total`, warns when the start-of-session skill listing
  is past Claude Code's listing budget (info from 90% of it), with the `claude` preset configured.
  `[lint.load_budgets] claude-skill-listing-total = N` replaces the computed budget.

```toml
[exposure]
context_window = 200000            # listing budget: 8000 characters
start_budget = 6000                # AR9W3 above 6000 estimated start tokens
```

In the example repository, `start_budget = 300` gives:

```text
$ ai-rulez validate
.ai-rulez/config.toml:38: error AR9W3 exposure-start-budget: a session started at the repository root loads about 438 estimated tokens (5 artifacts), 138 past the [exposure] start_budget of 300; run `ai-rulez exposure` for the heaviest artifacts
```

#### Listing collisions

`AR9W2` `exposure-area-collision` is off until `[exposure] collision_min_score` is set, which turns it on at warning
with that threshold. It reports the 20 highest pairs `exposure collisions` finds, each on the description line of the
pair's first listing, and one more finding on the configuration that counts the rest. With
`collision_min_score = 0.3` and the `search-lookup` skill above:

```text
.claude/skills/account-lookup/SKILL.md:2: warning AR9W2 exposure-area-collision: skill "account-lookup" of area "billing" and skill "search-lookup" of area "unclassified" list overlapping words at session start (score 0.60, at least 0.30): asked, email, look, lookup, owns, who
```

#### A gate that cannot be read

`paths:`, `disable-model-invocation` and `user-invocable` decide when Claude Code shows a skill or rule. When the
frontmatter around them is not valid YAML, Claude Code sometimes recovers the gate and sometimes drops it:

| Frontmatter of a skill with `paths: ["src/**"]` | Claude Code |
| --- | --- |
| `description: Use when: testing` (unquoted colon) | Recovers: hidden until a file under `src/` is read |
| `description: "Use when testing` (unclosed quote) | Drops the gate: listed at start, description replaced by the first body line |
| `paths` indented with a tab | Drops the gate: listed at start |

The same doubt applies to a gate with a value of the wrong type: `paths` that is not a string or a list of strings,
or `disable-model-invocation` that is not `true` or `false`. Claude Code reads `yes`, `no`, `on` and `off` as booleans
(YAML 1.1); ai-rulez reads them as strings (YAML 1.2), so write `true` and `false`.

ai-rulez does not guess:

- `exposure inventory` gives such a root rule or skill the phase `unknown`, and the start-of-session reports count it
  as start.
- `validate` reports `AR9W4` `exposure-gate-unreadable` (warning) next to `AR306` for frontmatter that does not parse.
  It runs for the `claude` preset and without a configuration, with or without an `[exposure]` table.
- The [MCP server](mcp-server.md) never returns such a rule for a `find_context` path query, and does not serve a skill
  whose frontmatter does not parse. Only `paths:` fails closed there: a Cursor rule (`.cursor/rules/*.mdc`) whose broken
  frontmatter names `globs:` is served as a rule that applies everywhere.

Quote the value YAML cannot read (`description: "Use when: testing"`) and write gates with valid types.

#### Changed-only runs

Under `validate --changed` or `--since`, an exposure finding is kept when its own file changed or when one of the
files that shape the session changed: the areas file, the configuration, `.claude/settings.json`,
`.claude/settings.local.json` and the repository marketplace. In addition:

- `AR9W3` and the `AR964` listing total sit on the configuration and are kept when any start-of-session artifact
  changed.
- `AR9W2` sits on the first listing of a pair and is kept when either listing changed.

#### Rule codes

| Code | Name | Default | Reports |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AR9W0` | `exposure-area-term` | error | A term of a non-shared area in start-of-session text |
| `AR9W1` | `exposure-area-term-ambiguous` | warning | A start-of-session listing that names only ambiguous words |
| `AR9W2` | `exposure-area-collision` | off | Overlapping listings of different areas; on with `collision_min_score` |
| `AR9W3` | `exposure-start-budget` | off | Start tokens over `start_budget`; on (error) with `start_budget` |
| `AR9W4` | `exposure-gate-unreadable` | warning | A gate whose frontmatter does not parse or whose value has the wrong type |
| `AR9W5` | `exposure-map-invalid` | error | An unusable `[exposure]` table or area map; while it stands, no rule that reads the map runs |
| `AR9W6` | `exposure-skill-area-unknown` | warning | A `skill_areas` key that names no skill |

`AR9W5` covers a duplicate, reserved or non-kebab area name, a bad path claim (absolute, trailing slash, empty, `.` or
`..` segment, `*` other than at the end), a `skill_areas` value that names no area, an `areas_file` that is missing,
outside the project or has an unknown key, both `areas_file` and inline areas, and invalid scalar keys.

Every rule's entry, with examples, is in the [rule reference](strict-validation.md#rule-reference).

## GitHub Actions

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/github-actions/

ai-rulez ships three composite actions:

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `Goldziher/ai-rulez@v5` | installs the CLI and, optionally, exports LLM settings for later steps |
| `Goldziher/ai-rulez/check@v5` | installs the CLI and runs the full governance gate on every configuration root |
| `Goldziher/ai-rulez/update@v5` | installs the CLI, moves version-range pins with `ai-rulez update`, and opens a pull request |

All three download a release binary, verify its SHA-256 against the release's `checksums.txt`, cache it by OS,
architecture and version, and put `ai-rulez` on `PATH`. They need no Go, Node or Python.

| Platform | Supported |
| --- | --- |
| Linux amd64, arm64 | yes (glibc 2.36 or newer; Alpine/musl is not supported) |
| macOS amd64, arm64 | yes |
| Windows amd64 | yes |
| Windows arm64 | no |

#### Quick start

```yaml
name: Check agent configuration
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: Goldziher/ai-rulez@v5
        with:
          version: 5.10.0
      - run: ai-rulez generate --check
      - run: ai-rulez validate --strict
      - run: ai-rulez lock --check
```

The setup action only installs the CLI; it does not generate, validate or call a model. Put every command and its
flags (`--config`, `--profile`, `--format`, ...) in later `run:` steps. See [lock checks in CI](lockfile.md#ci-usage)
for the difference between lock drift and generated-output drift.

#### Action ref and CLI version

`uses:` and `with: version` are independent choices:

- **Action ref** (`@v5`): the action code. `v5` is a floating tag that moves to each stable 5.x release once it is
  fully published. Release candidates never move it. Pin a full release tag (`@v5.10.0`) or a commit SHA for
  reproducible action code.
- **`version`**: the CLI binary. Accepts `X.Y.Z`, `vX.Y.Z`, a release candidate `X.Y.Z-rc.N`, or `latest` (the
  default). `latest` resolves to the newest published stable release, never a draft or release candidate. `v5` is not
  a valid `version`: it is an action ref, not a release.

Omitting `version` installs the latest release even when the action ref is pinned, and `latest` may eventually install
a newer major version. Set `version` for a reproducible binary.

The action installs the requested version even when another `ai-rulez` is already on `PATH`.

##### Inputs and outputs of the setup action

| Input | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `latest` | CLI version to install |
| `llm-*` | empty | LLM settings exported to later steps; see [LLM configuration inputs](#llm-configuration-inputs) |

| Output | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | the installed CLI version, without the leading `v` |
| `path` | absolute path to the installed binary |

Give the step an `id` to read them:

```yaml
- id: setup
  uses: Goldziher/ai-rulez@v5
- run: echo "ai-rulez ${{ steps.setup.outputs.version }} at ${{ steps.setup.outputs.path }}"
```

#### Governance gate: `check`

`Goldziher/ai-rulez/check@v5` installs the CLI the same way and runs the whole gate, so a workflow does not have to list
the commands:

```yaml
name: ai-rulez
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: Goldziher/ai-rulez/check@v5
        with:
          version: 5.10.0
          expected-config-count: "2"   # the root and one module
          plugin: "true"
```

For every configuration root, in its own directory, it runs:

1. `ai-rulez migrate okf --check` (skipped for a `source = "agents"` project);
2. `ai-rulez validate --strict --no-local`;
3. `ai-rulez lock --check`, when the root has an `ai-rulez.lock`;
4. `ai-rulez generate --strict-config --no-local`, then `ai-rulez generate --check --strict-config --no-local`;
5. `ai-rulez verify --plugin`, with `plugin: true`;
6. `ai-rulez tokens --budget N --no-local`, with `token-budget: N`.

Then `git diff --exit-code HEAD` must be clean and generation must have left no new untracked file. The gate stops at
the first failing command, and fails when the checkout has no tracked files, so an empty or wrong checkout cannot pass.
It writes a job summary listing each command and its result.

| Input | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `latest` | CLI version, as for the setup action |
| `config-directories` | discover | Newline-separated configuration directories (`.ai-rulez`, `.agents`, `.config/ai-rulez`, or the project root holding one), relative to the workspace. Empty discovers every **tracked** `.ai-rulez/config.toml`, `.config/ai-rulez/config.toml` and `.agents/ai-rulez.toml` |
| `expected-config-count` | none | Fail unless exactly this many roots are checked, so a renamed or deleted module fails instead of silently checking fewer |
| `plugin` | `false` | Also run `verify --plugin` |
| `strict` | `true` | `false` drops `--strict` from `validate` and `--strict-config` from `generate` |
| `local` | `false` | `true` reads the machine-local overlay; `false` passes `--no-local` |
| `token-budget` | none | Run `tokens --budget N`: fail when the always-loaded token count exceeds `N` |

Booleans accept only `true` or `false`, counts only positive integers, and directories only relative paths without
`..`.

| Output | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | the installed CLI version |
| `roots` | the number of configuration roots checked |
| `files-examined` | the number of tracked files the clean-checkout check examined |

`token-budget` is one ceiling on the always-loaded count. A per-harness budget and the MCP tool-schema cost are not
measured; run `ai-rulez tokens` in a step for those.

#### Scheduled pin updates: `update`

Dependabot and Renovate do not read `ai-rulez.lock`, and nothing runs `ai-rulez update` on its own.
`Goldziher/ai-rulez/update@v5` runs it on a schedule and moves the version-range pins (`version = "^1.2"`) of includes,
installed skills, skill sources, marketplaces and plugins:

```yaml
name: ai-rulez update
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 6 * * 1"   # Mondays
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
jobs:
  update:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: Goldziher/ai-rulez/update@v5
        with:
          version: 5.10.0
```

The action:

1. runs `ai-rulez lock --outdated --format json`, and stops with a notice (`updated: false`) when no source has an
   update its constraint allows;
2. runs `ai-rulez update`. The pre-pin security scan applies: a refused source fails the job with its `AR` code and
   nothing is committed;
3. runs `ai-rulez generate --no-local`, then `ai-rulez lock --content-only`, and stops with a notice when nothing
   changed;
4. commits every change as `github-actions[bot]`, pushes it to `branch`, and opens a pull request into the checked-out
   branch (or refreshes the open one). The pull request body lists each source with its kind, locked tag and new tag.
   With `direct: true` it pushes the commit to the checked-out branch instead.

| Input | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `latest` | CLI version, as for the setup action |
| `names` | all | Sources to update, separated by spaces or newlines |
| `kind` | all | `include`, `skill`, `source`, `marketplace` or `plugin` |
| `direct` | `false` | `true` pushes to the checked-out branch instead of opening a pull request |
| `branch` | `ai-rulez/update` | Pull request branch. The action owns it and replaces it on each run with `--force-with-lease`, so a push by someone else in between fails the run instead of being lost |
| `token` | `github.token` | Token for `git push` and `gh`. It reaches git and `gh` through environment variables, never the command line. When `GITHUB_TOKEN` is unset it is also exported as `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which `ai-rulez` uses to read github.com release dates for `min_release_age` |
| `working-directory` | `.` | Project root holding the configuration, relative to the workspace |

| Output | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | the installed CLI version |
| `updated` | `true` when a commit was pushed |
| `commit` | SHA of the pushed commit |
| `pull-request-url` | URL of the opened or refreshed pull request (pull request mode only) |

Requirements and caveats:

- The job needs `contents: write`, plus `pull-requests: write` in pull request mode.
- The checkout must be on a branch (not a detached HEAD) with no uncommitted changes.
- A pull request opened with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` does not start other workflows. Pass a GitHub App or
  fine-grained token as `token` when the pull request must run CI.
- To hold back tags that are too new, set `min_release_age` on each source in the configuration; the action has no
  input for it.

#### LLM configuration inputs

The setup action can export LLM settings for later steps in the same job. Every input is optional. A nonempty input sets
its `AI_RULEZ_LLM_*` variable through `GITHUB_ENV`; an empty input leaves the existing environment alone. Values are
passed literally, never executed or printed. The action does not contact a provider; the CLI validates the values when
an LLM-aware command reads them.

| Input | Environment variable | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `llm-provider` | `AI_RULEZ_LLM_PROVIDER` | Provider, for example `openai` or `bedrock` |
| `llm-model` | `AI_RULEZ_LLM_MODEL` | Model, optionally prefixed with `provider/` |
| `llm-base-url` | `AI_RULEZ_LLM_BASE_URL` | Gateway or local model server URL |
| `llm-api-key-env` | `AI_RULEZ_LLM_API_KEY_ENV` | The **name** of the variable holding the key, never the key itself |
| `llm-embedding-model` | `AI_RULEZ_LLM_EMBEDDING_MODEL` | Embedding model for search |
| `llm-max-cost-usd` | `AI_RULEZ_LLM_MAX_COST_USD` | Maximum estimated spend in USD per run; `0` is unlimited |
| `llm-max-tokens` | `AI_RULEZ_LLM_MAX_TOKENS` | Maximum total prompt and completion tokens; `0` is unlimited |
| `llm-max-calls` | `AI_RULEZ_LLM_MAX_CALLS` | Maximum provider calls; `0` is unlimited |
| `llm-timeout-seconds` | `AI_RULEZ_LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Per-call timeout including retries, at most 3600 |
| `llm-cache` | `AI_RULEZ_LLM_CACHE` | `true` or `false` |
| `llm-allow-network` | `AI_RULEZ_LLM_ALLOW_NETWORK` | `true` permits model requests; unset leaves them disabled |
| `llm-allow-plain-http` | `AI_RULEZ_LLM_ALLOW_PLAIN_HTTP` | `true` allows credentials over plain HTTP to the hosts in `llm-plain-http-hosts` |
| `llm-plain-http-hosts` | `AI_RULEZ_LLM_PLAIN_HTTP_HOSTS` | Comma-separated `host` or `host:port` allowlist for plain HTTP |
| `llm-price-input-per-mtok` | `AI_RULEZ_LLM_PRICE_INPUT_PER_MTOK` | Input price override, USD per million tokens |
| `llm-price-output-per-mtok` | `AI_RULEZ_LLM_PRICE_OUTPUT_PER_MTOK` | Output price override, USD per million tokens |
| `llm-temperature` | `AI_RULEZ_LLM_TEMPERATURE` | `omit` to leave temperature out of requests |

There is no input for retries; set `max_retries` in the user configuration. Network and credential settings in a
repository configuration cannot enable requests. For defaults, budgets and provider routing, see [LLM access](llm.md).

#### Credentials

Set the provider key on the **command step** (or the job), not on the setup action: `env:` on the setup step does not
reach later steps.

```yaml
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v7
    with:
      fetch-depth: 2                 # history for --changed=HEAD~1
  - uses: Goldziher/ai-rulez@v5
    with:
      version: 5.10.0
      llm-provider: openai
      llm-model: gpt-4o-mini
      llm-api-key-env: OPENAI_API_KEY
      llm-allow-network: "true"
      llm-max-cost-usd: "2.00"
      llm-max-calls: "20"
  - name: Review agent configuration
    env:
      OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
    run: ai-rulez judge --allow-llm --changed=HEAD~1 --format json
```

- `judge` also needs `--allow-llm`; the action does not grant that consent.
- Run credentialed model reviews only on changes you trust. GitHub does not normally give secrets to pull requests from
  forks.
- Job-level `env:` reaches every step; a step's own `env:` overrides a variable the action exported.

You can skip the `llm-*` inputs and set the variables directly. `llm doctor` checks the configuration without making a
request; it must run in a repository with an ai-rulez configuration.

```yaml
- uses: Goldziher/ai-rulez@v5
  with:
    version: 5.10.0
- name: Inspect LLM configuration
  env:
    AI_RULEZ_LLM_PROVIDER: openai
    AI_RULEZ_LLM_MODEL: gpt-4o-mini
    AI_RULEZ_LLM_API_KEY_ENV: OPENAI_API_KEY
    OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
  run: ai-rulez llm doctor
```

For [Bedrock](llm.md#amazon-bedrock), configure AWS credentials through the AWS SDK credential chain (GitHub OIDC
works), set `AWS_REGION` on the command step or job, and use `llm-model: bedrock/<model-or-inference-profile-id>`.
`llm-base-url` and `llm-api-key-env` are not needed.

#### See also

- [Lock file](lockfile.md#ci-usage)
- [Strict validation](strict-validation.md)
- [Publish](publish.md), for building release artifacts in CI

## Poly hooks

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/poly-hooks/

ai-rulez publishes a hook catalog for [Poly](https://github.com/Goldziher/poly), `poly-hooks.toml` at the root of
its repository. Point your `poly.toml` at it and select the hooks you need to validate the configuration, check for
drift or regenerate output before each commit. The catalog needs Poly 0.14.0 or later.

#### Example

Add the source to your repository's `poly.toml`:

```toml
[[hooks.sources]]
id = "ai-rulez"
git = "https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez.git"
revision = "v5.10.0"
hooks = ["ai-rulez-validate", "ai-rulez-check"]
```

Choose how the hook runs ai-rulez in your gitignored `poly.local.toml`:

```toml
[hook_preferences]
channels = ["system", "npm"]
```

Resolve the revision, commit the lock and install the Git shims:

```bash
poly hooks update
git add poly.toml poly-hooks.lock
poly hooks install
```

Every commit now runs `ai-rulez validate --no-local` and `ai-rulez generate --check --no-local`.

#### Available hooks

| Hook | Runs | Purpose | Triggers on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ai-rulez-validate` | `validate --no-local` | Validate the configuration and content | `.ai-rulez/` changes |
| `ai-rulez-check` | `generate --check --no-local` | Fail when generated files are out of date | every commit |
| `ai-rulez-generate` | `generate --no-local` | Regenerate the root project | `.ai-rulez/` changes |
| `ai-rulez-recursive` | `generate --recursive --no-local` | Regenerate every project in the repository | `.ai-rulez/` changes |
| `ai-rulez-plugin-generate` | `generate --recursive --plugin --if-configured` | Regenerate plugin bundles and marketplaces | `.ai-rulez/` changes |
| `ai-rulez-plugin-verify` | `verify --recursive --plugin --if-configured` | Verify plugin bundles without writing | every commit |

`.ai-rulez/` changes means the root `.ai-rulez/` and any nested one. `ai-rulez-validate` is the non-mutating default;
repositories that publish plugins add `ai-rulez-plugin-verify`:

```toml
hooks = ["ai-rulez-validate", "ai-rulez-check", "ai-rulez-plugin-verify"]
```

The two read-only checks, `ai-rulez-check` and `ai-rulez-plugin-verify`, run on every commit, including one that
only deletes files, so a change to a preset, a custom output path or a generated file cannot skip them.

`--if-configured` makes the plugin hooks succeed when the repository has no [plugin authoring](plugins.md)
configuration: a `[plugin]` block, a `[marketplace]` with `members` or `[marketplace.from_domains]`, or
`[[plugins_authoring]]` / `[[marketplaces_authoring]]` entries. `[[plugins]]` and `[[marketplaces]]` declarations write
nothing and do not count. Real generation or verification errors still fail the hook. A marketplace root renders or
verifies its member plugins and indexes together.

##### Machine-local configuration in hooks

The `validate` and `generate` hooks pass `--no-local`: they use the shared view a teammate or CI sees and ignore your
gitignored `config.local.*` overlay and `.ai-rulez/local/` content. Machine-local outputs are left in place; run
`ai-rulez generate` without the flag to refresh them. Plugin generation and verification always use the shared view.
Do not add `--allow-local-drift` to a hook. See [Local configuration](local-overrides.md#drift-guard).

#### Sources

A Git source needs an explicit `revision` and a non-empty `hooks` list. An unknown hook ID is an error, and hooks added
to a later catalog never run unless you select them. Hook runs use the commit locked in `poly-hooks.lock`; run
`poly hooks update` after you change `revision`.

For hook development, use a local checkout instead of `git` and `revision`:

```toml
[[hooks.sources]]
id = "ai-rulez"
path = "../ai-rulez"
hooks = ["ai-rulez-validate"]
```

The path may be relative or absolute. Poly reads the catalog from it on every run and does not lock it. A source sets
exactly one of `git` and `path`.

#### Execution channels

Each hook has two channels:

| Channel | Check | Runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `system` | `command -v ai-rulez` | the installed `ai-rulez` |
| `npm` | `command -v npx` | `npx -y ai-rulez@latest` |

Poly tries the channels in the order of `[hook_preferences] channels` and runs the first whose check succeeds. With an
external hook source configured, a missing preference list, or a source with no eligible channel, is an error. When
the selected command fails, the hook fails; it does not fall through to the next channel.

The catalog revision pins the hook definitions, not the ai-rulez version. `system` runs whatever version is installed,
so install the version you reviewed in local setup and CI. `npm` runs whatever `latest` resolves to; list only
`system` when a review gate must not move with a release.

!!! warning
    Hook catalogs run commands with your user permissions. Review changes to the source and the lock before you run
    or install hooks.

#### Catalog format

Only the producer repository has a `poly-hooks.toml`; consumers do not create one. Each hook has at least one
execution path, and Poly appends the hook's `args` to the chosen path's `run` command:

```toml
version = 1

[[hooks]]
id = "ai-rulez-validate"
stages = ["pre-commit"]
args = ["validate", "--no-local"]
files = [".ai-rulez/**", "**/.ai-rulez/**"]
workspace = true
pass_filenames = false

[[hooks.paths]]
channel = "system"
check = "command -v ai-rulez"
run = "ai-rulez"

[[hooks.paths]]
channel = "npm"
check = "command -v npx"
run = "npx -y ai-rulez@latest"
```

Workspace hooks run from the repository root. Duplicate hook IDs, duplicate channels within a hook, empty paths and
unsupported catalog versions are errors.

The root hooks check the repository's own configuration once; they do not treat plugin-authoring configurations as
projects of their own, which `ai-rulez-plugin-verify` covers.

## Trust model

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/trust-model/

A repository's `.ai-rulez/` directory is content someone else may have written. ai-rulez lets you clone it and run
`ai-rulez generate` without it spending your money, sending your data anywhere or running code you did not ask for,
and gives you tools to pin, review, sign and bound everything it contributes.

The rule: **repository configuration can only tighten. Anything that leaves the machine or starts a process needs
user scope (your user config file or an environment variable) or an explicit flag.**

#### Example

A cloned repository tries to send model traffic to its own endpoint:

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml in the checkout
[llm]
allow_network = true
base_url = "https://llm.evil.example/v1"
```

ai-rulez ignores both keys and says so:

```console
$ ai-rulez llm doctor
...
network allowed: false
warning:         repository [llm] keys ignored (user scope only: set them in the user config file ~/.config/ai-rulez/config.toml or via AI_RULEZ_LLM_*): allow_network, base_url

$ ai-rulez validate --strict
.ai-rulez/config.toml:9: warning AR9L1 llm-untrusted-key: llm: repository [llm] keys ignored ...
```

To enable the network for the model, set `allow_network = true` under `[llm]` in your user config file, or
`AI_RULEZ_LLM_ALLOW_NETWORK=1` in your shell.

#### Scopes

| Scope | Where | Who controls it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repository | `.ai-rulez/config.toml` and the machine-local overlay `config.local.*` (it lives in the checkout, so it counts as repository scope) | whoever can commit to the repository |
| User | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ai-rulez/config.toml`, else `~/.config/ai-rulez/config.toml` | you, on this machine |
| Environment | `AI_RULEZ_*` variables, `DO_NOT_TRACK` | you, in this shell |
| Command line | flags such as `--allow-egress`, `--allow-exec`, `--runner-command`, `--token`, `--policy` | you, for this run |
| Organization | a [policy file](policy.md) named by `--policy`, `AI_RULEZ_POLICY` or the managed path, never found inside the repository | your security or platform team |

#### What a repository can set

| Setting | From the repository | Needs user scope, environment or a flag |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[llm]` network, endpoint, key and price keys (`allow_network`, `base_url`, `api_key_env`, ...) | **ignored**, reported by `doctor`, `llm doctor` and `AR9L1`. Budget keys are honoured but can only tighten; `provider`, `model` and the other behavior keys are honoured. Per-key list: [LLM trust rule](llm.md#trust-rule) | user file or `AI_RULEZ_LLM_*`; the environment wins over the user file |
| `[telemetry]` network and export keys (`allow_network`, `otlp_endpoint`, `headers_env`, ...) | **ignored**, reported by `telemetry doctor` and `AR9K1`; `enabled` and `sample` are honoured (a repository can at most switch on the local log). Per-key list: [telemetry trust rule](telemetry.md#the-trust-rule) | user file, `AI_RULEZ_TELEMETRY_*`, or the consent record `ai-rulez telemetry enable` writes. `AI_RULEZ_TELEMETRY=off` and `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` override everything |
| Git credentials | **no key exists** | `AI_RULEZ_GIT_TOKEN` or `--token` (see [Credentials](#credentials)) |
| External scanners (`[[lint.external]]`) | may declare a scanner and its `egress` | nothing runs without `validate --external`; an `egress = true` scanner also needs `--allow-egress=<name>` (`AR9E4`) |
| `[search.embeddings] command`, `[search] log_queries` | **ignored** with a warning; the other `[search]` keys only change ranking and are honoured | user file; `--allow-exec` honours a repository `command` for one run; the MCP server never honours it. See [Skill search](search.md#data-egress) |
| Verifiers (`[[verifiers]]`) | content predicates run; `command` and `llm` predicates may be declared | `verifiers run --allow-exec` (or `AI_RULEZ_VERIFIERS_ALLOW_EXEC=1`) runs commands; `--allow-llm` plus user-scope `[llm] allow_network` calls a model. A verifier from an include runs only when `[verifiers_settings] trust_exec_from` names it and the lock pins it. `generate`, `validate`, hooks and the MCP server never do either |
| Evals | cases are repository files | `--runner-command` picks the command; `--allow-exec` lets `command_exit` assertions run |
| `[[hooks]]` | written into the harness settings files by `generate`; pinned by the [lock](lockfile.md) and scanned | review the pull request; `generate` lists new or changed commands and asks you to review them (silence with `--yes` or `AI_RULEZ_ACK_COMMANDS=1`); `generate --user` installs hooks from your user config |
| `[[mcp_servers]]` | written into the harness MCP files by `generate`; pinned as `settings:mcp-servers` and listed in the same command acknowledgment | review the pull request; an organization policy bounds them with `mcp.allowed_commands` and `mcp.deny_transports` |
| Remote sources (`[[includes]]`, `[[installed_skills]]`, `[[skill_sources]]`) | may name a source over https, ssh or a local path (`http://` is rejected) | a content change is caught by the lock digest, and imported content is security-scanned before it is written |
| `[lock]`, `[governance]`, `[signing]` | honoured, and editable by any pull request | an [organization policy](policy.md) sets a floor the repository cannot lower. `verify --public-key` and `--identity`/`--issuer` only add signers; restricting who may sign takes a policy `[[signing.trust]]` list or `allow_repo_identities = false` |
| Organization policy | **never read** from the repository | `--policy`, `AI_RULEZ_POLICY`, or `/etc/ai-rulez/policy.toml` (and the macOS and Windows equivalents) |

A repository therefore cannot turn on network access for the model or telemetry, give itself credentials, or make a
scanner, verifier or eval run a program.

#### Credentials

- **Git token** (`AI_RULEZ_GIT_TOKEN` or `--token`) for private includes and installed skills. It is sent only to
  `github.com`, or to the comma-separated hosts in `AI_RULEZ_GIT_TOKEN_HOSTS` (environment only; replaces the
  default). It travels as a per-command `Authorization` header, so it is not in the URL, the process arguments or the
  cached clone's `.git/config`. A source on another https host gets no token and a warning; `http://`, `git://`, ssh
  and file sources never get it. Skill sources run git with no credential helper and no prompt: use public
  repositories or an SSH agent.
- **GitHub API token** (`GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN` or `gh auth token`) for release dates, review-linked approvals and `--resolve-teams`.
  It is a separate grant, sent only to `github.com` or the hosts in `AI_RULEZ_FORGE_HOSTS`. See
  [Forge client](forge.md).

Use tokens with the least scope that can read what you include.

#### Supply-chain controls

The trust rule keeps a checkout from acting on its own. The governance features make every change to what your
assistants are told explicit, reviewable and attributable:

| Question | Control | Page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Did anything change since it was reviewed? | `ai-rulez.lock` pins every remote source, authored item and generated output by digest; `lock --check` and `generate --locked` fail on drift | [Lock file](lockfile.md) |
| Who reviewed this content? | `ai-rulez approve` records a reviewer against a digest; `[governance]` makes content unusable until approved | [Approvals](approvals.md) |
| Who vouches for the lock? | `ai-rulez sign` writes a Sigstore bundle; `verify --attestation` checks it offline against named signers | [Signing](signing.md) |
| What may a repository never loosen? | an organization policy outside the repository clamps `[lock]`, `[governance]`, `[signing]`, sources, lint severities and more | [Organization policy](policy.md) |
| What is the configuration made of? | `ai-rulez sbom` writes CycloneDX or SPDX for security tooling | [SBOM](sbom.md) |
| How does ai-rulez talk to GitHub? | read-only, allowlisted hosts, token from the environment only | [Forge client](forge.md) |

Each layer is an assertion of a different strength. A digest proves bytes did not change; an approval is a recorded
claim that someone looked; a signature proves which identity produced the lock; a policy holds only if it is set from
outside the repository. None of them judges whether content is safe: pair them with the
[security checks](strict-validation.md#security-checks) and human review.

#### Limits

- The checks cover the configuration ai-rulez reads and the files it generates. A hand-written `.claude/settings.json`,
  `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json` or other harness file committed to the repository is outside its control: review
  those like code, and set `AI_RULEZ_TELEMETRY=off` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` when you open a checkout you do not trust.
- A `telemetry record --sink-command` is code you chose to run; it runs with a 3 second timeout and an output cap.
- `[lock]`, `[governance]` and `[signing]` in the repository are changed by the same pull request they gate. Protect
  them with branch protection and code owners, or enforce them with an [organization policy](policy.md).

## Lock file

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/lockfile/

`ai-rulez.lock` records exactly what your AI configuration is made of: every remote source by commit and digest, every
authored rule, skill, hook and role by content digest, and every generated file by output digest. Commit it, and CI
fails whenever any of it changes without a reviewed lock update.

#### Example

```bash
ai-rulez generate
ai-rulez lock               # writes .ai-rulez/ai-rulez.lock
git add .ai-rulez/ai-rulez.lock
```

```toml
# .ai-rulez/ai-rulez.lock (excerpt)
version = 1
ai_rulez_version = '5.10.0'
scope = 'all'
outputs_pinned = true
tree = 'sha256:4dd87fd5ae23b632928921220800a83b679b58a58cd0e2fa3127cd5196dfcbee'

[[item]]
kind = 'hook'
id = 'PreToolUse:Bash:0'
digest = 'sha256:b99ff8c5372c10a70d8862804dbbbc53d26999e3a78f97ebfea20b4cd1312fd3'

[[item]]
kind = 'skill'
id = 'deploy'
path = 'skills/deploy'
digest = 'sha256:70094bee730997ae05d11499b29571a05dde6cb5f17a4af98ed29465ba50d855'
owner = 'platform'
version = '1.2.0'

[[output]]
path = '.claude/skills/deploy/scripts/run.sh'
digest = 'sha256:e1bc260327c43375d60e256fc3326b836570497802c043c40572acbc921831a4'

[[output]]
path = 'AGENTS.md'
digest = 'sha256:2f8b8a8663f9f37c61f43723c6588bcf0b0191d90a558f59bce03ea24727d3e9'
...
```

Someone then edits a skill script and adds a rule. The check names each difference and exits `2`:

```console
$ ai-rulez lock --check
ai-rulez.lock does not match /work/acme/.ai-rulez:
  ...
  source added    rule security (rules/security.md)
  source changed  skill deploy (skills/deploy)
  output changed  output .agents/skills/deploy/scripts/run.sh
  output changed  output .claude/skills/deploy/scripts/run.sh
  output changed  output AGENTS.md
run `ai-rulez lock` to refresh it (after reviewing the change with `ai-rulez lock --diff`)
```

Review the change, then accept it with `ai-rulez lock`. `generate` never writes the lock; accepting a change is always
an explicit `ai-rulez lock`.

#### What is pinned

| `kind` | id | What the digest covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rule`, `context`, `agent`, `command`, `check` | the item name | the source file; a command's resources; the project scripts that frontmatter `hooks` run (a word starting with `./`, `../` or `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/`) |
| `skill` | the skill directory name | `SKILL.md`, every loaded resource (`references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/`) and the project scripts its frontmatter `hooks` run |
| `hook` | `<event>:<matcher or *>:<n>` | the `[[hooks]]` group as declared and each `script` file |
| `role` | the role name | the `[[roles]]` entry as declared |
| `settings` | `permissions`, `claude-managed`, `mcp-servers`, `verifiers-settings` | the `[permissions]`, `[claude.settings.managed]`, `[[mcp_servers]]` (placeholders unresolved) and `[verifiers_settings]` tables |
| `verifier` | the verifier name | the declaration as written, in `config.toml` or `.ai-rulez/verifiers/*.toml`; lowering a `severity`, widening an `exclude` or deleting a verifier changes the pin |
| `rubric` | the rubric directory name | every file under `.ai-rulez/rubrics/<id>/`, including golden cases and `calibration.json` ([Review](review.md#rubrics)) |
| `local-include` | the include name | the content directories of an include whose `source` is a local path; an OKF include is pinned whole |
| `local-skill` | the skill name | the directory of an `[[installed_skills]]` entry with a local source |
| `local-marketplace`, `local-plugin` | the entry name | the whole tree of an `[[installed_marketplaces]]` or `[[installed_plugins]]` entry with a local source |

Remote sources have their own tables, pinned by commit and tree digest: `[[include]]`, `[[skill]]` (installed skills),
`[[source]]` (skill sources), `[[marketplace]]` and `[[plugin]]`
([Installed plugins](installed-plugins.md#lock-update-and-refresh)).
Built-in packs are pinned by the ai-rulez version.

**Outputs** (`[[output]]`) are pinned from the in-memory rendering with the `Content-Hash`, `Source-Hash` and
`Generated:` header lines removed, so the digests do not depend on `[header]` settings. Not pinned: machine-local
outputs, outputs that may carry resolved secrets, and merged documents in which you own some keys (their ai-rulez
sources are pinned instead).

**Not pinned at the source**: profiles, `include` configuration, scoped (monorepo) configuration, plugin and
marketplace authoring, and the machine-local overlay. A change there shows up only through the output pins, so keep
`include_outputs` on if you rely on the lock for them. A `local_override` path is a development shortcut and is not
pinned.

A hook script outside the project cannot be pinned: `lock --check` reports it until it moves inside the project. A
symlink inside a pinned tree is never followed; it is pinned by its target string. A symlinked `ai-rulez.lock` is
refused by every command that reads it, and `lock` replaces it with a regular file.

#### File format

| Key or table | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | Lock format: `1`, or `2` when the lock holds role output pins. Any other version is refused with a request to run `ai-rulez lock` |
| `ai_rulez_version` | The release that wrote the content pins. A different running version is a note, not a failure |
| `profile` | The profile the output pins were rendered for, when not the default |
| `scope`, `outputs_pinned` | The `[lock]` settings the pins were written with; `lock --check` reports a mismatch, so a changed `[lock]` table cannot silently weaken the check |
| `tree` | One digest over every pin and remote entry. It catches accidental edits and bad merges; it is not a signature (see [Signing the lock](#signing-the-lock)) |
| `[[include]]`, `[[skill]]`, `[[source]]`, `[[marketplace]]`, `[[plugin]]` | Remote sources: `name`, `source`, `path`, `ref`, `commit`, `digest`, and with a [version constraint](#version-constraints) `tag`, `tag_object`, `released`, `released_from` |
| `[[served]]` | Skills the MCP skills server serves ([Served skills](#served-skills-and-skill-sources)) |
| `[[item]]` | Authored content: `kind`, `id`, `domain`, `path`, `digest`, and `owner` and `version` from frontmatter |
| `[[output]]` | Generated files: `path` and `digest`, or `role` and `digest` for a [role pin](#composing-with-roles) |
| `[[approval]]`, `[[deny]]` | Reviewer approvals and denied digests ([Approvals](approvals.md)); outside `tree` |
| `[[scan]]` | External scanner results ([Scan records](#scan-records)); outside `tree` |

The file is deterministic: entries sorted, no timestamps, no machine paths. A skill that comes from an include is
recorded as `include:<name>/<path>`. Running `lock` twice produces the same bytes, and the digests are the same on
every operating system as long as git records the executable bit of your scripts (see [Hashing scheme](#hashing-scheme)).

##### Scan records

`lock` writes one `[[scan]]` record per `egress = false` [external scanner](strict-validation.md#lock-records) that has
a cached result for the current content. `scan --external` fills the cache; `lock` starts no program.

```toml
[[scan]]
scanner = "cisco-skill-scanner"
version = "skill-scanner 1.2.0"
tree = "sha256:…"          # digest of the content staged for the scanner
findings = 2               # before the scanner baseline
max_severity = "warning"
result = "pass"            # fail when a finding reaches [lint.scanner_policy] fail_on
```

Records tell a reviewer what was scanned at lock time. They do not make `lock --check` fail, and a scanner with no
cached result for the content has no record.

#### Commands

```bash
ai-rulez lock                 # pin remotes (network), content and outputs
ai-rulez lock --content-only  # re-pin authored content and outputs only; offline, remote pins kept
ai-rulez lock shared          # re-pin one source by name; other pins stay as they are
ai-rulez lock --kind skill    # re-pin one kind: include, skill, source, marketplace, plugin or served
ai-rulez lock --check         # verify everything offline; exit 2 on any difference
ai-rulez lock --diff          # what `ai-rulez lock` would change; always exit 0
ai-rulez lock --subject       # the digest a signature over the lock covers
ai-rulez lock --outdated      # sources whose constraint allows a newer tag (network)
ai-rulez update --dry-run     # what moving the range pins would change
ai-rulez generate --locked    # fail when a source or output differs from the lock
ai-rulez generate --frozen    # --locked without the network
```

`lock` pins outputs for `--profile`, else the profile recorded in the lock, else the configured default. `lock` runs
the security scan over every remote tree it pins to something new and refuses error findings unless you pass
`--accept-findings` after reviewing them. `ai-rulez skill update` is `lock --kind skill`.

| `lock` exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | written, or `--check`: in sync |
| `1` | the command could not run; `--check` with no `ai-rulez.lock` |
| `2` | `--check`: differences; `lock`: a refused pin (scan findings, a moved tag, a denied digest, a policy violation) |
| `3` | written, but served skills the security scan refuses were left unpinned; `--refuse-findings` makes this exit `2` and write nothing |

With `--recursive` the most severe code over all roots wins: `1`, then `2`, then `3`.

##### `lock --check`

Offline. It renders the outputs in memory, then compares the remote pins with the local cache, every authored item
with its pin, and every output with its pin. `source` lines say an authored item changed; `output` lines say what
your assistants see changed. An output can change alone (a new ai-rulez release, a different include revision), which
is worth a look too.

It also fails (exit `2`) on a lock that pins no content, whatever `enforce` says, so stripping the content pins
