cannot switch the check off. If remote includes are configured but not in the local cache, it compares sources only and
says so in a note, or fails under `enforce`.

##### `lock --diff`

The same comparison for a pull request description or a bot, always exit `0`. `--format json` follows
[`schema/lock-diff.schema.json`](https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/blob/main/schema/lock-diff.schema.json):

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "in_sync": false,
  "lock_version": 1,
  "lock_ai_rulez_version": "5.10.0",
  "ai_rulez_version": "5.10.0",
  "changes": [
    {
      "scope": "source",
      "change": "changed",
      "kind": "skill",
      "id": "deploy",
      "path": "skills/deploy",
      "old": "sha256:1741f834511e63e2a855dbcf0510ff822543f127b3735f786971099bc5ba87e6",
      "new": "sha256:015acba08ec153ad3737ab523d24b647112572b129555371a5dccc4b0f566359"
    },
    {
      "scope": "output",
      "change": "changed",
      "path": ".claude/skills/deploy/scripts/run.sh",
      "old": "sha256:e1bc2603…",
      "new": "sha256:b9bd9b58…"
    }
  ]
}
```

| `scope` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `source` | an authored item was added, removed or changed |
| `output` | a generated file differs from its pin |
| `remote` | a remote source's cached tree no longer matches its pin |
| `served` | a served skill differs from its pin, or is no longer served |
| `lock` | the lock itself: hand-edited pins, or written with different `[lock]` settings |
| `approval` | content whose [approval](approvals.md) is missing, stale or insufficient |

`lock --check --format json` prints the same document and exits `2` on any difference.

#### Configuration

```toml
[lock]
enforce = true
include_outputs = true
scope = "all"
min_release_age = "7d"
min_release_age_source = "auto"
verify_tags = false
refresh_on_generate = false
```

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enforce` | bool | `true` when `ai-rulez.lock` exists | `validate` reports drift (`AR981`, `AR982`), `AR010` is an error so `generate` refuses an unpinned remote source, `lock --check` fails on a missing lock, `generate --locked` requires content pins, and the skills server refuses unpinned or changed skills. `false` opts out |
| `include_outputs` | bool | `true` | `false` pins sources only |
| `scope` | string | `"all"` | `"skills"` pins only skills, remote includes and installed skills (implies no output pins) |
| `min_release_age` | string | none | Default [minimum release age](#minimum-release-age) for sources with a version constraint |
| `min_release_age_source` | string | `"auto"` | Where a tag's release time comes from: `auto`, `forge`, `first-seen` or `commit` |
| `verify_tags` | bool | `false` | `generate` and `lock --check` [ask the remotes](#checking-pinned-tags-online) whether a pinned tag moved |
| `refresh_on_generate` | bool | `false` | `generate` [refreshes the lock](#refreshing-on-generate) before writing outputs |

With `enforce` on, `validate` adds:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `AR981` `lock-source-drift` | An authored item was added, removed or changed since the lock was written; or the lock has no content pins, or cannot be read or compared |
| `AR982` `lock-output-drift` | A generated output differs from its pinned digest |

Both default to `error` and can be tuned in `[lint.severity]`.

#### CI usage

```yaml
- run: ai-rulez lock --check          # pins match: sources, outputs, remote cache
- run: ai-rulez generate --check      # the committed output matches the sources
- run: ai-rulez generate --locked     # fail if a source changed without a lock update
```

`generate --check` asks "was the output regenerated after the sources changed?". `lock --check` asks "was the change
accepted?": a source edit, a new skill or a moved include must come with a lock update, which is a separate, small,
reviewable diff. Paste `ai-rulez lock --diff` into the pull request description.

##### Scheduled outdated report

A scheduled job reports sources that fall behind. It reads tags only and writes nothing. It also records every tag it
sees in the machine's `first-seen` history (`~/.cache/ai-rulez/observed-tags.toml`), which a
[minimum release age](#minimum-release-age) can use. That history is local to the machine: on a hosted runner it is lost
after the job unless you cache it, and it never helps a `lock` or `update` that runs on another machine.

```yaml
name: ai-rulez outdated
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 6 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  outdated:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: Goldziher/ai-rulez@v5
        with:
          version: 5.10.0
      - uses: actions/cache@v4                    # keep the first-seen history between runs
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/ai-rulez/observed-tags.toml
          key: ai-rulez-observed-tags-${{ github.run_id }}
          restore-keys: ai-rulez-observed-tags-
      - name: Report outdated sources
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}   # release dates; sent only to github.com
        run: ai-rulez lock --outdated --format json --fail-on-outdated | tee outdated.json
      - name: Verify pinned tags did not move
        run: ai-rulez lock --check --verify-tags
```

`--fail-on-outdated` turns the job red until someone runs `ai-rulez update` and merges the lock. To have CI open the
update pull request itself, use the [`update` sub-action](github-actions.md#scheduled-pin-updates-update). To report
updatable sources as findings instead, enable `AR734`:

```toml
[lint.severity]
AR734 = "warning"     # "error" also makes lock --outdated exit 2
```

#### Reviewing lock diffs

One block per item, sorted by kind, domain and id, so `git diff ai-rulez.lock` reads like a change list:

- a new `[[item]]` is a new rule, skill, hook or role: open the file at `path`;
- a changed `digest` with an unchanged `version` means the content moved but nobody bumped the version;
- a changed `owner` is a change of responsibility;
- a new or changed `kind = "hook"` item, or a skill script, is code that runs on developers' machines: read it;
- `[[output]]` churn with no `[[item]]` change means the rendering changed (a release, an include): find out why.

The digest tells you *that* something changed, not what. Read it next to the source diff; a lock change with no
matching source change deserves a question.

#### Version constraints

A remote include, installed skill or skill source can ask for a range of versions instead of a ref. ai-rulez resolves
the range against the repository's semantic-version tags, records the exact tag, its commit and the tree digest, and
never moves the pin on its own.

```toml
[[includes]]
name = "shared"
source = "https://github.com/acme/ai-rules"
version = "^1.2"
tag_prefix = "v"                 # optional; default accepts "1.2.3" and "v1.2.3"
include_prerelease = false       # optional
min_release_age = "7d"           # optional, see below

[[installed_skills]]
name = "deploy"
source = "https://github.com/acme/skills"
version = "~2.1.0"
tag_prefix = "deploy/v"          # monorepo tags such as deploy/v2.1.3

[[skill_sources]]
name = "vendor"
url = "https://github.com/acme/skills"
version = ">=1.4.0 <2.0.0"
```

The lock records the constraint as `ref` and what it resolved to:

```toml
[[include]]
name = 'shared'
source = 'https://github.com/acme/ai-rules'
ref = '^1.2'                          # the constraint, as written
tag = 'v1.2.4'                        # the resolved tag
tag_object = '7a9c…'                  # annotated tag object; absent for a lightweight tag
commit = '0f3e…'                      # the peeled commit
digest = 'sha256:…'                   # tree digest
released = '2026-09-28T10:00:00Z'     # only with min_release_age
released_from = 'forge'               # forge, first-seen or commit
```

| Topic | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Syntax | npm-style: `^1.2`, `~2.1.0`, `>=1.4.0 <2.0.0` (a space is AND), `1.x`, `1.2.*`, `1 - 2`, `1.x \|\| 3`, `*`. `^0.2.3` stays below `0.3.0` |
| `ref` shorthand | `ref = "^1.2"` means `version = "^1.2"` when the value contains `^`, `~`, `*` or a space (git forbids those in ref names). Setting both `ref` and `version` is `AR731` |
| Version tags | a plain version, one after a single `v`, or with `tag_prefix` the prefix plus a plain version. Annotated tags are peeled to their commit. The highest allowed tag wins |
| Prereleases | skipped unless the constraint names a prerelease of the same version (`^1.3.0-rc.1`) or `include_prerelease = true`. Build metadata is ignored |
| Who resolves | `lock` resolves a range the lock does not cover yet, and keeps a pin that still satisfies its constraint. `generate` uses the pinned commit; without a pin it resolves once, like a branch. `generate --locked`/`--frozen` fail on an unpinned range. Only `update` moves a range pin |
| Pin validity | a pin covers the config while `source`, `path` and `ref` match and the recorded tag still satisfies the constraint and `tag_prefix`. Edit the constraint and the pin is stale until `lock` |

`released` and `released_from` are informational: they are outside `tree` and `lock --check` never compares them.

##### Minimum release age

A tag published a moment ago may be a compromised release. `min_release_age` makes `lock` and `update` take the newest
allowed tag that has existed for at least that long:

```toml
[lock]
min_release_age = "7d"             # default for every source with a version constraint
min_release_age_source = "auto"

[[includes]]
name = "shared"
source = "https://github.com/acme/ai-rules"
version = "^1.2"
min_release_age = "3d"             # per source; "0" turns the gate off for it
```

Ages are a whole number with `h`, `d` or `w` (`12h`, `7d`, `2w`), at most 3650 days. A tag held back is reported as
`AR733` (info) and the next older tag that passes is used. The pinned tag is exempt: the gate never rolls a pin back.
If every allowed tag is too young and the source is not pinned yet, the result is `AR730` with the date the newest tag
becomes eligible. `lock --check` does not re-evaluate ages.

The release time comes from:

| `min_release_age_source` | Release time | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `forge` | the publish time of the tag's GitHub release ([Forge client](forge.md)) | a committer cannot forge it. When the release names a commit and the tag now points elsewhere, the time does not count. When the release names a branch, the time is the later of the publish time and the commit's first-seen time (no first-seen record: held back). A tag without a release has no time |
| `first-seen` | when this machine first saw the tag at that commit (`~/.cache/ai-rulez/observed-tags.toml`) | a tag never seen before counts as released now, so it is held back. A tag that moves counts as new |
| `commit` | the tagger or committer date | anyone who can push can forge it; protects against accidental adoption only |
| `auto` (default) | `forge`, then `first-seen` | never falls back to `commit`; when the first-seen record cannot be read or written, it warns and holds the tag back |

Every source fails closed: a tag whose time cannot be found is held back. With `auto` and a non-GitHub source, a new
project cannot lock a range until the age passes, because every tag is "seen now". The first-seen history only helps
on the machine that recorded it: run `lock --outdated` regularly on the same machine that later runs `lock` or `update`
(a self-hosted runner, or a hosted runner that caches `~/.cache/ai-rulez/observed-tags.toml`), use `commit` if that is
acceptable for the source, or pin a commit SHA.

##### `lock --outdated`

```console
$ ai-rulez lock --outdated
SOURCE  KIND     CONSTRAINT  LOCKED         ALLOWED        LATEST         NOTE
shared  include  ^1.2        v1.2.4         v1.3.1         v2.0.0         update available; newer major available
deploy  skill    ~2.1.0      deploy/v2.1.3  deploy/v2.1.3  deploy/v2.2.0  up to date within the constraint
2 source(s): 1 updatable, 1 with a newer major, 0 moved tag(s), 0 error(s)
```

It lists tags only (one `git ls-remote` per repository) and writes nothing. Limit it with source names or
`--kind` (`include`, `skill`, `source`, `marketplace` or `plugin`). With a minimum release age, `ALLOWED` is the newest tag that is old enough. `--format json`
follows [`schema/lock-outdated.schema.json`](https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/blob/main/schema/lock-outdated.schema.json),
with a `status` per source: `up-to-date`, `updatable`, `not-locked`, `tag-moved` (`AR732`), `tag-missing` (`AR735`),
`unsatisfiable` (`AR730`), `invalid` (`AR731`), `downgrade-only` or `locked-non-version`.

Exit codes: `0`, also when updates exist; `2` with `--fail-on-outdated` when any source has an allowed update, and
always for a moved or deleted tag or an unsatisfiable constraint; `1` when it could not run. It needs the network:
`--offline` refuses. `lock --check` is the offline verification.

##### `update`

```console
$ ai-rulez update --dry-run
include shared: v1.2.4 -> v1.3.1 (b21c0f3e1a9d)
  released 2026-10-20T08:00:00Z (forge)
  M  rules/security.md
  A  skills/deploy/scripts/run.sh
  tree sha256:... -> sha256:...
  scan: 0 findings
  run `ai-rulez generate`, then `ai-rulez lock` (it refreshes the output pins and the served-skill pins, which stay stale until then)
would update 1 source(s)

$ ai-rulez update shared          # rewrites the lock only
$ ai-rulez update --kind skill    # only installed skills
```

`update [name...]` moves range pins to the newest allowed tag and rewrites the lock; it edits `config.toml` only with
`--major --write-config`. Output pins are not recomputed: run `generate` and `lock` afterwards. `--format json` follows
[`schema/update.schema.json`](https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/blob/main/schema/update.schema.json).

| Situation | Behavior | Override after review |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A pinned tag now points to another commit (`AR732`) | refused, exit `2`, nothing written; `lock` refuses it too | `--accept-moved-tag` |
| The pinned tag was deleted (`AR735`) | warning; the pinned commit is still used | |
| The only newer tag has lower precedence | never selected (a truncated tag list or a mirror could roll a pin back) | `--allow-downgrade` |
| No tag satisfies the constraint (`AR730`) | exit `2` | fix the constraint |
| A tag is younger than `min_release_age` (`AR733`) | the newest old-enough tag is chosen | |
| The new tree has error-level security findings | refused, exit `2`, nothing written | `--accept-findings` |

`--dry-run` fetches and scans the new trees and writes nothing. The MCP server exposes the same operations as the tools
`lock_outdated`, `update_plan`, `lock_diff` and `update`; overrides such as `--accept-findings` stay on the command line
([Pin tools](mcp-server.md#pin-tools-lock_outdated-update_plan-update)).

###### Taking a new major version

```console
$ ai-rulez update --major
include shared: newer major v2.0.0: version = "^2.0" (now "^1.2"); `update --major --write-config` applies it
$ ai-rulez update --major --write-config shared
```

`--write-config` rewrites only the `version` value of that entry in `config.toml` (comments and layout stay), then
moves the pin with the same refusals as a plain `update`. If anything is refused, `config.toml` is restored byte for
byte. The entry must be a `[[includes]]`, `[[installed_skills]]` or `[[skill_sources]]` table with a `name` in the
project's own `config.toml`; anything else is refused with a hint to edit by hand.

##### Checking pinned tags online

`lock --check` and `generate` stay offline. To ask the remotes whether the pinned tags moved, use
`lock --check --verify-tags`, `generate --verify-tags`, or `[lock] verify_tags = true`. One `git ls-remote` per
repository compares each locked tag with its pinned commit: a moved tag is `AR732` (exit `2`, `generate` writes
nothing), a deleted one `AR735` (warning). An unreachable remote is exit `1`. The config key is skipped under
`--offline` and `--frozen`; the flag with them is an error.

##### Refreshing on generate

`generate --refresh-remote` (or `[lock] refresh_on_generate = true`) runs a lock refresh before the outputs are
written: every remote source moves to the newest version its constraint allows (a plain `ref` follows its tip),
`ai-rulez.lock` is rewritten, and generation continues from the new pins. All the defenses of `lock` apply: the
security scan, moved-tag and downgrade refusals, and `min_release_age`. Any refusal ends the run before an output is
written and leaves the lock unchanged; after review, `generate --refresh-remote --accept-findings` pins the trees anyway.

It needs the network and cannot be combined with `--check`, `--dry-run`, `--emit-plan`, `--locked`, `--frozen`,
`--offline`, `--watch`, `--recursive`, `--user` or `--plugin`; the config key is skipped in those runs.

#### Served skills and skill sources

The same lock pins [dynamic skill loading](mcp-server.md#dynamic-skill-loading), so one `lock` pins everything and one
`lock --check` verifies everything:

```toml
[[source]]            # one per [[skill_sources]] entry
name = 'vendor'
source = 'https://github.com/acme/skills'
ref = 'v1.2.0'
path = 'skills'
commit = '0f3e…'
digest = 'sha256:…'

[[served]]            # one per skill the skills server serves
name = 'deploy'
source = '.ai-rulez/skills/deploy/SKILL.md'
commit = ''
digest = 'sha256:a7a18f7b364fef319e5cdab7388daa7d0a63d3e302493d44eca4811c09427304'

[[served]]            # the same skill in another view
name = 'deploy'
view = 'role:backend'
source = '.ai-rulez/skills/deploy/SKILL.md'
commit = ''
digest = 'sha256:…'
```

A served entry is keyed by name and `view`, the way the skills server is started: `role:<name>` for `--role`,
`profile:<name>`, `targets:<preset>`, `static` for `--include-static`, and `source:<name>` per `--source`, joined by `+`
(`role:backend+static`). The default view has no `view` key. A plain `lock` pins the default view, every role and every
view the lock already records; `lock --role`, `--profile`, `--targets`, `--include-static` and `--source` add a view.

The served digest covers the files the server returns, with the generated header lines that change without the skill
changing left out. Served files are digested at mode `100644`: the executable bit is not served over MCP.

| Command | Effect on served pins |
| --- | --- |
| `lock` | a skill the security scan refuses is left unpinned and `lock` exits `3`; `--refuse-findings` writes nothing and exits `2` |
| `lock --check`, `lock --diff` | a changed served skill is a `served` change, a source whose cached tree no longer matches is a `remote` change; no network |
| `lock --kind source` / `--kind served` | refreshes one kind |
| `lock --content-only` | recomputes authored content and the served digests of local skills offline |
| `mcp --serve-skills` | with a lock, refuses unpinned or changed skills (`AR995`); `--frozen` never uses the network |

#### Composing with roles

[Roles](roles.md) are pinned as items (`kind = "role"`), so a new role or a changed `include`/`exclude` list is a lock
change. A role's rendered outputs are pinned only on request, as one aggregate digest per role:

```toml
[[output]]
role = 'backend'
digest = 'sha256:…'
```

A role is pinned when it declares `pin = true`, with `lock --roles` (every role) or `lock --role <name>`. Pins from the
command line carry `requested = true` and stay pinned on a plain `lock`. Removing `pin = true` unpins a role that only
its own key pinned. A lock with role pins is `version = 2`; an older ai-rulez refuses it rather than misreading it.

- The digest covers the files `generate --role <name>` would write, including the ai-rulez part of
  `.claude/settings.json`. The role is rendered in memory; nothing is written.
- `lock --check` compares every pinned role (`output changed  outputs of role backend`), including changes that leave
  the sources alone, such as a new generator release. `--role <name>` limits the comparison to one role.
- `lock --diff` adds the per-file digests of a changed role's current rendering (`files` in the JSON).
- `generate --locked --role <name>` verifies every source and, for a pinned role, its rendered outputs.

`ai-rulez catalog` reports, per item, its digest and whether the sources are in sync with the lock.

#### Signing the lock

The lock proves that bytes did not change; a signature says who vouched for them. `ai-rulez sign --lock` and
`ai-rulez verify --attestation` do this with a `[signing]` policy ([Signing](signing.md)). You can also sign with
`cosign` directly, as below; `verify --attestation` accepts the bundle it writes.

What is signed is the **lock subject**, a digest over the meaning of the lock rather than its bytes, so line endings and
key order do not matter, while a hand-edited pin changes the subject:

```text
lock_subject = SHA256( lp("ai-rulez/lock-subject/v1") || lp(tree) || lp(approvals_digest)
                       || u64(hash_version) || lp(scope) || u8(outputs_pinned) )
```

- `tree` is recomputed from the lock entries, never read from the file. `lock --subject` fails (exit `2`) when the
  stored `tree` disagrees, so a hand-edited lock is never signed.
- `approvals_digest` is `sha256( lp("ai-rulez/approvals/v1") || records )` over every `[[approval]]` and `[[deny]]`
  record in lock order, each field length-prefixed (kind, domain, id, digest, reviewer, assurance, `approved_at`,
  `expires`, `note`, accepted findings, `ref`, `attestation`; then the deny digest and reason). It is the empty string
  when the lock holds neither. Adding or changing an approval changes the subject, so sign after the last `approve`.
- `hash_version` is `1`; `scope` is the recorded `[lock] scope` (`all` when none); `outputs_pinned` is `1` or `0`.
- `lp`, `u64` are defined in [Hashing scheme](#hashing-scheme); `u8` is one byte.

```console
$ ai-rulez lock --subject
sha256:99d64ff310d90f8f15b52414748bf8a43f56d3f5abcdbd8750fcd01f459a4464  (lock-subject/v1; tree sha256:4dd87fd5ae23b632928921220800a83b679b58a58cd0e2fa3127cd5196dfcbee, approvals none, hash_version 1, scope all, outputs_pinned true)

$ ai-rulez lock --subject --output lock-subject.json
sha256:99d64ff310d90f8f15b52414748bf8a43f56d3f5abcdbd8750fcd01f459a4464  (lock-subject/v1; tree sha256:4dd87fd5…, approvals none, hash_version 1, scope all, outputs_pinned true)
wrote lock-subject.json
```

The statement (`schema/lock-subject.schema.json`) is deterministic, so the file a verifier recomputes is byte-identical
to the one that was signed:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "type": "ai-rulez/lock-subject/v1",
  "subject": "sha256:99d64ff310d90f8f15b52414748bf8a43f56d3f5abcdbd8750fcd01f459a4464",
  "tree": "sha256:4dd87fd5ae23b632928921220800a83b679b58a58cd0e2fa3127cd5196dfcbee",
  "approvals_digest": "",
  "hash_version": 1,
  "scope": "all",
  "outputs_pinned": true
}
```

##### Sign in the release workflow

Keyless with cosign from GitHub Actions (the signer is the workflow identity):

```yaml
permissions: { id-token: write, contents: read }
steps:
  - run: ai-rulez lock --check
  - run: ai-rulez lock --subject --output lock-subject.json
  - run: cosign sign-blob --yes --bundle .ai-rulez/ai-rulez.lock.sigstore.json lock-subject.json
```

Commit `.ai-rulez/ai-rulez.lock.sigstore.json` next to the lock. With a key: `cosign sign-blob --key cosign.key
--bundle ... lock-subject.json`. `ai-rulez sign --lock` writes the same file name (a DSSE attestation instead of a blob
signature); both verify with `ai-rulez verify --attestation`. Use one kind per release.

##### Verify

Recompute the statement from the committed lock and tell cosign who may sign:

```bash
ai-rulez lock --check                         # the lock still matches the sources
ai-rulez lock --subject --output lock-subject.json
cosign verify-blob \
  --bundle .ai-rulez/ai-rulez.lock.sigstore.json \
  --certificate-identity "https://github.com/acme/ai-config/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/main" \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  lock-subject.json
```

Verification fails when the lock changed after signing, a pin was edited, or the bundle belongs to another
repository's lock. `lock --check` is still needed: it compares the lock with the sources, while the signature only says
who vouched for the lock. The plain cosign recipe has no freshness or rollback check; `ai-rulez verify --attestation`
adds an identity policy, `max_age` and rollback detection on top of the same bundle. Plugin bundles and served skills
are signed separately ([Bundles, skills and SBOMs](signing.md#bundles-skills-and-sboms)).

#### Hashing scheme

Use this section to check a digest with an independent implementation. All digests are SHA-256, written
`sha256:<64 hex digits>`. The scheme is part of the lock format: a change to it would change the lock `version`.

Notation: `lp(x)` is the 8-byte big-endian length of `x` followed by `x`; `u64(n)` is `n` as 8 bytes big-endian.

**File leaf**, one file of an item:

```text
leaf = SHA256( lp("ai-rulez/file/v1") || lp(path) || lp(mode) || lp(data) )
```

- `path` is relative to the item, `/`-separated, with no `.`, `..`, empty segment or backslash.
- `mode` is `100755` when the file is executable, else `100644`. On Linux and macOS the owner execute bit decides; on
  Windows the mode comes from the git index (`git ls-files -s`), else `100644`. Commit the executable bit
  (`git update-index --chmod=+x`) so every operating system pins the same digest.
- `data` is the raw bytes on disk. For documents and data files (`.md .markdown .mdc .mdx .txt .toml .yaml .yml .json
  .jsonc`) `CRLF` becomes `LF` first, so a checkout with `autocrlf` pins the same digest. Scripts (`.sh .bash .zsh .py
  .js .mjs .cjs .ts`) and every other file are hashed byte for byte, because `#!/bin/sh\r` fails to run: keep scripts
  `LF` in git (`*.sh text eol=lf` in `.gitattributes`).

**Item tree**, domain-separated per kind (`rule`, `context`, `skill`, `agent`, `command`, `check`, `hook`, `role`,
`verifier`, `rubric`, `settings`, `output`, `include`, `okf-include`, `installed-skill`, `skill-source`, `served-skill`):

```text
digest = SHA256( lp("ai-rulez/<kind>/v1") || u64(n) || leaf_1 || … || leaf_n )
```

The `n` leaves (32 bytes each) are sorted by `path`, bytewise; duplicate paths are an error. A single-file item is a
tree of one leaf named after the file (`SKILL.md`, `style.md`). A declared item (a hook, a role, a settings table) is a
leaf holding its compact JSON encoding, plus one leaf per hook script.

A remote tree (include, OKF include, installed skill, skill source) is the item tree over its regular files, with `.git`
and the root `.cache_meta.json` left out. A symlink is the leaf `SHA256(lp("ai-rulez/symlink/v1") || lp(path) ||
lp(target))` and is never followed; any other non-regular entry is `SHA256(lp("ai-rulez/irregular/v1") || lp(path))`.

**Top-level `tree`**:

```text
tree = SHA256( lp("ai-rulez/tree/v1") || u64(n) || { lp(kind) || lp(key) || lp(digest) }… )
```

over every pin, sorted by `(kind, key)`: `item/<kind>` with key `<domain> NUL <id>`; `output` with the path (role
pins: `output-role` with the role name); `include`, `installed-skill`, `skill-source` and `served-skill` with the name
and `<commit> <digest>`. `digest` is the `sha256:<hex>` text of the pin. `tree` also covers the `source`, `ref`, `path`,
`tag` and `tag_object` of remote entries and the `view` of served entries. Two items with the same kind, domain and id
get a `#2` suffix on the second, in path order.

##### Test vectors

| Input | Digest |
| --- | --- |
| leaf `SKILL.md`, mode `100644`, data `# Title\nbody\n` | `cbac10c14a090ab0301ad17b0013e8c960c5960d5574dcabf38867b98987c621` (hex, no prefix) |
| tree `rule`: `style.md` = `# Style\n` | `sha256:f9c0b1ef53a34e543828ff3459f4f117e08edc2976c22a3ee32d0a65ee212c9c` |
| the same with `# Style\r\n` | the same digest (CRLF normalized) |
| tree `context`: `empty.md` = (empty) | `sha256:6e09fc1d734e8a2db85a25265407b4e78e44e45e712d4f60d2682c121f95c40b` |
| tree `rule` with no files | `sha256:c36b2dc178586a67dfcf7bc1e18ab82e0aa267eb5c5a7d7cba0a6ee7b062ec26` |
| tree `skill`: `SKILL.md` = `---\nname: deploy\n---\nDeploy.\n` (`100644`), `scripts/run.sh` = `#!/bin/sh\necho hi\n` (`100755`), `assets/logo.bin` = bytes `00 01 0d 0a 02` (`100644`) | `sha256:262d721306783b4c3b554a1345253c266f6f991733dad6a347e1b55d5e57ac05` |
| the same skill with `run.sh` at `100644` | `sha256:aea011299a41f59be23cee1a602ab3c03fb3e60aa6ce4dc31f947255925d5c73` |
| top digest of `(item/skill, "\0deploy", <the skill digest above>)` and `(output, "CLAUDE.md", "sha256:" + "ab"×32)` | `sha256:6cd1d810fce0e91263b3ebfa3610821a820a07b415a8f2a4b9415de191b6c24e` |
| tree `skill`: `run.sh` = `echo hi\n` (`100755`) | `sha256:d7aec0e55512be14e8c20554ee6da9911881211fec26eec3927bb18b21212b54` |
| the same with `echo hi\r\n` (scripts are not normalized) | `sha256:5b9fcff355356346b64a0f8146b7c65b765f377d1deddf29318ef9e686e7ee92` |
| tree `installed-skill`: `SKILL.md` = `# S\n` | `sha256:018df4aac28d9eca573a05cb491c6704407d9b5de8ca10e0dfe20300928140db` |
| tree `skill-source`: `SKILL.md` = `# S\n` | `sha256:cf90b42b8c9bbb2e9bc94075e4d8a183117f45b46d0b746b7bc617587f64bc7b` |
| tree `served-skill`: `SKILL.md` = `# x\n` | `sha256:2225664563ac4bc0affa10d8ca1ea4dcd5ed2a61792b124824005493dffb458c` |
| directory, kind `include`: `rules/a.md` = `# A\n` (`100644`), `hooks/x.sh` = `#!/bin/sh\n` (`100755`) | `sha256:94a2c6de5e10aa7eef64adb55330c4a84c02d49566d56adcedbd7f5db2ddf01c` |
| the same directory, kind `okf-include` | `sha256:990b39514f6589c5e61d584b7f59173cb8b1a3bd260ee93af92ebedc819da5e7` |
| top digest of no entries | `sha256:e8c93a22e1ed47e16dd881a55dc4fbc5ba685af20083b93469265da901784029` |

#### What the lock does not do

It does not say who published a change, sandbox anything, or tell a malicious edit from a good one. It makes every
change explicit and reviewable; a human still reviews it. Add [approvals](approvals.md) to record who reviewed,
[signing](signing.md) to prove who vouched for the lock, and the [security checks](strict-validation.md#security-checks)
for the content itself.

#### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `no ai-rulez.lock in …: nothing to check` (exit `1`) | no lock yet | `ai-rulez lock` |
| `ai-rulez.lock does not exist but [lock] enforce = true` (exit `2`) | `enforce = true` and no lock | `ai-rulez lock` |
| `unsupported lock version N` | the lock was written by a newer or much older ai-rulez | upgrade ai-rulez, or run `ai-rulez lock` with the version your team uses |
| `lock --check` reports `output changed` after an upgrade, with no source change | a new ai-rulez renders differently | review the output diff, then `ai-rulez lock` |
| Digests differ between Windows and Linux | a script is executable on disk but not in git, or a script has CRLF line endings | `git update-index --chmod=+x <file>`; `*.sh text eol=lf` |
| `lock` exits `3` | a served skill fails the security scan and was left unpinned; the skills server will refuse it | fix the finding the warning names, then `ai-rulez lock` |
| `generate --locked` fails with `authored content differs from ai-rulez.lock` | a source changed without a lock update | `ai-rulez lock --diff`, review, `ai-rulez lock` |
| A new range source cannot be locked: every tag held back | `min_release_age` with `auto` and no release history | wait; build first-seen history by running `lock --outdated` regularly on the machine that runs `lock`; or use `min_release_age_source = "commit"` for that source |

## Approvals

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/approvals/

A scan says content looks clean; an approval records that a named person read it and accepted it. `ai-rulez approve`
writes the approval into [`ai-rulez.lock`](lockfile.md), bound to the content's exact digest, and `[governance]` makes
selected content unusable until it is approved. An approval is a human assertion, never a safety proof, and on its own
it is not authentication (see [Approvals are assertions](#approvals-are-assertions)).

#### Example

Require approval for every hook and skill:

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml (excerpt)
[governance]
require_approval = ["kind:hook", "kind:skill"]
approvers        = ["alice@example.org", "bob@example.org"]
max_age          = "365d"
enforce          = true
```

After `ai-rulez lock`, nothing is approved yet and the lock check fails:

```console
$ ai-rulez approve --list
KIND   ID                 DIGEST         STATUS   REVIEWER  EXPIRES  ASSURANCE
hook   PreToolUse:Bash:0  b99ff8c5372c…  missing  -         -        -
skill  deploy             70094bee7309…  missing  -         -        -
2 require approval: 0 ok, 0 stale, 2 missing, 0 expired, 0 unauthorized, 0 insufficient

$ ai-rulez lock --check
ai-rulez.lock does not match /work/acme/.ai-rulez:
  approval: AR710 missing: hook:PreToolUse:Bash:0 requires approval and has none; review it, then run `ai-rulez approve hook:PreToolUse:Bash:0`
  approval: AR710 missing: skill:deploy requires approval and has none; review it, then run `ai-rulez approve skill:deploy`
...
```

Review the content, then approve it:

```console
$ ai-rulez approve --diff skill:deploy
skill:deploy  sha256:70094bee730997ae05d11499b29571a05dde6cb5f17a4af98ed29465ba50d855
  SKILL.md  112 bytes
  scripts/run.sh  28 bytes (executable)
  scan: no findings

$ ai-rulez approve skill:deploy --note "read scripts/run.sh" --yes
...
approved skill:deploy at 70094bee7309… by alice@example.org (assurance=asserted, expires 2027-11-05)

$ ai-rulez approve hook:PreToolUse:Bash:0 --reviewer bob@example.org --yes
approved hook:PreToolUse:Bash:0 at b99ff8c5372c… by bob@example.org (assurance=asserted, expires 2027-11-05)
```

Each approval is an `[[approval]]` table in the lock:

```toml
[[approval]]
kind = 'skill'
id = 'deploy'
digest = 'sha256:70094bee730997ae05d11499b29571a05dde6cb5f17a4af98ed29465ba50d855'
reviewer = 'alice@example.org'
assurance = 'asserted'
approved_at = '2026-11-05T00:00:00Z'
expires = '2027-11-05'
note = 'read scripts/run.sh'
```

Commit the lock. When the skill changes, its approval goes stale and the check fails again:

```text
approval: AR711 stale: skill:deploy was approved at sha256:70094bee7309… but its content is now sha256:015acba08ec1…; review the change, then run `ai-rulez approve skill:deploy`
```

#### Recording an approval

| Topic | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Naming | `kind:id` or `kind:domain/id`; a bare id works when unambiguous. Kinds are the pinned item kinds (`rule`, `context`, `skill`, `agent`, `command`, `check`, `hook`, `role`, `settings`, `verifier`, `rubric`, `local-include`, `local-skill`, `local-marketplace`, `local-plugin`) and the lock's remote entries: `include`, `installed-skill`, `source`, `served` (a served skill, with its serve view as the domain), `marketplace`, `installed-plugin`, and `role-output` ([Role outputs](#role-outputs)) |
| Pinned only | only content in the lock can be approved: run `ai-rulez lock` first. `approve` never fetches |
| What it shows | the files behind the item, the security scan findings and any earlier approval. Content with an error-level finding is refused unless you name its code with `--accept`; accepted codes are stored with the record |
| Confirmation | without `--yes` it asks on a terminal and refuses elsewhere, so a script cannot approve by accident |
| Reviewer | `--reviewer`, else `$AI_RULEZ_REVIEWER`, else the git `user.email`. A free-form string, compared lower-cased and trimmed; `github:alice`, `@alice` and `alice` are one reviewer. Use a handle if you do not want an email in a committed file |
| Expiry | `--expires YYYY-MM-DD`, else today plus `[governance] max_age`, else none. An approval holds through its expiry date, judged by the wall clock |
| Time | `approved_at` is now, or `--at`, or `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, for reproducible runs. It is re-emitted byte for byte when the lock is rewritten, so `ai-rulez lock` never makes an approval diff |
| Re-approving | replaces that reviewer's earlier record of the item; other reviewers' records stay |
| Removing | `--revoke <item>` removes the records of an item (`--reviewer` limits it to one reviewer); `--prune` removes records of content that no longer exists or whose digest changed |
| Output safety | control, bidirectional and zero-width characters in printed paths, findings and notes are shown as `\u{XXXX}`. `--note` and `--reason` are scanned for secrets and refused when they hold one |

#### When an approval stops applying

An approval is bound to the digest the lock pins ([hashing scheme](lockfile.md#hashing-scheme)). It goes **stale**
(`AR711`) on any change to the bytes of the item or of any file its digest covers (a skill's scripts and resources, a
hook's script, a remote tree) and on an executable-bit flip. A CRLF-only edit of a markdown or other text file does not
change the digest; the same edit of a script does. A remote source that moves to a new commit with an identical tree
keeps its approval.

`ai-rulez lock` keeps every approval. Stale ones stay until the content is approved again or `approve --prune` removes
them; approvals of content that no longer exists are dropped with a warning (`AR715`). A renamed item must be
approved again under its new name.

#### Requiring approvals

```toml
[governance]
require_approval = ["remote", "kind:hook", "kind:mcp_server"]
exempt           = ["skill:acme-internal/*"]
min_approvers    = 2
approvers        = ["alice@example.org", "bob@example.org", "@acme/security"]
approvers_from   = "CODEOWNERS"
min_assurance    = "review-linked"
forbid_self_approval = true
max_age          = "365d"
enforce          = true

[governance.teams]
"@acme/security" = ["carol@example.org", "github:dave"]
```

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `require_approval` | list | `[]` | What needs approval: `remote` (includes, installed skills, skill sources and remote served skills), `local` (every authored item), `all`, or `kind:<kind>` with a kind from the naming row above or `mcp_server` (the pinned `[[mcp_servers]]` declarations) |
| `exempt` | list | `[]` | Globs over `kind:id` or `kind:domain/id` (`*` any run of characters, `?` one) that never need approval |
| `min_approvers` | int | `1` | Distinct reviewers needed for one digest |
| `approvers` | list | any reviewer | Allowlist of reviewer strings. An `@org/team` entry stands for its members ([Who may approve](#who-may-approve)) |
| `approvers_from` | string | none | `"CODEOWNERS"` (in `.github/`, the repository root or `docs/`) or a path to a CODEOWNERS file inside the project: only owners of an item's path may approve it |
| `[governance.teams]` | table | none | Maps `"@org/team"` to the reviewers it stands for, offline |
| `min_assurance` | string | `"asserted"` | The weakest [assurance level](#assurance-levels) that counts |
| `forbid_self_approval` | bool | `false` | An approval by an author of the content does not count ([Self-approval](#self-approval)) |
| `max_age` | string | none | Default and maximum lifetime of an approval, `365d` or a Go duration such as `720h`. Past `approved_at` plus `max_age` an approval is expired (`AR712`) whatever its `expires` says |
| `enforce` | bool | `false` | Make `lock --check`, `generate --locked` and `mcp --serve-skills` fail. `validate` reports either way |

`[governance]` in the machine-local overlay is ignored with a warning. An [organization policy](policy.md) can set a
floor under it: `enforce` on, selectors that `exempt` cannot narrow, a minimum `min_approvers` and `min_assurance`,
`forbid_self_approval`, `approvers_from = "CODEOWNERS"`, and the only `approvers` that count. A repository that loosens
one is clamped and reported as `AR740`.

Under `enforce` the check never fails open: a missing `ai-rulez.lock`, or one that pins no content, is `AR710`.

#### Where it is enforced

| Where | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `validate` | `AR710` to `AR719` at their default severities, with or without `enforce` |
| `lock --check`, `generate --locked` | with `enforce`, exit `2` for content whose approval is missing, stale, expired, unauthorized or insufficient. `lock --diff --format json` lists them with `scope: "approval"` |
| `mcp --serve-skills` | with `enforce`, a selected served skill without a valid approval of its served digest is refused with its `AR71x` code. Provenance gains `approved` and `approvers` |
| `catalog --format json --schema-version 2` | `items[].approval` is `{required, status, reviewers, assurance, expires}` (`schema/catalog.schema.json`) |
| `approve --list --format json` | the policy and the status of every item (`schema/approve-list.schema.json`); `--all` also lists content that needs no approval |
| `sbom` | per-component `ai-rulez:approval` status ([SBOM](sbom.md#approvals-and-signature)) |

| Code | Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AR710` | `approval-missing` | Required, no record |
| `AR711` | `approval-stale` | Records exist, none for the current digest |
| `AR712` | `approval-expired` | Every record of the current digest is past `expires` or `max_age` |
| `AR713` | `approver-not-authorized` | Every record of the current digest is by a reviewer outside `approvers` or CODEOWNERS |
| `AR714` | `approval-insufficient` | Fewer distinct valid reviewers than `min_approvers`, or none at `min_assurance` |
| `AR715` | `approval-orphan` | A record names content that no longer exists (warning) |
| `AR716` | `approval-with-change` | An approval arrived in the same change as its content, or by an author of it ([Approvals are assertions](#approvals-are-assertions)) |
| `AR717` | `approval-denied` | The digest is on the [deny list](#deny-list) |
| `AR718` | `approval-unverified` | Every approval of the current digest claims an assurance that could not be verified |
| `AR719` | `approver-unresolved` | `approvers_from` or a team cannot be resolved, so nobody is authorized by it |

#### Assurance levels

| Level | Written by | The record carries | How it is checked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `asserted` | `approve` | a free-form reviewer string | not at all: it is as strong as the review of the change that adds it |
| `review-linked` | `approve --from-github-review` | `github:<login>` and `ref`, the URL of an approving pull request review | offline, the `ref` must be a well-formed review link of the `origin` repository; `verify --approvals --online` asks the forge |
| `signed` | `approve --sign` | a DSSE attestation under `.ai-rulez/attestations/`; the signer is the reviewer | offline, against `[[signing.trust]]` entries with `subject = "approval"` |

With `min_assurance = "signed"` an `asserted` record never counts. A record that claims a level it cannot back (a
`signed` one whose attestation does not verify, a `review-linked` one without a `ref`) does not count (`AR718`).
`approve --list` shows the weakest assurance among the approvals that apply.

#### Who may approve

Without `approvers` and `approvers_from`, any reviewer string counts. With both set, both must hold.

- `approvers` is an allowlist; an `@org/team` entry expands through `[governance.teams]`, or from the forge with
  `approve --resolve-teams` (a token with `read:org`, see [Forge client](forge.md)). `validate` and the skills server
  never call the forge, so list teams in `[governance.teams]` for them.
- `approvers_from = "CODEOWNERS"` resolves the owners of the item's source path: the file of a rule, the directory of
  a skill, or `.ai-rulez/ai-rulez.lock` for content without a source file (includes, installed skills, sources,
  served skills, role outputs). Owners can be `@user`, `@org/team` or an email.

CODEOWNERS is matched with GitHub's rules: gitignore-like patterns, the last matching line wins, a pattern without a
slash matches at any depth, a leading `/` anchors, a trailing `/` owns everything below, `docs/*` owns only the files
directly in `docs/`, `**` crosses directories. Lines with `!` or `[abc]` are ignored, as GitHub does.

Everything fails closed: a CODEOWNERS file that cannot be found, a path no line covers and a team with no known members
authorize nobody, and `validate` says why (`AR719`).

#### Review-linked approvals

```console
$ git fetch origin pull/42/head
$ ai-rulez approve include:shared --from-github-review 42 --yes
approved include:shared at 51e0a1b2c3d4… by github:alice (assurance=review-linked, expires 2027-11-05)
```

`--from-github-review <pr>` records one `review-linked` approval per qualifying reviewer of the pull request
(`--reviewer github:alice` picks one). The repository comes from the git `origin` (or `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`) and its host
must be on the [forge allowlist](forge.md#safety-properties). A review counts when all of these hold:

- it is the reviewer's latest decisive review and it is `APPROVED` (a later `CHANGES_REQUESTED` or `DISMISSED`
  withdraws it);
- the reviewer is named by `approvers` or CODEOWNERS for the item, or is an `OWNER`, `MEMBER` or `COLLABORATOR` of the
  repository with a `write`, `maintain` or `admin` role (the role is read when the token has push access; otherwise the
  association is the evidence). A drive-by approval on a public repository approves nothing;
- the review was made on the pull request's **final head commit**. A review of an earlier head approves nothing: push,
  then ask for a new review;
- the content at that commit has the digest being approved. Authored content is recomputed from the files of that
  commit, never read from the lock committed there; content only the lock describes (remote includes, installed skills,
  remote served skills, role outputs) is taken from the lock at that commit. The head must be in the local clone;
- the reviewer passes `approvers` and `approvers_from`, and with `forbid_self_approval` is not the pull request author.

Approving in the same pull request that changes the content is still `AR716`: record the approval from the merged pull
request, in a later change (see the [workflow](#approval-bot-workflow)).

#### Signed approvals

```console
$ ai-rulez approve hook:PreToolUse:Bash:0 --sign --key approver.key --yes
...
approved hook:PreToolUse:Bash:0 at b99ff8c5372c… by key:sha256:c49716c6aeb4b89ba6176d8b7e7951b9a8801e92498d9104b4e4c58f8d8e0ac9 (assurance=signed, expires 2027-11-05)
```

```toml
[[approval]]
kind = 'hook'
id = 'PreToolUse:Bash:0'
digest = 'sha256:b99ff8c5372c10a70d8862804dbbbc53d26999e3a78f97ebfea20b4cd1312fd3'
reviewer = 'key:sha256:c49716c6aeb4b89ba6176d8b7e7951b9a8801e92498d9104b4e4c58f8d8e0ac9'
assurance = 'signed'
approved_at = '2026-11-05T00:00:00Z'
expires = '2027-11-05'
attestation = 'sha256:a001cd034d1a7a18282a2ec965cf38aaa5908df98c90c40d76a5d9186c6923de'
```

`--sign` signs an in-toto statement (predicate `https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/attestations/approval/v1`) over the
item digest, the expiry and the accepted findings, and writes the bundle to
`.ai-rulez/attestations/<sha256>.sigstore.json`. Commit it with the lock. `--key` signs offline; `--keyless` uses a
Fulcio certificate and a public Rekor entry, with the same flags as [`sign`](signing.md#sign). The verified signer
replaces the reviewer string: `key:<fingerprint>` for a key, the certificate identity for keyless. `--reviewer` does
not combine with `--sign`. With `approvers` set, list the signer as it is recorded (`key:sha256:…` or the identity).

Name who may sign approvals with `[[signing.trust]]` entries whose `subject` is `"approval"`:

```toml
[governance]
require_approval = ["remote"]
min_assurance    = "signed"
approvers        = ["https://github.com/acme/ai-config/.github/workflows/approve.yml@refs/heads/main"]

[[signing.trust]]
subject  = "approval"
identity = "https://github.com/acme/ai-config/.github/workflows/approve.yml@refs/heads/main"
issuer   = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
```

A signed record counts only when its bundle verifies against those entries, covers exactly this item and digest, and
agrees with the record (reviewer, `approved_at`, expiry, accepted findings), so editing the lock after signing breaks it
(`AR718`). For keyless signing, `approvers` and CODEOWNERS are checked before anything reaches the public log. The
approval set is part of the signed [lock subject](lockfile.md#signing-the-lock): sign the lock after the last
`approve`.

#### Deny list

```console
$ ai-rulez approve --revoke hook:PreToolUse:Bash:0 --deny --reason "runs curl | sh"
revoked 1 approval(s) of hook:PreToolUse:Bash:0
denied hook:PreToolUse:Bash:0 sha256:b99ff8c5372c10a70d8862804dbbbc53d26999e3a78f97ebfea20b4cd1312fd3
```

```toml
[[deny]]
digest = 'sha256:b99ff8c5372c10a70d8862804dbbbc53d26999e3a78f97ebfea20b4cd1312fd3'
reason = 'runs curl | sh'
```

A denied digest can be neither approved nor used, whether or not `[governance]` selects the item:

- `approve` refuses it, `validate` reports `AR717` for any pinned content with that digest, and the skills server never
  serves a denied skill;
- `ai-rulez lock` refuses to pin it: change the content and lock again;
- the entry names the digest, not the item, so it survives re-locking and blocks a rollback to the old bytes.

Remove an entry by editing the lock in a reviewed change. An organization policy's `sources.deny_digests` is a second,
organization-wide list (`AR747`, see [Organization policy](policy.md)).

#### Role outputs

A role whose outputs are pinned ([`pin = true`](lockfile.md#composing-with-roles), or `lock --roles`) has an approval
subject of kind `role-output` (`role-output:backend`): the rendering the role produces, not only the sources it selects.

- Only `require_approval = ["kind:role-output"]` selects it; `all`, `local` and `remote` do not.
- `approve role-output:backend` renders the role in memory, shows the files and scans them. It refuses when the
  rendering differs from the pin: run `ai-rulez lock --roles` first.
- `role:backend` (the role declaration) and `role-output:backend` are separate subjects.

#### Self-approval

With `forbid_self_approval = true` an approval does not count when its reviewer authored a commit that touched the item
since a base revision:

- `approve` counts commit authors since `--base <rev>`, else the branch's upstream, else `origin/HEAD`, and refuses
  when none can be found;
- `approve --verify-base <rev>` and `validate --approvals-base <rev>` report such approvals as `AR716`;
- with `--from-github-review`, the pull request author's own review is skipped.

Authors are matched by commit email (with `.mailmap`) or the GitHub noreply address of a `github:` login against the
reviewer string. It catches honest mistakes, not collusion. A key signature names no person, so with
`forbid_self_approval` it is `AR716` unless its trust entry names the owner:

```toml
[[signing.trust]]
subject  = "approval"
key_file = ".ai-rulez/keys/alice.pub"
reviewer = "alice@example.org"
```

#### Verifying approvals

```console
$ ai-rulez verify --approvals
OK    signed        hook:PreToolUse:Bash:0  key:sha256:c49716c6aeb4b89ba6176d8b7e7951b9a8801e92498d9104b4e4c58f8d8e0ac9
SKIP  review-linked include:shared  github:alice: needs --online: a review link cannot be verified offline

$ ai-rulez verify --approvals --online
OK    signed        hook:PreToolUse:Bash:0  key:sha256:c49716c6aeb4b89ba6176d8b7e7951b9a8801e92498d9104b4e4c58f8d8e0ac9
OK    review-linked include:shared  github:alice
```

`verify --approvals` re-checks the approvals above `asserted` that apply to the current content: signed ones against
their attestations offline, and with `--online` review-linked ones against the forge (the review still exists, still
approves, and was made on content with the approved digest). Exit `0` every checked approval holds, `2` one does not
(`AR718`), `1` the check could not run, including an unreachable forge or a missing token. `--format json` follows
`schema/verify-approvals.schema.json`. Run it in CI wherever `min_assurance = "review-linked"` is the policy.

#### Approval-bot workflow

The strongest setup needs no person to hold a signing identity: a workflow records approvals from the reviews of a
merged pull request, in a follow-up pull request that a code owner of `ai-rulez.lock` merges.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/approve.yml
name: record approvals
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [closed]
permissions:
  contents: write        # push the approval branch
  pull-requests: write   # open the follow-up pull request
jobs:
  approve:
    if: github.event.pull_request.merged == true
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
          fetch-depth: 0
      - run: git fetch origin "pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}/head"
      - uses: Goldziher/ai-rulez@v5
        with:
          version: 5.10.0
      - name: Record the approvals of the merged pull request
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          ai-rulez approve --list --format json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.status != "ok") | .ref' > pending.txt
          xargs -r ai-rulez approve --from-github-review "${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}" --yes < pending.txt
          ai-rulez verify --approvals --online
      - uses: peter-evans/create-pull-request@v6
        with:
          branch: approvals/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          title: "chore: record approvals of #${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}"
          add-paths: .ai-rulez/ai-rulez.lock
```

- Pin the actions by commit.
- Put `ai-rulez.lock` under CODEOWNERS and require that owner's review on the follow-up pull request.
- To sign instead, add `id-token: write`, call `approve --sign --keyless`, and trust the workflow in
  `[[signing.trust]]` with `subject = "approval"`. The identity is the workflow file at a ref: protect both.
- A pull request from a fork gets a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Do not widen it, and never run pull request code in a
  workflow that holds a write token.

#### Approvals are assertions

An `asserted` approval is a string in a committed file. ai-rulez does not know who ran `approve`, and anyone who can
edit the lock can add a record for any reviewer. Its strength is the review of the change to the lock. The
`[governance]` table itself is changed by the same pull request it gates, which is why an organization
[policy](policy.md) can set a floor under it.

Run this on every pull request whose base branch is trusted:

```bash
ai-rulez approve --verify-base origin/main        # exit 2 on AR716
ai-rulez validate --approvals-base origin/main
```

Both compare the lock with the one at the merge base and report (`AR716`):

- every new `[[approval]]` whose item is also new or changed in the same change;
- a change to the CODEOWNERS file `approvers_from` names, or to the `[governance]` table;
- a new approval whose reviewer did not own the item in CODEOWNERS as it was at the merge base.

An approval of content the base already pinned at the same digest is a later review and passes. An unknown revision is
an error (exit `1`), never a pass. A finding means the change cannot vouch for itself: land the content first and
approve it in a following change, or require a second reviewer through code owners on `ai-rulez.lock`. Treat any pull
request that touches `[[approval]]`, `[[deny]]` or `[governance]` as sensitive.

Where approvals must hold against a hostile change, set `min_assurance = "review-linked"` or `"signed"` and run
`verify --approvals --online` in CI.

#### Troubleshooting

| Message | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `not a terminal: refusing to approve without --yes` | `approve` in a script or CI | pass `--yes` |
| `… is not in [governance] approvers` | the reviewer, or the signing key's `key:sha256:…` identity, is not allowlisted | add it to `approvers`, or approve as an allowlisted reviewer |
| `… changed while it was being reviewed; nothing was written` | the content's digest changed between the review and the write | review it again, then re-run `approve` |
| `AR711 stale` after `ai-rulez lock` | the content changed since it was approved | `approve --diff <item>`, then `approve <item>` |
| `AR717 … is on the deny list … and cannot be approved` | the digest is in `[[deny]]` or the policy's `deny_digests` | change the content |
| `AR719 approver-unresolved` | no CODEOWNERS file, no line covers the path, or a team has no known members | add the CODEOWNERS line or `[governance.teams]` entry, or use `--resolve-teams` |
| `AR716` on a pull request | the approval arrived with the content it approves | approve in a later change |

## Signing

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/signing/

A digest proves that bytes did not change; a signature says who produced them. `ai-rulez sign --lock` signs the
[lock](lockfile.md) into a [Sigstore](https://www.sigstore.dev) bundle, and `ai-rulez verify --attestation` checks it
offline against a policy that names who may sign. The same commands sign [plugin bundles, published skills and SBOM
files](#bundles-skills-and-sboms), support [KMS keys](#kms-keys), [k-of-n signers](#thresholds) and
[SLSA provenance](#slsa-provenance), and can [gate served skills](#served-skills-and-publisher-signed-skills).

Signing is opt-in; nothing is enforced until `[signing] require` says so. A valid signature means "produced by this
identity", not "safe": a validly signed skill still needs [approval](approvals.md) and the
[security checks](strict-validation.md#security-checks).

#### Example

Sign with a key, offline:

```bash
openssl genpkey -algorithm EC -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-256 -out release.key   # or: cosign generate-key-pair
ai-rulez lock
ai-rulez sign --lock --key release.key --public-key-out .ai-rulez/keys/release.pub
```

```text
INFO  Signed ai-rulez.lock signer=key sha256:c49716c6aeb4b89ba6176d8b7e7951b9a8801e92498d9104b4e4c58f8d8e0ac9 subject=sha256:f4a4a2b1382eab3578b7f76eb4495651fc208f6161aaa83ef94618f64ae1e0a2 bundle=/work/acme/.ai-rulez/ai-rulez.lock.sigstore.json
```

Name the trusted key and require the signature:

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml (excerpt)
[signing]
require  = ["lock"]
key_file = ".ai-rulez/keys/release.pub"
```

Commit `.ai-rulez/ai-rulez.lock.sigstore.json` and the public key. Verify:

```console
$ ai-rulez verify --attestation
warning: the trusted signers come from this repository's own [signing] configuration: whoever can change the repository can change who may sign. Pass --public-key or --identity with --issuer from CI configuration outside the repository to pin them
OK  lock  signer=sha256:c49716c6aeb4b89ba6176d8b7e7951b9a8801e92498d9104b4e4c58f8d8e0ac9
    issuer=none (key)  logged=no  age=7s  hash_version=1
    no transparency log or timestamp: the signing time is the signer's own claim (weak freshness)
```

Any later change to the lock, including a new approval, invalidates the signature. `lock --check`, `generate --locked`
and `validate` then fail:

```text
ai-rulez.lock does not carry the signature [signing] require asks for:
  AR724 attestation-subject-mismatch: ai-rulez.lock changed since it was signed (its subject is sha256:1b13f187d8e956cb156b25f9a0610264879b584b55b93f8929433d41478e6dad)
```

Re-sign after the final `ai-rulez lock` and `ai-rulez approve`.

#### What is signed

The bundle holds a DSSE envelope over an in-toto statement v1. Its subject is the **lock subject** that
[`lock --subject`](lockfile.md#signing-the-lock) prints, not the bytes of `ai-rulez.lock`, so a signature survives
line-ending changes and TOML re-ordering, while a hand-edited pin or approval changes the subject.

```json
{
  "_type": "https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1",
  "subject": [{ "name": "ai-rulez.lock", "digest": { "sha256": "<lock subject hex>" } }],
  "predicateType": "https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/attestations/lock/v1",
  "predicate": {
    "hash_version": 1,
    "tree": "sha256:...",
    "approvals_digest": "",
    "scope": "all",
    "outputs_pinned": true,
    "ai_rulez_version": "5.10.0",
    "repository": "https://github.com/acme/ai-config",
    "ref": "refs/heads/main",
    "issued_at": "2026-11-05T12:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

`repository` and `ref` come from the GitHub Actions variables or the git origin (credentials removed). They identify
the project for rollback detection; they are claims, not proof. `sign --embed-items` adds the pinned item ids and
digests (`items`), so a reviewer can compare two signed states; it is off by default because ids can be sensitive.

The bundle is written to `.ai-rulez/ai-rulez.lock.sigstore.json`; `[signing] attestation` or `sign --output` change it.

#### Sign

| Mode | Command | Network | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Key | `sign --lock --key <file>` | none; `--tlog` adds a Rekor entry | an ECDSA P-256/P-384/P-521 or ed25519 PEM key (PKCS#8 or a cosign key) |
| KMS | `sign --lock --key awskms:///alias/release` | the KMS; `--tlog` adds a Rekor entry | a [KMS key](#kms-keys) and the provider's credentials |
| Keyless | `sign --lock --keyless` | Fulcio and Rekor | an OIDC token |

A key's password is read from `AI_RULEZ_SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD`, then `COSIGN_PASSWORD` (`--key-password-env` names
another variable); it is never a flag. `--public-key-out <file>` writes the key's public half for `key_file`.

Keyless signing exchanges an OIDC token for a short-lived Fulcio certificate and records the signature in Rekor. The
token comes from the variable `--identity-token-env` names, else the GitHub Actions runtime (`permissions: id-token:
write`), else `--interactive` opens a browser. **Your OIDC identity, the certificate and the subject digest go to the
public transparency log** unless `--rekor-url` and `--fulcio-url` point at a private Sigstore deployment. Use key mode
when you do not want identities logged.

```yaml
# GitHub Actions, keyless
permissions: { id-token: write, contents: read }
steps:
  - run: ai-rulez lock --check
  - run: ai-rulez sign --lock --keyless
  - run: ai-rulez verify --attestation
```

`sign --format json` prints `schema/sign-report.schema.json`.

#### Policy

`[signing]` in `.ai-rulez/config.toml` says what must be signed, who may sign and how fresh a signature must be:

```toml
[signing]
require = ["lock"]
max_age = "180d"
tlog = "required"
trusted_root = ".ai-rulez/keys/trusted_root.json"
min_hash_version = 1

# shorthand: one trusted keyless signer for the lock
identity = "https://github.com/acme/ai-config/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/main"
issuer = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
# or one trusted key for the lock
# key_file = ".ai-rulez/keys/release.pub"

# full form: repeatable, scoped, with validity windows
[[signing.trust]]
subject = "lock"
identity_regexp = "^https://github\\.com/acme/[^/]+/\\.github/workflows/release\\.yml@refs/heads/main$"
issuer = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
valid_from = "2026-01-01"
valid_until = "2027-01-01"

[[signing.trust]]
key_file = ".ai-rulez/keys/release.pub"
```

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `require` | list | `[]` | Subjects that must carry a valid attestation: `lock` (`lock --check`, `generate --locked` and `validate` fail without one), `served` and `skill` ([served skills](#served-skills-and-publisher-signed-skills)) |
| `max_age` | string | none | Oldest acceptable signature (`180d`, `720h`); older is `AR723` |
| `tlog` | string | `required` with a certificate identity, `off` with keys only | `required`, `optional` (a log entry or a signed timestamp) or `off` (keys only) |
| `trusted_root` | string | the `trust update` cache | Sigstore trusted root for keyless verification |
| `min_hash_version` | int | none | Reject attestations of an older hash scheme (`AR724`) |
| `attestation` | string | `ai-rulez.lock.sigstore.json` | Lock bundle path, relative to the configuration directory |
| `identity`, `issuer` | string | none | Shorthand: one trusted keyless signer for the lock |
| `key_file` | string | none | Shorthand: one trusted public key for the lock |
| `[[signing.trust]]` | table list | none | Full trust entries (below) |
| `[signing.thresholds]` | table | `1` per subject | [k-of-n signers](#thresholds) |
| `require_provenance`, `builders` | bool, list | `false`, any | [SLSA provenance](#slsa-provenance) requirements |

| `[[signing.trust]]` key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `subject` | What the signer may vouch for: `lock` (default), `bundle`, `skill`, `sbom` or `approval` ([signed approvals](approvals.md#signed-approvals)). A key trusted for the lock does not vouch for a skill |
| `identity`, `identity_regexp`, `issuer` | A keyless signer. `identity` and `issuer` are matched exactly; `identity_regexp` is matched against the whole identity and must be anchored with `^` and `$` (otherwise `AR722`). An identity always needs an `issuer` |
| `key_file` | A PEM public key, matched by its SHA-256 fingerprint |
| `reviewer` | The person a key belongs to (`alice@example.org`, `github:alice`), for thresholds and [self-approval](approvals.md#self-approval) checks |
| `source` | Skill entries only: limit a publisher to one `[[skill_sources]]` or `[[installed_skills]]` name |
| `valid_from`, `valid_until` | Inclusive UTC bounds on the signing time the entry accepts, so an expiry is a reviewed event |

`key_file`, `trusted_root` and `attestation` must stay inside the project; `key_file` and `trusted_root` are relative
to the project root. A symlink out of the project is refused. `[signing]` in the machine-local overlay is ignored with a
warning, so it cannot add a signer.

Verification without a trusted signer for the subject is an error (exit `1`), never "accept any valid signature".

The repository can edit its own `[signing]` table, so a pull request can weaken it or name its own signer.
`verify --attestation` warns when the signers come from the repository alone. `--public-key` and `--identity` with
`--issuer` **add** signers; they do not replace the repository's, so they protect you only when the repository's table
is empty. To stop a pull request from naming its own signer, restrict the signers with an
[organization policy](policy.md) (`[[signing.trust]]` in the policy, or `allow_repo_identities = false`), or fail CI
when the `[signing]` table changes.

#### Verify

```console
$ ai-rulez verify --attestation --public-key ci/release.pub
OK  lock  signer=sha256:c49716c6aeb4b89ba6176d8b7e7951b9a8801e92498d9104b4e4c58f8d8e0ac9
    issuer=none (key)  logged=no  age=0s  hash_version=1
    no transparency log or timestamp: the signing time is the signer's own claim (weak freshness)
```

A keyless signature reports its identity and log time instead:

```text
OK  lock  signer=https://github.com/acme/ai-config/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/main
    issuer=https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com  logged=2026-11-04T09:12:03Z  age=1d  hash_version=1
```

Verification is offline: it reads the bundle, the lock and a trusted root, and sends nothing. It checks the signature,
certificate chain and log proof (`AR721`, `AR725`, `AR726`), that the signed digest is the lock's recomputed subject
(`AR724`), the signer against the policy (`AR722`), `max_age` and future timestamps (`AR723`), and rollback (`AR727`).

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | verified |
| `1` | could not check: no trusted signer, no trusted root for a certificate bundle, unreadable lock |
| `2` | verification failed (`FAIL  lock  AR724 …`) |

`--format json` prints `schema/verify-attestation.schema.json`. With `[signing] require = ["lock"]`, `lock --check`,
`generate --locked` (and `--frozen`) and `validate` run the same checks and report the same `AR720` to `AR728` codes.

##### Trusted root

A keyless certificate is checked against a Sigstore trusted root (the Fulcio and Rekor roots and CT log keys). It is
read from `--trusted-root <file>`, then `[signing] trusted_root`, then the cache `ai-rulez trust update` fills
(`~/.cache/ai-rulez/sigstore/trusted_root.json`). `trust update` fetches the public-good root over TUF and is the only
verification step that uses the network. For a private Sigstore deployment pass its root file. Key-signed bundles need
no root unless they carry a log entry.

A root committed to the repository is as trustworthy as the repository's review process; for a stronger guarantee pass
`--trusted-root` from CI configuration.

##### Freshness and rollback

- **`max_age`** compares the time a transparency log or timestamp authority saw the signature with now. A key bundle
  without a log entry has only the `issued_at` the signer wrote, reported as `weak`: use `sign --tlog` or keyless when
  freshness matters. A signing time more than five minutes in the future fails with `AR723`.
- **Rollback** is detected per machine: `verify --attestation` records the newest signing time it verified for each
  signer and project, and an older attestation fails with `AR727` (the message names the state file to delete if the
  newer one was wrong). A bundle with no time records the lock versions this machine has seen instead.
- The state lives outside the checkout (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/ai-rulez/signing-state.json`, else
  `~/.local/state/ai-rulez/`) and is authenticated with a per-user secret, so a repository cannot plant or reset it.
  `lock --check`, `generate --locked` and `validate` read it; only `verify --attestation` advances it. `--no-state`
  skips it.
- A fresh machine or CI runner starts with no state, so an old valid bundle passes there within `max_age`. Set
  `max_age` to your release cadence.

#### Bundles, skills and SBOMs

```console
$ ai-rulez sign --bundle dist/acme-plugin --key release.key
INFO  Signed bundle path=dist/acme-plugin signer=key sha256:91be... subject=sha256:4f1a... bundle=dist/acme-plugin/.ai-rulez.sigstore.json
$ ai-rulez verify --bundle dist/acme-plugin --public-key release.pub
OK  bundle  signer=sha256:91be...
    issuer=none (key)  logged=no  age=3s
    digest=sha256:4f1a...
```

| Subject | Sign | Verify | Statement subject | Sidecar |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Plugin bundle | `sign --bundle <dir>` | `verify --bundle <dir>` | tree digest of every file in the directory | `<dir>/.ai-rulez.sigstore.json` |
| Published skill | `sign --skill <dir>` | `verify --skill <dir> [--source <name>]` | tree digest of the skill directory | `<dir>/.ai-rulez.sigstore.json` |
| SBOM | `sign --sbom <file>` | `verify --sbom <file>` | SHA-256 of the file's bytes | `<file>.sigstore.json` |
| Organization policy | `sign --org-policy <file>` | loaded by the [policy](policy.md#signed-policies) loader | the policy digest | `<file>.sigstore.json` |

The directory digest uses the lock's [hashing scheme](lockfile.md#hashing-scheme): adding, removing or editing a file,
or flipping an executable bit, invalidates the signature (`AR724`). The attestation files at the root of the directory
are not part of what they sign. A symlink, an irregular file or a nested `.git` in the directory is refused. The
directory's own name is not part of the digest.

The verify commands take the same checks and exit codes as the lock (`--attestation-file` names another sidecar). They
read `[[signing.trust]]` entries for their subject when a project exists; a consumer without a project passes
`--public-key`, or `--identity` with `--issuer`.

#### Thresholds

`[signing.thresholds]` asks for k distinct trusted signers of a subject:

```toml
[signing.thresholds]
lock = 2

[[signing.trust]]
key_file = ".ai-rulez/keys/alice.pub"
reviewer = "alice@example.org"

[[signing.trust]]
key_file = ".ai-rulez/keys/bob.pub"
reviewer = "bob@example.org"
```

```bash
ai-rulez sign --lock --key alice.key
ai-rulez sign --lock --key bob.key --append     # writes ai-rulez.lock.2.sigstore.json
```

Each signer writes their own bundle (at most 16). Verification counts distinct people: a certificate by its identity,
a key by its entry's `reviewer` (else its fingerprint), so two bundles by one person count once. Too few valid signers is
`AR728`. A threshold of k needs at least k trust entries for the subject, or an `identity_regexp`. Thresholds apply per
subject (`lock`, `bundle`, `skill`, `sbom`) wherever that subject is verified.

#### SLSA provenance

`sign --bundle <dir> --provenance` also writes `.ai-rulez.provenance.sigstore.json`: an in-toto statement with the
[SLSA provenance v1](https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.0/provenance) predicate over the bundle's tree digest. It records the
repository, ref and commit, the CI run URL, and a builder id: `--builder-id`, else `GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF`, else
`https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/builders/cli/v1`.

ai-rulez does not run a hermetic build, so this is the signer's own account of where the bundle was generated (at most
SLSA build level 1). Provenance from a CI builder such as `slsa-github-generator` verifies the same way.

```toml
[signing]
require_provenance = true      # verify --bundle demands it (or pass --require-provenance)
builders = ["https://github.com/acme/plugin/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/main"]
```

A provenance file that exists is always verified, like the bundle attestation. A missing file under
`require_provenance`, a predicate that is not SLSA provenance v1, or a builder outside `builders` is `AR729`.

#### KMS keys

`--key` accepts a cosign key URI: `awskms:///alias/release`,
`gcpkms://projects/p/locations/l/keyRings/r/cryptoKeys/k`, `azurekms://vault.vault.azure.net/key` or
`hashivault://key` (a `sigstore-kms-<name>` plugin binary adds others). The private key never leaves the KMS.
Credentials come from the provider's usual environment (`AWS_*`, `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, `AZURE_*`,
`VAULT_*`), never from a flag. Use ECDSA P-256 or ed25519 keys; RSA keys are not supported.

The bundle names the key by fingerprint, so verification stays offline. Export the public key once and trust it by file:

```bash
ai-rulez sign --lock --key awskms:///alias/release --public-key-out .ai-rulez/keys/release.pub
```

#### Served skills and publisher-signed skills

`ai-rulez mcp --serve-skills` can refuse skills the policy does not vouch for; `load_skill` then says why.

```toml
[signing]
require = ["served", "skill"]

[[signing.trust]]              # the lock's signers, for "served"
key_file = ".ai-rulez/keys/release.pub"

[[signing.trust]]              # a publisher, for one skill source
subject = "skill"
source = "shared"
key_file = ".ai-rulez/keys/publisher.pub"
```

| `require` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `served` | The lock must carry a valid attestation (otherwise every skill is refused with `AR720` to `AR728`), and a skill the signed lock does not pin with exactly its served digest is refused (`AR995`). Your own release workflow signs the lock. Recommended |
| `skill` | Every skill from a `[[skill_sources]]` or `[[installed_skills]]` entry must carry `.ai-rulez.sigstore.json` (`ai-rulez sign --skill`) signed by a `subject = "skill"` entry for that source. Project skills are not checked; a skill from an include cannot carry an attestation and is refused, so cover includes with `served` |

The server recomputes each skill's digest from the files on disk and compares each served file with the signed bytes,
so a file changed after signing, or not covered by the signature, is `AR724`. Only the `name:` line of `SKILL.md` may
differ, because a source serves it under the served name.

`generate` applies `skill` to the installed skills it writes into harness directories: each needs a valid attestation
covering the directory on disk, otherwise nothing is written and the error lists each skill with its `AR72x` code. Only
a dry run skips the check.

#### Verifying ai-rulez itself

`ai-rulez verify --self` checks the running binary against the Sigstore bundle its release published: a SLSA
provenance statement whose subject is the binary's SHA-256, signed by the release workflow pinned in the binary:

- identity `^https://github\.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/\.github/workflows/publish\.yaml@refs/tags/v[0-9][^/]*$`;
- issuer `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com`;
- a transparency-log proof.

```bash
ai-rulez trust update                       # once: cache the public-good trusted root
ai-rulez verify --self --attestation-file ai-rulez_5.10.0_linux_amd64.sigstore.json
```

Without `--attestation-file` the bundle is read from `<binary>.sigstore.json` next to the resolved binary. For a build
from another workflow, `--public-key` or `--identity` with `--issuer` replace the pinned identity. Exit `0` official
build; `1` could not check (`AR720` no bundle, `AR725` no usable trusted root); `2` the check failed (`AR722` another
signer, `AR724` different bytes).

Limits:

- **A tampered binary can lie.** `verify --self` runs the binary it verifies. When the binary itself is in doubt, verify
  it with a trusted copy or compare `sha256sum` with the release page.
- **No rollback protection.** An older, genuinely signed release verifies; compare the reported version with the one you
  expect.
- **The trusted root is not embedded.** By default it is the user cache `trust update` writes; pass `--trusted-root`
  with a read-only copy where that matters.

#### Cosign interoperability

`ai-rulez` writes a standard Sigstore bundle. Because the payload is an in-toto attestation, verify it with
`cosign verify-blob-attestation` and the subject digest `lock --subject` prints:

```bash
cosign verify-blob-attestation --bundle .ai-rulez/ai-rulez.lock.sigstore.json \
  --key cosign.pub --type https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/attestations/lock/v1 \
  --digest "$(ai-rulez lock --subject --format json | jq -r .subject | cut -d: -f2)" --digestAlg sha256 \
  --insecure-ignore-tlog=true   # only for a key bundle signed without --tlog
```

The other direction works too: `verify --attestation` accepts the blob-signature bundle of the
[`cosign sign-blob` recipe](lockfile.md#sign-in-the-release-workflow), and a bundle written by
`cosign attest-blob --type <predicate type>`. Such bundles name no repository and have no `issued_at`, so without a log
entry they have no signing time: `max_age` cannot be met and no rollback mark applies.

#### Codes

| Code | Name | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AR720` | `signature-missing` | `require` asks for a signature and none exists | `ai-rulez sign --lock` and commit the bundle |
| `AR721` | `signature-invalid` | bad bundle, envelope, signature, certificate chain or log proof | re-sign |
| `AR722` | `signer-not-trusted` | the signer matches no trust entry, is outside its validity window, or an `identity_regexp` is unanchored | add or fix the trust entry, or sign with a trusted key |
| `AR723` | `signature-stale` | older than `max_age`, no time to measure it, or a signing time in the future | re-sign; add `--tlog` for a trustworthy time |
| `AR724` | `attestation-subject-mismatch` | the lock (or bundle, skill, SBOM) changed after signing, or the hash version is below `min_hash_version` | review the change, then re-sign |
| `AR725` | `trusted-root-unavailable` | a certificate bundle and no trusted root | `ai-rulez trust update` or `--trusted-root` |
| `AR726` | `tlog-proof-missing` | `tlog = "required"` and the bundle has no log entry | sign keyless or with `--tlog`, or set `tlog` for key-only trust |
| `AR727` | `signature-rollback` | older than the newest attestation this machine verified | find out why an older lock is checked out; delete the named state file if the newer one was wrong |
| `AR728` | `signature-threshold-not-met` | fewer distinct trusted signers than `[signing.thresholds]` | collect the missing signatures with `sign --append` |
