  `served` nobody can run it (`AR9R2`); combined with `both`, a rule that points at it by name leaves the model declining
  (`AR9R1`). Use `both` with a file-path pointer, drop the flag, or set `[mcp] serve_user_invoked_skills = true`.

##### What generate does

- A `served` skill is not written to any preset's skill tree; `static` and `both` skills are.
- When any skill is `served` or `both`, or a `[[skill_sources]]` entry exists, the `dynamic-skills` stub is added to
  every preset whose harness can call MCP tools (in `.agents/skills` when `agents_md` is on). An authored skill named
  `dynamic-skills` replaces the stub. [`[delivery.stub]`](configuration.md#deliverystub) customises its text.
- A preset whose harness cannot call MCP (for example `cline` or `rovodev`) keeps served skills as static files and
  gets no stub, with a warning (`AR992`). Skills of `[[skill_sources]]` never reach such a preset. See
  [Installed skills vs skill sources](installed-skills.md#installed-skills-vs-skill-sources).
- `AR993` warns when skills are served but nothing runs `--serve-skills` (`self_server = false` and no
  `[[mcp_servers]]` entry with the flag).

To serve a second view (another profile, role or source) as its own server, declare it:

```toml
[[mcp_servers]]
name = "ai-rulez-backend"
command = "ai-rulez"
args = ["mcp", "--serve-skills", "--role", "backend"]
```

##### Skill sources

A source is a repository or directory of skill directories that is served and never written to the static trees.

```toml
[[skill_sources]]
name = "acme"                                  # identifies the source in the lock
url = "https://github.com/acme/skills.git"     # https, ssh or file URL, or a local directory
ref = "v1.2.0"                                 # a tag or full commit SHA; or version = "^1.2"
path = "skills"                                # subdirectory whose children are skills
include = ["pdf-*", "sql"]                     # directory-name globs; exclude wins
exclude = ["*-wip"]
name_prefix = "acme-"                          # served as acme-pdf-forms
trust = "error"                                # scan level: error (default) or warn
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | ------- | ------- |
| `version`, `tag_prefix`, `include_prerelease` | | A semver range resolved by `ai-rulez lock` and moved only by `ai-rulez update`; excludes `ref`. See [Version constraints](lockfile.md#version-constraints). |
| `max_skills` | 200 | Skills the source may load |
| `max_bytes` | 64 MiB | Bytes of skill files it may load |
| `max_clone_bytes` | 256 MiB | Size of the git clone; also `AI_RULEZ_MAX_CLONE_BYTES` or `--max-clone-bytes` |
| `max_clone_files` | 20000 | Entries of the git clone |

- **Pinning.** `ai-rulez lock` records the commit and tree digest of each source. With the lock, serving fetches the
  pinned commit and fails when the tree does not match. A branch, or a tag the lock does not cover, is reported as
  unpinned (`AR010`).
- **Private repositories.** Git runs without hooks, prompts, submodules or credential helpers, over `https`, `ssh` and
  `file` only. A private repository needs an `ssh` URL that works non-interactively (an ssh-agent key).
- **Clones.** A git source is fetched as a partial clone, and with `path` only that subdirectory is checked out. A
  clone that grows past `max_clone_bytes` is stopped and leaves nothing in the cache.
- **Cache.** Trees are cached per commit under `~/.cache/ai-rulez/skill-sources/`. `--frozen` needs the lock and a
  cached commit; `--offline` uses the lock's commit or one an earlier online run recorded.
- **Local directories.** A local `url` in the project config must resolve inside the project. `--source <dir>` and
  sources in your user configuration may point anywhere.
- **Names.** A source skill is served under its directory name plus `name_prefix`. One that collides with a project
  skill or an earlier source's skill is skipped; the project's skill wins.

##### Served files: scripts and assets

A served skill's files stay in the server. To run a bundled script, a client fetches it, writes it out and restores its
mode.

- `list_skill_resources`, `load_skill`, `get_skill` and `read_skill_file` report per file `mode` (such as `"0755"`),
  `executable`, and an `interpreter` hint from the shebang or extension (`sh`, `python3`, `node`, ...). The extension
  methods carry the same in `_meta`.
- `read_skill_file` returns text, or base64 for a binary file (or with `encoding: "base64"`). One call returns at most
  256 KiB; continue with `offset` while the reply carries `next_offset`.
- To materialise a skill: for each entry of `list_skill_resources`, refuse a `path` that is absolute or contains `..`,
  read the file with `read_skill_file {uri, encoding: "base64", offset}` until `next_offset` is absent, write the
  bytes under a directory you own and `chmod` to `mode`.

Or set `delivery: both` and run `ai-rulez generate`, which writes the files to disk.

##### Security scan

Every served skill is scanned before it is served, with the rules of `ai-rulez scan`: secrets, hidden characters,
prompt-injection phrases, risky shell, unrestricted `allowed-tools`, encoded blobs. Inline `ai-rulez-lint-ignore`
comments are not honoured. A skill that fails is not served: it is absent from every listing, a warning names the
finding on stderr, and `load_skill` says why.

| Level | Blocks | Default for |
| ----- | ------ | ----------- |
| `error` | Any finding | Skill sources, installed skills and skills from `[[includes]]` (`lint.security.scan_imports = "warn"` lowers the last two) |
| `warn` | Only findings that are errors by their own severity (secrets, hidden characters, risky shell) | Skills authored in the project |

A file the scan cannot read (binary, or over 512 KiB) is `AR989`. At `error` it is not served; a `SKILL.md` that
cannot be scanned refuses the skill. At `warn` it is served with the warning.

##### Lock enforcement

`ai-rulez lock` records a `[[served]]` entry with the digest of every skill the server would serve, and a `[[source]]`
entry per skill source. With `[lock] enforce` (the default whenever `ai-rulez.lock` exists), the server refuses a
skill the lock does not pin or whose digest differs (`AR995`).

The lock pins each *serve view* separately: the profile, role, `--targets`, `--include-static` and `--source` a server
starts with. A plain `lock` pins the default view, every role and every view the lock already records. Pin another view
with the flags the server uses:

```bash
ai-rulez lock --role backend
ai-rulez lock --targets cursor
ai-rulez lock --source git+https://github.com/acme/skills@v1.2.0#skills
ai-rulez mcp --serve-skills --role backend --frozen
```

A skill the scan refuses is not pinned: `lock` reports it, pins the rest and exits 3, or with `--refuse-findings`
writes nothing. See [Lock file](lockfile.md#served-skills-and-skill-sources).

##### Live reload

The server checks the configuration directory, local includes, local policy files and local skill sources every two
seconds (`--reload-interval`). When a file changes it rebuilds the catalog and swaps it in, and sends
`notifications/resources/list_changed` only when a served skill was added, removed or edited. A failed rebuild, or a
`SKILL.md` caught half-saved, keeps the previous catalog serving and is retried. Git sources are immutable per commit
and are not re-fetched.

Every minute (also with `--no-watch`) the server re-checks approval expiry and signature validity, and stops serving a
skill whose approval expired, whose signature no longer verifies, or whose digest an organization policy denies
(`AR747`, `AR717`).

##### Start-up cost and the catalog cache

Rendering and scanning every skill of a large monorepo takes several seconds. The admitted catalog is cached in
`~/.cache/ai-rulez/serve/<project-hash>/catalog.json`, keyed by the files live reload watches and the view's flags,
and authenticated with a key in `~/.config/ai-rulez/serve-cache.key`. A restart with unchanged content restores it
without rendering or scanning; any change, or an entry that fails its check, rebuilds. The cache is off while
discovery is on (discovery has the [index cache](#the-index-cache) instead).

##### Shared daemon

`--daemon` (or `[mcp] daemon = true`) makes one long-lived process per repository build the catalog once and serve
every session over a private unix socket. The first session starts the daemon; later sessions connect in milliseconds
and proxy their stdin and stdout to it.

```bash
ai-rulez mcp --serve-skills --daemon
```

- **Identity.** A daemon is keyed by the repository, the ai-rulez version and the command line. A different MCP entry
  or version gets its own daemon; sessions in subdirectories of one checkout share one. Content edits are picked up by
  live reload.
- **Lifetime.** It exits after `daemon_idle_timeout` (default 15 minutes) with no client, and at once when its
  repository is removed. Its log is `daemon.log` beside the socket under `~/.cache/ai-rulez/daemons/`.
- **Security.** The socket is mode `0600` in a `0700` directory. A client refuses a socket owned by another user or
  open to group or others, and serves in-process instead.
- **Fallback.** On any failure (no daemon can start, a stale or unsafe socket, a version or view mismatch) the session
  is served in-process exactly as without `--daemon`. On Windows `--daemon` always serves in-process, with a warning.

Settings such as `serve_user_invoked_skills` are read when the daemon starts; restart it after changing them.

##### Usage telemetry

Nothing is recorded unless you opt in with `--usage-log <file>`, `--usage-sink <command>` or
`[usage] skills_index = true` (which logs to `<config dir>/local/usage.jsonl`). Each successful `load_skill` is then one
identifier-only JSON line: time, skill name, a salted session hash, the client name, the role, the content hash and
digest. A sink receives the same line on stdin from a queue of 256 records, so a slow sink never delays a load. See
[Usage telemetry](usage-telemetry.md).

##### Validation codes

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
| ---- | -------- | ------- |
| `AR989` | warning or error | A served file cannot be scanned (binary or over 512 KiB) |
| `AR990` | warning | Always-loaded content names a served skill |
| `AR991` | error | A harness that can call MCP has no `dynamic-skills` stub |
| `AR992` | warning | A harness without MCP keeps served skills as static files |
| `AR993` | warning | Skills are served but no MCP entry runs `--serve-skills` |
| `AR994` | error | `delivery` is not `static`, `served` or `both` |
| `AR995` | error | `[lock] enforce` and a served skill is unpinned or its digest differs |

See [Strict validation](strict-validation.md) for the full list.

#### Repository discovery

##### Discovering skills already in the repository

A repository often keeps skills ai-rulez does not define: a `skills/` folder, `.claude/skills` in a package, a
directory set up for another harness. `--discover-skills` (or `[mcp] discover_skills`) serves them through the same
`find_skill`, `load_skill` and `skill://` resources, under the same scan, budget and `--allow`/`--deny` rules, with no
`generate` run and no copy.

```toml
[mcp]
serve_skills = true
discover_skills = "repo"   # off (default), repo or all
```

```bash
ai-rulez mcp --serve-skills --discover-skills        # repo
ai-rulez mcp --serve-skills --discover-skills=all
```

| Mode | Serves |
| ---- | ------ |
| `off` | The skills ai-rulez defines and the skill sources |
| `repo` | The above, plus every skill directory found in the working tree |
| `all` | `repo`, plus installed and included skills whatever their delivery |

Either mode also indexes nested instruction files, rules and agents ([Monorepos](#monorepos-scopes-and-nested-context)).

**Where it looks.** A directory with a `SKILL.md`, at most six levels deep, below:

- `skills/` (not inside a hidden directory);
- `.claude/skills`;
- the skill directory of each configured preset (`.agents/skills`, `.cursor/skills`, `.github/skills`, ...).

In a git repository only files git lists are read (tracked, or untracked and not ignored), so `.gitignore` applies.
`.ai-rulez/`, `.git/` and `node_modules/` are never searched and symlinks are not followed. A skill directory ai-rulez
generated is skipped, so nothing is served twice. A skill has the limits of a skill source (2 MiB a file, 8 MiB and
2000 files a skill, 500 skills in all).

**Names.** A skill is served under its frontmatter `name` (or its directory name). The skills ai-rulez defines and the
skill sources claim names first and *shadow* a repository skill of the same name; a builtin skill is the exception and
is replaced by a repository skill. Among repository skills the shallowest wins, and a later one is served under its
path with `/` turned into `.` and leading dots dropped: `pkg/.claude/skills/bar` becomes `pkg.claude.skills.bar`.
Every rename and shadowing is a start-up warning and is listed under `skill_discovery` in `ai-rulez://catalog`.

**Trust and lock.** A discovered skill is scanned at the level of a skill authored in the project. Under
`[lock] enforce` it must be pinned: set `discover_skills` in the configuration, not only the flag, so `ai-rulez lock`
sees it.

**Without a configuration.** `--discover-skills` works in a directory with no `.ai-rulez/`. It then behaves as if the
`claude` and `codex` presets were configured, and registers only the tools that need no configuration: the skill and
context tools, `get_version`, `list_builtins`, `show_builtin`, `policy_show`, `okf_validate` and `init_project`.

```bash
cd ~/src/web            # has .claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md, no .ai-rulez/
ai-rulez mcp --serve-skills --discover-skills
```

##### Monorepos, scopes and nested context

A harness loads a nested `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/` tree only once it works inside that directory, so a
planner at the repository root never sees it. With discovery on, the server indexes the repository by **scope** and
answers "what applies to this path?" the way a harness would.

**Scopes.** A scope is a directory that holds `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.claude/`, `.agents/`, `.codex/`,
`.cursor/rules`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` or a `skills/` directory with a skill. The root is the scope `.`.
Scopes are inferred from the files; nothing is configured, and the `presets` list does not matter (only the skill
directories follow it). Each indexed item has a `kind` (`skill`, `instruction`, `rule`, `agent`, `command`), a `source`
(`claude`, `agents`, `codex`, `cursor`, `copilot`, `gemini`, `skills-dir`), a `name`, a `description` and a content
`hash`.

**What applies to a path.** The scope of the path and its ancestors, nearest first. A skill, agent or command is
shadowed by one of the same name in a nearer scope; instruction files and rules add up.

For a repository with `pkg/api/AGENTS.md`, `pkg/api/.claude/rules/handlers.md` and
`pkg/api/.claude/skills/lint/SKILL.md`:

```jsonc
// find_skill {"task": "lint the code", "path": "pkg/api/handlers/user.go"}
{"task": "lint the code", "path": "pkg/api/handlers/user.go", "scopes": ["pkg/api", "."], "count": 2,
 "results": [
  {"name": "lint", "scope": "pkg/api", "score": 1.83, "description": "Lint the api package with golangci-lint", ...},
  {"name": "code-reviewer", "score": 1.67, "description": "Specialized agent for code review and quality assurance", ...}]}
```

A skill ai-rulez defines belongs to no scope and applies everywhere. `scope` asks for one exact scope (`"."` is the
root), and `recursive: true` adds the scopes below it. `path` and `scope` are mutually exclusive.

**`find_context`** takes the same `path`, `scope` and `recursive`, plus `task` to rank by, `kind` (`instruction`, `rule`
or `agent`) and `limit` (default 10, max 50), and returns summaries:

```jsonc
// find_context {"path": "pkg/api/handlers/user.go"}
{"count": 2, "total": 2, "scopes": ["pkg/api", "."],
 "results": [
  {"name": "AGENTS.md", "kind": "instruction", "scope": "pkg/api", "source": "agents",
   "description": "API conventions", "uri": "context://pkg/api/AGENTS.md", "hash": "sha256:..."},
  {"name": "handlers", "kind": "rule", "scope": "pkg/api", "source": "claude", "paths": ["handlers/**"],
   "description": "Handler rules", "uri": "context://pkg/api/handlers", "hash": "sha256:..."}]}
```

**`load_context`** reads one item, by `scope` and `name` or by `uri`, with an optional `budget_bytes`. The text is read
from the repository at call time, never from the index:

```jsonc
// load_context {"scope": "pkg/api", "name": "AGENTS.md"}
{"name": "AGENTS.md", "kind": "instruction", "scope": "pkg/api", "uri": "context://pkg/api/AGENTS.md",
 "content": "# API conventions\n\nHandlers return typed errors.\n", "bytes": 49, "truncated": false,
 "hash": "sha256:...", "budget_remaining_bytes": 262095}
```

The result carries `changed_since_index: true` when the file changed since the index was built. Commands are indexed
and counted but not served as context.

The context tools apply the skill rules: `--allow` and `--deny` match an item's `name` or `scope/name`; the security
scan runs when the index is built and again on every load, and a file with an error finding is withheld; reads count
against the session budget. Domains, roles, the lock and approvals apply to skills only.

**Catalog and instructions.** `ai-rulez://catalog` gains a `scopes` array with per-kind counts and sources, narrowed
with `?path=`, `?scope=` and `&recursive=true`. The server instructions name the first eight scopes with their counts
(`pkg/api (1 skill, 1 instruction, 1 rule)`), so a planner knows nested content exists without a call.

**Limits.** The index holds at most 20000 items, keeping the shallowest scopes (`skill_discovery.index.truncated` says
when it cut). An instruction, rule or agent file over 1 MiB is skipped. `path`, `scope` and `uri` must be relative to the
project, without `..`, backslashes or control characters.

###### Rules and skills with `paths`

A rule or skill can name the files it applies to: `paths:` in the frontmatter of a Claude Code rule or `SKILL.md`, and
`globs:` of a Cursor `.mdc` rule that is not `alwaysApply`. With a `path` query, `find_context` and `find_skill` return
such an item only when the path matches one of its globs. The globs are relative to the scope directory:
`pkg/api/.claude/rules/handlers.md` with `paths: "handlers/**"` applies to `pkg/api/handlers/user.go`, not to
`pkg/api/other/handlers/user.go`. `**/*.py` matches at any depth, `*.py` only directly in the scope; a Cursor glob such as
`*.tsx` also matches at any depth.

- A directory `path` keeps an item when some glob could match a path below it.
- A `scope` query lists every rule and skill of the scope whatever its globs; loading one by name is unchanged.
- A rule whose `paths:` cannot be read (broken YAML, or a value that is not a string or list of strings) fails closed:
  a `path` query never returns it, and a `scope` query lists it with `"paths_unreadable": true`. `ai-rulez validate`
  reports `AR306` and `AR9W4`. A Cursor rule with broken `globs:` is served as applying everywhere until fixed.

##### Writing a skill into a scope

`create_skill` and `update_skill` with `scope` write a harness skill file into a repository directory, where a harness
working there loads it, instead of editing ai-rulez content. `allow_write: true` is required on the call.

```jsonc
// create_skill {"scope": "pkg/web", "name": "e2e", "description": "Run the Playwright end-to-end tests of the web app",
//               "allow_write": true}
{"success": true, "operation": "create_skill", "name": "e2e", "scope": "pkg/web", "harness": "claude",
 "path": "pkg/web/.claude/skills/e2e/SKILL.md",
 "message": "Skill written to pkg/web/.claude/skills/e2e/SKILL.md; it is the harness's file, not ai-rulez content"}
```

- **Where.** `<scope>/<harness skills dir>/<name>/SKILL.md`. `harness` names an enabled preset; by default the first
  enabled preset that keeps skills in a directory (`claude` is `.claude/skills`, `codex` is `.agents/skills`).
- **Checks.** The scope must be an existing project directory with no symlink on the way; a path that leaves the
  project is refused. A generated copy is refused (edit the source under `.ai-rulez/`). The content is scanned at the
  strictest level and any finding refuses the call.
- **Create and update.** `create_skill` refuses an existing skill; `update_skill` refuses a missing one. Without
  `content`, `create_skill` builds a `SKILL.md` from `description`.
- **Lock.** The file is not ai-rulez content and is not generated. With an `ai-rulez.lock`, the result carries `lock`
  because the new file is drift until `ai-rulez lock` records it.

`scope` cannot be combined with `domain`, `priority`, `targets` or `local`. Instruction files and rules stay read-only
over MCP, and a `--read-only` server does not register the writing tools.

##### The index cache

A cold build of the index is dominated by the security scan of every item. The index cache keeps the summary of each
indexed file (name, description and content hash, keyed by path, size and modification time) and the scan verdicts of
content found clean, so the next start skips that work. It never stores a file body.

```toml
[mcp]
index_cache = "user"   # user (default), repo or off
```

| Mode | Location |
| ---- | -------- |
| `user` | `<user cache>/ai-rulez/monorepo-index/<repo-id>/index.json`, nothing in the repository. Falls back to `repo` when the user cache is not writable. |
| `repo` | `.ai-rulez/.cache/monorepo-index/` (`.ai-rulez-cache/monorepo-index/` in the root layout), listed in `.git/info/exclude` |
| `off` | No cache |

```bash
ai-rulez cache status    # location, size, entries and problems
ai-rulez cache clear     # drop it
```

`ai-rulez doctor` reports the cache too.

- **Freshness.** A summary is reused while the file's size and modification time and the git tree are unchanged. A new
  tree drops the summaries and keeps the verdicts, which are keyed by content. A new ai-rulez build or changed `[lint]`
  settings drop the verdicts.
- **Safety.** The file is written with mode `0600` under a lock, so several servers on one repository share it. It
  carries an HMAC with a per-user key outside the cache (`~/.config/ai-rulez/index-cache.key`); a file that was edited,
  truncated or planted is discarded and rebuilt. A cached verdict is used only for the exact bytes and trust level it
  was recorded for, `--allow` and `--deny` run on every build, and `load_context` scans what it reads every time.

A warm start of a large monorepo takes a fraction of a cold one.

##### Live refresh of the index

While `--serve-skills --discover-skills` runs, a file watcher follows the project tree with a 300 ms debounce. When an
instruction file, a `SKILL.md`, anything under `.claude`, `.agents`, `.codex`, `.cursor`, `.github` or `skills`, or a
directory appears, changes or goes, the server rebuilds the index. The rebuild re-reads only the changed files and
scans only content without a clean verdict.

When the index changed, the server sends one `notifications/resources/list_changed`; the client then calls
`find_context` or `find_skill` again. Reading `ai-rulez://index` returns the current generation, the item and scope
counts and the cache report:

```json
{"generation": 1, "items": 3, "scopes": 2, "found": 9, "truncated": false,
 "cache": {"mode": "user", "dir": "/home/dev/.cache/ai-rulez/monorepo-index/8674292ae5a9225b",
           "hits": 0, "misses": 9, "entries": 9, "verdicts": 5}}
```

- `.git`, `node_modules`, `vendor`, `target`, `dist`, `build`, excluded paths and the configuration directory (which
  live reload polls) are not watched.
- The watcher holds at most 2048 descriptors, watching shallow directories first; past that, and when the operating
  system's watch limit is reached, the server warns and refreshes on the poll interval only.
- `--no-watch` (or `no_watch = true`) turns the watcher off with the rest of live reload.
- The server instructions are written at start-up and are not rewritten.

##### Excluding paths

`--exclude <glob>` (repeatable) and `[mcp] exclude` keep paths out of discovery entirely:

```toml
[mcp]
discover_skills = "repo"
exclude = ["third_party/**", "**/fixtures/"]
```

```bash
ai-rulez mcp --serve-skills --discover-skills --exclude 'examples/**' --exclude '**/testdata/'
```

- Globs are relative to the project root with slashes. `**` crosses directories, `*` and `?` stay within one, `{a,b}`
  alternates. A pattern without a slash (`AGENTS.md`, `legacy`) matches at any depth, and a pattern naming a
  directory (`third_party`, `third_party/`, `third_party/**`) excludes everything below it.
- The flag's globs are added to the configuration's.
- An excluded file is dropped before anything is read: no parsing, scan or cache entry. The globs apply to skill
  directories and the whole context index (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md`, Copilot instructions, rules, agents
  and commands). An excluded directory marks no scope, and the watcher ignores it.
- A glob that leaves the project (`../x`) or is empty is rejected. `--exclude` without discovery is an error; the
  configuration key is ignored while discovery is off.

#### Settings in the configuration

Pin how `ai-rulez mcp` runs in the `[mcp]` table, so every launcher (`.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`,
`.codex/config.toml`, a teammate's editor) runs the same server without repeating flags.

```toml
[mcp]
serve_skills = true                                   # a bare `ai-rulez mcp` serves skills
discover_skills = "repo"
read_only = true
tools = ["find_skill", "load_skill", "find_context", "load_context"]
deny = ["draft-*"]
daemon = true
```

| Key | Flag | Applies | Meaning |
| --- | ---- | ------- | ------- |
| `serve_skills` | `--serve-skills` | always | Serve skills from a bare `ai-rulez mcp` |
| `read_only` | `--read-only` | always | Register only tools that change nothing |
| `tools` | `--tools` | always | Register exactly these tools; an unknown name stops the server with the valid list |
| `authoring` | | serving | Keep the read-only authoring tools and `review-config` on a read-only skills server |
| `allow`, `deny` | `--allow`, `--deny` | serving | Globs on served skill and context names |
| `discover_skills` | `--discover-skills` | serving | `off`, `repo` or `all` |
| `exclude` | `--exclude` (adds) | serving | Paths discovery never reads |
| `index_cache` | | serving | `user`, `repo` or `off` |
| `no_watch` | `--no-watch` | serving | Turn live reload and the watcher off |
| `daemon` | `--daemon` | serving | Share one server per repository |
| `daemon_idle_timeout` | | serving | How long the daemon outlives its last client, as a duration (default `15m`) |
| `serve_user_invoked_skills` | | serving | Also serve skills that set `disable-model-invocation: true` |

The `self_server*` and `skills_instructions*` keys of the same table control generation; see
[Configuration: `mcp`](configuration.md#mcp).

- **A flag wins.** A flag on the command line replaces the key, including `--read-only=false` and an empty `--tools=`.
- **Serving keys need serving.** A "serving" key set while skills are not served logs one warning naming it. The same
  setting as a flag stops the server with `requires --serve-skills`.
- **Layers.** The keys are read from `.ai-rulez/config.toml`, a root `ai-rulez.toml`, `config.<name>.toml` layers and
  `config.local.toml`; a list in a later layer replaces the earlier one.
- **Read at start.** Change a key, then restart the server (or let a daemon idle out).
- **Policy only tightens.** An [organization policy](policy.md) with `[mcp] read_only = true` keeps the server read-only
  whatever the project or the flags say; a project that sets `read_only = false` under it is reported as `AR740`.
- **The surface follows the tools.** The server instructions and the prompts list only what is registered, so a
  read-only server does not tell the model to use `generate_outputs`.

#### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
| ------- | ------------- |
| The client shows the server as failed or timed out on first use | A cold `npx` download. Install the binary and use `self_server_launcher = "binary-then-npx"`, or raise the client timeout (`MCP_TIMEOUT=60000` for Claude Code). |
| No `ai-rulez` entry in `.gemini/settings.json` | Gemini gets the self entry only when `[[mcp_servers]]` is non-empty. Declare `ai-rulez` there. |
| A tool answers that `working_directory` "is outside the directory this server is allowed to use" | The server is confined to its start directory. Start it with `--root <dir>` or `--allow-any-dir`. |
| `find_skill` does not return a skill | It is `static` and the project serves only `served`/`both` skills (use `--include-static`), it sets `disable-model-invocation`, the scan refused it (see stderr), or the lock does not pin it (`AR995`; run `ai-rulez lock`). |
| `Error: --exclude requires --serve-skills` | A serving flag on a plain `ai-rulez mcp`. Add `--serve-skills` or set `serve_skills = true`. |
| `find_context` is not listed | Discovery is off. Set `discover_skills` or pass `--discover-skills`. |
| A setting change has no effect | Settings are read at start. Restart the client's server, or the daemon. |

#### See also

- [Configuration: `mcp`](configuration.md#mcp) and [`mcp_servers`](configuration.md#mcp_servers)
- [Monorepo](monorepo.md)
- [Skill search](search.md)
- [Lock file](lockfile.md)
- [CLI: `mcp`](cli.md)

## Skill search

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/search/

`ai-rulez search` ranks your project's skills against a query with the same ranker the MCP `find_skill` tool uses,
and `search --eval` measures that ranking against labeled queries. By default the ranking is lexical: nothing is sent
anywhere and the same input always gives the same order. Optionally it is hybrid, fusing the lexical ranking with
embedding similarity, so a paraphrase such as "customer wants money back" finds the skill described as "Issue a
refund".

Use it to check which skill an agent would find for a task, to tune skill descriptions, and to gate a pull request on
search quality.

#### Example

```text
$ ai-rulez search refund a duplicate charge
RANK  SCORE   NAME           DOMAIN  DESCRIPTION
1     4.4971  refund-policy  root    Issue a refund for a duplicate or disputed charge.

$ ai-rulez search "customer wants money back"
no served skill matches
```

The paraphrase shares no words with the skill, so lexical search misses it; [hybrid ranking](#hybrid-ranking)
finds it.

```bash
ai-rulez search --format json --limit 10 deploy staging
ai-rulez search --role platform rotate credentials
ai-rulez search --mode hybrid --explain "customer wants money back"
```

#### Searching

The skills searched are the ones `mcp --serve-skills` would serve, selected with the same flags: `--profile`,
`--role` (not both), `--targets`, `--domain`, `--allow`, `--deny`, `--source` (repeatable) and `--include-static`. A
project that sets no `delivery` anywhere searches every skill; otherwise only `served` and `both` skills, unless you
pass `--include-static`. Skills the server would refuse (lock or scan state) are not ranked. Remote skill sources are
fetched unless you pass `--offline` or `--frozen`.

All words after the flags form one query. A query that is only `index`, `status` or `mine` runs that subcommand; add
a word to search for it.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--mode lexical\|hybrid\|vector` | Override `[search] mode` and `AI_RULEZ_SEARCH_MODE` for this run |
| `--limit N` | Maximum results (default 5, max 20) |
| `--explain` | Show each skill's rank in the lexical and vector lists, and how the query was embedded |
| `--format json` | Print [`search.v1.schema.json`](https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/blob/main/schema/search.v1.schema.json) |

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "query": "deploy staging",
  "ranking": "lexical",
  "degraded": null,
  "count": 1,
  "results": [
    {
      "name": "deploy-staging",
      "description": "Deploy the web app to the staging cluster.",
      "score": 4.455101,
      "domain": "root",
      "digest": "sha256:897e58c3...",
      "lexical_rank": 1
    }
  ]
}
```

- `ranking` is what produced the order (`lexical`, `hybrid` or `vector`).
- `degraded` says why a hybrid or vector search fell back to lexical: `no_index`, `provider_unavailable`, `timeout`,
  `budget` or `network_disabled`. The reason is also printed on stderr.
- A hybrid result adds `vector_rank` and `vector_sim`; `stale_vector: true` marks a skill that changed since it was
  indexed and ranks lexically only.
- `abstained: true` means no skill was close enough (see [Abstaining](#abstaining)).

#### The ranker

The lexical ranker is BM25F over four skill fields, weighted name 3, `triggers` 2.5, `keywords` 2 and description 1,
after lowercasing, dropping stopwords and light stemming (`migrations` matches `migration`). Ties are ordered by name.
An empty or stopword-only query returns nothing. It is the reference for every other mode and the fallback when they
cannot run.

A query containing a skill's exact id as whole words ("use the deploy-staging skill") puts that skill first. An id
that is one ordinary word (`test`, `build`) does so only when the query calls it a skill ("use the build skill").

To make a skill easier to find, give it a precise `description` and `triggers` or `keywords` frontmatter (see
[Skills](skills.md)).

#### Hybrid ranking

Off by default. Configure a `[search]` table and an embedding provider, then [build the index](#building-the-index).

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml (excerpt)
[search]
mode = "hybrid"
```

```toml
# ~/.config/ai-rulez/config.toml (network settings apply only from the user config)
[llm]
allow_network   = true
provider        = "gemini"            # or base_url = "http://localhost:11434/v1" for Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio
embedding_model = "gemini-embedding-001"
api_key_env     = "GEMINI_API_KEY"
max_calls       = 200
```

Embeddings go through the [`[llm]`](llm.md) provider, so its network gate (`allow_network`, off by default), budget
(`max_cost_usd`, `max_tokens`, `max_calls`), response cache and error redaction apply. A `[search]` table in the user
config overrides the repository's key by key.

| `[search]` key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | `lexical` | `lexical`, `hybrid` or `vector` (also `AI_RULEZ_SEARCH_MODE`) |
| `fields` | `["name", "triggers", "keywords", "description"]` | Skill fields sent to the embedder |
| `index_body` | `false` | Also embed the first `body_chars` characters of `SKILL.md` |
| `body_chars` | `1200` | See `index_body` |
| `fusion` | `auto` | `auto`, `rrf` or `weighted` |
| `rrf_k` | `60` | RRF constant |
| `weights` | `{ lexical = 1.0, vector = 1.0 }` | List weights for `rrf` and `weighted` |
| `candidates` | `50` | Length of each list before fusion |
| `vector_min_sim` | `0` (off) | Cosine below which a skill is not a match; see [Abstaining](#abstaining) |
| `query_timeout_ms` | `800` | Timeout of the query embedding; on timeout the ranking is lexical |
| `batch_size` | `64` | Texts per embedding call of `search index` |
| `index_dir` | `local/search` | Index directory under the configuration directory |
| `dtype` | `float32` | `float32` or `float16` (half the size) |
| `log_queries` | `false` | User config only; see [Query mining](#query-mining) |
| `embeddings.model` | | Overrides `[llm] embedding_model` for search |
| `embeddings.command`, `embeddings.pass_env` | | A [command provider](#command-provider) |

##### Fusion

| `fusion` | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` | While every skill has a current vector, rank by cosine alone (`ranking` is `vector`; an exact id still pins first). When a skill is new or changed since indexing, fall back to `rrf` so it still ranks lexically |
| `rrf` | Reciprocal rank fusion: `score = sum(weight / (rrf_k + rank))` over the lists a skill is in |
| `weighted` | Each list's scores are scaled to [0, 1] and mixed by `weights.lexical / (weights.lexical + weights.vector)` |

Compare the modes on your catalog with `search --eval cases.yaml --mode lexical,vector,hybrid` before choosing.

`vector` mode ranks by cosine alone; skills without a current vector follow in lexical order, and when no skill has
one the search is `degraded: no_index`.

`find_skill` uses the same ranker. The MCP server never builds the index: it reads the files `search index` wrote,
reloads them when they change, and embeds only the query. See [MCP server](mcp-server.md#dynamic-skill-loading).

##### Abstaining

A query unrelated to any skill ("what is the weather in Berlin") still has nearest skills. Set `vector_min_sim` to
treat a skill whose cosine is below it as no match:

- a vector ranking (including `auto` on a fresh index) with no skill above the threshold returns nothing;
  `search --format json` reports `"abstained": true` and `find_skill` returns no skill;
- `rrf` and `weighted` drop only the weak vector candidates, so a skill that matches by words still ranks.

Cosines differ per model, so there is no default. `search --eval` with positive and negative cases suggests one
(`calibration` in the JSON): the threshold that answers the most positives while abstaining on the most negatives.
Re-run the evaluation with the value set before committing it. A `vector_min_sim` in the user config wins over the
repository's; `0` there switches it off.

#### Building the index

```bash
ai-rulez search index --dry-run       # provider, texts, bytes and estimated cost; nothing is sent
ai-rulez search index                 # embed what changed and write the index
ai-rulez search index --rebuild       # re-embed everything
ai-rulez search index --items refund-policy,deploy-staging   # also re-embed these
ai-rulez search status                # compare the index with the served skills, offline
```

```text
$ ai-rulez search index --dry-run
provider   gemini@default   (allow_network=true)
model      gemini-embedding-001
items      25   cached 0   to embed 25   withheld 0   est. tokens 1627   est. cost <= $0.000244
fields     name, triggers, keywords, description   body: no
egress     25 texts, 4.7 KiB -> default
```

- A skill's embedded text is built from the configured `fields` (and the body with `index_body`). A vector is reused
  while the provider, model, fields and exact text are unchanged, so editing a skill's body costs nothing (unless
  `index_body` is set) and an edited description costs one text. A new model or field set re-embeds everything.
- A batch the provider rejects is split until the refused skill stands alone; that skill is skipped and named. A
  budget, network, key or provider error stops the build. Either way the finished vectors are written, the missing
  skills are listed, and the command exits 2.
- `search status` reports `none`, `unreadable`, `incompatible` (other provider, model or fields), `stale` or `fresh`,
  and lists skills that are current, changed, not indexed, or no longer served.

```text
$ ai-rulez search status
index      .ai-rulez/local/search
state      none
mode       lexical
...
next       run 'ai-rulez search index'
```

The index is two files in `index_dir`: `manifest.json` (provider, model, fields and a digest per skill, sorted and
without timestamps) and `vectors.bin`. A damaged or tampered file is treated as no index.

The default `local/search` is machine-local and gitignored. Set `index_dir` to a directory outside `local/` (for
example `search-index`) to commit the index, so CI can run a hybrid evaluation without an API key. `validate` then
warns (`AR9D1`) when the committed index no longer matches the skills. A tampered index can only change the order of
results: `load_skill` still enforces the lock, approval and scan state.

##### Command provider

A program can produce the vectors instead of `[llm]`:

```toml
# user config
[search.embeddings]
command  = ["/usr/local/bin/embed"]
model    = "my-local-model"      # recorded in the index
pass_env = ["EMBED_TOKEN"]
```

It runs without a shell in the project root, with only `PATH`, `HOME` and the `pass_env` variables, a 30 s timeout
and a 64 MiB output cap. It reads `{"input": ["text", ...]}` on stdin and prints `{"vectors": [[...], ...]}`, one
vector per input in order.

Because it runs a program, a repository config cannot set it: it is honoured from the user config, or from the
repository config with `--allow-exec`. The MCP server honours only the user config.

#### Data egress

| Operation | Data sent | To |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `search index` | One text per changed skill: the configured fields (by default name, triggers, keywords and description, already visible to agents) and, with `index_body`, the start of the body | The embedding endpoint |
| `search` and `find_skill` in hybrid or vector mode | The query, up to 2 KiB (an agent's task description can contain user data) | The same endpoint |
| Lexical mode | Nothing | |

Each skill text is checked with the secret scanner of `AR001` before sending; a hit withholds that skill (`AR9D3`) and
it ranks lexically only. Queries are not scanned. `allow_network` stays off until you enable it in the user config,
for loopback hosts too, and `--dry-run` shows the host first. For data residency, use a local or in-region endpoint;
the manifest records which provider produced the vectors.

#### Evaluating the ranking

```bash
ai-rulez search --eval search-cases.yaml
ai-rulez search --eval search-cases.yaml --min top1=0.6,mrr=0.7
ai-rulez search --eval search-cases.yaml --mode lexical,hybrid
ai-rulez search --eval search-cases.yaml --output result.json
ai-rulez search --eval search-cases.yaml --baseline result.json --max-flips 0
ai-rulez search --from-evals
```

```text
$ ai-rulez search --eval search-cases.yaml
cases: 3 (+1 negative), k=3, mode: lexical
top1      0.6667  (95% CI 0.0000-1.0000)
recall@3  0.6667  (95% CI 0.0000-1.0000)
hit@3     0.6667
mrr       0.6667  (95% CI 0.0000-1.0000)

by tag:
  paraphrase (1): top1 0.0000  recall@3 0.0000  hit@3 0.0000  mrr 0.0000

negatives (nothing should match; shown is what ranked first, with the ranker's own score):
  weather: nothing;

misses:
  refund-paraphrase: expected refund-policy, got [] (not retrieved)
```

- `--mode` takes a comma-separated list (`lexical`, `vector`, `hybrid` or `all`). The first is the primary mode the
  gates check; the default is the configured mode. Modes that need vectors need the index.
- `--k` overrides the file's cut-off (max 100).
- `--from-evals` derives cases from the skills' [eval cases](evals.md#layout), alone or
  added to `--eval`: a prompt with `expect_trigger: true` expects that skill; a near-miss or `expect_trigger: false`
  prompt must not rank it first. These cases are tagged `from-evals`.

##### Cases file

```yaml
version: 1          # required
k: 5                # cut-off of recall@k, hit@k and nDCG@k (default 5, max 100)
cases:
  - id: refund-paraphrase
    query: "customer wants money back for a double charge"
    expect: [refund-policy]       # any of them counts
    tags: [paraphrase, billing]
  - id: graded
    query: "set up staging deploy pipeline"
    expect: [{id: deploy-staging, grade: 3}, {id: ci-pipeline, grade: 1}]   # grades enable nDCG
  - id: scoped
    query: "rotate credentials"
    role: platform                # rank only this role's skills
    expect: [rotate-keys]
  - id: near-miss
    query: "deploy to production"
    expect: []
    avoid: [deploy-staging]       # must not rank first
  - id: negative
    query: "what is the weather tomorrow"
    expect: []                    # nothing relevant; reported separately
```

Skills are named as in the catalog. The file is read strictly: an unknown field, a missing `version`, `id` or
`query`, a duplicate id, an unknown skill, a grade outside 1-9, a skill both expected and avoided, an unknown `role`,
or an expected skill the role does not serve is reported together as `AR9D2` (exit 1).

##### Metrics and gates

| Metric | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `top1` | A relevant skill ranked first |
| `recall_at_k` | Share of relevant skills in the top k |
| `hit_at_k` | Any relevant skill in the top k |
| `mrr` | 1 / rank of the first relevant skill (0 if none) |
| `ndcg_at_k` | With graded cases |
| `avoid_top1` | With `avoid` lists: share where an avoided skill ranked first (lower is better) |

Metrics are reported overall and per tag, with 95% bootstrap intervals; negative cases are listed separately. With
several modes, `paired_vs_lexical` gives each mode's difference to lexical over the same cases: an interval that
excludes 0 is a real change. A vector mode that fell back to lexical for any case is an error, not a pass.

| Gate | Fails when |
| --- | --- |
| `--min top1=0.6,recall=0.8,hit=0.9,mrr=0.7,ndcg=0.7` | A metric of the primary mode is below its floor |
| `--baseline prev.json --max-flips N` | More than N cases went from hit to miss since the baseline (default 0) |

With few cases, one case moves `top1` by several points, so prefer the flip count to a floor. A baseline must use the
same primary mode and `--k`. `--output` and `--format json` write
[`search-eval.v1.schema.json`](https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/blob/main/schema/search-eval.v1.schema.json);
`--output` is not written when embeddings were degraded.

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Every gate passed |
| `1` | The command could not run (bad flags or cases file, unknown skill, unreadable baseline, a mode without an index, degraded embeddings) |
| `2` | A gate failed (printed as `AR9D4`), or `search index` stopped early |

```text
$ ai-rulez search --eval search-cases.yaml --min top1=0.9
...
gate failed
AR9D4: top1 is 0.6667, below the minimum 0.9000
```

#### Query mining

Real queries make the best test cases. Query logging is opt-in and only from the user config (or
`AI_RULEZ_SEARCH_LOG_QUERIES=1`; a repository config cannot turn it on):

```toml
# user config
[search]
log_queries = true
```

`find_skill` then appends each query (up to 512 bytes; secret-looking queries are skipped) and the skill
the session loaded next to `<config dir>/local/search-queries.jsonl`. The file is mode 0600, gitignored, capped at
8 MiB, stores hashed session ids, and is never sent anywhere. `search mine` turns it into cases:

```bash
ai-rulez search mine --output mined-cases.yaml   # a query followed by loading S expects S
ai-rulez search mine --min-count 2 --purge       # keep pairs seen twice; delete the log
```

A query is labeled with the first skill loaded after it in the same session; queries followed by nothing, or by
different skills with no clear winner, are dropped. The agent's choice is not necessarily right, so mined cases are
tagged `mined`: review them before they gate anything.

#### Validation codes

| Code | Raised by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AR9D0` | `validate` | Invalid `[search]` table |
| `AR9D1` | `validate` | A committed index no longer matches the skills (warning) |
| `AR9D2` | `search --eval` | Invalid cases file |
| `AR9D3` | `search index` | A skill text looked like it held a secret and was not sent |
| `AR9D4` | `search --eval` | A gate failed |

`search_skills` (the MCP listing tool) always ranks lexically.

## Usage telemetry

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/usage-telemetry/

Usage telemetry tells you which skills your team's agents actually use, which ones were edited since they were last
used, and which ones never fire and can be retired. Everything stays on your machine: a hook appends one
identifier-only line per skill load to a local log, and `ai-rulez telemetry report` joins that log with your source
skills, feedback and [eval scores](evals.md). Nothing is enabled by default and nothing here makes a network call.

This page covers skill usage and the local log. Rule, agent and context-file loads, and optional export to an
OpenTelemetry collector, are on [Item-load telemetry and OTLP export](telemetry.md).

#### Example

Turn on the skills index and generate:

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml (excerpt)
presets = ["claude", "codex", "cursor"]

[usage]
skills_index = true
```

```bash
ai-rulez generate
ai-rulez telemetry hook --syntax toml    # paste the printed [[hooks]] into config.toml, then generate again
```

Work as usual. Each skill load appends a line to `.ai-rulez/local/usage.jsonl`. Then:

```console
$ ai-rulez telemetry report
Skill usage: 3 events

Used (1)
  deploy-staging                                3  last 2026-11-05T16:22:17Z  feedback: stale 1

Never used (1)
  release-notes

Changed since used (0)

Not in the index (0)
```

`release-notes` was never loaded: it is a candidate for removal, or its description needs work.

#### The skills index

With `[usage] skills_index = true`, `generate` writes `.ai-rulez/skills-index.json`. It is derived from the source
tree, byte-stable across runs and safe to commit. Turning the option off removes the file on the next `generate`.

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "skills": [
    {
      "id": "deploy-staging",
      "kind": "skill",
      "source": ".ai-rulez/skills/deploy-staging/SKILL.md",
      "hash": "blake3:43646786af80...",
      "digest": "sha256:11b96b692d42...",
      "owner": "platform",
      "version": "1.2.0",
      "outputs": {
        "claude": [".claude/skills/deploy-staging/SKILL.md"],
        "shared": [".agents/skills/deploy-staging/SKILL.md"]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | The skill's directory name, which is the name every harness invokes it by. |
| `kind` | `skill`, or `command` for a command a harness runs as a skill (for example commands the `claude` preset writes into `.claude/skills`). |
| `domain` | The domain the skill belongs to; omitted for root skills. |
| `source` | The authored `SKILL.md`. |
| `hash` | blake3 of the authored skill (`SKILL.md`, then each bundled resource in path order). Changes when, and only when, the skill changes. |
| `digest` | The skill's canonical digest, the same one [`ai-rulez lock`](lockfile.md) pins (scheme `ai-rulez/skill/v1`: `SKILL.md` plus `references/`, `scripts/` and `assets/`). The skill's `evals/` directory is not part of it, so editing a case does not make the skill look edited. Usage lines and eval results carry this digest, which is how a score is tied to the version that was used. |
| `owner`, `version` | From the `owner` and `version` frontmatter keys, when set. `[lint] require_metadata` can make them mandatory (see [strict validation](strict-validation.md)). |
| `outputs` | Per preset, the `SKILL.md` files it writes. Paths that several presets share (such as `.agents/skills`) are listed under `shared`. |

The index covers the active profile at the repository root. Scoped (monorepo) outputs and machine-local skills are not
listed.

#### Wiring the hooks

`ai-rulez telemetry hook` prints a hook template that runs `ai-rulez telemetry record` on the events that load a
skill. Nothing installs it for you: either merge the JSON into the harness's hooks file, or paste the `--syntax toml`
form into `config.toml` as [`[[hooks]]`](settings.md) so `generate` keeps it in sync without touching hooks you wrote
by hand.

```bash
ai-rulez telemetry hook                     # Claude Code, JSON for .claude/settings.json
ai-rulez telemetry hook --syntax toml       # the same as [[hooks]] groups for config.toml
ai-rulez telemetry hook --harness codex     # merge into .codex/hooks.json
ai-rulez telemetry hook --harness cursor    # merge into .cursor/hooks.json
ai-rulez telemetry hook -o hooks.json       # write to a file
```

```toml
# printed by `ai-rulez telemetry hook --syntax toml` (abridged)
[[hooks]]
event = "PreToolUse"
targets = ["claude"]
matcher = "Skill"
[[hooks.hooks]]
command = "ai-rulez telemetry record --log \"${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.ai-rulez/local/usage.jsonl\""
async = true
timeout = 5
...
```

The template registers these events. The skill events go to this page's log; the rule, agent and context events are
described on [Item-load telemetry](telemetry.md#what-is-collected).

| Harness | Event (matcher) | Records |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `PreToolUse` (`Skill`) | a skill the model invoked (`tool_input.skill`), `invocation: "tool"` |
| Claude Code | `UserPromptExpansion` | a skill the user invoked by slash command (`command_name`), `invocation: "slash"` |
| Claude Code | `InstructionsLoaded`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop` | rule, context-file and agent loads |
| Codex | `PreToolUse` (`Bash`) | a shell command that reads `skills/<id>/SKILL.md`, `invocation: "read"` |
| Codex | `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop` | agent runs |
| Cursor | `preToolUse` (`Shell`) | a shell command that reads `skills/<id>/SKILL.md`, `invocation: "read"` |
| Cursor | `subagentStart`, `subagentStop` | agent runs |

Codex and Cursor have no skill tool: they load a skill by reading its `SKILL.md`, so the recorder infers a load from the
path. It counts a read tool (`Read`, `read_file`, `view`, `open`) given `skills/<id>/SKILL.md`, and a shell reader
(`cat`, `head`, `tail`, `less`, `more`, `bat`, `nl`, `sed` without `-i`, `Get-Content`) run on that path, including after
`cd x &&`, variable prefixes and inside pipelines. Writes and edits are never loads (`sed -i`, `tee`, a redirect into the
file, `git add`, `rm`, editor tools). The generated templates match only the shell tool (`Bash` for Codex, `Shell` for
Cursor); widen the matcher if you also want reads through the file-read tool. Check the log after wiring the hook; the
harnesses' payload fields may change.

Other harnesses (`--harness gemini`, `copilot`, ...) get a warning and no template, because their skill-load payload is
not documented:

```console
$ ai-rulez telemetry hook --harness gemini
warning: no usage hook template for the gemini harness: its skill-load hook payload is not documented in ai-rulez (supported: claude, codex, cursor)
```

##### Hook and record flags

`telemetry hook` accepts the same `--log`, `--index`, `--role` and `--sink-command` flags as `record` and writes them
into the generated command.

| Flag | Command | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--harness` | `hook`, `record` | `claude` (default), `codex` or `cursor`. |
| `--syntax` | `hook` | `json` (default, a hooks block) or `toml` (`[[hooks]]` groups). |
| `--executable` | `hook` | Command the hook runs (default `ai-rulez`). Quoted as one word, so `npx -y ai-rulez` is not split. |
| `-o`, `--output` | `hook` | Write the template to a file instead of standard output. |
| `--log` | `hook`, `record` | Log file (default `.ai-rulez/local/usage.jsonl`). |
| `--index` | `hook`, `record` | Skills index used to resolve hashes and digests (default: `.ai-rulez/skills-index.json` below the hook payload's `cwd`; a payload without `cwd` logs no hash or digest). |
| `--role` | `hook`, `record` | Active role, recorded as given (else `$AI_RULEZ_ROLE`). |
| `--sink-command` | `hook`, `record` | Shell command that also receives each log line on standard input. |
| `--outcome` | `record` | `loaded` (default), `used` or `abandoned`, for a hook you wire to a later event. |
| `--served` | `record` | Mark the load as served by the MCP skills server. |
| `--salt-file` | `record` | File holding the session-hash salt (default `usage.salt` beside the log; `$AI_RULEZ_USAGE_SALT` wins). |
| `--root` | `record` | Project root (default `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, else the directory holding the configuration). |

`ai-rulez telemetry record` never fails a session: it prints nothing on standard output, reports problems on standard
error and always exits 0. It ignores events it does not handle.

A sink command gets 3 seconds per line; after that its process group is killed. A failing sink does not drop the
entry, which still goes to the log. The same limits apply to `ai-rulez mcp --usage-sink`.

#### The usage log

Each skill load appends one JSON line to the log, which lives under the machine-local `.ai-rulez/local/` directory and
is never committed:

```json
{"v":3,"ts":"2026-11-05T16:22:17Z","event":"skill_invoked","skill":"deploy-staging","id":"deploy-staging","hash":"blake3:43646786af80...","session":"abf5a79b8deede5d","invocation":"tool","harness":"claude","outcome":"loaded","digest":"sha256:11b96b692d42...","digest_scheme":"ai-rulez/skill/v1","event_id":"322f26b2184274ce"}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `v` | Log format version, currently `3`. |
| `ts`, `event` | UTC time; `skill_invoked`. |
| `skill`, `id` | The name the harness reported, and the index id it resolves to (a `plugin:` prefix is dropped). |
| `hash` | The index hash at load time. |
| `digest`, `digest_scheme` | The canonical digest from the index and its scheme (`ai-rulez/skill/v1`). A load through the MCP skills server without an index digest logs the served skill's digest under `ai-rulez/served-skill/v1`, which does not join with eval results. Omitted when the skill is not in the index. |
| `invocation` | `tool`, `slash` or `read`. |
| `harness`, `role` | As given to the recorder; `role` is omitted when unset. |
| `session` | A salted hash of the harness session id (16 hex digits), never the raw id; see [What is collected](telemetry.md#what-is-collected). The salt is in `usage.salt` beside the log. |
| `outcome` | `loaded`, `used` or `abandoned`. |
| `served` | `true` for a load through the MCP skills server; omitted otherwise. |
| `event_id` | 16 hex digits identifying the line, so a merged or replayed line is counted once. Derived from the machine salt, so it links nothing across machines. |

**Never recorded**: prompts, slash-command arguments, tool inputs other than the skill name (or, for Codex and Cursor,
the `SKILL.md` path), transcripts, raw session ids and file contents. The recorder decodes only the fields it needs, so
nothing else can reach the log.

The recorder refuses to write through a symlink: if the log or any directory between the project root and the log is a
symlink, the write fails. A committed symlink therefore cannot redirect the log. Point `--log` at a real directory.

Older log lines stay readable: version 1 lines (which may hold a raw session id; delete or rotate such a log if it must
not keep them) and version 2 lines (no digest or event id) are reported, and unknown fields of newer lines are ignored.

#### Feedback

```bash
ai-rulez telemetry feedback deploy-staging --kind stale --note-file ./why.txt
```

Records that a skill `misled` you, is `stale`, is `wrong`, or was `great`. One line goes to
`.ai-rulez/local/feedback.jsonl` (change it with `--log`) with the skill, its index hash, the kind, and `--harness` and
`--role` when given. With `--note-file` the text is copied to `feedback-notes/` beside the log (mode 0600, at most
64 KB) and only the file name is logged. A note never enters a log line, the index or `eval-results.json`, so it does
not leave the machine unless you copy it.

Feedback changes nothing by itself: `telemetry report` shows the counts, and
[`telemetry report evals`](evals.md#reports) recommends a rewrite when `misled`, `wrong` and `stale` outweigh `great`.

#### Reports

```bash
ai-rulez telemetry report                          # default log, index, feedback and eval results
ai-rulez telemetry report path/to/usage.jsonl --format json
ai-rulez telemetry report evals                    # rank skills to keep, review, rewrite or prune
```

`telemetry report` lists:

| Section | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Used | Indexed skills with at least one logged load: count, last load, feedback counts and the recorded eval pass rate. |
| Never used | Indexed skills with no logged load: retirement candidates. |
| Changed since used | Skills whose logged loads carry a hash other than the current one: the usage evidence describes an older version. |
| Not in the index | Logged ids the index does not know (renamed, removed, or from outside the project). |

When the log holds rule, agent or context events, the report adds the item sections described in
[Item-load telemetry](telemetry.md#the-item-report) (`--items` always includes them).

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[log]` argument | `.ai-rulez/local/usage.jsonl` | The usage log to read. |
| `--index` | `.ai-rulez/skills-index.json` | Skills index to join against. |
| `--feedback` | `feedback.jsonl` beside the log, when present | Feedback log to join; a named file must exist. |
| `--evals` | `.ai-rulez/eval-results.json`, when present | Eval results to join; a named file must exist. |
| `--items` | off | Always include the rule, agent and context sections. |
| `--format` | `text` | `text` or `json`. |

The command always exits 0.

##### Joining several logs

`telemetry report evals` (documented on [Evals](evals.md#reports)) accepts `--usage` more than once to merge the
usage of several repositories or machines. A line that appears in more than one log counts once, by `event_id`. With
`--from-otlp` every `--usage` file is read as OTLP JSON, as written by
[`telemetry export --to file`](telemetry.md#exporting-to-a-file) or a collector's file exporter.

#### Log maintenance

| Task | Command | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Copy the log as an OTLP JSON file (no network) | `ai-rulez telemetry export --to file usage.ndjson` | [Exporting to a file](telemetry.md#exporting-to-a-file) |
| Push the log to your collector | `ai-rulez telemetry export --to otlp` | [Export and consent](telemetry.md#the-consent-record) |
| Delete old lines | `ai-rulez telemetry prune --keep-days 90` | [Pruning the usage log](telemetry.md#pruning-the-usage-log) |

To discard everything, delete `.ai-rulez/local/usage.jsonl`, `usage.salt`, `feedback.jsonl` and `feedback-notes/`.

## Item-load telemetry (OTLP)

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/telemetry/

Item-load telemetry records which rules, agents and context files a harness actually loaded, so you can see how many
rules a session carries and which ones never load. It can also ship those identifier-only events, together with the
[skill usage](usage-telemetry.md) lines, to an OpenTelemetry (OTLP) collector you run. Everything is off by default,
the local log needs no network, and a repository can never switch on network export for the people who clone it.

This page covers item events, consent, export and the OTLP format. Skill usage, the hook setup, feedback and the
reports are on [Usage telemetry](usage-telemetry.md).

Recording rule and context loads currently supports Claude Code only (its `InstructionsLoaded` hook). Agent runs are
also recorded for Codex and Cursor.

#### Example

Wire the hooks (see [Wiring the hooks](usage-telemetry.md#wiring-the-hooks)) and consent to export from your own
machine. `telemetry enable` turns recording on for you; `[telemetry] enabled = true` in the repository is only needed
for local-only recording without export:

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml (excerpt)
[telemetry]
enabled = true
```

```console
$ ai-rulez telemetry enable --endpoint https://collector.acme.example:4318
consent recorded for https://collector.acme.example:4318 (http/json)
  stored in ~/.config/ai-rulez/telemetry-consent.json (mode 0600)
  exports: event.name, ai_rulez.item.kind, ai_rulez.item.id, ai_rulez.item.digest, ...
  withheld: ai_rulez.item.path, ai_rulez.session
  cursor: at the end of the usage log; only events recorded from now on are exported (--backfill sends history)
export is on. Hooks record events (ai-rulez telemetry hook); preview what is sent with `ai-rulez telemetry preview`.

$ ai-rulez telemetry status
telemetry: export on, recording on
consent:   granted by the consent record (2026-11-05T16:22:33.245Z) for collector.acme.example:4318
endpoint:  collector.acme.example:4318 (http/json, host only)
...
pending:   0 in the outbox, 0 in the usage log past the cursor
last flush: never
totals:    sent 0, dropped 0, rejected 0, failed flushes 0 (0 in a row)
```

From then on, hooks record events and flush them to the collector in the background. `ai-rulez telemetry disable`
withdraws consent.

#### Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `telemetry enable --endpoint URL` | Store your consent to export to one collector. |
| `telemetry disable` | Delete the consent record. Export stops; the log and outbox are kept. |
| `telemetry status` | On or off, consent, pending events, delivery failures. |
| `telemetry doctor` | Resolved settings with their source, consent state, outbox and last flush. |
| `telemetry preview` | Print exactly what an export would send. Sends nothing. |
| `telemetry flush` | Send the outbox now (hooks do this in the background). |
| `telemetry export --to file FILE` | Write the usage log as an OTLP JSON file. No network, no consent needed. |
| `telemetry export --to otlp` | Push the usage log past the export cursor to the consented collector. |
| `telemetry prune --keep-days N` | Delete log lines older than N days that were already exported. |
| `telemetry report` | Skill usage plus rules per session and never-loaded items (see [below](#the-item-report)). |
| `telemetry hook`, `telemetry record` | The hook template and the command it runs ([Usage telemetry](usage-telemetry.md#wiring-the-hooks)). |

`status` and `doctor` take `--format json`. `enable`, `disable`, `status`, `doctor`, `flush`, `preview`, `prune` and
`record` accept `--root` (default `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, else the directory holding the configuration).

#### What is collected

One `item_event` line per load, appended to the same `.ai-rulez/local/usage.jsonl` as skill usage:

```json
{"v":1,"event":"item_event","ts":"2026-11-05T16:22:17Z","event_id":"084c1be76a6c5207","kind":"rule","id":"atomic-commits","source":"hook","harness":"claude","session":"abf5a79b8deede5d","outcome":"loaded","load_reason":"session_start","memory_type":"Project"}
```

| Field | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `v`, `event`, `ts` | Schema version (`1`), `item_event`, UTC time | `1` |
| `event_id` | 16 hex digits; stays the same when a line is replayed, so a backend can de-duplicate | `084c1be76a6c5207` |
| `kind` | `skill`, `rule`, `agent`, `command` or `context` | `rule` |
| `id` | A rule's file name without `.md`, an agent type, a skill name, or a context file's repository-relative path | `atomic-commits` |
| `path` | Repository-relative path, exported only with `include_paths = true` | `.claude/rules/atomic-commits.md` |
| `digest`, `digest_scheme` | Content digest when known; for skills the canonical `ai-rulez/skill/v1` digest | `blake3:fa37c294...` |
| `source` | `hook`, `mcp` or `cli` | `hook` |
| `harness`, `role` | As given to the recorder | `claude` |
| `served` | The load came through the MCP skills server | `false` |
| `session` | Salted hash of the harness session id, never the raw id; exported only with `include_session = true` | `abf5a79b8deede5d` |
| `outcome` | `loaded`, `used` or `abandoned` (an agent's stop event is `used`) | `loaded` |
| `load_reason` | Claude Code: `session_start`, `nested_traversal`, `path_glob_match`, `include`, `compact`; agents: `subagent_start`, `subagent_stop`; MCP: `read`, `list` | `session_start` |
| `memory_type` | Claude Code's `User`, `Project`, `Local` or `Managed` | `Project` |
| `duration_ms` | Agent run time, from the paired start and stop events (Cursor reports it directly) | `2500` |

A file outside the repository (a user-level `~/.claude/rules/x.md`) contributes only its base name.

With telemetry on, `ai-rulez mcp` also records `source=mcp` events: after a successful `read_skill`, `read_rule`,
`read_context` or `get_skill` (reason `read`), and after `list_*` and `search_skills` calls with the id `_list`
(reason `list`; reports count these under load reasons and never list them as items). A rule's generated
file is mapped back to the source rule by its file name.

**Never collected**: prompts, model output, tool inputs or results, file contents, command arguments, transcripts,
user, host or repository names, environment values, absolute paths, the raw session id and feedback notes. The hook
handler decodes only the fields above from a hook payload, so other payload fields (`prompt`, `transcript_path`,
`last_assistant_message`, ...) cannot reach an event.

##### Eval results

An export can also carry `eval_result` events (`--with-evals` on `export` and `preview`): one per verified result in
`.ai-rulez/eval-results.json`, built at export time and never written to the usage log. It holds the skill id, the
canonical digest the run covered, the harness, the run date and the four scores (`pass_rate`, `trigger_precision`,
`trigger_recall`, `ablation_delta`), and no case, prompt, output or load field. Results that are not signed with your
key, and activation-only results, are never exported. See [Evals](evals.md#scores-and-the-results-file).

#### The item report

`ai-rulez telemetry report` adds these sections when the log holds item events:

```console
$ ai-rulez telemetry report
...
Item loads: 4 events in 1 sessions
Rules per session: median 1.0, mean 1.00, max 1 (over 1 sessions)

Rules loaded (1)
  atomic-commits                                1 loads     1 sessions  last 2026-11-05T16:22:17Z  [session_start=1]
Rules never loaded (0)

Agents loaded (1)
  code-reviewer                                 1 loads     1 sessions  last 2026-11-05T16:22:17Z  [subagent_start=1]
Agents never loaded (0)

Context files loaded (1)
  CLAUDE.md                                     1 loads     1 sessions  last 2026-11-05T16:22:17Z  [session_start=1]
Context files never loaded (1)
  AGENTS.md
...
```

"Never loaded" joins the log with the generated manifest, which a metrics backend cannot do: an item that never
loaded has no series. Flags are listed under [Reports](usage-telemetry.md#reports).

#### Configuration

```toml
[telemetry]
enabled         = false        # local recording into .ai-rulez/local/usage.jsonl
sample          = 1.0          # fraction of sessions exported, decided per session hash (0 to 1)

# User scope only (the user config file or AI_RULEZ_TELEMETRY_*); ignored in a repository config:
allow_network   = false        # consent as a setting; `telemetry enable` is the other way
otlp_endpoint   = "https://collector.acme.example:4318"
otlp_protocol   = "http/json"  # http/json, http/protobuf or grpc
headers_env     = ["OTLP_HEADERS"]   # NAMES of variables holding "k=v,k2=v2"
service_name    = "ai-rulez"
include_paths   = false        # export item paths
include_session = false        # export the salted session hash
salt_file       = ""

[telemetry.resource]           # extra OTLP resource attributes; user scope only
team = "platform"
"deployment.environment" = "prod"
```

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | bool | `false` | Record item events locally. |
| `sample` | float | `1.0` | Share of sessions exported, decided per session hash (`0` exports nothing). The local log records every session. |
| `allow_network` | bool | `false` | Consent to export without a consent record. User scope only. |
| `otlp_endpoint` | string | none | Collector base URL (`https://`; `http://` only for a loopback host). For `grpc`, `host[:port]`. User scope only. |
| `otlp_protocol` | string | `http/json` | `http/json`, `http/protobuf` or `grpc`. User scope only. |
| `headers_env` | list | `[]` | Names of environment variables whose `k=v,k2=v2` values become request headers. Read at flush time, never written anywhere. User scope only. |
| `service_name` | string | `ai-rulez` | The `service.name` resource attribute. User scope only. |
| `include_paths` | bool | `false` | Export `ai_rulez.item.path`. User scope only. |
| `include_session` | bool | `false` | Export `ai_rulez.session`. User scope only. |
| `salt_file` | string | `usage.salt` beside the log | File holding the session-hash salt. User scope only. |
| `resource` | table | none | Up to 8 resource attributes. Keys are lower-case dotted names of at most 64 characters, values non-empty strings of at most 128. The `service.*`, `host.*`, `user.*`, `process.*`, `os.*`, `cloud.*`, `k8s.*`, `container.*`, `telemetry.*` and `ai_rulez.*` namespaces are reserved. User scope only. |

##### Environment variables

Precedence, highest first: kill switches, environment, user config, repository config, defaults.

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `AI_RULEZ_TELEMETRY=off`, `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` | Kill switches: nothing is recorded or exported. |
| `AI_RULEZ_TELEMETRY` | Turn recording on or off. |
| `AI_RULEZ_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT`, `_PROTOCOL`, `_ALLOW_NETWORK`, `_SERVICE_NAME`, `_SAMPLE`, `_INCLUDE_PATHS`, `_INCLUDE_SESSION`, `_SALT_FILE` | The keys of the same name. |
| `AI_RULEZ_TELEMETRY_HEADERS_ENV` | Comma-separated variable names. |
| `AI_RULEZ_TELEMETRY_RESOURCE` | `key=value,key2=value2`; overrides user-config entries per key. |

##### The trust rule

A committed repository config is input from whoever wrote it: cloning a repository must not start sending data to a
host its author picked.

| Key | Repository config and `config.local.*` | User config and environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled`, `sample` | honored (local recording only) | honored |
| every other key | ignored, reported by `telemetry doctor` and `AR9K1` | honored |

The local overlay lives in the checkout, so it counts as repository scope. Network export is active only when
recording is on, consent is present and a valid endpoint remains after this filtering, so a repository can at most turn
on the local log. The [trust model](trust-model.md) applies the same rule to every setting that reaches the network.

##### The consent record

`telemetry enable` stores your consent in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ai-rulez/telemetry-consent.json` (else
`~/.config/ai-rulez/`), mode 0600:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "endpoint": "https://collector.acme.example:4318",
  "protocol": "http/json",
  "scope": { "fields": ["event.name", "ai_rulez.item.kind", "..."], "fields_hash": "a1f742a2..." },
  "granted_at": "2026-11-05T16:22:33.245Z",
  "ai_rulez_version": "5.10.0"
}
```

```bash
ai-rulez telemetry enable --endpoint https://collector.acme.example:4318
ai-rulez telemetry enable --endpoint collector.acme.example:4317 --protocol grpc --include-session
ai-rulez telemetry enable --endpoint https://collector.acme.example:4318 --backfill   # also send existing history
ai-rulez telemetry disable
```

| `enable` flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--endpoint` | Collector endpoint (default: the configured one). |
| `--protocol` | `http/json` (default), `http/protobuf` or `grpc`. |
| `--include-paths`, `--include-session` | Also consent to exporting item paths or the session hash. |
| `--backfill` | Also export the events already in the usage log. |

- **Only you can grant it.** The record is read from the user config directory only; a repository cannot grant, edit
  or point to one. A record that is group- or world-writable, a symlink, malformed or has an unknown field is ignored,
  and `telemetry status` says why.
- **It covers what you agreed to.** It names the endpoint, the protocol and a hash of the exported attribute names. A
  different endpoint or protocol, an opt-in you turned on later (`include_paths`, `include_session`), or a newer
  release that exports more attributes makes it stale: nothing is sent until you run `enable` again.
- **It supplies, never overrides.** With a valid record, recording turns on for you, and the consented endpoint,
  protocol and opt-ins are used where your user config and environment set none. `AI_RULEZ_TELEMETRY_ALLOW_NETWORK=0`
  refuses export even with a record. The kill switches and an organization [policy](policy.md) win over everything.
- **It is not retroactive.** Only events recorded after `enable` are sent, unless you pass `--backfill`.
- **`disable` deletes it.** Export stops, and so does recording that the record turned on. Recording that your config
  or `AI_RULEZ_TELEMETRY` turns on continues, and `disable` says so. The usage log and outbox are kept.

#### How export works

Hooks are short-lived, so the recorder never touches the network:

1. A hook appends the event to the usage log and, while export is active, to an outbox
   (`.ai-rulez/local/telemetry-outbox.jsonl`, mode 0600, at most 10,000 events, oldest dropped first). If the outbox
   is busy for 25 ms the event is not queued (a later catch-up queues it); the harness is never delayed.
2. When the outbox is due, the recorder starts one detached `telemetry flush --background` (at most one a minute,
   8-second deadline, always exits 0). A long-running `ai-rulez mcp` server flushes from a timer and once on exit.
3. A flush first catches up: it queues log lines past the [export cursor](#the-export-cursor-and-catch-up) that the
   outbox does not hold yet. It then sends batches of 200 events to `/v1/logs` and `/v1/metrics`, gzipped.
4. 408, 425, 429, every 5xx except 501 and 505, and network errors are retried with exponential backoff (1 s, 2 s,
   4 s, plus jitter; `Retry-After` honored up to 30 s); if retries run out, the events stay in the outbox for the next
   flush. Every other status (400, 401, 403, 404, 413, 501, 505, a 3xx redirect, ...) drops the batch and counts it as
   rejected. Redirects are never followed.
5. Delivery is at-least-once. Backends de-duplicate on `ai_rulez.event_id`, which is the same on every attempt.

Background failures are silent to the harness but recorded: `telemetry status` shows the last error and the
delivered, dropped, rejected and failed-flush counts. Stored errors hold a status code or a reason such as `timeout`,
never the URL or a header.

| `flush` flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--timeout` | `8s` | Overall deadline; at most `30s`. |
| `--background` | off | Silent mode used by hooks: exit 0 whatever happens. |

##### The export cursor and catch-up

The usage log is the source of truth; the outbox is only a delivery queue. The cursor
(`.ai-rulez/local/telemetry-cursor.json`) records how far into the log events are accounted for, plus the ids of the
last 4,096 delivered or rejected events, so a catch-up never sends an event twice.

- A cursor that was never set is placed at the end of the log, and nothing is queued: history is exported only when
  you ask (`telemetry enable --backfill`, `telemetry export --to otlp --all`).
- One catch-up queues at most 2,000 events; the next flush picks up the rest.
- Sampling (`sample`) applies to catch-up events too.
- A rotated or truncated log is detected and read from the start.

##### Pushing by hand

`telemetry export --to otlp` runs the same catch-up and delivery in the foreground. It refuses without consent and
exits 1 when delivery fails, so a CI job notices.

```console
$ ai-rulez telemetry export --to otlp
queued 12 events from the usage log and 0 eval results (3 already queued or delivered); delivered 12 in 1 batches
$ ai-rulez telemetry export --to otlp --dry-run
would queue 0 events from the usage log (0 already queued or delivered), 0 eval results; 0 events already wait in the outbox (nothing sent)
```

| `export` flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--to` | required | `file` or `otlp`. |
| `--file` | | Destination for `--to file` (or pass it as the argument). |
| `--log` | `<config dir>/local/usage.jsonl` | Usage log to export. |
| `--all` | off | `--to otlp`: start from the beginning of the log instead of the cursor. |
| `--max-batches` | `10` | `--to otlp`: stop after this many catch-up rounds of up to 2,000 events. |
| `--with-evals` | off | Also export verified [eval results](#eval-results). |
| `--evals` | `<config dir>/eval-results.json` | Eval results file for `--with-evals`. |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | off | Report only: write, queue and send nothing. |

##### Exporting to a file
