```console
  model gemini-2.5-flash-lite  host (provider default)  network allowed: false  content: descriptions
  skill:deploy-staging         2 call(s)   2829 bytes  sha256 adb401f984a3
  skill:release-notes          2 call(s)   2800 bytes  sha256 ac147370b05a
  2 items, 4-12 calls, ~3038-9114 input tokens, up to 18000 output tokens
  cost $0.0009 to $0.0081 (cap $0.5, 300 calls)
```

With `[llm] allow_network = true` in your user config, a judged run looks like this:

```text
$ ai-rulez review --semantic --content full
rubric skill-quality@2 (builtin:skill-quality, sha256:537e621b)  model gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-lite (resolved gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-lite)  votes<=3  content full  advisory
skill:deploy-staging         skill    score 100/100  semantic 45/100
  AR9G1  trigger-quality      fail - The description does not name a concrete trigger or when not to use the skill.  [judge, agree 2/2]
  AR9G2  overlap              fail "Write the release notes for the rollout." - overlaps release-notes.  [judge, unstable agree 2/3]
skill:leak                   skill    withheld: AR001 secret-detected: never sent to a judge
3 items: 2 scored, 1 withheld, 0 excluded, 0 skipped; mean score 100; mean semantic score 45 over 2 judged
2 items judged, 0 answers cached; calls 9, tokens 11204, cost $0.0113 (cap $0.5)
calibration: missing
  no calibration record: run `ai-rulez review calibrate`
```

Other commands:

```bash
ai-rulez review skill:deploy-staging             # one item: an id, a name or a path
ai-rulez review calibrate --golden tests/review/golden/skill-quality
ai-rulez review --semantic --gate                # exit 2 on a stable fail of a calibrated dimension
ai-rulez review fix skill:deploy-staging --model gemini-2.5-flash   # print a patch; --apply writes it
ai-rulez review explain AR9G2                    # what a code means, with the rubric's definitions
ai-rulez rubric lint                             # check .ai-rulez/rubrics/*
```

#### The offline score

Each rubric dimension lists `twins`: the lint rules that already say something about it (`trigger-quality` has
`AR801`-`AR803`). The dimension's verdict comes from the twin findings on the item and, for a skill or command, on its
resource files:

| Twin finding | Verdict | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none, or only `info` | `pass` | 1 |
| a warning | `warn` | 0.5 |
| an error | `fail` | 0 |

`score = round(100 * sum(weight_i * value_i) / sum(weight_i))` over the scored dimensions. A dimension with no twin
(the built-in `instruction-conflict`) is `not-scored` and left out. `pass` means no lint rule fired, not that a person
would call the description good: read the offline score as a floor.

A dimension below `pass` is reported with its code (`AR9G1`-`AR9G7`, see [Rule codes](#rule-codes)) at the dimension's
severity ceiling (`warning` or `info`, never `error`). Every finding is advisory and carries a fingerprint that
survives line moves.

The built-in rubric `builtin:skill-quality` (`ai-rulez rubric show`):

| Dimension | Code | Weight | Group | Body needed | Twins |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger-quality` | `AR9G1` | 0.30 | intrinsic | no | `AR801`, `AR802`, `AR803` |
| `overlap` | `AR9G2` | 0.25 | contextual | no | `AR701`, `AR702` |
| `body-accuracy` | `AR9G3` | 0.15 | intrinsic | yes | `AR201`, `AR202`, `AR301`, `AR302`, `AR401`, `AR402` |
| `injection-intent` | `AR9G4` | 0.10 | intrinsic | yes | `AR003`, `AR004`, `AR017`, `AR018`, `AR020` |
| `scope-creep` | `AR9G5` | 0.10 | intrinsic | yes | `AR007`, `AR013` |
| `instruction-conflict` | `AR9G6` | 0.05 | contextual | yes | none |
| `body-structure` | `AR9G7` | 0.05 | intrinsic | yes | `AR805`, `AR806`, `AR901`, `AR902` |

It applies to skills, agents and commands.

#### What is never sent

These filters run before anything is planned, and decide what may ever leave the machine:

- An item with a credential or hidden character (`AR001`, `AR002`) in its file or its skill resources is **withheld**:
  no score, no manifest entry, an `AR9G0` note. Review scans the text itself, so lint ignores and severity overrides
  cannot make such an item eligible. With `[review] on_secret = "redact"`, an item whose own text holds a credential
  is sent with it replaced by `[REDACTED:AR001]`; it is still withheld when the masked text still looks like a
  credential, when the credential is in a resource file, or when it has a hidden character.
- A twin **error** pre-empts its dimension: the judge is not asked, and the lint verdict stands.
- `[review] exclude` globs (matched against name, id and path) exclude an item.
- Content from includes, installed skills, skill sources and builtins is skipped unless `--include-imports`.
- An item the rubric does not apply to, or that cannot be read, is skipped with the reason.

Withheld, excluded and skipped items are always listed with their reason.

#### Estimate and the egress manifest

`--estimate` prints what a judged run would send and sends nothing. It works offline and is the recommended first
step.

- **What**: per item, the planned calls (an `intrinsic` call with the item, a `contextual` call with its description
  and up to `max_siblings` sibling descriptions), their size, and the SHA-256 of the data. Never the content.
- **Where**: the host of the resolved `[llm] base_url` (`(provider default)` when unset) and whether `allow_network`
  is on. A repository `base_url` is ignored, by the [trust rule](llm.md#trust-rule).
- **How much**: tokens at one per three bytes; the low bound is one vote per call and a 400-token answer, the high
  bound `votes.max` votes at `max_output_tokens`. Prices come from the built-in table or `[llm]
  price_input_per_mtok`/`price_output_per_mtok`.
- **Caps**: `--max-cost`/`--max-calls`, else `[review] max_cost_usd`/`max_calls`, else 0.50 USD and 300 calls
  (`--max-cost 0` is unlimited). A run is refused (exit 1) when even the low bound exceeds a cap, or when the model has
  no price and a cost cap is set.
- `--show-prompt` prints the exact planned messages.

#### The judge: `--semantic`

```text
ai-rulez review --semantic [--content descriptions|full] [--k N] [--model M | --models A,B]
                           [--max-cost USD] [--max-calls N] [--no-cache] [--cache-dir DIR]
                           [--gate [--gate-level info|warning|error]] [--baseline F] [--write-baseline F]
```

Two opt-ins are required: `--semantic`, and `[llm] allow_network = true` in user scope (the user config file or
`AI_RULEZ_LLM_ALLOW_NETWORK`; see the [trust rule](llm.md#trust-rule)). A model must be set (`[llm] model` or
`--model`). Nothing is sent until every check, including the caps, has passed.

**Content.** `--content descriptions` (default) sends the name, description and frontmatter keys. Dimensions that need
the body (`body-accuracy`, `injection-intent`, `scope-creep`, `instruction-conflict`, `body-structure`) are then
`skipped` ("needs --content full"), not guessed, so a default run judges `trigger-quality` and `overlap`.
`--content full` adds the frontmatter and body, truncated head and tail at the rubric's `max_item_tokens`. A truncated
item's verdicts are capped at `info`, and `--gate` refuses to run on it.

**Prompt.** The item is sent inside a fence whose delimiter carries a nonce derived from the request, so the item's
author cannot close it. The model is told the fenced text is data, and that text addressed to the reviewer is itself a
finding. No tools are exposed. The reply must match a JSON schema exactly; an invalid reply is retried once, then the
dimension is `error`, never `pass`.

**Evidence.** Every quote a verdict cites must appear verbatim (whitespace-normalized) in what was sent, and be 8
characters to 20 words long. A quote that does not is dropped and counted (`hallucinated_evidence`); a `warn` or
`fail` left with no valid quote is reported as `pass`, unless the dimension sets `allow_absence` (the problem is that
something is missing).

**Votes.** The first vote runs at `first_temperature`. A pass is accepted, except for `injection-intent`, which is
always voted on again. A flagged dimension gets up to `--k` votes (default the rubric's `votes.max`, 3) with the
dimensions and siblings reshuffled, stopping once two votes agree. The verdict is the median (`pass < warn < fail`);
`agreement` is the share of votes equal to it. Below `instability_threshold` (0.67) the dimension is `unstable`: it is
reported at `info`, counts as a pass and never gates.

**Semantic score.** The same formula over the dimensions the judge answered.

**Cache and caps.** Answers are cached by the [model layer](llm.md), keyed by the request and a prompt version that
includes a digest of the rubric and its `system.md`, so editing the rubric invalidates them. A cache hit costs nothing,
so an unchanged project costs nothing to re-run. When `--max-cost` or `--max-calls` is reached the run stops: the
report is `incomplete`, lists the items it did not judge, and exits 0 (1 with `--gate`). A repository `[review]` cap
can only lower the default; the user config, environment and flags can set any value.

**Hosts.** A user-scope `[review] allowed_hosts` (or `AI_RULEZ_REVIEW_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, comma-separated) restricts where
a judged run may send; `provider-default` names the provider's own endpoint. A run to another host is refused before
anything is sent. Without a list, review warns and accepts any host. See
[Data egress](llm.md#data-egress-and-residency).

**Findings.** One code per dimension (`AR9G1`-`AR9G7`), at the dimension's severity ceiling, marked `advisory: true`
and `origin: "llm-judge"`, with the first quote, rationale, suggestion, vote agreement and a fingerprint of
`code | item | dimension | normalized first quote`.

#### Calibration and the gate

The judge may fail a build only after it was measured. `review calibrate` judges every case of a golden set the way
`--semantic` does (all `k` votes) and compares the verdicts with adjudicated human labels.

```bash
ai-rulez review calibrate --golden tests/review/golden/skill-quality --model gemini-2.5-flash-lite
ai-rulez review calibrate --models gemini-2.5-flash-lite,gemini-2.5-flash   # compare models; writes nothing
ai-rulez review calibrate --compare .ai-rulez/calibration/skill-quality.builtin.json   # drift check
```

A golden case (`golden/*.golden.yaml`, paths relative to the golden directory) is labeled by at least two people and
adjudicated:

```yaml
schema_version: 1
id: vague-trigger-01
kind: skill
item: { path: fixtures/vague-trigger-01/SKILL.md }
siblings: [fixtures/shared/sibling-a/SKILL.md]
labelers:
  - { id: a, labels: { trigger-quality: fail, overlap: pass } }
  - { id: b, labels: { trigger-quality: warn, overlap: pass } }
adjudicated: { trigger-quality: fail, overlap: pass }
probes: [pad, reorder, rename, canary]
```

Per dimension the calibration measures:

| Measure | Meaning | Threshold (`[calibration]`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| weighted kappa | agreement with the adjudicated labels | `min_weighted_kappa` |
| precision, recall | of "flagged" (not `pass`), with Wilson 95% intervals | `min_precision`, `min_recall.<dimension>` |
| human kappa | agreement between the labelers; below it the dimension is `ill-defined` (fix the rubric, not the model) | `min_human_kappa` |
| consistency | share of cases with identical votes across `k` | `min_consistency` |
| probes | `pad` (filler must not improve a verdict), `reorder` (sibling order must not change it), `rename` (the name must not change it), `canary` (text addressed to the reviewer must be flagged by `injection-intent`) | `min_probe` |

A dimension with fewer than 6 labeled cases is `uncalibrated`. The record passes when no calibrated dimension is `fail`
or `ill-defined`, at least one passes, and the set has `golden_min_items` cases.

The record is `calibration.json` in the rubric directory, or `.ai-rulez/calibration/<id>.builtin.json` for a built-in
rubric. It binds the result to the rubric digest, the prompt digest, the golden-set digest, the resolved model id (what
the provider answered with, not the alias), the content mode and `k`.

`review --semantic --gate` is refused (exit 1, nothing spent) unless a record matches all of those, passed, and is
younger than `max_age_days` (`[review.gate] calibration_max_age_days` overrides it). It is also refused for a floating
alias (`...-latest`) and when the answering model differs from the record's. It then exits 2 on a **stable** `fail`
of a dimension whose calibration passed, at or above `--gate-level` (default `warning`). Unstable, pre-empted,
errored, truncated and baselined verdicts never gate, and an errored or truncated item makes the gated run refuse as
incomplete. `[review.gate] require_calibration = false` lets `--gate` run without a record.

`AR9G9 judge-calibration-stale` (info) is reported by every judged run on a floating alias, under another model id, or
without a matching record.

`calibrate` needs the same opt-in as `--semantic` and is capped by `--max-cost` (default 2.00 USD) and `--max-calls`
(default 1000); a run cut short writes nothing. It exits 0 when the judge passes and 2 when it does not or drifted.
`--content` defaults to `full` for `calibrate` (the record binds the content mode, so calibrate with the mode you gate
with). `--no-probes` skips the probes, `--no-write` and `-o FILE` control where the record goes.

#### Drift and model comparison

`review calibrate --compare calibration.json` is the scheduled drift job: it calibrates again, compares with the
committed record, prints every golden verdict that changed, and exits 2 when a dimension's kappa fell by more than
0.05, a dimension stopped passing, the resolved model changed, or the judge no longer meets its thresholds.

`--models A,B` (on `review --semantic` and `calibrate`) judges with each model and reports pairwise agreement and kappa
per dimension, and lists the items the models disagree on as "review first". The first model is the primary one; the
caps are split between the models. On `calibrate` it writes no record.

#### `review fix`

```text
ai-rulez review fix [id|name|path...] [--finding FINGERPRINT] [--model FIXER] [--judge-model JUDGE]
                    [--output fix.patch] [--apply] [--allow-same-model] [--patch fix.patch]
```

For each authored item with a stable judged finding, the fixer model proposes exact-text edits (each `old` text must
occur once in the file); ai-rulez builds the unified diff from them. A proposal is kept only when all of this holds,
with up to two attempts (the second sees why the first failed), else the item reports "no safe fix":

1. The edits apply exactly and change the file.
2. In the frontmatter, only `description` changed: `name` and the tool list are untouched.
3. The item grew by at most `[review.fix] max_growth_percent` (default 25%, at least 200 bytes allowed).
4. The security scan finds nothing new, and no credential, hidden character, link or executable line was added.
5. A judge that is a **different model from the fixer** (unless `--allow-same-model`) rates every targeted dimension
   better and no other worse.

Only authored content in the configuration directory is touched; items from includes, installed skills, builtins, the
local overlay and generated outputs are reported as not fixable. The patch goes to `--output` or standard output, with
a header naming the item digest, finding, models and rubric version:

```text
# ai-rulez review fix
# item: skill:deploy-staging
# path: .ai-rulez/skills/deploy-staging/SKILL.md
# digest: sha256:2da78adb...
# finding: 51c0e2... AR9G1 trigger-quality
--- a/.ai-rulez/skills/deploy-staging/SKILL.md
+++ b/.ai-rulez/skills/deploy-staging/SKILL.md
@@ -1,5 +1,5 @@
...
```

`--apply` writes the verified edits. It refuses a file whose digest differs from the patch header (stale patch), and a
file with uncommitted changes or outside a git repository; every file is checked before the first is written. Run
`ai-rulez lock` afterwards (with [approvals](approvals.md), the change needs a new approval). `--patch FILE` verifies
and applies a patch from an earlier run without calling a model; it may only name items a fix run could edit.

The fixer is `--model`, else `[review.fix] model`; the judge is `--judge-model`, else `[llm] model`. `review fix`
defaults to `--content full`. It exits 2 when a finding had no safe fix. The same pipeline backs
[`improve --with builtin:review-fix`](improve.md#bundled-adapters), where a held-out eval gate decides whether the fix
is kept.

#### Selecting items

- `[id|name|path...]`: an id such as `skill:deploy-staging` or `skill:ops/deploy-staging`, a name, or a path. A selector that
  matches nothing is an error.
- `--since REV`: only items whose files changed since the revision (committed, staged, unstaged, untracked). Siblings
  are still drawn from every item.
- `--role NAME` / `--profile NAME`: only the content slice `generate --role` or `--profile` renders. The two are
  exclusive.
- `--no-local`: ignore the machine-local overlay and `local/` content.

`--concurrency N` (default 4, at most 16) sets how many items `review`, `review fix` and `review calibrate` judge at
once.

#### Baselines

`--write-baseline FILE` writes the fingerprints of this run's findings; `--baseline FILE` hides them in a later run, so
a team can adopt review without fixing everything first. Baselined findings are listed as `baselined` in JSON, left
out of text and SARIF, and never gate. An earlier `--format json` report also works as a baseline. A finding whose
quote changed has a new fingerprint.

#### Rubrics

A rubric is a versioned directory you own. It is never written into a harness's output tree, and
[`ai-rulez lock`](lockfile.md) pins it as kind `rubric` over every file in the directory, so an edit to a rubric, its
prompt, its labels or its calibration shows as lock drift (`AR981`) until you lock again.

```text
.ai-rulez/rubrics/<id>/
  rubric.toml                 # dimensions, weights, limits, votes, thresholds
  system.md                   # optional system prompt override
  golden/*.golden.yaml        # human-labeled cases for calibration
  fixtures/...                # the items the cases point at
  calibration.json            # written by `review calibrate`
```

`builtin:skill-quality` is embedded in the binary. Select a rubric with `--rubric <id>` or `[review] rubric`. A rubric
that fails `rubric lint` is refused.

```toml
schema_version = 1
id = "my-rubric"                 # must equal the directory name
version = 1                      # bump on any change that can alter output
applies_to = ["skill", "agent", "command"]   # also: rule

[limits]
max_item_tokens = 6000           # longer bodies are head+tail truncated; verdicts are capped at info
max_siblings = 5
max_output_tokens = 700          # the judge's completion cap; unset means 1500

[votes]
first_temperature = 0.0
extra_temperature = 0.7
max = 3
instability_threshold = 0.67

[calibration]
golden_min_items = 40
min_weighted_kappa = 0.60
min_consistency = 0.85
min_human_kappa = 0.70
min_precision = 0.70
min_probe = 0.95
max_age_days = 90
[calibration.min_recall]
injection-intent = 0.90

[[dimension]]
id = "trigger-quality"
code = "AR9G1"                   # AR9G1-AR9G7
group = "intrinsic"              # intrinsic: the item alone; contextual: needs siblings
weight = 0.6                     # weights must sum to 1
severity = "warning"             # ceiling: warning or info, never error
twins = ["AR801", "AR802"]       # lint rules that pre-empt and score this dimension
allow_absence = true             # a missing element needs no quote
needs_body = false               # true: judged only with --content full
question = "Does the description say when to use the skill?"
pass = "Names a concrete trigger and a non-trigger."
warn = "Names the task but the trigger is generic."
fail = "Could apply to almost any request."
```

A custom rubric can reorder, reweight or retarget dimensions, but uses only the codes `AR9G1`-`AR9G7`.

##### `ai-rulez rubric`

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `rubric list` | The built-in and project rubrics with version and digest. |
| `rubric show [id]` | Dimensions, weights, twins and the formula. |
| `rubric lint [id...]` | Check rubrics (default: every project rubric; `builtin:<id>` is accepted). `--format text\|json\|sarif`. Exit 2 with findings, 1 when unreadable. |

`rubric lint` reports `AR9G8` for: a wrong `schema_version`, an `id` other than the directory name, weights that do not
sum to 1, duplicate dimension ids or codes, a code outside `AR9G1`-`AR9G7`, a twin that is not a lint rule, a
`severity` of `error`, thresholds out of range, an unknown key, a golden case with fewer than two labelers, an unknown
dimension, verdict or probe, a path with `..`, a calibration record for another rubric, and any symlink.

##### Rule codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `AR9G0` | Run note: an item was withheld, excluded, skipped, or not judged because the run stopped. |
| `AR9G1`-`AR9G7` | The rubric's dimensions (built-in: see the table under [The offline score](#the-offline-score)). |
| `AR9G8` | `rubric-invalid`. |
| `AR9G9` | `judge-calibration-stale`. |

`review` and `rubric lint` emit them; `validate` does not. `review explain AR9G2` prints the explanation and the
rubric's definitions. See [code ranges](strict-validation.md#code-ranges).

#### Configuration

```toml
[review]
rubric = "builtin:skill-quality"   # or a directory name under .ai-rulez/rubrics
content = "descriptions"           # descriptions | full
exclude = ["internal-*"]           # name globs
max_cost_usd = 0.50                # a repository value can only lower the default
max_calls = 300
on_secret = "withhold"             # withhold | redact
allowed_hosts = []                 # honored only from the user config file

[review.gate]
level = "warning"                  # info | warning | error
require_calibration = true         # false: --gate runs without a matching record
calibration_max_age_days = 90

[review.fix]
model = ""                         # must differ from the judge unless --allow-same-model
max_growth_percent = 25
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rubric` | `builtin:skill-quality` | Rubric to score against. |
| `content` | `descriptions` | What a judge receives. |
| `exclude` | `[]` | Items never reviewed (globs on name, id and path). |
| `max_cost_usd`, `max_calls` | `0.50`, `300` | Caps of a judged run. A repository value can only lower them. |
| `on_secret` | `withhold` | `withhold` or `redact` an item whose own text holds a credential. |
| `allowed_hosts` | `[]` (any, with a warning) | Hosts a judged run may send to. User config only; `AI_RULEZ_REVIEW_ALLOWED_HOSTS` overrides. |
| `gate.level` | `warning` | Lowest severity ceiling that gates. |
| `gate.require_calibration` | `true` | Refuse `--gate` without a matching calibration record. |
| `gate.calibration_max_age_days` | the rubric's `max_age_days` | Maximum age of the record. |
| `fix.model` | none | Fixer model. |
| `fix.max_growth_percent` | `25` | Most an item may grow in a fix. |

An invalid `[review]` table is an error. To price a model the built-in table does not know while a cost cap is set,
set `[llm] price_input_per_mtok` and `price_output_per_mtok` in user scope.

#### Output and exit codes

`--format text` (default), `json` ([`review-report.schema.json`](schema.md), `review-report/1`) or `sarif`.
`-o FILE` writes the report to a file. SARIF results use the dimension codes as rule ids, carry `advisory: true`,
`origin: "lint-twin"` or `"llm-judge"`, and the `aiRulezReviewFingerprint/v1` fingerprint. A judged run's JSON adds
`run` (calls, cache hits, tokens, cost, caps, `incomplete`, requested and resolved models, `hallucinated_evidence`),
`items[].semantic`, `findings`, `egress`, `calibration`, `gate`, `models` and `baseline`.

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Reviewed. Advisory findings never change it. |
| 1 | Could not run or was refused: a bad flag or config, an invalid rubric, no network opt-in or model, a host outside `allowed_hosts`, an estimate over a cap, `--gate` without a matching calibration, an incomplete run with `--gate`. |
| 2 | `--gate` failed; `calibrate` did not pass or drifted; `review fix` found no safe fix; `rubric lint` found problems. |

## Judge

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/judge/

`ai-rulez judge` audits agent configuration with language models and reports security, governance and quality
findings. It reads what a harness would read (skills with their scripts and references, agents, commands, rules,
`CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` files, MCP and settings files), whether or not ai-rulez generated it, and needs no
configuration file. Every finding must quote the file, a second model adjudicates what survives, and the scores and the
pass/fail decision are computed in code.

Use judge to find what deterministic checks cannot see: an instruction that tells an agent to hide a step from the
user, a skill whose scripts do more than its description says, a rule that contradicts the `CLAUDE.md` above it. For
the free, exact checks, use [`validate` and `scan`](strict-validation.md). For scoring skill descriptions dimension by
dimension against a rubric you calibrate, with an offline baseline and verified fixes, use [Review](review.md).

#### Example

See what would be sent, to whom, and what it would cost. `--estimate` sends nothing:

```console
$ ai-rulez judge .ai-rulez/skills/deploy-staging .ai-rulez/rules/atomic-commits.md --estimate
judge estimate (nothing was sent)
categories: security, governance, quality
model:      security    bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5
model:      governance  bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5
model:      quality     bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5
model:      adjudicator bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
egress:     (the provider's default endpoint)
  send  .ai-rulez/rules/atomic-commits.md (rule, 1 files)  +0 rules, 2 instruction files
  send  .ai-rulez/skills/deploy-staging (skill, 2 files)  +0 rules, 2 instruction files
units to send: 2, calls: 8, prompt tokens: ~45957, max completion tokens: 49152
worst-case cost: <= $0.7765 (expected ~$0.1519)
```

Then run it. `--allow-llm` is your consent to send the files to the model's provider:

```bash
ai-rulez judge --allow-llm                                   # everything below this directory
ai-rulez judge .claude/skills/deploy --allow-llm --fail-on security:medium,governance:high
ai-rulez judge --changed=origin/main --allow-llm --format sarif > judge.sarif
ai-rulez judge --allow-llm --model openai/gpt-4o --adjudicator-model openai/o3
```

Judge needs model access configured as described on [LLM access](llm.md). By default it uses Amazon Bedrock; pass
`--model provider/model` (or set `[llm]` in your user config) to use another provider.

#### How a review works

1. **Units.** The files become units: a skill is its directory, anything else is one file.
2. **Static facts.** `validate` and `scan` run over the units. Their findings reach the reviewers as numbered leads
   (at most 64 per unit). A lead is never a finding by itself: a reviewer has to confirm it in the text.
3. **Reviewers.** One call per category and unit: **security** (`JR-S01` to `JR-S15`), **governance** (`JR-G01` to
   `JR-G07`) and **quality** (`JR-Q01` to `JR-Q13`). Each reviewer must separate a threat (an active instruction,
   executable code, a capability grant) from context (a prohibition, documentation, an example, a fixture), and state
   the strongest innocent reading of every finding next to the reason it fails.
4. **Verifier.** Every finding carries a verbatim quote and a line range, checked in code against the text that was
   sent (whitespace-normalized). A finding that fails goes back to its reviewer once with the exact cited lines; if it
   still fails it is dropped and counted.
5. **Adjudicator.** A separate call sees the surviving findings with eight lines of context, the static facts, the
   conventions and a list of known false-positive shapes, and decides `keep`, `downgrade`, `drop` or `merge` for each.
6. **Scoring.** Code computes the scores, the unit status and the decision. A model never emits a score or verdict.

The adjudicator is asymmetric. A **security** finding is dropped only with a concrete benign context (a prohibition,
a documented example, a placeholder, a declared service, a static literal) and a counter-quote taken verbatim from the
file; otherwise it stays. **Quality** and **governance** findings are dropped unless they show a concrete defect or a
violated binding convention. Static findings such as hidden characters in an instruction file (`AR002`) bypass the
adjudicator. `--explain-drops` lists every dropped candidate with the stage, the reason and the counter-quote.

#### What it judges

With no paths, judge takes every unit below the working directory that a harness reads:

| Unit kind | Where |
| --- | --- |
| `skill` | a directory with a `SKILL.md`, with every file below it |
| `agent`, `command`, `rule` | `agents/`, `commands/`, `rules/` below a `.claude/`, `.agents/`, `.ai-rulez/`, `.cursor/` or `.github/` directory, at any depth |
| `claude-md`, `agents-md` | `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.local.md`, at any depth |
| `mcp-config` | `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json` |
| `settings` | `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json` |
| `plugin` | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `marketplace.json` |

Name files or directories to judge only those. Any Markdown or JSON file you name is a unit (kind `other` when no
convention applies), and a file inside a skill selects the whole skill. A file with the ai-rulez generated header is
skipped (`generated file: judge its sources`): judge the `.ai-rulez/` sources instead.

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Units per run | 200 (`--estimate` is not limited; name paths or use `--changed`) |
| File size | 2 MiB |
| Unit size | 40 files, 512 KiB |
| Input per call | 24,000 tokens of file text; a larger unit is split into chunks (at most eight per category) |

Judge needs a project: a git repository, or a directory with its own `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, `.agents/`
or ai-rulez configuration. It refuses to run in `$HOME` or `/`. Symlinks are never followed, and paths must stay
inside the project.

**Changed units.** `--changed=REV` judges only units changed since `REV` (committed, staged, unstaged and untracked);
a bare `--changed` compares with `HEAD`. Write the base with `=`: a separate word is a path to judge. `--since REV` is
the same as `--changed=REV`. With `--impact` (on by default) it also judges the units a changed rule or `CLAUDE.md`
applies to.

#### Governance and your conventions

The governance reviewer enforces only what is written down, and it is shown the conventions that apply to each unit:

- **Path-scoped rules.** For every ancestor directory `D` of a unit's file, the Markdown files below `D/.claude/rules/`.
  A rule with a `paths:` list attaches when one of its globs (relative to `D`; `**`, `*`, `?`, `[abc]`, `{a,b}`)
  matches a file of the unit or a path the unit mentions. A rule without `paths:` always attaches.
- **Instruction files.** `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/CLAUDE.md` of every ancestor
  directory, root first and nearest last, with the files they `@import` (five levels deep). A nearer file overrides a
  farther one on the same topic.
- **Binding versus guidance.** `MUST`, `NEVER`, `ALWAYS`, "required" and "forbidden" are binding; `SHOULD`, "prefer"
  and "recommended" are guidance, and a deviation from guidance is at most `low`.
- **Two quotes.** A governance finding quotes both the file and the convention it violates, or it is dropped.

`--attach-rules=false` and `--attach-claude-md=false` (or `attach_rules`, `attach_claude_md` in `[judge]`) turn the
two kinds off. `--estimate` lists what is attached to every unit.

#### Rubric skills

A skill whose body has `## C1 - title` sections is a rubric: each section is a checkable criterion.

```markdown
---
name: acme-skill-standards
description: Acme rubric for skill files.
---

## C1 - Trigger in the description
The `description` contains "Use when" followed by a concrete situation.

## C2 - Verify section
The body has a `## Verify` heading followed by a command or an observable check.
```

```bash
ai-rulez judge --allow-llm --skill acme-skill-standards               # governance review
ai-rulez judge --allow-llm --skill-for quality=path:rubrics/style      # another category
```

The reviewer must report every criterion as `pass`, `fail` or `not_applicable`. A failed criterion becomes a `JR-G06`
finding with the criterion id (`rubric:acme-skill-standards/C1`). A criterion nobody reported is `not_evaluated`,
never a silent pass. When a failure is an absence (no `## Verify` heading) the finding is raised for the unit as a
whole, without a quote.

#### Trust tiers

What reaches a model is split into tiers by marker lines that carry a per-request token, which the author of a
reviewed file cannot predict.

| Tier | Content | Authority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| T0 | the built-in system prompt and output schema | cannot be changed |
| T1 | rubric text and prompt extensions you configured: a `path:DIR` skill, a pinned skill, a prompt file | adds checks; can never relax the evidence rules, change the schema or name a verdict |
| T2 | repository conventions, static facts, unpinned or inline skills | reference data, never obeyed |
| T3 | the files under review | inert data; text that addresses a "reviewer" or "AI", claims to be approved, or asks for a score is itself a finding (`JR-S01`) |

A repository decides neither where content goes nor what a run may spend. A repository `[judge]` or `[llm]` table
cannot set the models, provider, base URL, consent, key variable or spend caps: they come from flags, the environment
and your user config file, and a repository value is ignored and reported in the run's notices. A rubric skill from the
project is T2 unless `[judge.skills.pins]` pins its hash and the hash matches.

#### Scores, gating and exit codes

Per category: `100 - sum(points x confidence weight x decay)`. Points are 40 critical, 20 high, 8 medium, 3 low;
confidence weights are 1.0 high, 0.6 medium, 0.3 low; the largest deductions are weighted 1, 0.5 and 0.25, and a fourth
adds nothing. A category that did not run is `null`, not 100.

`--categories` limits the run to some of `security`, `quality` and `governance` (default all; `[judge] categories`).

`--fail-on` takes a comma-separated list of `category:severity`, `category:none`, `score:N` (any category below N) or
`category:score:N`. The default is `security:high,governance:high,quality:none`: quality findings are advice unless you
say otherwise. A category the list does not name keeps its default. `--min-confidence` drops findings below a
confidence.

A unit is `fail` (a `--fail-on` rule is met), `partial` (not fully reviewed), `warn` (findings below the gate), `pass`,
`withheld_secret`, `skipped` or `error`. The run decision is `fail`, `incomplete` or `pass`.

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Every unit passed or warned. For `--estimate`: the estimate is within `--max-cost`. |
| `1` | The run could not complete: the provider refused, a cap was reached, a model failed, nothing was left to judge, or a unit was only partly reviewed (`--allow-partial` accepts that). For `--estimate`: the estimate exceeds `--max-cost`. |
| `2` | A unit met `--fail-on`, or a unit was withheld because it holds a secret. |

##### Coverage and secrets

Nothing is left out silently. Files that were not sent (binary, unreadable, over a limit), chunks beyond the limit,
calls the caps prevented, a provider refusal (retried once) and replies that were never valid make the unit `partial`
and the run `incomplete`; the report lists what was not reviewed and why.

A unit holding a credential that the security scan (`AR001`) recognizes is withheld whole and reported with
`file:line` and the pattern, never the secret. `--redact` masks the text and sends it instead. Rubrics, prompt files and
trap text are redacted too.

#### Models and providers

| Role | Default |
| --- | --- |
| reviewers (security, quality, governance) | `bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| adjudicator | `bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5` |

Override them with `--model` (all reviewers; the adjudicator follows unless named), `--adjudicator-model`,
`--model-for ROLE=MODEL` (`security`, `quality`, `governance` or `adjudicator`), `AI_RULEZ_LLM_MODEL`, the `[llm]`
table of your user config, or `[judge.models]` there. All roles use one provider and one credential. `--provider` sets
the prefix for a bare `--model`. Use the strongest model you have for the adjudicator.

Every call requests JSON against a schema limited to what all providers accept, and the reply is validated strictly in
code. Each call gets 6,144 completion tokens, which thinking models also spend. For a model the price table does not
know, pass `--price-input` and `--price-output` (USD per million tokens). Provider setup, Bedrock credentials and
gateways are on [LLM access](llm.md#amazon-bedrock).

#### Cost, caps and the cache

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--estimate`, `-n`, `--dry-run` | off | Build and price every request without calling anything. |
| `--max-cost` | `2` | Spend cap in USD; `0` removes it. With a cap, every model must be priced. |
| `--max-tokens` | `0` (none) | Cap on prompt plus completion tokens. |
| `--max-calls` | `0` (none) | Cap on model calls. |
| `--concurrency` | `4` | Calls in flight. |
| `--rpm` | `0` (none) | Calls started per minute. |
| `--no-cache` | off | Neither read nor write the response cache. |
| `--cache-readonly` | off | Serve cached answers, store none. |

Caps come from flags and your user config, never from a repository. Calls are admitted in priority order (security,
then governance, then quality) until the expected cost reaches a cap; the worst case of each call is enforced as a hard
stop. What does not fit is reported, and the run is `incomplete`. The estimate counts tokens at 3 bytes per token and
leaves out repair calls, so a run that repairs many quotes costs more than estimated.

Answers are cached in your user cache directory, keyed by everything in the request (prompt version, model, schema,
rubric text, attached conventions, unit content, static facts). Only validated replies are stored, entries expire after
30 days, and the cache is authenticated with a per-user secret.

#### Configuration

Everything works without configuration. The repository's `[judge]` table records what a team agrees on:

```toml
[judge]
categories       = ["security", "quality", "governance"]
fail_on          = ["security:high", "governance:high", "quality:none"]
min_confidence   = "low"
attach_rules     = true
attach_claude_md = true
traps_file       = ".ai-rulez/judge/traps.yaml"      # known false-positive shapes for the adjudicator

[judge.skills]
load = ["acme-skill-standards"]                       # rubric skills for the governance review
[judge.skills.for]
quality = ["style-rubric"]
[judge.skills.pins]
acme-skill-standards = "3f9c1e0a"                     # a matching hash makes the skill configured text (T1)

[judge.prompts.security]
mode = "extend"                                       # or "override": needs --allow-prompt-override
file = ".ai-rulez/judge/security.md"

[[judge.suppress]]
code    = "JR-S05"
path    = ".claude/skills/setup/SKILL.md"
quote   = "curl -fsSL https://tools.acme.example/install.sh | sh"
reason  = "sanctioned installer, tracked in SEC-1234"
expires = "2026-12-31"
```

- **Prompts.** `extend` adds your text to a reviewer's instructions. `override` replaces the category's role prompt;
  the shared core (trust tiers, evidence rules) and the schema stay. An override from a repository file applies only
  with `--allow-prompt-override`, or `allow_prompt_override = true` in your user config.
- **Traps** add known false-positive shapes for the adjudicator:

  ```yaml
  - id: R01
    name: internal_cli_download
    text: "`acli` downloads pinned tool bundles from artifactory.acme.example; that is the sanctioned installer."
    applies_to: [JR-S05, JR-S10]
  ```

- **Suppressions** are pinned to the quote (changed text brings the finding back), need a reason, and expire at most
  366 days ahead. An expired suppression is reported and no longer applies. Suppressed findings stay in the report
  under `suppressed`.
- **User scope only** (`~/.config/ai-rulez/config.toml`): `[judge.models]` (`security`, `quality`, `governance`,
  `adjudicator` or `reviewers`), `max_cost_usd`, `max_tokens`, `max_calls`, `concurrency`, `rpm`, `allow_llm` and
  `allow_prompt_override`.

`validate` reports `model`, `provider` and `base_url` in a repository `[judge]` table as unknown keys; judge names
where to set them instead.

#### Output

`--format text` (default), `json` or `sarif`.

**JSON** follows [`schema/judge-report.schema.json`](https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/blob/main/schema/judge-report.schema.json)
(`schema_version` 2): the run (prompt version, models, egress hosts, gate, cost, coverage), one entry per unit (status,
scores, attached conventions, rubric results, gaps, findings) and the summary. A finding has a stable `id`, `code`,
`severity`, `confidence`, `verdict` (`confirmed` or `contextual_risk`), `location`, `quote`, `chain`,
`benign_reading`, `why_not_benign`, the `convention` it rests on, `suggested_fix`, its `origin` (`reviewer`,
`adjudicator` or `static-only`) and a `fingerprint`. It never contains file text beyond the quotes, and never the
prompts.

**SARIF** maps `ai-rulez/JR-xxx` to rules: critical and high are `error`, medium `warning`, low and info `note`, with
`security-severity` 9.5, 8.0, 5.5, 3.0 and 1.0. Chains become `codeFlows`, the convention a related location, and
`partialFingerprints` carry the fingerprint. Coverage gaps are tool execution notifications, and an incomplete run has
`executionSuccessful: false`.

Finding text is model output: treat it as untrusted in your own tooling.

#### MCP

The `judge` tool of `ai-rulez mcp` runs the same engine for an agent; `mcp --read-only` does not register it. It takes
the review inputs (paths, categories, `fail_on`, `min_confidence`, `changed`, `since`, `impact`, the attach switches,
`skills` and `skill_for` as a `name`, a project `path` or `inline_markdown`, `explain_drops`, `allow_partial`,
`estimate`, `redact`) and no model, provider, price or spend cap. A real run needs `allow_llm: true` in the call and
`allow_llm = true` in the `[judge]` table of your user config; `estimate: true` always works and sends nothing.

#### What is sent

File content up to the limits above, and for governance the attached conventions, goes to the model's provider.
Nothing else does: no keys, environment or configuration. The egress host is printed first. Under an organization
[policy](policy.md) that forbids model use, only `--estimate` runs. The `--policy*` flags and `--discover-org` load
and verify such a policy for the run; see [Policy](policy.md).

#### Measured accuracy

Judge ships with a labeled synthetic corpus in
[`bench/judge/`](https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/tree/main/bench/judge) (malicious units for every security
code, benign lookalikes, false-positive traps, quality defects, a governance fixture with nested rules). On a 67-unit
subset with the default models, at about $0.075 per unit:

| Category | Precision | Recall | F1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| security | 1.00 | 0.85 | 0.92 |
| governance | 1.00 | 0.86 | 0.92 |
| quality | 0.89 | 0.89 | 0.89 |

The corpus is small and synthetic: read the numbers as a baseline, not a field measurement. Some malicious samples are
declined by the provider's content filter; judge reports such units as partly reviewed, never as a pass.

## LLM access

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/llm/

The `[llm]` table configures the one model connection every model-backed ai-rulez feature shares: the provider and
model, the spend caps, the response cache and the privacy rules. Nothing calls a model unless you turn it on:
`allow_network` defaults to `false`, and every call is refused with a message that names the setting.

These features use it:

| Feature | What it sends |
| --- | --- |
| [`judge`](judge.md) | the agent configuration files it reviews, plus the rules and instruction files that apply to them |
| [`review --semantic`](review.md), `review calibrate`, `review fix` | skill, agent and command descriptions (and bodies with `--content full`) |
| [`eval run --grader builtin`](evals.md#the-built-in-grader) | the rubric and the transcript an eval runner returned |
| [`improve --with builtin:review-fix`](improve.md#bundled-adapters) | the `SKILL.md` being improved |
| LLM-backed [`[[verifiers]]`](verifiers.md) and `verifiers suggest` | the verifier's prompt and inputs |
| [`search`](search.md) embeddings | skill text, with `embedding_model` set |
| `llm doctor --ping` | a one-token `ping` |

#### Example

Opt in once in your **user** config file (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ai-rulez/config.toml`, else
`~/.config/ai-rulez/config.toml`):

```toml
# ~/.config/ai-rulez/config.toml
[llm]
provider      = "anthropic"
model         = "claude-haiku-4-5"
api_key_env   = "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"   # the NAME of the variable, never the key
allow_network = true
max_cost_usd  = 1.00
```

Check what ai-rulez would use, and what a prompt costs, without calling anything:

```console
$ ai-rulez llm doctor
liter-llm:       v2.4.4
model:           anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5
embedding model: (none)
base_url host:   (provider default)
api key env:     ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (set: true)
network allowed: true
cache:           /home/dev/.cache/ai-rulez/llm/0b2e76eb32b753f0
limits:          max_cost_usd=1 max_tokens=0 max_calls=0 (0 = unlimited)

$ ai-rulez llm estimate .ai-rulez/skills/deploy-staging/SKILL.md
model:         anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5
file bytes:    277
prompt tokens: ~100
max output:    1024
worst-case cost: <= $0.005220
(approximate; nothing was sent)
```

`ai-rulez llm doctor --ping` makes one 1-token call to confirm the key and endpoint work.

#### Providers

ai-rulez reaches models through [liter-llm](https://github.com/xberg-io/liter-llm), which routes on a
`provider/model` name. Set `provider` and a bare `model`, or put the prefix in `model` (`openai/gpt-4o-mini`).

| Provider | `provider` | Example model | Credentials |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI | `openai` | `gpt-4o-mini` | `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or the variable `api_key_env` names |
| Anthropic | `anthropic` | `claude-haiku-4-5` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or `api_key_env` |
| Google Gemini | `gemini` | `gemini-2.5-flash` | `GEMINI_API_KEY`, or `api_key_env` |
| Google Vertex AI | `vertex_ai` | `gemini-2.5-flash` | the provider's credentials, or `api_key_env` |
| Amazon Bedrock | `bedrock` | `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5` | the AWS credential chain, see [Amazon Bedrock](#amazon-bedrock) |
| OpenAI-compatible gateway (LiteLLM proxy, vLLM, Ollama, Azure OpenAI or Bedrock gateways) | `openai`, or the gateway's provider | the gateway's model name | `api_key_env` for the gateway credential, with `base_url` |

liter-llm supports further providers under their own prefixes; the ones above are the supported providers.
With a `base_url`, a named provider keeps its own wire format, so a Gemini or Vertex model behind a gateway still
speaks the Gemini protocol.

When no `api_key_env` is set, the provider's own key variable is read.

#### Configuration

```toml
[llm]
provider        = "openai"
model           = "gpt-4o-mini"
embedding_model = "text-embedding-3-small"
max_cost_usd    = 2.00
max_tokens      = 500000
max_calls       = 200
cache           = true

# User scope only (see "Trust rule"):
allow_network   = false
base_url        = "https://llm-gateway.acme.example/v1"
api_key_env     = "OPENAI_API_KEY"
```

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | string | none | Provider prefix for `provider/model` routing. |
| `model` | string | none | Chat model, bare or with a `provider/` prefix. |
| `embedding_model` | string | none | Embedding model for search. |
| `allow_network` | bool | `false` | Allow any provider call. User scope only. |
| `base_url` | string | the provider's endpoint | Gateway or model-server URL. No credentials or query string. User scope only. |
| `api_key_env` | string | the provider's variable | Name of the environment variable that holds the key. User scope only. |
| `max_cost_usd` | float | `0` (unlimited) | Stop before the worst-case estimate would exceed this. |
| `max_tokens` | int | `0` (unlimited) | Prompt plus completion tokens for the whole run. |
| `max_calls` | int | `0` (unlimited) | Provider calls for the whole run. |
| `cache` | bool | `true` | Use the response cache. |
| `timeout_seconds` | int | `60` | Time limit per call including retries; at most 3600. |
| `max_retries` | int | `3` | Retries of transient failures; `-1` disables, at most 10. |
| `price_input_per_mtok`, `price_output_per_mtok` | float | built-in price table | USD per million tokens for the model you set in user scope. Needed for a cost cap on a model the table does not know. User scope only. |
| `allow_plain_http`, `plain_http_hosts` | bool, list | `false`, `[]` | Send a key over plain http to the listed hosts; see [Plain-http gateways](#plain-http-gateways). User scope only. |

Individual commands add their own caps on top (`judge --max-cost`, `review --max-cost`, `eval run --grader-max-cost`).
Whichever limit is reached first stops the run.

##### Environment variables

Precedence, highest first: environment, user config file, repository config, defaults. An unparsable value is an
`AR9L0` error, not a silent default.

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `AI_RULEZ_LLM_PROVIDER`, `_MODEL`, `_EMBEDDING_MODEL` | Routing and models. |
| `AI_RULEZ_LLM_ALLOW_NETWORK`, `_BASE_URL`, `_API_KEY_ENV` | The user-scope keys of the same name. |
| `AI_RULEZ_LLM_MAX_COST_USD`, `_MAX_TOKENS`, `_MAX_CALLS`, `_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `_CACHE` | Limits and cache. |
| `AI_RULEZ_LLM_ALLOW_PLAIN_HTTP`, `_PLAIN_HTTP_HOSTS` | Plain-http opt-in; hosts comma-separated. |
| `AI_RULEZ_LLM_PRICE_INPUT_PER_MTOK`, `_PRICE_OUTPUT_PER_MTOK` | Price override for the model named by `AI_RULEZ_LLM_MODEL`. |
| `AI_RULEZ_LLM_TEMPERATURE=omit` | Leave `temperature` out of every request, for a model that rejects it. Environment only. |

The [GitHub Action](github-actions.md) accepts matching `llm-*` inputs. Keep credentials in the job's environment.

##### Trust rule

A committed repository config is input from whoever wrote it: cloning a repository must not switch on network use,
choose the host a prompt goes to, or pick which of your keys is sent.

| Key | Repository config and `config.local.*` | User config file and `AI_RULEZ_LLM_*` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `allow_network`, `base_url`, `api_key_env`, `allow_plain_http`, `plain_http_hosts`, `price_input_per_mtok`, `price_output_per_mtok` | ignored, reported by `llm doctor`, `ai-rulez doctor` and `AR9L1` | honored |
| `provider`, `model`, `embedding_model`, `cache`, `timeout_seconds`, `max_retries` | honored, except for provider routing (below) | honored |
| `max_cost_usd`, `max_tokens`, `max_calls` | can only tighten: the lower non-zero value wins | honored |

The local overlay lives in the checkout, so it counts as repository scope.

```console
$ ai-rulez llm doctor
...
warning:         repository [llm] keys ignored (user scope only: set them in the user config file ~/.config/ai-rulez/config.toml or via AI_RULEZ_LLM_*): base_url
```

**Provider routing and the key.** The provider decides which service receives the request, and with it your key. When
the provider (or a `provider/` prefix in `model` or `embedding_model`) comes only from the repository config, ai-rulez
refuses to send a key (`AR9L0`), whether the key comes from `api_key_env` or from the provider's own variable. Set
`provider` and `model` in the user config file, or with `AI_RULEZ_LLM_PROVIDER` and `AI_RULEZ_LLM_MODEL`. A repository
`model` whose prefix matches the provider you set is fine. A per-request model (a verifier's `llm.model`, a search
embedding model) is held to the same rule: a bare name is pinned to your provider, and a prefix that names another
provider is refused before anything is sent.

See the [trust model](trust-model.md) for every setting that reaches the network or runs a process.

##### Plain-http gateways

By default a key is never sent over plain http except to a loopback host (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`). For a
private gateway that only speaks http, opt in from user scope and list the host exactly as it appears in `base_url`:

```toml
# ~/.config/ai-rulez/config.toml
[llm]
base_url         = "http://gateway.internal:8080/v1"
api_key_env      = "GATEWAY_KEY"
allow_plain_http = true
plain_http_hosts = ["gateway.internal:8080"]
```

The match is exact and case-insensitive on `host` or `host:port`: `gateway.internal` does not cover
`gateway.internal:8080`. `llm doctor` warns while the opt-in is in use. The key and every prompt cross that network
unencrypted, so prefer https, or a loopback tunnel (`ssh -L 8080:gateway.internal:8080`, then
`base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1"`, which needs no opt-in).

#### What happens on every call

- **Budget, fail closed.** Before each call, the worst case (estimated prompt plus completion cap) is reserved against
  `max_cost_usd`, `max_tokens` and `max_calls`; a call that does not fit is refused. Afterwards the reservation is
  replaced by the reported usage. Tokens are estimated at one per three UTF-8 bytes, deliberately high. Thinking tokens
  count as completion. A rejection the provider does not bill (400, 401, 403, 404, 422) releases its cost; a 429, 5xx,
  timeout or transport failure keeps the worst case charged, since it may have run upstream. With `max_cost_usd` set,
  a model with no known price is refused.
- **Prices** come from liter-llm's model catalog plus a few fixed entries (the `haiku`, `sonnet` and `opus` short names
  eval cases use, and the Claude families). A Bedrock id is reduced to the model it names before the lookup. Set
  `price_input_per_mtok` and `price_output_per_mtok` for any other model. Reported costs are estimates, not a bill.
- **Cache.** Answers are cached in `~/.cache/ai-rulez/llm/<project hash>/`, outside the repository, keyed by the
  endpoint (provider, base URL, key variable name, never its value), the model, the request and the feature's prompt
  version. Every entry is authenticated with a per-user secret (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ai-rulez/llm-cache.key`, mode 0600):
  a modified or planted entry is discarded, and a cache restored from another machine simply misses. A cache hit costs
  nothing. Turn it off with `cache = false` or `AI_RULEZ_LLM_CACHE=0`.
- **Retry.** 429, 500, 502, 503, 504, 529 and transport failures are retried up to `max_retries` times with jittered
  backoff, honoring `Retry-After`. Authentication, context-length and other 4xx errors are not retried.
- **Redaction.** Logs and estimates carry counts, sizes, hashes and cost, never prompt or completion text and never
  keys. Provider error text has the configured key and key-shaped tokens masked, and URLs lose their query string.
- **Temperature** is left out for models that reject it (Claude 5.x, OpenAI reasoning models), and a request rejected
  for its temperature is retried once without it.

##### Cost controls

Set `max_cost_usd`, `max_tokens` and `max_calls` for any feature that loops, and run the feature's estimate first:
`judge --estimate`, `review --estimate`, `eval run --dry-run`, or `ai-rulez llm estimate <file>` for a single prompt
(`--max-output N` sets the completion tokens to assume; default 1024). Use `--format json` on `llm` commands for
machine-readable output.

#### Data egress and residency

With `allow_network` on, each feature sends the text listed in the table at the top of this page to the configured
endpoint, and nothing else: no config files, keys or environment. `judge` prints the egress host and models before it
sends anything, and only runs with `--allow-llm`. An eval grader sends a transcript of an agent session, which can
contain source code, file paths, tool output and anything a user typed.

To keep data inside your network, point `base_url` at a gateway you run (a LiteLLM proxy, a Bedrock or Azure OpenAI
gateway in your VPC, vLLM or Ollama on an internal host) and use `api_key_env` for its credential. `llm doctor` shows
the host so a reviewer can check it. HTTP redirects are refused, never followed, so a prompt is never re-sent to
another host. A key is sent only to the configured host and only over https, except to a loopback host or a listed
plain-http host.

Retention and training terms are the provider's; check them before sending transcripts that contain private code.

##### Amazon Bedrock

A `bedrock/...` model is signed with AWS credentials from the AWS SDK's default chain: environment variables,
`AWS_PROFILE` and the shared config (SSO and assume-role profiles included), web identity
(`AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE`), and container and instance roles. A Bedrock API key (`AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`) or a
key pair in the environment is used as is. Temporary credentials are renewed before they expire, and a call refused as
unauthenticated renews them and is tried once more, so a long run does not fail halfway.

The region comes from `AWS_REGION`, `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` or the profile, and the egress host is
`bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com`. Inference-profile ids (`global.anthropic.claude-...`, `us.`, `eu.`, ...) are
priced.

```bash
export AWS_PROFILE=acme-dev AWS_REGION=eu-north-1
export AI_RULEZ_LLM_ALLOW_NETWORK=1
ai-rulez judge --allow-llm --estimate      # Bedrock is judge's default provider
```

#### Validation: AR9L0 and AR9L1

| Code | Name | Severity | Finds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AR9L0` | `llm-config-invalid` | error | A literal secret where a variable name belongs (`api_key = ...`, or a key-shaped `api_key_env` such as `sk-proj-...`); credentials or a query in `base_url`; plain `http://` to a non-loopback host when a key is sent; `allow_plain_http` without `plain_http_hosts`; `max_retries` above 10; `timeout_seconds` above 3600; negative or non-finite limits and prices; provider routing chosen by the repository. |
| `AR9L1` | `llm-untrusted-key` | warning | A repository `[llm]` table (or its local overlay) sets a key only user scope honors. |

`validate`, the JSON schema, `llm doctor` and `ai-rulez doctor` report them. A message never repeats the offending
value.

```console
$ ai-rulez validate
.ai-rulez/config.toml:12: warning AR9L1 llm-untrusted-key: llm: repository [llm] keys ignored (user scope only: ...): base_url
```

#### Commands

| Command | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ai-rulez llm doctor [--ping]` | Print the liter-llm version, model, `base_url` host (never the key), whether the key variable is set, the network gate, cache directory and limits. `--ping` makes one 1-token call and needs `allow_network`. Needs a project configuration. Also a section of `ai-rulez doctor`. |
| `ai-rulez llm estimate <file> [--max-output N]` | Approximate tokens and worst-case cost of sending the file as a prompt. No call. Works with only the user configuration. |

## Performance

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/performance/

What the common ai-rulez operations cost on a typical project, which settings change that, and how a slowdown in
ai-rulez itself is caught before release.

The numbers below come from the benchmarks in the repository on synthetic projects, measured on a 4-vCPU Intel Xeon
2.1 GHz virtual machine with a slow file system, so rows dominated by file writes (such as `generate`) are
likely faster on a local SSD. Compare rows with each other; your machine will differ in absolute terms.

#### At a glance

| Operation | Project | Time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `generate`, 2 presets | 200 content files | 243 ms (142 ms when nothing changed) |
| `generate`, 10 presets | 200 content files | 500 ms (213 ms when nothing changed) |
| `generate`, every built-in preset | 200 content files | 1.9 s (670 ms when nothing changed) |
| Strict lint of the content (`validate`) | 200 content files | 112 ms |
| Loading one installed skill | 1 / 100 / 2,000 files | 3 ms / 6 ms / 52 ms |
| Loading 200 installed skills | 10 files each | 0.84 s |
| MCP server start with skill discovery, cold | 20,000-file monorepo, 30 / 300 / 1,500 items | 65 ms / 291 ms / 1.2 s |
| Same, with a warm index cache | same | 23 ms / 54 ms / 106 ms |
| `find_skill` / `find_context` query | same | under 2 ms |

#### generate

`generate` spends its time rendering and writing outputs, about 30 ms per preset on the 200-file project. A run in
which nothing changed costs roughly a third to a half as much.

- List only the presets your team uses in `presets`; each one adds rendering and writes.
- Use `generate --check` in CI to compare the committed outputs with the sources without writing.

#### validate and lint

The strict lint of a 200-file project takes about a tenth of a second. On large projects, report only what changed:

```bash
ai-rulez validate --changed            # against HEAD
ai-rulez validate --changed=origin/main
```

An external scanner (`[[lint.external]]`) is cached by a digest of the files it scans. With a warm cache, preparing
the scan costs about 1.7 ms for 50 skills and 17 ms for 500, and grows linearly.

#### Installed skills

Installing or serving a skill reads its whole directory, honoring the bundle's excludes and the work tree's
`.gitignore`. That costs about 3 ms per skill plus 25 microseconds per file. A skill at the 2,000-file limit takes
about 50 ms; a catalog of 200 installed skills of 10 files each takes under a second.

#### MCP server with skill discovery

With `mcp --serve-skills --discover-skills` (or `[mcp] discover_skills`), the server indexes the skills, instruction
files, rules, agents and commands of the whole repository at start-up and security-scans every item before serving it.

Cold start (no index cache), 20,000 files:

| Scopes | Items | Catalog build | Memory allocated |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10 | 30 | 65 ms | 22 MB |
| 100 | 300 | 291 ms | 59 MB |
| 500 | 1,500 | 1.2 s | 221 MB |

The security scan is most of that. The [index cache](mcp-server.md#the-index-cache) (`[mcp] index_cache`, on by
default with `"user"`) stores summaries and scan verdicts, so a later start rereads only changed items:

| Scopes | Items | No cache | Cold (fills the cache) | Warm | Warm vs no cache |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10 | 30 | 49 ms | 58 ms | 23 ms | -54% |
| 100 | 300 | 317 ms | 292 ms | 54 ms | -83% |
| 500 | 1,500 | 1.25 s | 1.45 s | 106 ms | -92% |

Keep the cache on. Setting `index_cache = "off"` makes every start pay the cold cost, and the live refresh of the
index pays the warm cost per change.

Queries on a running server, 20,000 files:

| Query | 10 scopes | 100 scopes | 500 scopes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `find_skill` with a task | 0.59 ms | 0.76 ms | 1.71 ms |
| `find_skill` with a task and a path | 0.51 ms | 0.71 ms | 1.73 ms |
| `find_context` with a path | 0.51 ms | 0.54 ms | 0.46 ms |
| `find_context` with a task and a path | 0.33 ms | 0.34 ms | 0.32 ms |

`find_skill` ranks the whole served catalog (at most 500 discovered skills), so it grows with the number of skills;
`find_context` ranks only the scopes that apply to the path.

##### Repository index

The index build alone (without the security scan) is fast even on large monorepos. Cold build in milliseconds, by files
and scopes; `git` lists files with `git ls-files`, `walk` is the fallback outside a git repository:

| Files | Scopes | Items | git | walk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1,000 | 100 | 300 | 25 | 23 |
| 5,000 | 100 | 300 | 47 | 51 |
| 5,000 | 500 | 1,500 | 78 | 90 |
| 20,000 | 100 | 300 | 51 | 89 |
| 20,000 | 500 | 1,500 | 129 | 202 |

Listing grows with the number of files (about 36 ms for `git ls-files` on 20,000 files); reading items costs about 20
to 35 microseconds each.

#### Model-backed commands

`judge`, `review --semantic`, `eval run` and `improve` are bound by the model provider, not by ai-rulez. Their cost and
duration are dominated by the number of model calls:

- Run the estimate first: `judge --estimate`, `review --estimate`, `eval run --dry-run`, `improve run --dry-run`.
- Use `--changed` (`judge`), `--since` (`review`) or `--changed-only` (`eval run`) to limit the run to what changed.
- Responses are cached per user ([LLM access](llm.md)); an unchanged project costs nothing on a re-run.
- `judge --concurrency` (default 4) and `--rpm` trade speed against provider rate limits.

#### Running the benchmarks

```bash
mise run test:benchmark          # every benchmark, small and medium synthetic projects
mise run test:benchmark:large    # adds the 2,000-file project and 20,000-file monorepos
go test ./internal/lint -run '^$' -bench RunFull -benchmem
```

Benchmarks build synthetic projects in a temporary directory and make no network calls.

#### Regression tracking

CI compares benchmarks against each change's base revision; see the [maintainer notes](maintainers/benchmarks.md).

## Architecture

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/architecture/

How ai-rulez turns a source tree into the native files of 52 assistants, and where each step lives in the code. This
page is for contributors and for anyone embedding the engine; for what each option does, see
[Configuration](configuration.md).

#### Repository layout

| Path | Contents |
| ---- | -------- |
| `cmd/ai-rulez` | The `main` package of the CLI |
| `cmd/commands` | The Cobra command tree: flags, output rendering and exit codes for every command |
| `internal/` | The engine; no compatibility promise ([package map](#package-map)) |
| `pkg/airulez` | The public Go API ([Embedding](embedding.md)) |
| `schema/` | JSON schemas of the configuration and of every `--format json` report |
| `tests/` | Golden, end-to-end, integration, conformance and architecture tests |
| `docs/` | This documentation; `docs/cli-reference.md` and `docs/llms*.txt` are generated |

#### The pipeline

Every command that reads a project goes through the same stages:

```text
load  ->  merge  ->  validate  ->  render  ->  write
```

| Stage | What happens | Code |
| ----- | ------------ | ---- |
| **Load** | Find the configuration, read it through a `workspace` view, scan the content tree and fetch what it references. | `internal/project`, `internal/config`, `internal/workspace` |
| **Merge** | Layer `config.<name>.toml` files and the machine-local `config.local.toml` over the base file, fold in `plugins/` and `marketplaces/` definition files, and resolve includes, installed skills, installed plugins and builtin packs. | `internal/config`, `internal/includes`, `internal/skillsource`, `internal/pluginresolve`, `internal/builtins` |
| **Validate** | Reject an invalid configuration (unknown or conflicting keys, a profile that names nothing) and apply the [organization policy](policy.md) before anything is rendered. `validate` adds the content checks. | `Config.Validate`, `internal/policy`, `internal/lint` |
| **Render** | Resolve the profile (or `--role`), collect MCP servers and render every preset into a plan: the files to write, merge into or remove, each with a digest. Nothing is written yet. | `internal/generator` |
| **Write** | Apply the plan: write outputs, merge settings documents, remove stale files, and update the manifest, the lock and the managed `.gitignore` block. | `internal/generator` (appliers) |

`internal/config` cannot import the packages that implement includes, installed skills, the `.agents` source or the
presets, because they import it. `internal/project` wires them into one set of resolvers; the CLI, the MCP server and
`pkg/airulez` all load a project through it.

##### Plan and apply

`generate` is `Plan` followed by `Apply` with an applier. Every mode uses the same plan, so they cannot disagree
about what a run would do:

| Applier | Used by | Effect |
| ------- | ------- | ------ |
| disk | `generate` | Writes the plan |
| dry run | `generate --dry-run` | Lists what the disk applier would do |
| check | `generate --check` | Compares the plan with the disk and the managed `.gitignore` block; writes nothing; exits 2 on drift |
| describe | `generate --emit-plan`, `pkg/airulez` | Reports the plan as a JSON document ([`schema/plan.schema.json`](https://github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/blob/main/schema/plan.schema.json)) |

Two presets that write the same path must render identical bytes, or the plan fails and names both. Settings files such
as `.claude/settings.json`, `opencode.json` and `.codex/config.toml` are merged document by document: ai-rulez owns the
keys it writes and keeps everything else, comments included.

##### Presets

Presets are registered in `internal/generator/registry`; nothing registers itself from an `init()`.

| Kind | Where | Presets |
| ---- | ----- | ------- |
| Declarative provider specs | `internal/generator/providers/builtin/*.toml` | 42 harnesses, plus the shared `mcp` spec for `.mcp.json` |
| Go presets | `internal/generator/presets` | `antigravity`, `baz`, `cline`, `codex`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `devin`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `xum` |
| Output presets (not harnesses) | `internal/generator/presets` | `llms-txt`, `okf` |
| Custom presets | `config.toml` | Markdown, directory or JSON outputs, or a user-supplied provider spec ([Custom presets](profiles.md)) |

`tests/golden` records the output of every built-in preset. See [Supported harnesses](harnesses.md).

#### Source layouts

The load stage reads four layouts. Everything after it works on the same content tree.

| Layout | Selected by | Content lives in | `generate` writes |
| ------ | ----------- | ---------------- | ----------------- |
| `.ai-rulez/` | `.ai-rulez/config.toml` or `.config/ai-rulez/config.toml` | `.ai-rulez/` (`rules/`, `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/`, `checks/`, `domains/`) | Every preset's files, including `AGENTS.md` |
| `.agents/` and `AGENTS.md` | `source = "agents"`, or a configuration at `.agents/ai-rulez.toml` | The root and nested `AGENTS.md` files and `.agents/` | Every preset's files **except** `AGENTS.md` and anything under `.agents/` |
| Root file only | `ai-rulez.toml` at the project root (`init --minimal`) | No content tree; only what the file declares (installed skills, MCP servers, hooks, permissions, lint settings) | Skills, MCP and settings files; never an instruction file ([Config without a .ai-rulez folder](config-without-folder.md)) |
| OKF bundle | `export okf`, `import okf`, `okf validate`, `format = "okf"` includes | Any [OKF](okf.md) bundle | The bundle, with `export okf` |

`internal/config` (`FindProjectRoot`) picks the layout in the order given in
[Configuration discovery](configuration.md#configuration-discovery).

**`.ai-rulez/` as OKF.** `.ai-rulez/` is itself an OKF bundle: `init`, `add` and the MCP tools write concepts with
`type`, `title` and `x-ai-rulez` frontmatter and refresh the `index.md` files. `internal/okfbridge` maps content to and
from a bundle and `internal/okf` reads and validates bundles. A tree without a root `index.md` is the pre-OKF layout;
it still loads with a deprecation notice, and `migrate okf` converts it.

**`.agents/` and `AGENTS.md`.** `internal/agentssource` completes the content scan under `.agents/`: it adds the root
`AGENTS.md` as the context item `agents` (or one item per `##` heading with `agents_md_split = true`), reads each nested
`AGENTS.md` as context scoped to its directory (`agents-<dir>`, glob `<dir>/**`), and drops files that carry the
generated header, so a project is never fed its own output. The nested walk honors `.gitignore`, skips symlinks and
dependency trees, and stops at a directory that is a project of its own. On output, the generator drops everything
that would land on `AGENTS.md` or under `.agents/` (also through a symlink). See [.agents as a source](agents-source.md).

#### Recursive runs

`generate --recursive`, `generate --check --recursive` and `validate --recursive` find every configuration root below
the working directory and process them concurrently, on at most `GOMAXPROCS` workers (`cmd/commands/roots.go`). The
result is deterministic:

- **Ordered output.** Roots finish in any order but are reported in path order, each as a `[n/N] path (elapsed)` line
  on stderr. The exit code does not depend on timing. `--quiet` and a structured `--format` silence the lines.
- **Per-root warnings.** Each root collects the log records its work produces (`internal/diag`,
  `cmd/commands/roots_notes.go`), and the run prints them with that root's result.

With `gitignore = true`, a recursive run writes one managed `.gitignore` block per git repository, at its top level,
holding the patterns of the roots inside it. See [Monorepo](monorepo.md).

#### The managed `.gitignore` block

With `gitignore = true` (or `generate --gitignore`), ai-rulez maintains a `# BEGIN ai-rulez` / `# END ai-rulez` block in
`.gitignore` that lists the generated files, the same on every machine, and edits nothing outside it. Outputs that only
a developer's local inputs create go to `.git/info/exclude`. The entries, probes and exclusions are described in
[`gitignore`](configuration.md#gitignore).

Code: `internal/gitignore` (the fenced block) and `internal/generator/gitignore*.go` (patterns, probes, the recursive
sink).

#### Plugins, marketplaces and Agent Plugins

`generate --plugin` is a second render over the same content tree. It builds distributable bundles instead of project
files:

1. **Definitions.** `[plugin]` bundles the whole root. `[[plugins_authoring]]` (or `[[marketplace.plugins]]`) defines
   several plugins, each selecting skills, commands, agents, domains, MCP servers and hooks by name or glob.
   `[[marketplaces_authoring]]` groups plugin definitions into marketplaces. Definitions can also live in
   `plugins/<name>.toml` and `marketplaces/<name>.toml`.
2. **Bundles.** For each plugin and runtime (`claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, `gemini`, `kimi`, `opencode`, `factory`,
   `hermes`, and the opt-in `pi`, `copilot` and `agent-plugins`), `internal/generator/plugin` writes the runtime's
   manifest and content under `<output_dir>/plugins/<name>/`, with provenance headers.
3. **Marketplace indexes.** One index per marketplace (`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, plus the Codex and Cursor
   indexes where a listed plugin targets them), each with a provenance sidecar.
4. **Verify.** `verify --plugin` regenerates in memory and reports drift per plugin and marketplace.
5. **Publish.** `publish` runs `validate --strict`, `lock --check`, `verify --plugin` and a secret scan, then writes a
   byte-reproducible archive, manifest, `SHA256SUMS` and release notes (`internal/publish`). `--to` with
   `--execute --yes` uploads to a GitHub release, npm or an OCI registry. Emitters turn the plugin into other formats:
   `agent-plugins` (`internal/agentplugins`), `ard` (`internal/ard`) and `mcp-server-card` (`internal/mcpcard`).

Emitters are pure functions of the manifest: no network, clock or file system. `internal/agentplugins` and
`internal/ard` do not import the config loader; callers map content to a model, which keeps their output deterministic
and testable against the vendored schemas in `tests/conformance`. See [Authoring plugins](plugins.md) and
[Publish](publish.md).

#### The lint pipeline

`validate` and `scan` run on the same engine, `internal/lint`; `scan` selects only the security analyzer.

```text
configuration or implicit root  ->  targets  ->  analyzers  ->  filters  ->  report  ->  exit code
```

1. **Configuration or implicit root.** With a configuration, the content tree is the subject. Without one, `validate`,
   `scan` and `doctor` use an implicit configuration (no presets, default `[lint]` settings, the repository top level as
   the root) and find content by convention: `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `SKILL.md`, `.claude/`, `.agents/`,
   `.cursor/rules`, plugin manifests, hook files and `.mcp.json`. `generate`, `clean` and `lock` still need a
   configuration.
2. **Targets.** `--path`, `--glob` and `[lint] paths` add files outside the content tree. A file is classified by its
   content (plugin manifest, marketplace, hook file, MCP file) or by its name and place (`SKILL.md`, `AGENTS.md`); a text
   file of no known kind gets the secret scan only.
3. **Outputs.** `--outputs` (or `[lint] lint_outputs`) also lints generated files. Only the analyzers that judge what a
   model reads (security, references, descriptions) run over them, and a problem the source already has is reported
   once.
4. **Analyzers.** `security`, `references`, `hooks`, `mcp`, `duplicates`, `descriptions`, `budgets`, `metadata`,
   `plugin`, `config`, `roles`, `lock`, `delivery`, `evals`, `okf`, `llmstxt`, `traps`, `convert`, `exposure`, `search`
   and `verifiers`; `--analyzer` runs a subset. Each finding has a stable `AR` code, a severity and a `file:line`.
5. **Filters.** `[lint.severity]`, `[lint.ignore]`, the baseline, and `--since` / `--changed`.
6. **Report and exit code.** Text, JSON, SARIF, GitHub annotations, JUnit or Markdown. Exit `0` valid, `1` invalid
   configuration or an unreadable named target, `2` findings at or above `--fail-on`.

`--recursive` repeats this per root and merges the findings. See [Strict validation](strict-validation.md).

#### Judge

`ai-rulez judge` is the lint-adjacent command that calls a model. It runs in any repository: models come from flags,
`AI_RULEZ_LLM_*` variables and the user config, never from the repository.

`cmd/commands/judge*.go` discovers the units (a skill directory, or a single agent, command, rule, instruction, MCP or
settings file), runs the `validate` analyzers over them for static facts, and reads the `[judge]` table.
`internal/judge` is the engine and does no I/O of its own: it attaches the rules that apply to each unit, builds the
prompts, plans the calls under the spending caps, verifies every quoted piece of evidence against the text that was
sent, asks the adjudicator, and computes scores and the decision in code. `internal/llm` is the single abstraction for
model calls. Nothing is sent without `--allow-llm`; `--estimate` shows the plan and cost without sending.
`bench/judge` is its evaluation. See [Judge](judge.md) and [Review](review.md).

Packages inside `internal/generator`:

| Package | Role |
| ------- | ---- |
| `presets` | The Go presets and custom presets |
| `providers` | The declarative provider specs and their loader |
| `registry` | Assembles the preset registry |
