#### `ai-rulez search`

Rank the served skills against a query, build the embedding index, or evaluate the ranking

```text
ai-rulez search <query> [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
ai-rulez search "customer wants money back"
ai-rulez search --mode hybrid --explain "customer wants money back"
ai-rulez search --format json --limit 10 deploy staging
ai-rulez search index --dry-run
ai-rulez search status
ai-rulez search --eval search-cases.yaml --min top1=0.6,mrr=0.7
ai-rulez search --eval search-cases.yaml --mode lexical,hybrid
ai-rulez search --from-evals --output result.json
ai-rulez search --eval search-cases.yaml --baseline result.json --max-flips 0
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `--allow` | string list |  | Only search skills whose name matches one of these glob patterns |
| `--allow-exec` | bool |  | Honor [search.embeddings] command from the repository config (it runs a program; the user config needs no flag) |
| `--baseline` | string |  | With --eval: a result file of an earlier run (--output) to compare against |
| `--deny` | string list |  | Never search skills whose name matches one of these glob patterns; wins over --allow |
| `--domain` | string list |  | Only search skills of these domains; 'root' selects skills in no domain |
| `--dry-run` / `-n` | bool |  | With 'search index': show the provider, the number of texts and bytes and an estimate; send nothing |
| `--eval` | string |  | Evaluate the ranking against the labeled queries of this YAML file instead of running a query |
| `--explain` | bool |  | Show each skill's rank in the lexical and vector lists and how the query was embedded |
| `--format` | string | `text` | Output format: text, json |
| `--from-evals` | bool |  | Evaluate with cases derived from the skills' eval-runner cases (alone, or added to --eval) |
| `--frozen` | bool |  | Never use the network and require ai-rulez.lock to cover every remote source |
| `--include-static` | bool |  | Also search skills whose delivery is static |
| `--items` | string list |  | With 'search index': also re-embed these skills (by name) although their text did not change; skills that changed or have no vector are embedded anyway |
| `--k` | int | `0` | With --eval: cut-off of recall@k, hit@k and nDCG@k (default: the file's k, then 5) |
| `--limit` | int | `5` | Maximum results (max 20) |
| `--max-flips` | int | `0` | With --eval --baseline: fail when more cases than this went from found to missed |
| `--min` | string |  | With --eval: fail when a metric is below a floor, e.g. top1=0.6,mrr=0.7 (metrics: top1, recall, hit, mrr, ndcg) |
| `--min-count` | int | `1` | With 'search mine': keep a query only when it was followed by the same skill at least this many times |
| `--mode` | string |  | Ranking: lexical, hybrid or vector (default: [search] mode, then lexical). With --eval a comma-separated list, or all |
| `--offline` | bool |  | Never use the network; use cached content |
| `--output` / `-o` | string |  | With --eval: also write the result as JSON to this file |
| `--profile` | string |  | Profile whose skills to search (default: the configured default profile) |
| `--purge` | bool |  | With 'search mine': delete the query log after reading it |
| `--rebuild` | bool |  | With 'search index': re-embed every skill, ignoring the existing index |
| `--role` | string |  | Search only the skills of this role (see 'ai-rulez roles list'); mutually exclusive with --profile |
| `--source` | string list |  | Also search the skills of a source, repeatable: [git+]<url>[@<tag\|commit>][#<subdir>] or a local directory |
| `--targets` | string |  | Preset whose rendering of the skills to search |

#### `ai-rulez sign`

Sign the lock, a plugin bundle, a skill or an SBOM into a Sigstore bundle

```text
ai-rulez sign [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
ai-rulez sign --lock --keyless
ai-rulez sign --lock --key cosign.key --output ai-rulez.lock.sigstore.json
ai-rulez sign --sbom sbom.cdx.json --keyless
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `--append` | bool |  | Write a co-signature file next to the existing attestation instead of replacing it (for [signing] thresholds) |
| `--builder-id` | string |  | With --provenance: the builder id to record (default: the GitHub Actions workflow reference, else ai-rulez's own) |
| `--bundle` | string |  | Sign the plugin bundle directory (tree digest of its files) into <dir>/.ai-rulez.sigstore.json |
| `--embed-items` | bool |  | Put the pinned item ids and digests in the statement (ids can be sensitive in a private repository) |
| `--format` | string | `text` | Output format: text, json |
| `--fulcio-url` | string |  | With --keyless: Fulcio URL (default <https://fulcio.sigstore.dev>) |
| `--identity-token-env` | string |  | With --keyless: environment variable holding the OIDC token (default: the GitHub Actions runtime token) |
| `--interactive` | bool |  | With --keyless: open a browser for the OIDC login when no token is available |
| `--key` | string |  | PEM private key file, or a KMS key URI (awskms://, gcpkms://, azurekms://, hashivault://), to sign with |
| `--key-password-env` | string |  | Environment variable holding the key password (default AI_RULEZ_SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD, then COSIGN_PASSWORD) |
| `--keyless` | bool |  | Sign with a short-lived Fulcio certificate and log the signature in Rekor (network; public log) |
| `--lock` | bool |  | Sign the lock-subject statement of ai-rulez.lock |
| `--org-policy` | string |  | Sign an organization policy file into <file>.sigstore.json |
| `--output` / `-o` | string |  | Write the bundle here instead of next to the lock |
| `--provenance` | bool |  | With --bundle: also write a SLSA v1 provenance statement (.ai-rulez.provenance.sigstore.json); it is the signer's own account of the build |
| `--public-key-out` | string |  | With --key: write the signing key's PEM public key to this file |
| `--rekor-url` | string |  | Rekor URL for --keyless or --tlog (default <https://rekor.sigstore.dev>) |
| `--sbom` | string |  | Sign an SBOM file into <file>.sigstore.json |
| `--skill` | string |  | Sign a skill directory a publisher ships into <dir>/.ai-rulez.sigstore.json |
| `--tlog` | bool |  | With --key: also record the signature in the Rekor transparency log (network; public log) |

#### `ai-rulez skill install`

Install a named skill from a git repository or local path

```text
ai-rulez skill install <name> [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash

```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `--domain` | string |  | Place the skills in this domain, so a profile or role selects them by domain |
| `--exclude` | string list |  | Glob of skill directory names to skip; wins over --include (repeatable) |
| `--format` | string | `text` | Output format: text, json |
| `--include` | string list |  | Glob of skill directory names to install from a directory of skills (repeatable) |
| `--include-prerelease` | bool |  | Let --version match pre-release tags |
| `--local` | bool |  | Write to the machine-local config.local.* overlay instead of the shared config |
| `--local-override` | string |  | Directory used instead of the source while it exists (local development of a remote skill) |
| `--min-release-age` | string |  | Skip tags younger than this, such as 7d (holds back brand-new releases) |
| `--name-prefix` | string |  | Prefix added to every installed skill name |
| `--path` | string |  | Path within repo to skill directory (defaults to skills/<name>) |
| `--profile` | string list |  | Restrict the skills to these profiles (repeatable) |
| `--ref` | string |  | Git reference: branch, tag, or commit hash |
| `--resources` | string list |  | Extra file patterns to bundle with each skill, "!" removes (repeatable) |
| `--source` | string |  | Git URL or local path (required) |
| `--tag-prefix` | string |  | Only consider tags with this prefix when resolving --version, such as v or skills/ |
| `--trust` | string |  | Scan level for the installed skills: error (default) or warn |
| `--version` | string |  | Version range of the source's tags, such as ^1.2 (instead of --ref) |

| `--role` | string |  | Role active in this session (recorded as given; else $AI_RULEZ_ROLE) |
| `--root` | string |  | Project root (default $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, else the nearest directory holding the config directory) |
| `--salt-file` | string |  | File holding the session-hash salt (default usage.salt beside the log; $AI_RULEZ_USAGE_SALT wins) |
| `--served` | bool |  | Mark the skill load as served by the MCP server |
| `--sink-command` | string |  | Shell command that receives each usage log line on stdin |

#### `ai-rulez tokens`

Report the prompt-token cost of generated artifacts

```text
ai-rulez tokens [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
ai-rulez tokens
ai-rulez tokens --budget 20000
ai-rulez tokens --by-role
ai-rulez tokens --format json
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `--budget` | int | `0` | Fail when the headline always-loaded count exceeds this ceiling |
| `--by-role` | bool |  | Report every declared role as one column of a comparison table |
| `--compare-profiles` | string list |  | Report this profile as one column of a comparison table; repeat per column |
| `--discover-org` | bool |  | Also load the organization policy of the repository's GitHub owner (ai-rulez-policy.toml in <owner>/.github); needs a digest from [policy.digests] in the user config or --policy-trust-tofu. A convenience layer, not an anchor: see docs/policy.md |
| `--format` | string | `text` | Output format: text, json |
| `--no-local` | bool |  | Ignore the machine-local config.local.* overlay and local/ content (the view a teammate without them sees) |
| `--policy` | string |  | Organization policy: a file, or an https URL pinned with @sha256:<hex> (tighten-only; also AI_RULEZ_POLICY and the managed path). A repository can only add restrictions to it; see docs/policy.md |
| `--policy-digest` | string |  | The digest (sha256:<hex>) the --policy file or URL must have; a mismatch fails closed (AR741) |
| `--policy-max-stale` | string |  | How long a cached copy of a URL policy may stand in for an unreachable URL, for example 7d or 168h; 0 allows none (default 7d, or AI_RULEZ_POLICY_MAX_STALE) |
| `--policy-mode` | string |  | How a repository that loosens the organization policy is treated: enforce (default, the run fails) or warn (reported as warnings, for rollout; the policy values are still enforced) |
| `--policy-offline` | bool |  | Load a URL policy from the user cache only (also AI_RULEZ_POLICY_OFFLINE=1); a cached copy older than --policy-max-stale fails closed |
| `--policy-require-signed` | bool |  | Refuse a policy that has no valid signature (<policy>.sigstore.json next to it); needs a trusted signer (also AI_RULEZ_POLICY_REQUIRE_SIGNED=1) |
| `--policy-signer-identity` | string |  | Certificate identity trusted to sign the policy, with --policy-signer-issuer (keyless signing) |
| `--policy-signer-issuer` | string |  | OIDC issuer of --policy-signer-identity |
| `--policy-signer-key` | string list |  | PEM public key trusted to sign the policy (repeatable; also AI_RULEZ_POLICY_SIGNER_KEY and [[policy.signers]] in the user config) |
| `--policy-trust-tofu` | bool |  | Accept the digest of an unpinned --policy URL once, in a terminal, and record it in the user cache; pin it afterwards |
| `--policy-trusted-root` | string |  | Sigstore trusted root file for keyless policy signatures (default: the root that ai-rulez trust update cached) |
| `--profile` | string |  | Profile to report on, or a comma-separated list to compose several |
| `--role` | string |  | Report on this role's content slice instead of a profile (see 'ai-rulez roles list') |
| `--tokenizer` | string | `cl100k_base` | Token counter to use: cl100k_base or estimate |

#### `ai-rulez update`



| `--major` | bool |  | Handle only sources that have a newer major version: print the constraint that would take it |
| `--offline` | bool |  | Refuse to run: update reads the remote's tags |
| `--policy` | string |  | Organization policy: a file, or an https URL pinned with @sha256:<hex> (tighten-only; also AI_RULEZ_POLICY and the managed path). A repository can only add restrictions to it; see docs/policy.md |
| `--policy-digest` | string |  | The digest (sha256:<hex>) the --policy file or URL must have; a mismatch fails closed (AR741) |
| `--policy-max-stale` | string |  | How long a cached copy of a URL policy may stand in for an unreachable URL, for example 7d or 168h; 0 allows none (default 7d, or AI_RULEZ_POLICY_MAX_STALE) |
| `--policy-mode` | string |  | How a repository that loosens the organization policy is treated: enforce (default, the run fails) or warn (reported as warnings, for rollout; the policy values are still enforced) |
| `--policy-offline` | bool |  | Load a URL policy from the user cache only (also AI_RULEZ_POLICY_OFFLINE=1); a cached copy older than --policy-max-stale fails closed |
| `--policy-require-signed` | bool |  | Refuse a policy that has no valid signature (<policy>.sigstore.json next to it); needs a trusted signer (also AI_RULEZ_POLICY_REQUIRE_SIGNED=1) |
| `--policy-signer-identity` | string |  | Certificate identity trusted to sign the policy, with --policy-signer-issuer (keyless signing) |
| `--policy-signer-issuer` | string |  | OIDC issuer of --policy-signer-identity |
| `--policy-signer-key` | string list |  | PEM public key trusted to sign the policy (repeatable; also AI_RULEZ_POLICY_SIGNER_KEY and [[policy.signers]] in the user config) |
| `--policy-trust-tofu` | bool |  | Accept the digest of an unpinned --policy URL once, in a terminal, and record it in the user cache; pin it afterwards |
| `--policy-trusted-root` | string |  | Sigstore trusted root file for keyless policy signatures (default: the root that ai-rulez trust update cached) |
| `--write-config` | bool |  | With --major, rewrite the version line of those sources in config.toml and move their pins |

#### `ai-rulez validate`

Validate AI rules configuration and content

```text
ai-rulez validate [flags]
```

Aliases: `val`

Examples:

```bash
ai-rulez validate
ai-rulez validate --strict
ai-rulez validate --changed
ai-rulez validate --changed=origin/main
ai-rulez validate --explain AR001
ai-rulez validate --format sarif --output ai-rulez.sarif
ai-rulez validate --fix --dry-run
ai-rulez validate --path catalog --glob "plugins/**/*.json"
ai-rulez validate --outputs
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `--allow-egress` | string list |  | With --external, allow the named [[lint.external]] scanners that declare egress = true to run (repeatable) |
| `--analyzer` | string list |  | Run only these analyzers (repeatable or comma-separated; replaces [lint] analyzers): budgets, config, convert, delivery, descriptions, duplicates, evals, exposure, hooks, llmstxt, lock, mcp, metadata, okf, plugin, references, roles, search, security, traps, verifiers |
| `--approvals-base` | string |  | Report approvals added since this git revision for content that also changed since it (AR716) |
| `--baseline` | string |  | Accept the findings recorded in this baseline file (default: <config dir>/lint-baseline.json when it exists); only new findings count toward the exit code |
| `--baseline-reason` | string |  | With --update-baseline, the reason stored on new entries (required for security findings) |
| `--changed` | string |  | Like --since, with an optional base: bare --changed is --since HEAD (only files with uncommitted or untracked changes) and --changed=REV is --since REV |
| `--config-only` | bool |  | Check the configuration file only and skip the content checks |
| `--discover-org` | bool |  | Also load the organization policy of the repository's GitHub owner (ai-rulez-policy.toml in <owner>/.github); needs a digest from [policy.digests] in the user config or --policy-trust-tofu. A convenience layer, not an anchor: see docs/policy.md |
| `--dry-run` / `-n` | bool |  | With --fix or --fix-unsafe, print the unified diff and change nothing |
| `--exclude` | string list |  | Leave the files matching this glob (relative to the project root, for example "x/src/public/skills/**") out of the files found by convention, --path and --glob; works without a configuration. Findings in the configured content tree are dropped with [lint] ignore_paths in config.toml (repeatable) |
| `--explain` | string |  | Print what a rule (code or name, for example AR001) checks, why, examples and how to suppress it, then exit |
| `--external` | bool |  | Also run the scanners configured in [[lint.external]] and merge their findings |
| `--fail-on` | string |  | Lowest severity that exits 2: error (default), warning, info or none |
| `--fix` | bool |  | Apply the safe automatic fixes to authored sources: executable bits (AR502, AR503, AR505), frontmatter key renames (AR303), quoted booleans (AR304), unclosed code fences (AR806) and missing final newlines (AR807). Harness trap fixes (AR9C7 and project AR9CA key-misspelled rows) also rewrite a misspelled frontmatter key in hand-written harness files outside .ai-rulez/. Never touches generated outputs or security findings |
| `--fix-unsafe` | bool |  | Also apply fixes that can change meaning: skill name normalization (AR804). Implies --fix |
| `--format` | string | `text` | Output format: text, json, sarif, github, junit, markdown |
| `--glob` | string list |  | Also lint the files matching this glob, relative to the project root (repeatable, for example "catalog/**/*.json"). A matched file that is not linted is named on stderr as "<file>: not linted (<reason>)" and in the JSON report's notices, and a glob that matches nothing warns |
| `--lint-profile` | string |  | Lint preset: default, strict or permissive (overrides [lint] profile; distinct from the generation --profile) |
| `--mcp-user-scope` | bool |  | Also check MCP servers against the configured harnesses' user and local scopes, and warn about a user-scope server whose launch command does not resolve (reads files outside the project, for example ~/.claude.json or ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json); needs --strict |
| `--min-severity` | string |  | With --write-baseline, record only findings of at least this severity (info, warning, error) |
| `--no-local` | bool |  | Ignore the machine-local config.local.* overlay and local/ content (the view a teammate without them sees) |
| `--no-scan-cache` | bool |  | With --external, ignore and do not update the scanner result cache |
| `--offline` | bool |  | Skip fetching remote includes, use cached content only (as generate --offline) |
| `--output` / `-o` | string |  | Write the report to this file instead of stdout |
| `--outputs` | bool |  | Also lint the generated files (what generate writes, or would write) for secrets, broken references and descriptions; a finding in one is marked as output and a problem the authored source already has is reported once (the same as [lint] lint_outputs) |
| `--path` | string list |  | Also lint this file or directory, which must lie inside the project root (repeatable; outside git a path above the configuration's directory widens the root to the nearest directory holding both, if it lies inside the working directory; a marketplace, plugin, hook file or skill is recognized by its content wherever it is). A path that does not exist or leaves the root exits 1, and so does a named file that is unreadable or over 2 MiB. A text file named here that is no content kind (.env, YAML) is scanned for secrets only |
| `--policy` | string |  | Organization policy: a file, or an https URL pinned with @sha256:<hex> (tighten-only; also AI_RULEZ_POLICY and the managed path). A repository can only add restrictions to it; see docs/policy.md |
| `--policy-digest` | string |  | The digest (sha256:<hex>) the --policy file or URL must have; a mismatch fails closed (AR741) |
| `--policy-max-stale` | string |  | How long a cached copy of a URL policy may stand in for an unreachable URL, for example 7d or 168h; 0 allows none (default 7d, or AI_RULEZ_POLICY_MAX_STALE) |
| `--policy-mode` | string |  | How a repository that loosens the organization policy is treated: enforce (default, the run fails) or warn (reported as warnings, for rollout; the policy values are still enforced) |
| `--policy-offline` | bool |  | Load a URL policy from the user cache only (also AI_RULEZ_POLICY_OFFLINE=1); a cached copy older than --policy-max-stale fails closed |
| `--policy-require-signed` | bool |  | Refuse a policy that has no valid signature (<policy>.sigstore.json next to it); needs a trusted signer (also AI_RULEZ_POLICY_REQUIRE_SIGNED=1) |
| `--policy-signer-identity` | string |  | Certificate identity trusted to sign the policy, with --policy-signer-issuer (keyless signing) |
| `--policy-signer-issuer` | string |  | OIDC issuer of --policy-signer-identity |
| `--policy-signer-key` | string list |  | PEM public key trusted to sign the policy (repeatable; also AI_RULEZ_POLICY_SIGNER_KEY and [[policy.signers]] in the user config) |
| `--policy-trust-tofu` | bool |  | Accept the digest of an unpinned --policy URL once, in a terminal, and record it in the user cache; pin it afterwards |
| `--policy-trusted-root` | string |  | Sigstore trusted root file for keyless policy signatures (default: the root that ai-rulez trust update cached) |
| `--reason` | string |  | With --write-baseline, why the findings are accepted (stored on each new entry); {rule}, {severity} and {scanner} are replaced per entry |
| `--reason-for` | string list |  | With --write-baseline, RULE=text: the reason of new entries of that rule (a glob; repeatable); --reason covers the rest |
| `--recursive` | bool |  | Validate every configuration file found recursively |
| `--repo-root` | string |  | Repository root that repo-relative paths and git-tracked globs resolve against (env AI_RULEZ_REPO_ROOT; default: the git toplevel, else the config's parent directory) |
| `--rule` | string list |  | With --write-baseline, record only findings of this scanner rule id, scanner:rule or AR code (a glob; repeatable) |
| `--scanner-baseline` | string |  | With --external, the scanner baseline file (default: [lint.scanner_policy] baseline, else <config dir>/scanner-baseline.json) |
| `--show-policy` | bool |  | Print the effective organization policy with the origin of every value and what the repository tried to loosen (text, or JSON with --format json), then exit |
| `--show-suppressed` | bool |  | With --external, also show scanner results the tool marked suppressed, as info |
| `--since` | string |  | Report only findings in files changed since this git revision (committed, staged, unstaged and untracked) and in files that refer to them; references are still resolved against the whole tree |
| `--since-depth` | string | `1` | With --since or --changed, how many reference hops to follow from the changed files: a number or "all" for every file that depends on them, directly or not (findings are marked changed, dependent or transitive(n) in json) |
| `--since-max-files` | int | `0` | With --since or --changed, report at most this many files besides the changed ones, nearest first (0: no cap) |
| `--strict` | bool |  | Fail on warnings as well as errors (the same as --fail-on warning) |
| `--strict-baseline` | bool |  | Also fail (exit 2) when the baseline has stale or expired entries, so fixed findings must leave it |
| `--tracked-only` | bool |  | Report no findings in git-untracked files, except those --changed names, so results do not depend on untracked files a local run left behind, such as __pycache__ (same as [lint] tracked_only = true; outside a git work tree every finding is kept, with a warning) |
| `--update-baseline` | bool |  | Record every current finding in the baseline (keeping existing reasons and dropping stale entries) and exit 0 |
| `--verifiers` | bool |  | Also evaluate the verifiers (never a command or a model) and report them as AR9H findings |
| `--write-baseline` | bool |  | With --external, accept every current scanner finding in scanner-baseline.json (needs --reason) and exit as if they were clean |

#### `ai-rulez verifiers run`

Evaluate the verifiers and report pass or fail for each

```text
ai-rulez verifiers run [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash

ai-rulez verifiers run --staged --fail-on warning
ai-rulez verifiers run --format sarif --output verifiers.sarif
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `--all` | bool |  | Evaluate every file (the default) |
| `--allow-exec` | bool |  | Let command predicates run a program (or set AI_RULEZ_VERIFIERS_ALLOW_EXEC=1); never implied by another flag |
| `--allow-llm` | bool |  | Evaluate llm verifiers: sends the changed lines to the configured model (needs allow_network in the user config) |
| `--estimate` | bool |  | Print which files and how many bytes llm verifiers would send and the cost bound, and call nothing |
| `--fail-on` | string |  | Lowest failing severity: error (default), warning, info or none |
| `--format` | string | `text` | Output format: text, json, sarif, junit |
| `--gate-llm` | bool |  | Let a failing llm verifier of error severity fail the run when its calibration record (verifiers calibrate) is current and meets the bar; otherwise every llm verdict stays a warning |
| `--max-cost` | number | `0.5` | Most an llm verifier run may cost in USD (0 removes this cap; [llm] limits still apply) |
| `--name` | string list |  | Run only the named verifier (repeatable) |
| `--no-local` | bool |  | Ignore the machine-local config.local.* overlay and local/ content |
| `--output` / `-o` | string |  | Write the report to this file instead of stdout |
| `--profile` | string |  | Active profile: sets the profile of generated_in_sync verifiers that name none, and which rules count as active (default: from config) |
| `--role` | string |  | Active role: verifiers whose rule or skill the role does not keep are reported inactive |
| `--rule` | string |  | Run only the verifiers that enforce this rule, skill, agent or command |
| `--since` | string |  | Evaluate only files changed since the merge base of REV and HEAD (plus uncommitted and untracked) |
| `--staged` | bool |  | Evaluate only staged changes |
| `--strict` | bool |  | Also exit non-zero when a warning-severity verifier fails |
| `--strict-applicability` | bool |  | Report a verifier whose when_changed matches no file (AR9H5) |

#### `ai-rulez verify`

```text
ai-rulez verify [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
ai-rulez verify --plugin
ai-rulez verify --approvals
ai-rulez verify --attestation
ai-rulez verify --self
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `--approvals` | bool |  | Re-check the signed and review-linked approvals that apply to the current content |
| `--attestation` | bool |  | Verify the signed lock (ai-rulez.lock.sigstore.json) offline against the [signing] policy |
| `--attestation-file` | string |  | With --attestation: the bundle to verify (default: next to the lock) |
| `--bundle` | string |  | Verify the attestation of this plugin bundle directory (implies --attestation) |
| `--discover-org` | bool |  | Also load the organization policy of the repository's GitHub owner (ai-rulez-policy.toml in <owner>/.github); needs a digest from [policy.digests] in the user config or --policy-trust-tofu. A convenience layer, not an anchor: see docs/policy.md |
| `--format` | string | `text` | Output format: text, json |
| `--identity` | string |  | With --attestation: also trust this certificate identity (needs --issuer) |
| `--if-configured` | bool |  | Skip plugin verification when no plugin authoring configuration is present |
| `--if-generated` | bool |  | Skip plugin verification when the plugin bundle has not been generated yet |
| `--issuer` | string |  | With --attestation: the OIDC issuer of --identity |
| `--lock` | bool |  | With --attestation: verify the lock attestation (the default and only subject) |
| `--marketplace-name` | string list |  | With --plugin: only the marketplace of this name, its index and its plugins (repeatable) |
| `--no-state` | bool |  | With --attestation: do not read or update the per-user rollback state |
| `--online` | bool |  | With --approvals: also check review-linked approvals against the forge (needs the network and a token) |
| `--plugin` | bool |  | Verify generated plugin bundles using provenance hashes |
| `--plugin-name` | string list |  | With --plugin: only the plugin of this name (repeatable); the marketplace indexes are left alone |
| `--policy` | string |  | Organization policy: a file, or an https URL pinned with @sha256:<hex> (tighten-only; also AI_RULEZ_POLICY and the managed path). A repository can only add restrictions to it; see docs/policy.md |
| `--policy-digest` | string |  | The digest (sha256:<hex>) the --policy file or URL must have; a mismatch fails closed (AR741) |
| `--policy-max-stale` | string |  | How long a cached copy of a URL policy may stand in for an unreachable URL, for example 7d or 168h; 0 allows none (default 7d, or AI_RULEZ_POLICY_MAX_STALE) |
| `--policy-mode` | string |  | How a repository that loosens the organization policy is treated: enforce (default, the run fails) or warn (reported as warnings, for rollout; the policy values are still enforced) |
| `--policy-offline` | bool |  | Load a URL policy from the user cache only (also AI_RULEZ_POLICY_OFFLINE=1); a cached copy older than --policy-max-stale fails closed |
| `--policy-require-signed` | bool |  | Refuse a policy that has no valid signature (<policy>.sigstore.json next to it); needs a trusted signer (also AI_RULEZ_POLICY_REQUIRE_SIGNED=1) |
| `--policy-signer-identity` | string |  | Certificate identity trusted to sign the policy, with --policy-signer-issuer (keyless signing) |
| `--policy-signer-issuer` | string |  | OIDC issuer of --policy-signer-identity |
| `--policy-signer-key` | string list |  | PEM public key trusted to sign the policy (repeatable; also AI_RULEZ_POLICY_SIGNER_KEY and [[policy.signers]] in the user config) |
| `--policy-trust-tofu` | bool |  | Accept the digest of an unpinned --policy URL once, in a terminal, and record it in the user cache; pin it afterwards |
| `--policy-trusted-root` | string |  | Sigstore trusted root file for keyless policy signatures (default: the root that ai-rulez trust update cached) |
| `--profile` | string |  | Profile used to generate the plugin bundle |
| `--public-key` | string list |  | With --attestation: also trust this PEM public key for the lock (repeatable) |
| `--recursive` | bool |  | Verify plugin outputs for configurations recursively |
| `--require-provenance` | bool |  | With --bundle: require a verified SLSA provenance statement next to the bundle attestation |
| `--sbom` | string |  | Verify the attestation of this SBOM file (implies --attestation) |
| `--self` | bool |  | Verify this ai-rulez binary against its release's Sigstore bundle (offline) |
| `--skill` | string |  | Verify the publisher attestation of this skill directory (implies --attestation) |
| `--source` | string |  | With --skill: the skill source or installed skill name, to apply [[signing.trust]] entries scoped by source |
| `--trusted-root` | string |  | With --attestation: Sigstore trusted root file (default: [signing] trusted_root, else the cache of 'ai-rulez trust update') |

#### `ai-rulez version`

Print the version number of ai-rulez

```text
ai-rulez version [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
ai-rulez version
ai-rulez version --format json
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `--format` | string | `text` | Output format: text, json |

## Schema

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/schema/

ai-rulez publishes JSON Schemas for its configuration file and for every JSON document its commands print. Use the
configuration schema for editor completion and validation; use the report schemas to parse `--format json` output in
scripts and CI.

#### Configuration schema

`schema/ai-rules.schema.json` describes `.ai-rulez/config.toml` (and a root `ai-rulez.toml`). The schema is embedded
in the CLI: `ai-rulez validate` converts the TOML to JSON, validates it against the schema, then runs the structural
checks.

```toml
# .ai-rulez/config.toml
version = "5.0"
name = "billing"
presets = ["cursor", "codex"]
preset = "claude"
```

```bash
ai-rulez validate
```

```text
Error: configuration has 1 unknown or invalid key(s) in .../.ai-rulez/config.toml

Validation errors:
  - .../.ai-rulez/config.toml: unknown key "preset" (did you mean "presets"?)

Hint: Fix the keys above; a "did you mean" names the closest known key
```

The schema sets `additionalProperties: false` at the top level, so a misspelled key is an error, not a silent no-op.

##### Editor support

With the Even Better TOML extension in VS Code, associate the file with the schema in `.vscode/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "evenBetterToml.schema.associations": {
    ".ai-rulez/config.toml": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/main/schema/ai-rules.schema.json"
  }
}
```

The `main` URL tracks the development tip. To match the CLI you run, replace `main` with the release tag. The
configuration also accepts a `schema` key (the TOML spelling of `$schema`), so a file that carries a schema reference
still validates.

##### Required keys

| Key | Type | Constraint |
| --- | ---- | ---------- |
| `version` | string | Must be `"5.0"`. An older version fails with a hint to run `ai-rulez migrate v5`. |
| `name` | string | Project name, non-empty. |

##### Top-level keys

Every other key is optional. The table lists each key once; the linked page has the details.

| Key | Purpose | See |
| --- | ------- | --- |
| `description` | Project description | [Configuration](configuration.md) |
| `presets` | Harnesses to generate for (built-in names or custom preset objects) | [Supported harnesses](harnesses.md), [Custom presets](profiles.md) |
| `default`, `profiles` | Named domain combinations and the default one | [Domains & profiles](domains.md) |
| `default_layers` | `config.<name>.toml` layers always merged over this file | [Configuration](configuration.md) |
| `scopes` | Extra output roots, such as a subfolder `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` | [Monorepo](monorepo.md) |
| `recursive_exclude` | Directories `generate --recursive` never searches | [Monorepo](monorepo.md) |
| `source` | Where content is read from: `ai-rulez` (default) or `agents` | [.agents as a source](agents-source.md) |
| `agents_md`, `agents_md_split` | Shared `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/skills` output; split `AGENTS.md` by heading | [AGENTS.md](agents-md.md), [.agents as a source](agents-source.md) |
| `rules`, `compact` | How rules are written (`split` or `inline`) and whether priority labels are shown | [Rules](rules.md) |
| `header` | Header of generated files | [Configuration](configuration.md) |
| `defaults` | Global and per-preset effort and model | [Configuration](configuration.md) |
| `builtins` | Built-in domains (`true`, `false`, or a list with `!` exclusions) | [Configuration](configuration.md) |
| `gitignore`, `gitignore_exclude` | Managed `.gitignore` block (off by default) and patterns kept out of it | [Configuration](configuration.md) |
| `skip_outputs` | Output kinds ai-rulez never writes, overwrites or deletes | [Configuration](configuration.md) |
| `codex_skills_dir`, `codex` | Codex skill directory and options | [Configuration](configuration.md) |
| `claude` | Claude Code options (`[claude.settings]`, `[claude.skills]`) | [Configuration](configuration.md) |
| `bundle_exclude` | Files left out of skill and command resource bundles | [Configuration](configuration.md) |
| `includes` | Content sources (git or local) to merge | [Includes](includes.md) |
| `installed_skills` | Skills installed from other repositories | [Installed skills](installed-skills.md) |
| `installed_marketplaces`, `installed_plugins`, `enabled_plugins` | Plugins the project imports or enables | [Installed plugins](installed-plugins.md) |
| `plugins`, `marketplaces` | Declarations only; no output is written for them | [Configuration](configuration.md) |
| `plugin`, `plugins_authoring`, `marketplace`, `marketplaces_authoring`, `placement` | Authoring distributable plugin bundles and marketplace indexes | [Authoring plugins](plugins.md) |
| `mcp_servers` | MCP server definitions written into each harness's MCP file | [Configuration](configuration.md#mcp_servers) |
| `mcp` | ai-rulez's own MCP entry and the settings of `ai-rulez mcp` | [MCP server](mcp-server.md#settings-in-the-configuration) |
| `skills`, `domains`, `delivery`, `skill_sources` | Dynamic skill loading: delivery defaults, the `dynamic-skills` stub, served skill sources | [MCP server](mcp-server.md#dynamic-skill-loading) |
| `search` | Ranking of `ai-rulez search` and `find_skill` | [Skill search](search.md) |
| `hooks`, `permissions`, `guard` | Hooks, permission rules and the generated-file guard | [Hooks and settings](settings.md), [Permissions](permissions.md) |
| `session_start` | `SessionStart` hook that runs generate in remote sessions | [Run generate in remote sessions](session-start.md) |
| `roles`, `role_manifest` | Roles and the `roles.json` manifest | [Roles](roles.md) |
| `lock` | Content pinning in `ai-rulez.lock` | [Lock file](lockfile.md) |
| `governance` | Which pinned content needs an approval | [Approvals](approvals.md) |
| `signing` | Who may sign the lock | [Signing](signing.md) |
| `catalog` | Defaults of `ai-rulez catalog` | [Catalog](catalog.md) |
| `lint` | Strict-validation settings | [Strict validation](strict-validation.md) |
| `verifiers`, `verifiers_settings` | Deterministic repository checks and their limits | [Verifiers](verifiers.md) |
| `exposure` | Session exposure and the area map | [Session exposure and areas](exposure.md) |
| `okf` | Open Knowledge Format bundle | [OKF](okf.md) |
| `llms_txt` | `llms.txt` output | [llms.txt](llms-txt.md) |
| `ard` | Agentic Resource Discovery manifest | [Agentic resource discovery](ard.md) |
| `publish` | What `ai-rulez publish` ships | [Publish](publish.md) |
| `usage` | Usage telemetry | [Usage telemetry](usage-telemetry.md) |
| `telemetry` | Item-load telemetry and OTLP export | [Item-load telemetry](telemetry.md) |
| `llm` | Model access for features that call a language model | [LLM access](llm.md) |
| `review`, `judge`, `improve` | Settings of `ai-rulez review`, `judge` and `improve` | [Review](review.md), [Judge](judge.md), [Improve](improve.md) |
| `$schema`, `schema`, `$comment` | Schema reference and a free-form note; ignored by generation | |

Some keys are honoured only from the user configuration or the environment, never from a repository (for example
the network and credential keys of `[llm]` and `[telemetry]`). The [trust model](trust-model.md) lists them.

##### Content frontmatter

Rule, context and skill files are markdown with optional YAML frontmatter. Two keys are constrained:

| Key | Values |
| --- | ------ |
| `priority` | `critical`, `high`, `medium` (default), `low`, `minimal` |
| `targets` | Preset names (`claude`), root files (`CLAUDE.md`), paths or base names, directory prefixes (`.cursor/rules/`), globs (`.cursor/rules/*`) or `*`. See [Targets](rules.md#targets). |

```markdown
---
priority: high
targets: ["cursor", "CLAUDE.md"]
---

# Money types

Store amounts as integer cents.
```

#### Local overlay schema

`schema/ai-rules-local.schema.json` describes the machine-local `config.local.toml`. It accepts the same keys as the
main schema without requiring `version` and `name`, and adds the overlay-only markers: `remove = true` on a named list
entry and `"!name"` in `presets`. `ai-rulez validate`, `ai-rulez local set` and the MCP `validate_config` tool check
the overlay against it. See [Local configuration](local-overrides.md#config-overlay).

#### Report and file schemas

The documents carry a `schema_version` field (`schema` in the plan document) where the Version column gives a
number. The schemas below describe those documents and the files ai-rulez reads or writes. A failure that happens
before a command has a report prints the error document instead; see [JSON contracts](cli.md#json-contracts).

##### Configuration and declarations

| `schema/ai-rules-local.schema.json` | config `"5.0"` | `config.local.toml` overlay |
| `schema/provider.schema.json` | none | Declarative provider spec of a custom preset; see [Custom presets](profiles.md) |
| `schema/policy.schema.json` | `policy_version` | Organization policy file (`--policy`, `AI_RULEZ_POLICY`, the managed path); see [Organization policy](policy.md) |
| `schema/verifiers-spec.schema.json` | none | `.ai-rulez/verifiers/*.toml` declaration files; see [Verifiers](verifiers.md) |
| `schema/eval-case.schema.json` | 1 | `*.eval.yaml`, `.yml` and `.json` skill eval cases; see [Evals](evals.md) |

#### Validating

```bash
ai-rulez validate                              # the configuration found from the current directory
ai-rulez -C .ai-rulez/config.toml validate     # a specific file
ai-rulez validate --strict                     # also fail on warnings
```

A configuration with an unsupported `version` fails before any other check:

```text
Error: config version "4.0" is no longer supported: run `ai-rulez migrate v5`

Hint: Run `ai-rulez migrate v5` to rewrite this configuration for v5 (add --dry-run to preview the change list)
```

See [Strict validation](strict-validation.md) for the content checks and their codes.

## Embedding (Go API)

Source: https://goldziher.github.io/ai-rulez/embedding/

The package `github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/v5/pkg/airulez` runs the ai-rulez engine from Go: load a project, validate
it, plan or apply a generate run, and write or check its lock. Use it in a service that renders configuration for many
repositories, in a CI bot that reviews pull requests, or in tests that need generated output without a CLI process.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log"

	"github.com/Goldziher/ai-rulez/v5/pkg/airulez"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()

	ws := airulez.NewMemWorkspace()
	ws.Set(".ai-rulez/config.toml", "version = \"5.0\"\nname = \"billing\"\npresets = [\"claude\", \"cursor\"]\n", 0o644)
	ws.Set(".ai-rulez/rules/money.md", "# Money\n\nStore amounts as integer cents.\n", 0o644)

	project, err := airulez.Load(ctx, airulez.Options{Workspace: ws})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	plan, err := project.Plan(ctx, airulez.PlanOptions{})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, f := range plan.Files {
		fmt.Println(f.Action, f.Path)
	}
	fmt.Println("digest", plan.Digest)
}
```

```text
write .claude/settings.json
write .cursor/mcp.json
write .mcp.json
write AGENTS.md
write CLAUDE.md
digest 4cec194d5229d0f359d3e87078bb3a2ada5cc5e17c3c608c40c236116e00b3e1
```

Nothing was read from disk, no process was started and nothing was written.

The package is Experimental; see [Versioning](#versioning). Everything under `internal/` is private and carries no
compatibility promise.

#### Workspaces

A `Workspace` is a read-only view of a project tree: an `io/fs` file system plus `Lstat` and `ReadLink`. Names are
slash-separated and relative to the root; `..` and absolute names are rejected.

| Constructor | Reads | Can be written by `Generate` |
| ----------- | ----- | ---------------------------- |
| `DirWorkspace(dir)` | A directory of the real file system | Yes |
| `NewMemWorkspace()` | Files you add with `Set(name, content, mode)` | No |
| `GitSnapshot(ctx, repoDir, rev, runner)` | The tree of a commit, with nothing checked out | No |

`GitSnapshot` runs git through the `Runner` you pass: `nil` uses the real git, `DenyAll()` makes the call fail.

- A symlink resolves only inside the workspace. A refused symlink is reported to `Options.Logger`, and validation
  fails on one in the project's own content.
- Machine-local files (`config.local.toml`, `.ai-rulez/local/`) are ignored unless you set `Options.WithLocal`. They
  carry the trust of the machine that wrote them, which a service loading someone else's tree should not grant. A
  snapshot never has them.

#### Loading

`Load(ctx, Options)` reads the project the workspace holds. Every field except `Workspace` is optional.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
| ----- | ------- | ------- |
| `Workspace` | required | The project tree |
| `Runner` | `DenyAll()` | Starts the external commands a load needs (git, to resolve a remote include or to bundle skill files) |
| `Env` | empty | The environment the load reads (`MapEnv` is a fixed one) |
| `Clock` | wall clock | Stamps generated files that carry a time (`FixedClock(t)` pins it) |
| `Logger` | drops everything | Receives every warning of a load, validation or plan; a `*slog.Logger` satisfies it |
| `Remote` | `false` | Fetch the remote includes and installed skills the configuration declares, through `Runner` |
| `GitToken` | empty | Token for remote fetches; sent only to hosts the fetch code allowlists |
| `WithLocal` | `false` | Read the machine-local overlay and content of a directory workspace |

A load has no ambient authority: it reads no working directory, no process environment and starts no process unless
you pass them. No organization policy applies; the `--policy` and `AI_RULEZ_POLICY` settings of the command line do
not reach the library.

An `ai-rulez.lock` is enforced as by `ai-rulez generate`: when the lock exists and `[lock] enforce` is not `false`, a
remote source the lock does not cover fails `Load`.

Two `Project` values share no state, so a service can plan different projects concurrently. The operations of one
`Project` are serialized; load one per request or per worker.

`Project.Name()` returns the project name and `Project.Presets()` the configured presets in order.

#### Planning

`Project.Plan(ctx, PlanOptions{Profile, Role})` lists every file a generate run would write, merge into or remove,
and writes nothing. An empty `Profile` is the configured default; `Role` renders a role's slice instead.

| Field | Meaning |
| ----- | ------- |
| `Files` | One `PlanFile` per output, sorted by path: `Path`, `Action` (`write`, `merge` or `mkdir`), `Mode` (octal), `Size` and `SHA256` of the rendered content, and the flags `LocalOnly`, `Sensitive` (may carry a secret; no size or digest) and `Raw` |
| `Removals` | What a run takes back: `Path` and `Reason` (`stale`, `unmerge` or `delete`) |
| `Digest` | SHA-256 of the canonical plan document |
| `JSON()` | The plan document, indented and deterministic, as described by `schema/plan.schema.json` and printed by `ai-rulez generate --emit-plan` |

The plan reads existing outputs from the workspace too: the previous manifest, merged documents such as
`.claude/settings.json`, and hand-edited files. A workspace in memory or in a commit therefore plans its own removals
the way a directory does. As a consequence `Digest` covers the sources *and* the existing outputs: the same sources in
an empty directory and in one holding earlier outputs give different digests.

#### Generating

`Project.Generate(ctx, GenerateOptions{Profile, Mode})` applies a plan:

| Mode | Does | Result |
| ---- | ---- | ------ |
| `Write` | Writes the outputs; directory workspaces only | `Written`, the number of files written |
| `DryRun` | Lists the actions, writes nothing | `Lines` |
| `Check` | Reports files that differ from the plan, writes nothing | `Drift`, each with `Path` and `Kind` (`missing`, `stale`, `edited`, `orphan` or `blocked`) |

These are the same appliers as `generate`, `generate --dry-run` and `generate --check`.

```go
ws, err := airulez.DirWorkspace("/srv/checkouts/billing")
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}
project, err := airulez.Load(ctx, airulez.Options{Workspace: ws})
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}
res, err := project.Generate(ctx, airulez.GenerateOptions{Mode: airulez.Check})
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}
for _, d := range res.Drift {
	fmt.Println(d.Kind, d.Path)
}
```

`Write` on a memory or snapshot workspace fails with `CodeDiskRequired` before anything is read or written.

#### Validating

`Project.Validate(ctx, ValidateOptions{Strict})` checks the configuration and returns a `Report` of `Finding`s
(`Code`, `Severity`, `File`, `Line`, `Message`); `Report.OK()` is true when nothing was found. `Strict` here means "run
the content checks", unlike the CLI's `validate --strict` (which only fails on warnings): with it, `Validate` also
runs the content and security checks with their stable `AR` codes, which needs a directory workspace. Git, used to
list tracked files, runs through `Options.Runner`; with the default `DenyAll()` the directory is walked instead. A
canceled context stops validation between steps.

#### Locks

`Project.Lock(ctx, LockOptions)` writes `.ai-rulez/ai-rulez.lock` as `ai-rulez lock` does, with the same gates: the
minimum release age of version ranges, the security scan (`AR001`-`AR009`) of every remote tree about to be pinned and
of every served skill, the deny list (`AR717`) and the carry-over of approvals. The zero `LockOptions` pins everything.

| Field | Meaning |
| ----- | ------- |
| `Names` | Refresh only these remote includes, installed skills, skill sources or served skills |
| `Kind` | Refresh only one kind: `include`, `skill`, `source` or `served` |
| `ContentOnly` | Re-pin authored content and outputs only, keeping the remote pins, without the network |
| `Profile` | Profile whose outputs are pinned; empty is the one the lock recorded, else the default |
| `Roles` | Also pin the rendered outputs of every role |
| `AcceptFindings` | Pin a remote tree whose scan has error findings |
| `Strict` | Fail when the scan refuses a served skill, instead of leaving it unpinned |
| `ToolVersion` | ai-rulez version recorded in the lock |

The result has the lock `Path`, the `Tree` digest over every content pin, and `Unpinned`: the served skills the scan
refused and left out (without `Strict`).

- A remote tree with error findings, or under `Strict` a refused served skill, fails with `CodeFindings` and writes
  nothing. `errors.As(err, &fe)` with a `*airulez.FindingsError` gives each one as a `LockFinding` with its `Kind`,
  `Name`, `View` and `AR` code.
- Remote sources are re-resolved only when the project was loaded with `Options.Remote`; release times are then also
  asked of the forge over HTTPS.
- The `Project` keeps the configuration it was loaded with. Load again to plan against the new lock.

`Project.LockCheck(ctx, LockCheckOptions{Profile, ToolVersion})` is `ai-rulez lock --check` without the network. It
compares the lock with the sources, the rendered outputs and the cached remote content and returns `LockStatus`:
`InSync`, `Changes` (one line per difference) and `Notes` (differences that do not fail the check). Cached content
that disagrees with the lock is drift, not an error. The remote tag and signature checks of the command are not part of
it. A project with no lock and no `[lock] enforce` fails with `CodeLock`.

`Lock` and `LockCheck` need a directory workspace; any other fails with `CodeDiskRequired`.

#### Running commands

The engine starts external commands only through a `Runner`:

```go
type Runner interface {
	Run(ctx context.Context, spec Spec) Result
}
```

`Spec` carries `Argv`, `Dir`, `Env` (the complete child environment unless `InheritEnv`), `Stdin`, `Timeout` and
`MaxOutput`. `Result` carries a `Status` (`ok`, `exit`, `timeout`, `unavailable` or `error`), `ExitCode`, `Stdout`,
`Stderr`, truncation flags and timing; a failure is a status, never a Go error. Implement it to deny, record, sandbox
or fake commands. `DenyAll()` refuses every one and is the default.

#### Errors

Failures a caller needs to tell apart are `*airulez.Error` values with a stable `Code`; the cause is reachable with
`errors.Is` and `errors.As`.

| Code | Constant | Meaning |
| ---- | -------- | ------- |
| `load` | `CodeLoad` | The project could not be loaded |
| `plan` | `CodePlan` | The plan could not be rendered |
| `validate` | `CodeValidate` | Validation could not run (as opposed to findings) |
| `apply` | `CodeApply` | A generate run failed while applying its plan |
| `disk-required` | `CodeDiskRequired` | `Generate` with `Write`, strict `Validate`, `Lock` or `LockCheck` on a workspace that is not a directory; `errors.Is(err, airulez.ErrDiskRequired)` |
| `refused` | `CodeRefused` | A run would overwrite a file ai-rulez cannot prove it wrote (a hand-written file or a symlink); nothing was written; `errors.Is(err, airulez.ErrRefused)` |
| `lock` | `CodeLock` | `Lock` or `LockCheck` could not run |
| `findings` | `CodeFindings` | The security scan refused content while locking; the cause is a `*FindingsError` |

```go
_, err = project.Generate(ctx, airulez.GenerateOptions{Mode: airulez.Write})
var e *airulez.Error
if errors.As(err, &e) && e.Code == airulez.CodeDiskRequired {
	// plan only: this workspace lives in memory
}
```

#### Not in the API

The agent subcommand, file watching, the `init` prompts, the scanners, usage recording, the eval runners and the MCP
server are available only from the command line.

#### Versioning

- Minor releases add to the API; a breaking change comes only with a new major version and a new `/vN` module path.
- Every API is marked Experimental in its godoc for its first minor release, then follows these rules.
- The plan document has its own `schema` number: a new field is additive, a removed or re-typed field raises the
  number and is announced in the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md).
